 152          "input_profiles": {
 153              "tone": _safe_dict(state["option_context"].get("tone")),
 154              "length": _safe_dict(state["option_context"].get("length")),
 155              "brand_voice": _safe_dict(state["option_context"].get("brand_voice")),
 156              "creativity_level": _safe_str(
 157                  state["option_context"].get("creativity_level")
 158              ),
 159          },
 160          "quality_review": {
 161              "alignment_summary": rewrite["guideline_alignment_summary"],
 162              "improvements_applied": rewrite["improvements_applied"],
 163              "remaining_gaps": rewrite["remaining_gaps"],
 164              "quality_summary": quality["quality_summary"],
 165              "quality_scores": {
 166                  "overall": quality["overall_score"],
 167                  "brief_fidelity": quality["guideline_coverage_score"],
 168                  "informativeness": quality["informativeness_score"],
 169                  "originality": quality["originality_score"],
 170                  "brief_adherence": quality["brief_adherence_score"],
 171                  "seo": quality["seo_score"],
 172              },
 173              "constraint_checks": settled_checks,
 174              "readiness_blockers": list(verdict.blockers),
 175              "word_count_estimate": final_checks["word_count_estimate"],
 176              # A length blocker on its own tells the operator nothing about
 177              # which way the article missed, which is the only thing they can
 178              # act on.
 179              "word_count_check": {
 180                  key: final_checks[key]
 181                  for key in (
 182                      "target_word_count_met",
 183                      "word_count_estimate",
 184                      "word_count_delta",
 185                      "word_count_direction",
 186                      "word_count_target_min",
 187                      "word_count_target_max",
 188                  )
 189              },
 190              "repair_applied": state.get("repair_applied", False),
 191              "repair_attempts": state.get("repair_attempts", 0),
 192              # A `needs_revision` article the pipeline chose not to keep paying
 193              # for and one the auditor simply failed look identical without
 194              # this. It carries the reason, the problems and the spend.
 195              "repair_decision": state.get("repair_decision"),
 196              "groundedness": state["groundedness"],
 197              "outline_accepted": state.get("outline_accepted", False),
 198              "outline_section_count": len(
 199                  _safe_dict(state.get("outline")).get("sections") or []
 200              ),
 201              "outline_unsupported_requirements": _safe_dict(state.get("outline")).get(
 202                  "unsupported_requirements", []
 203              ),
 204              # The model that produced this review. It used to report the
 205              # worker model, which v3 never calls at all -- so a review written
 206              # by the audit model was filed under a Gemini name that had no part
 207              # in it.
 208              "model_used": state["audit_model"],
 209              # Whether the creativity control reached the stage that writes
 210              # prose. It sets `compose_temperature`, and the subscription CLI
 211              # has no temperature flag, so on a Claude-written draft the setting
 212              # is accepted and dropped. Recorded rather than hidden: a reader
 213              # comparing two drafts should not have to guess whether the dial
 214              # was connected.
 215              "creativity": {
 216                  "level": _safe_dict(state["option_context"]).get("creativity_level"),
 217                  "compose_temperature": state["compose_temperature"],
 218                  "applied_to_compose": temperature_is_honored(state["writing_model"]),
 219              },
 220              "stage_model_overrides": {
 221                  "stage_v3_outline": state["outline_model"],
 222                  "stage_v3_compose": state["writing_model"],
 223                  "stage_v3_repair": state["repair_model"],
 224                  "stage_v3_quality_audit": state["audit_model"],
 225                  "stage_v3_groundedness": state["groundedness_model"],
 226              },
 227          },
 228      }
 229      if state["include_debug"]:
 230          response_payload["debug"] = {
 231              "pipeline_input": {
 232                  "brief_fingerprint": brief["brief_fingerprint"],
 233                  "work_order_fingerprint": work_order["work_order_fingerprint"],
 234                  "form_id": brief["form_id"],
 235                  "topic_module_ids": list(brief["topic_module_ids"]),
 236                  "model_name": state["model_name"],
 237                  "outline_model": state["outline_model"],
 238                  "writing_model": state["writing_model"],
 239                  "repair_model": state["repair_model"],
 240                  "groundedness_model": state["groundedness_model"],
 241                  "audit_model": state["audit_model"],
 242                  "model_stack_id": state.get("model_stack_id"),
 243                  "include_debug": state["include_debug"],
 244                  "input_profiles": state["option_context"],
 245              },
 246              "stage_contexts": stage_context_manifest(state["stage_contexts"]),
 247              "evidence_records": evidence.get("records_text", ""),
 248              "pipeline_trace": state["trace"],
 249          }
 250  
 251      dependencies.recorder.record_stage(run_id, "pipeline_v3", response_payload)
 252      dependencies.recorder.record_artifact(
 253          run_id,
 254          {
 255              "markdown": final_markdown,
 256              "pipeline_v3": response_payload,
 257              "stages": {
 258                  "stage_v3_outline": state.get("outline", {}),
 259                  "stage_v3_compose": rewrite,
 260                  "stage_v3_groundedness": state["groundedness"],
 261                  "stage_v3_quality_audit": quality,
 262              },
 263          },
 264      )
 265      dependencies.recorder.complete(run_id)
 266      return {
 267          "current_stage": stage,
 268          "rewrite": rewrite,
 269          "final_title": final_title,
 270          "final_markdown": final_markdown,
 271          "response_payload": response_payload,
 272          "completed": True,
 273      }
apps/backend/app/features/prompt2blog/packet_v4.py
   1  """What reaches the writer's desk, and nothing else.
   2  
   3  Selection decides which facts belong in this article. Until now that decision
   4  was applied by setting a flag on the dossier and then handing the dossier
   5  down, so the writer received the cut and the receipt for it in the same
   6  breath. Measured on run `4a56545b` (`docs/audits/2026-09-06-research-redesign`):
   7  25 chosen facts arrived as 7,225 characters of claims, followed by 10,371
   8  characters naming all 28 research questions, eleven of them reading
   9  `claims: none kept for this article`. Cutting 267 of 292 facts did not make
  10  the writer's context smaller, because the context was never mostly facts.
  11  
  12  A packet is the other half of a cut: the dossier records what was learned, the
  13  selection records what belongs in this article, and this builds the view the
  14  writer reads. Three rules make it safe to be small.
  15  
  16  **It is derived, never authored.** Every string in it is copied from the
  17  dossier or the brief. No model call, no summary, no paraphrase -- a fact
  18  rewritten by a model is prose asserting something, and a drifted date inside
  19  one would pass groundedness, because groundedness checks the draft against the
  20  claim and the claim is the thing that moved.
  21  
  22  **A fact travels with what makes it true.** A source caveat, an operator's note
  23  on a venue, an unresolved disagreement about the same number: these are not
  24  spare length to trim. They come in through links -- the claim's own sources,
  25  the conflicts naming it -- so relevance is computed rather than judged, and a
  26  long note is kept precisely because it is long enough to change a sentence.
  27  
  28  **A stale packet refuses.** It carries the fingerprints of the brief, the work
  29  order, the dossier and the selection it was built from. If any of them has
  30  moved since the operator picked, the packet is not rebuilt from today's
  31  defaults and it is not silently widened back to everything -- it says so and
  32  stops. A missing selection is not permission to use every fact.
  33  
  34  Groundedness and the readiness follow-up are unaffected and still read the
  35  whole dossier. This is a projection of one record, not a second one.
  36  """
  37  
  38  from __future__ import annotations
  39  
  40  import hashlib
  41  import json
  42  from typing import Any, Literal
  43  
  44  from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
  45  
  46  from .contracts_v4 import (
  47      ArticleBrief,
  48      EvidencePackage,
  49      Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
  50  )
  51  from .selection_v4 import Selection
  52  
  53  # Bumped when the shape or the meaning of a packet changes. A run frozen under
  54  # an older one restarts rather than being reinterpreted: the whole point of
  55  # freezing the writer's input is that it means the same thing when it thaws.
  56  PACKET_POLICY_VERSION = 1
  57  
  58  # What a fact is here for. Editorial roles, and deliberately not the work
  59  # order's question kinds: a `load_bearing` question can produce a fact whose
  60  # job in the finished piece is colour, and a `texture` question can produce the
  61  # one price the reader needs. Empty means the selection did not say -- a
  62  # ranking pass that skipped the field, or a selection made before roles
  63  # existed. The outline reads that as "chosen for this article" and groups the
  64  # labelled facts around it.
  65  PacketRole = Literal["", "backbone", "practical", "texture"]
  66  
  67  
  68  class PacketRefused(ValueError):
  69      """The packet cannot be built from what it was given.
  70  
  71      Always a technical failure -- an id that names nothing, a fingerprint that
  72      moved, an empty choice. Never an editorial opinion: a packet somebody would
  73      not have chosen is still a valid packet, and this is not the place that
  74      argues with them.
  75      """
  76  
  77  
  78  class PacketModel(BaseModel):
  79      model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
  80  
  81  
  82  class PacketFact(PacketModel):
  83      """One chosen claim, verbatim, with what the writer needs to state it."""
  84  
  85      claim_id: str
  86      # Exactly what research returned. Never rewritten, never shortened.
  87      text: str
  88      role: PacketRole = ""
  89      # The selection's own one-liner on why this fact is here. Editorial intent,
  90      # not a fact, and it is what lets compose know a claim is available
  91      # material rather than a sentence it owes the reader.
  92      reason: str = ""
  93      as_of: str | None = None
  94      confidence: str
  95      # The operator looked at this place and wrote this down. It outranks
  96      # anything research said about the same venue.
  97      operator_note: str = ""
  98  
  99  
 100  class PacketNote(PacketModel):
 101      """A limitation that changes how one of the chosen facts may be stated."""
 102  
 103      note_id: str
 104      kind: Literal["source_note", "conflict"]
 105      text: str
 106      # Which of the chosen facts it bears on. Nothing reaches the packet
 107      # without at least one, which is what keeps this from becoming a second
 108      # dossier.
 109      claim_ids: list[str]
 110  
 111  
 112  class PacketMaterial(PacketModel):
 113      """Something the operator has, in their own words.
 114  
 115      Copied from the brief unchanged. First-hand material is never handed to a
 116      researcher to verify and never restated as an evidence claim -- a person
 117      saying what they saw is not a web page making an assertion.
 118      """
 119  
 120      kind: str
 121      statement: str
 122      note: str = ""
 123  
 124  
 125  class WritingPacket(PacketModel):
 126      """The material for one article, frozen at the moment writing was asked for."""
 127  
 128      policy_version: int = PACKET_POLICY_VERSION
 129      brief_fingerprint: str
 130      work_order_fingerprint: str
 131      evidence_fingerprint: str
 132      selection_fingerprint: str
 133      target_word_count: int
 134      facts: list[PacketFact]
 135      notes: list[PacketNote]
 136      supplied_material: list[PacketMaterial]
 137  
 138      def claim_ids(self) -> set[str]:
 139          """The only facts any writing stage may cite.
 140  
 141          The outline validator checks planned claim ids against this rather than
 142          against the dossier, so a section cannot be planned around a fact the
 143          writer will never see.
 144          """
 145          return {fact.claim_id for fact in self.facts}
 146  
 147      def receipt(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
 148          """What a finished run has to be able to show about its own hand-off.
 149  
 150          Sizes rather than text: the packet itself is already stored with the
 151          run, and a receipt that repeats it is a second copy to drift from.
 152          """
 153          return {
 154              "policy_version": self.policy_version,
 155              "brief_fingerprint": self.brief_fingerprint,
 156              "work_order_fingerprint": self.work_order_fingerprint,
 157              "evidence_fingerprint": self.evidence_fingerprint,
 158              "selection_fingerprint": self.selection_fingerprint,
 159              "target_word_count": self.target_word_count,
 160              "claim_ids": sorted(self.claim_ids()),
 161              "fact_count": len(self.facts),
 162              "note_count": len(self.notes),
 163              "material_count": len(self.supplied_material),
 164              "roles": {
 165                  role: sum(1 for fact in self.facts if fact.role == role)
 166                  for role in sorted({fact.role for fact in self.facts})
 167              },
 168              "characters": {
 169                  "facts": sum(len(fact.text) for fact in self.facts),
 170                  "notes": sum(len(note.text) for note in self.notes),
 171                  "material": sum(
 172                      len(item.statement) for item in self.supplied_material
 173                  ),
 174              },
 175          }
 176  
 177  
 178  def _digest(payload: Any) -> str:
 179      return hashlib.sha256(
 180          json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
 181      ).hexdigest()[:32]
 182  
 183  
 184  def selection_fingerprint(selection: Selection) -> str:
 185      """The editorial decision, as an identity.
 186  
 187      Over the decision and not over the reasoning: the order, the line, the
 188      overrides and the roles. Re-running the ranker and getting the same order
 189      back produces the same fingerprint, because the same article was chosen.
 190      """
 191      return _digest(
 192          {
 193              "order": list(selection.order),
 194              "merged": dict(sorted(selection.merged.items())),
 195              "keep_count": selection.keep_count,
 196              "rescued": sorted(selection.rescued),
 197              "dropped": sorted(selection.dropped),
 198              "texture_order": list(selection.texture_order),
 199              "texture_reserve": selection.texture_reserve,
 200              "roles": dict(sorted(selection.roles.items())),
 201              "target_word_count": selection.target_word_count,
 202          }
 203      )
 204  
 205  
 206  # A source note research writes when a source carried nothing worth recording.
 207  # It is not a limitation, and a packet full of them is a packet that has
 208  # learned to pad. Duplicated from `evidence_v3` rather than imported, because
 209  # the two projections are allowed to drift on everything else and this is the
 210  # one string they must agree on; a test holds them together.
 211  PLACEHOLDER_SOURCE_NOTE = "No note recorded for this source."
 212  
 213  
 214  def _is_limitation(note: str) -> bool:
 215      text = note.strip()
 216      return bool(text) and text != PLACEHOLDER_SOURCE_NOTE
 217  
 218  
 219  def _role_of(selection: Selection, claim_id: str) -> PacketRole:
 220      """What the selection said this fact is for.
 221  
 222      `texture_order` is the older, narrower version of the same idea: colour is
 223      ranked separately, on how much of the place it carries, so a claim in it is
 224      one the system has already called colour. Read second, so an explicit role
 225      wins -- and `select_evidence` writes `texture` over anything the ranking
 226      pass called a colour claim, so the two cannot disagree in practice.
 227      """
 228      role = selection.roles.get(claim_id, "")
 229      if role in {"backbone", "practical", "texture"}:
 230          return role  # type: ignore[return-value]
 231      return "texture" if claim_id in set(selection.texture_order) else ""
 232  
 233  
 234  def stale_reason(
 235      brief: ArticleBrief,
 236      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
 237      evidence: EvidencePackage,
 238      selection: Selection,
 239  ) -> str:
 240      """Why this choice no longer describes what it was made from, or "".
 241  
 242      One sentence, in the operator's terms, and one definition: the selection
 243      screen shows exactly what the write boundary would refuse with, so nobody
 244      discovers at the hand-off that the choice they were looking at was already
 245      out of date.
 246  
 247      An empty fingerprint is not a match. Every selection stored before bindings
 248      existed carries one, and those cannot be checked -- which is a thing to
 249      say, not a thing to assume is fine.
 250      """
 251      if (
 252          selection.evidence_fingerprint
 253          and selection.evidence_fingerprint != evidence.content_fingerprint()
 254      ):
 255          return (
 256              "The research has changed since these facts were chosen. Look at "
 257              "the list again before writing."
 258          )
 259      if (
 260          selection.brief_fingerprint
 261          and selection.brief_fingerprint != brief.brief_fingerprint
 262      ):
 263          return (
 264              "These facts were chosen against a different brief. Look at the "
 265              "list again before writing."
 266          )
 267      if (
 268          selection.work_order_fingerprint
 269          and selection.work_order_fingerprint != work_order.work_order_fingerprint
 270      ):
 271          return (
 272              "These facts were chosen against a different set of research "
 273              "questions. Look at the list again before writing."
 274          )
 275      return ""
 276  
 277  
 278  def build_packet(
 279      brief: ArticleBrief,
 280      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
 281      evidence: EvidencePackage,
 282      selection: Selection,
 283  ) -> WritingPacket:
 284      """Assemble the writer's material from a selection and a dossier.
 285  
 286      Pure code. It copies, it links, and it refuses; it never decides. The
 287      editorial decision was made by the ranker and the operator before this
 288      runs, and re-deciding anything here would put a second chooser beside the
 289      one the operator can see.
 290      """
 291      if reason := stale_reason(brief, work_order, evidence, selection):
 292          raise PacketRefused(reason)
 293  
 294      by_id = {claim.claim_id: claim for claim in evidence.claims}
 295      chosen_ids = selection.selected_claim_ids()
 296  
 297      unknown = sorted(chosen_ids - by_id.keys())
 298      if unknown:
 299          # Refusing rather than skipping. A chosen fact that no longer exists is
 300          # a selection describing a dossier that is gone, and quietly writing
 301          # from what is left hands the operator an article they did not pick.
 302          raise PacketRefused(
 303              "The selection names facts that are not in the research: "
 304              + ", ".join(unknown[:5])
 305              + ("…" if len(unknown) > 5 else "")
 306          )
 307      merged_away = sorted(
 308          claim_id for claim_id in chosen_ids if by_id[claim_id].merged_into
 309      )
 310      if merged_away:
 311          raise PacketRefused(
 312              "The selection names facts that were merged into others: "
 313              + ", ".join(merged_away[:5])
 314          )
 315      if not chosen_ids:
 316          raise PacketRefused(
 317              "No facts are selected — there is nothing to write from."
 318          )
 319  
 320      # Ranked order, so the packet reads most-needed first and two runs of the
 321      # same selection assemble byte-identically. A rescued fact from below the
 322      # line keeps its own position rather than being appended, because where the
 323      # ranker put it is still what the ranker thought.
 324      ordered = [
 325          claim_id for claim_id in selection.order if claim_id in chosen_ids
 326      ]
 327      ordered.extend(
 328          claim.claim_id
 329          for claim in evidence.claims
 330          if claim.claim_id in chosen_ids and claim.claim_id not in set(ordered)
 331      )
 332  
 333      facts = [
 334          PacketFact(
 335              claim_id=claim_id,
 336              text=by_id[claim_id].text,
 337              role=_role_of(selection, claim_id),
 338              reason=selection.reasons.get(claim_id, ""),
 339              as_of=(
 340                  by_id[claim_id].as_of.isoformat() if by_id[claim_id].as_of else None
 341              ),
 342              confidence=by_id[claim_id].confidence,
 343              operator_note=by_id[claim_id].venue_note,
 344          )
 345          for claim_id in ordered
 346      ]
 347  
 348      notes: list[PacketNote] = []
 349      for source in evidence.sources:
 350          bearing = sorted(
 351              claim_id
 352              for claim_id in chosen_ids
 353              if source.source_id in by_id[claim_id].source_ids
 354          )
 355          if not bearing:
 356              continue
 357          notes.extend(
 358              PacketNote(
 359                  note_id=source.source_id,
 360                  kind="source_note",
 361                  text=note.strip(),
 362                  claim_ids=bearing,
 363              )
 364              for note in source.notes
 365              if _is_limitation(note)
 366          )
 367      for conflict in evidence.conflicts:
 368          bearing = sorted(set(conflict.claim_ids) & chosen_ids)
 369          if not bearing:
 370              # A disagreement between two facts the article does not use is the
 371              # dossier's business. It stays there; grounding still reads it.
 372              continue
 373          settled = (conflict.resolution or "").strip()
 374          notes.append(
 375              PacketNote(
 376                  note_id=conflict.conflict_id,
 377                  kind="conflict",
 378                  text=(
 379                      f"{conflict.summary} Settled: {settled}"
 380                      if settled
 381                      else f"{conflict.summary} This is not settled — do not "
 382                      "state either version as certain."
 383                  ),
 384                  claim_ids=bearing,
 385              )
 386          )
 387  
 388      return WritingPacket(
 389          brief_fingerprint=brief.brief_fingerprint,
 390          work_order_fingerprint=work_order.work_order_fingerprint,
 391          evidence_fingerprint=evidence.content_fingerprint(),
 392          selection_fingerprint=selection_fingerprint(selection),
 393          target_word_count=selection.target_word_count,
 394          facts=facts,
 395          notes=notes,
 396          supplied_material=[
 397              PacketMaterial(
 398                  kind=item.kind, statement=item.statement, note=item.note
 399              )
 400              for item in brief.material
 401          ],
 402      )
 403  
 404  
 405  # What the checker is told about first-hand material, once, so the writer's
 406  # desk and the checker's desk describe it the same way.
 407  NO_SUPPLIED_MATERIAL = (
 408      "None. Every factual statement in this draft must rest on the evidence "
 409      "records above."
 410  )
 411  
 412  
 413  def supplied_material_text(packet: WritingPacket | dict[str, Any] | None) -> str:
 414      """The operator's own words, rendered for a stage that is not compose.
 415  
 416      Finding 01: compose received `brief.material` and grounding did not, so a
 417      checker reading only the web records had no way to tell a legitimate
 418      first-hand observation from an invented one. It could only call it
 419      unsupported -- and repair is instructed to delete unsupported assertions,
 420      which is how the one thing in the article nobody else could have written
 421      gets removed.
 422  
 423      Verbatim and by id, from the frozen packet rather than from the live
 424      brief, so a resumed run checks the draft against the material the draft
 425      was actually written from.
 426  
 427      This is a hand-off, not a verification: the material is supplied
 428      experience, not an independently checked fact, and the caller's prompt is
 429      responsible for saying so.
 430      """
 431      if packet is None:
 432          return NO_SUPPLIED_MATERIAL
 433      if isinstance(packet, dict):
 434          material = [
 435              item if isinstance(item, dict) else {}
 436              for item in (packet.get("supplied_material") or [])
 437          ]
 438          items = [
 439              PacketMaterial(
 440                  kind=str(entry.get("kind") or "").strip() or "material",
 441                  statement=str(entry.get("statement") or "").strip(),
 442                  note=str(entry.get("note") or "").strip(),
 443              )
 444              for entry in material
 445          ]
 446          items = [item for item in items if item.statement]
 447      else:
 448          items = [item for item in packet.supplied_material if item.statement.strip()]
 449  
 450      if not items:
 451          return NO_SUPPLIED_MATERIAL
 452  
 453      return "\n".join(
 454          f"- material_{index} [{item.kind}] {item.statement}"
 455          + (f" ({item.note})" if item.note else "")
 456          for index, item in enumerate(items, start=1)
 457      )
apps/backend/app/features/prompt2blog/instructions_v3.py
   1  """Canonical Prompt2Blog v3 instructions and stage-specific projections."""
   2  
   3  from __future__ import annotations
   4  
   5  import logging
   6  
   7  from hashlib import sha256
   8  from typing import Any, Literal
   9  
  10  from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
  11  
  12  from .contracts_v4 import ArticleBrief, Prompt2BlogV4Request, Prompt2BlogWorkOrder
  13  from .editorial_catalog import (
  14      DEFAULT_STRUCTURE_POLICY,
  15      EditorialCatalog,
  16      FormStructurePolicy,
  17      load_editorial_catalog,
  18  )
  19  from .evidence_v3 import NormalizedEvidence, normalize_evidence
  20  from .packet_v4 import WritingPacket
  21  
  22  logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  23  
  24  INSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION = 5
  25  
  26  # The one authority order in the system. It used to be stated twice -- here,
  27  # and again in prose at the top of `house-rules.md` -- in two vocabularies
  28  # ("approved commission" against "approved brief"), which is how a rule ends up
  29  # with two owners and neither of them current. House style no longer states an
  30  # order; it is the lowest layer of this one.
  31  PRECEDENCE = (
  32      "verified evidence",
  33      "approved brief",
  34      "article-form rules",
  35      "topic modules",
  36      "audience guidance",
  37      "house style",
  38  )
  39  
  40  # What each layer is actually allowed to decide. The bare list above says which
  41  # wins; it never said what any of them owns, so "the form controls structure"
  42  # and "house style controls structure" could both look true to a reader of the
  43  # assembled prompt.
  44  PRECEDENCE_OWNERSHIP = (
  45      "The facts and their stated limits control every factual claim. Nothing "
  46      "below may widen, flatten, or date a claim differently.",
  47      "The approved brief controls intent: subject, scope, promise, and what "
  48      "this piece fails if it does.",
  49      "The article form controls structure: how it opens, how it is divided, "
  50      "how it closes.",
  51      "Topic modules and audience guidance adjust emphasis only.",
  52      "House style controls expression, and only where nothing above has "
  53      "already decided.",
  54  )
  55  
  56  
  57  def precedence_block(role: str) -> str:
  58      """The authority order, written out once, for one stage's prompt."""
  59      order = " > ".join(PRECEDENCE)
  60      return "\n".join(
  61          (
  62              role,
  63              "",
  64              f"AUTHORITY ORDER: {order}.",
  65              *(f"- {line}" for line in PRECEDENCE_OWNERSHIP),
  66              "A lower layer may refine emphasis. It may never add a subject, "
  67              "comparator, factual claim, or obligation that conflicts with a "
  68              "higher one.",
  69          )
  70      )
  71  
  72  _HEADLINE_HEADING = "## Headline note"
  73  _OUTLINE_FORM_HEADINGS = (
  74      "## Reader promise",
  75      "## Required evidence",
  76      "## Allowed structures",
  77      "## Failure modes",
  78  )
  79  
  80  # What each editorial role is called where a model reads it. The role names in
  81  # the packet are short because they are data; these say what the job is.
  82  _ROLE_LABELS = {
  83      "backbone": "BACKBONE — what the piece argues from",
  84      "practical": "PRACTICAL — what the reader acts on",
  85      "texture": "TEXTURE — what makes the place real",
  86      "": "CHOSEN FOR THIS ARTICLE",
  87  }
  88  _ROLE_ORDER = (
  89      _ROLE_LABELS["backbone"],
  90      _ROLE_LABELS["practical"],
  91      _ROLE_LABELS["texture"],
  92      _ROLE_LABELS[""],
  93  )
  94  
  95  EVIDENCE_DISPOSITION_POLICY = """EVIDENCE DISPOSITION POLICY (IMMUTABLE)
  96  - Unsupported assertion: delete it. Never hedge it, qualify it, or label it
  97    unconfirmed. Omit unsupported points from reader-facing prose.
  98  - Supported uncertainty: preserve its exact scope, confidence, and limits.
  99  - Unpublished fact: omit it silently. Never narrate research absence.
 100  - Gap: record it in `remaining_gaps` as internal metadata only. Never put the
 101    gap or the research process in reader-facing prose."""
 102  
 103  
 104  class InstructionModel(BaseModel):
 105      model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
 106  
 107  
 108  class InstructionLayer(InstructionModel):
 109      layer: str
 110      title: str
 111      body: str
 112  
 113  
 114  class StageContext(InstructionModel):
 115      text: str
 116      included_sections: list[str]
 117      fingerprint: str
 118      # Characters per section, so a prompt's size can be read off the run
 119      # instead of guessed at. The compose call measured 29,218 tokens with only
 120      # about 11,000 traceable from stored data; the other 18,000 were invisible,
 121      # which made "what should we cut" unanswerable. Characters rather than
 122      # tokens because this is assembled before any tokenizer is in reach, and a
 123      # four-to-one ratio is close enough to find the big one.
 124      section_sizes: dict[str, int] = {}
 125  
 126      @property
 127      def characters(self) -> int:
 128          return len(self.text)
 129  
 130  
 131  class V3StageContexts(InstructionModel):
 132      outline: StageContext
 133      compose: StageContext
 134      audit: StageContext
 135      repair_lock: StageContext
 136      # The facts repair may work from. Separate from `repair_lock`, which is
 137      # the scope it may not move, because they answer different questions and
 138      # the lock is quoted at the model as immutable.
 139      #
 140      # Defaulted rather than required so a run snapshotted before this existed
 141      # still restores. Such a run repairs the way it always did: without the
 142      # facts, which is finding 03.
 143      repair_facts: StageContext = StageContext(
 144          text="", included_sections=[], fingerprint=""
 145      )
 146  
 147  
 148  StageContextName = Literal[
 149      "outline", "compose", "audit", "repair_lock", "repair_facts"
 150  ]
 151  
 152  
 153  class V3InstructionSet(InstructionModel):
 154      schema_version: int = INSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION
 155      precedence: list[str]
 156      layers: list[InstructionLayer]
 157      stage_contexts: V3StageContexts
 158      instruction_meta: dict[str, Any]
 159  
 160  
 161  def _brief_body(
 162      brief: ArticleBrief,
 163      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
 164  ) -> str:
 165      """The brief and its work order, rendered for a prompt.
 166  
 167      The order here is still the v3 order. Leading with the brief, and reframing
 168      evidence as the facts you may use rather than the article's reason for
 169      existing, is A5 and lands with the compose rework.
 170  
 171      The research questions used to be pasted in here. They arrived everywhere
 172      under a bare `Requirements:` heading with nothing saying what they were,
 173      and a plan can carry forty-four of them: a judge handed forty-four items
 174      called requirements marks a draft down for each one missing, and a repair
 175      pass handed the same list adds them back, one paragraph each, until the
 176      article is a coverage checklist. That is the mechanism behind #506.
 177  
 178      The outline was the last stage that needed the ids, because it named the
 179      `requirement_ids` each section served. It no longer does -- the packet says
 180      what a fact is for, which is the thing a section is actually organized
 181      around -- so the list has no reader left anywhere.
 182      """
 183      references = "\n".join(
 184          f"- {reference.name} — {reference.role}"
 185          for reference in work_order.scope.references
 186      )
 187      must_name = "\n".join(f"- {item}" for item in brief.must_name) or "- None recorded."
 188      material = (
 189          "\n".join(f"- [{item.kind}] {item.statement}" for item in brief.material)
 190          or "- None; this is a research-led piece."
 191      )
 192      tags = ", ".join(brief.reader.tags) or "none"
 193      lines = [
 194          f"Seed (provenance only, not a promise to keep): {brief.seed}",
 195          f"Location: {brief.location}",
 196          f"Spine: {brief.spine}",
 197          f"Primary subject: {work_order.primary_subject}",
 198          f"Scope mode: {work_order.scope.mode}",
 199          "References and roles:",
 200          references,
 201          f"Core reader question: {brief.reader_question}",
 202          f"The promise to keep: {brief.outcome}",
 203          f"Primary reader: {brief.reader.primary_reader}",
 204          f"Audience tags: {tags}",
 205          "Must name:",
 206          must_name,
 207          "Material the writer has:",
 208          material,
 209      ]
 210      lines += [
 211          f"This piece fails if: {brief.fails_if}",
 212          "Context-only references may calibrate a fact or explain significance. "
 213          "They may never become co-subjects, recurring sections, rankings, or "
 214          "verdicts, and the approved form may not change.",
 215      ]
 216      return "\n".join(lines)
 217  
 218  
 219  def _evidence_body(evidence: NormalizedEvidence, *, for_compose: bool = False) -> str:
 220      """The policy, then the records.
 221  
 222      `for_compose` selects the projection without the bibliography. The
 223      canonical layer keeps the full rendering, because that layer is the run's
 224      own record of what the evidence was, and groundedness and the readiness
 225      follow-up read `records_text` directly and are untouched by this.
 226      """
 227      return (
 228          f"{EVIDENCE_DISPOSITION_POLICY}\n\n"
 229          "These records are the only permitted source of fact. Use them exactly: "
 230          "preserve dates, units, geography, and stated uncertainty. Attribution "
 231          "is internal to these records. Never carry it into the prose: no "
 232          "\"sources report\", no \"outlets say\", no \"according to\", no "
 233          "\"the publication noted\", no naming the outlet, site, or report a "
 234          "fact came from. Never invent a bridge fact to close a gap. First-hand "
 235          "material "
 236          "is the writer's own knowledge: state it directly, as fact, with no "
 237          "attribution, no sourcing language, and no note about how it was "
 238          "obtained. A confirmed premise is simply a fact the article may use; "
 239          "never mention that it was checked, and never write a sentence about "
 240          "what the research established. A resolved conflict is the same: the "
 241          "resolution is the fact, and the disagreement behind it is internal. "
 242          "Write the settled figure as a plain sentence. Never tell the reader "
 243          "that two records disagreed, which one was chosen, or why.\n\n"
 244          f"{evidence.compose_records_text if for_compose else evidence.records_text}"
 245      )
 246  
 247  
 248  def _packet_facts_body(packet: WritingPacket) -> str:
 249      """The chosen facts, for the stage that decides where they go.
 250  
 251      Grouped by editorial role rather than by the question that found them.
 252      Grouping by search group was the previous answer and it inherited the
 253      research plan's shape: a section per subject researched, which is a
 254      section per question wearing a different hat. What the outline needs to
 255      know about a fact is what it is for -- the backbone of the argument, a
 256      decision the reader has to make, or the detail that makes a place real.
 257  
 258      The reason line travels with each fact. It is the selection saying what
 259      the article uses this for, which is the only thing that lets a plan put
 260      two facts in the same section because they do the same job.
 261      """
 262      by_role: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
 263      for fact in packet.facts:
 264          as_of = f" (as of {fact.as_of})" if fact.as_of else ""
 265          reason = f"\n    Why it is here: {fact.reason}" if fact.reason else ""
 266          note = (
 267              f"\n    The operator looked at this: {fact.operator_note}"
 268              if fact.operator_note
 269              else ""
 270          )
 271          by_role.setdefault(_ROLE_LABELS.get(fact.role, _ROLE_LABELS[""]), []).append(
 272              f"- {fact.claim_id} — {fact.text}{as_of} [{fact.confidence}]"
 273              f"{reason}{note}"
 274          )
 275  
 276      lines = ["THE FACTS THIS ARTICLE IS BEING WRITTEN FROM"]
 277      # Label order, not dictionary order, so two runs of the same packet
 278      # assemble byte-identically and the backbone is read first.
 279      for label in _ROLE_ORDER:
 280          if label in by_role:
 281              lines.extend(("", label, *by_role[label]))
 282      if not by_role:
 283          lines.append("- None supplied.")
 284  
 285      notes = _packet_notes(packet)
 286      if notes:
 287          lines.extend(("", notes))
 288      lines.extend(
 289          (
 290              "",
 291              "This is the whole desk. Research found more and a person chose "
 292              "these; the rest is not a hole to plan around and not work left "
 293              "undone. Do not plan a section whose subject is what is missing.",
 294          )
 295      )
 296      return "\n".join(lines)
 297  
 298  
 299  def _packet_notes(packet: WritingPacket) -> str:
 300      """The limitations attached to those facts, and nothing else.
 301  
 302      Long by design where it needs to be. A caveat is what makes a fact true;
 303      a packet that dropped it to save characters would be smaller and wrong.
 304      """
 305      if not packet.notes:
 306          return ""
 307      lines = ["HOW THESE FACTS MAY BE STATED"]
 308      lines.extend(
 309          f"- {', '.join(note.claim_ids)}: {note.text}" for note in packet.notes
 310      )
 311      return "\n".join(lines)
 312  
 313  
 314  def _packet_material(packet: WritingPacket) -> str:
 315      if not packet.supplied_material:
 316          return ""
 317      lines = ["MATERIAL THE WRITER ALREADY HAS"]
 318      lines.extend(
 319          f"- [{item.kind}] {item.statement}"
 320          + (f" ({item.note})" if item.note else "")
 321          for item in packet.supplied_material
 322      )
 323      return "\n".join(lines)
 324  
 325  
 326  def _packet_evidence_body(packet: WritingPacket) -> str:
 327      """The facts the writer may use, and the rules for using them.
 328  
 329      What is deliberately absent: the research questions, their statuses, their
 330      gaps, and the claims that were not chosen. Compose used to receive all of
 331      them under the same heading as the facts -- on run 4a56545b, 10,371
 332      characters of coverage bookkeeping against 7,225 characters of chosen
 333      facts, eleven rows of it reading `none kept for this article`. A writer
 334      handed a list of questions answers questions; the article that comes back
 335      is shaped like a research plan because it was given one.
 336  
 337      Grounding is unaffected and still reads the whole dossier. This is the
 338      writer's desk, not the record.
 339      """
 340      facts = [
 341          f"- {fact.claim_id} — {fact.text}"
 342          + (f" (as of {fact.as_of})" if fact.as_of else "")
 343          + f" [{fact.confidence}]"
 344          + (
 345              f"\n    The operator looked at this: {fact.operator_note}"
 346              if fact.operator_note
 347              else ""
 348          )
 349          for fact in packet.facts
 350      ]
 351      blocks = [
 352          EVIDENCE_DISPOSITION_POLICY,
 353          "These records are the only permitted source of fact. Use them exactly: "
 354          "preserve dates, units, geography, and stated uncertainty. Attribution "
 355          "is internal to these records. Never carry it into the prose: no "
 356          "\"sources report\", no \"outlets say\", no \"according to\", no "
 357          "\"the publication noted\", no naming the outlet, site, or report a "
 358          "fact came from. Never invent a bridge fact to close a gap. First-hand "
 359          "material is the writer's own knowledge: state it directly, as fact, "
 360          "with no attribution, no sourcing language, and no note about how it "
 361          "was obtained.\n\n"
 362          "These facts were chosen for this article by a person. They are "
 363          "available material, not a checklist: a fact you do not need is a fact "
 364          "you leave out, and using fewer of them well is better than using all "
 365          "of them badly. Nothing here is owed a sentence except what the brief "
 366          "itself asks for.",
 367          "THE FACTS\n" + ("\n".join(facts) if facts else "- None supplied."),
 368      ]
 369      blocks.extend(
 370          block for block in (_packet_notes(packet), _packet_material(packet)) if block
 371      )
 372      return "\n\n".join(blocks)
 373  
 374  
 375  def _audience_body(
 376      brief: ArticleBrief,
 377      catalog: EditorialCatalog,
 378  ) -> str:
 379      tags_by_id = {tag.id: tag for tag in catalog.audience_tags}
 380      lines = [f"Primary reader: {brief.reader.primary_reader}"]
 381      if brief.reader.tags:
 382          lines.append("Emphasis tags:")
 383          lines.extend(
 384              f"- {tags_by_id[tag_id].label} — {tags_by_id[tag_id].description}"
 385              for tag_id in brief.reader.tags
 386          )
 387      else:
 388          lines.append("Emphasis tags: none.")
 389      lines.append(
 390          "Tags adjust emphasis only. They do not change structure, scope, or the "
 391          "approved form."
 392      )
 393      return "\n".join(lines)
 394  
 395  
 396  def _markdown_section(instructions: str, heading: str) -> str:
 397      if heading not in instructions:
 398          return ""
 399      body = instructions.split(heading, 1)[1].split("\n## ", 1)[0].strip()
 400      return f"{heading}\n\n{body}" if body else ""
 401  
 402  
 403  def _form_structure(form_instructions: str) -> str:
 404      return "\n\n".join(
 405          section
 406          for heading in _OUTLINE_FORM_HEADINGS
 407          if (section := _markdown_section(form_instructions, heading))
 408      )
 409  
 410  
 411  def _packet_support_body(packet: WritingPacket) -> str:
 412      """What the writer had, so the audit does not ask for what it did not.
 413  
 414      The audit used to receive every research question with its status. That
 415      block existed for a real reason -- on run 95a74dce it read
 416      `water_refill_points` in the requirements, did not know research had filed
 417      it unsupported, and told repair to add water-fountain information, which
 418      repair is forbidden to invent -- and it solved that problem by handing the
 419      judge a checklist.
 420  
 421      A checklist is what the redesign is removing. An auditor that can see the
 422      facts a person cut will ask for them back, repair will oblige as far as it
 423      can, and the editorial cut is undone by the two stages downstream of it.
 424      So the audit is told the shape of what happened and not its contents: a
 425      person chose, material outside the draft is not a hole, and the only
 426      limitations named are the ones that constrain the facts actually used.
 427      """
 428      lines = [
 429          "WHAT THE WRITER HAD",
 430          f"- {len(packet.facts)} facts, chosen for this article by a person out "
 431          "of a larger dossier.",
 432          "- Material that is not in the draft was either never found or "
 433          "deliberately not chosen. Neither is a hole. Asking for it in "
 434          "required_revisions asks repair for a fact it is forbidden to invent, "
 435          "and a revision the stage it is addressed to cannot satisfy is a "
 436          "revision that fails in every run.",
 437          "- If something the brief itself promises is genuinely unsupported, "
 438          "say the article needs more research rather than more writing.",
 439      ]
 440      if notes := _packet_notes(packet):
 441          lines.extend(
 442              (
 443                  "",
 444                  notes,
 445                  "",
 446                  "A draft that states one of those facts within its limitation "
 447                  "is correct. Do not ask for a flatter, more confident sentence "
 448                  "than the evidence allows.",
 449              )
 450          )
 451      return "\n".join(lines)
 452  
 453  
 454  def _repair_lock_body(
 455      brief: ArticleBrief,
 456      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
 457      packet: WritingPacket,
 458      *,
 459      form_label: str,
 460  ) -> str:
 461      """The scope this repair may not move, and nothing else.
 462  
 463      The research questions used to be pasted here under `Requirements:`. They
 464      are not scope -- the outcome, spine, reader question, form and `fails_if`
 465      are -- and repair is separately forbidden to add facts, so the list could
 466      only ever be read as a checklist to satisfy. See `_brief_body`.
 467      """
 468      references = "\n".join(
 469          f"- {reference.name} — {reference.role}"
 470          for reference in work_order.scope.references
 471      )
 472      must_name = "\n".join(f"- {item}" for item in brief.must_name)
 473      # Repair rewrites the whole article. A caveat that reached compose and not
 474      # this pass is a caveat the rewrite can drop without noticing, which turns
 475      # a correctly hedged sentence into a confident wrong one -- and repair is
 476      # separately forbidden to add anything, so it could never put it back.
 477      limitations = _packet_notes(packet)
 478      return "\n".join(
 479          (
 480              f"The piece promises: {brief.outcome}",
 481              f"Spine: {brief.spine}",
 482              f"Article form: {form_label}",
 483              f"Primary subject: {work_order.primary_subject}",
 484              f"Scope mode: {work_order.scope.mode}",
 485              f"Core reader question: {brief.reader_question}",
 486              "Reference roles:",
 487              references,
 488              "Must name:",
 489              must_name or "- None recorded.",
 490              f"It fails if: {brief.fails_if}",
 491              *((limitations,) if limitations else ()),
 492              "Keep direct, specific prose for the named reader. Preserve the "
 493              "approved form and scope. The only facts you may use are the ones "
 494              "listed under THE FACTS AVAILABLE TO THIS REPAIR, and you may not "
 495              "remove a limitation from a fact you keep.",
 496          )
 497      )
 498  
 499  
 500  def _stage_context(*, parts: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> StageContext:
 501      included = [(name, body) for name, body in parts if body]
 502      text = "\n\n".join(body for _name, body in included)
 503      return StageContext(
 504          text=text,
 505          included_sections=[name for name, _body in included],
 506          fingerprint=sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
 507          section_sizes={name: len(body) for name, body in included},
 508      )
 509  
 510  
 511  def _validated_stage_contexts(
 512      stage_contexts: V3StageContexts | dict[str, Any],
 513  ) -> V3StageContexts:
 514      if isinstance(stage_contexts, V3StageContexts):
 515          return stage_contexts
 516      return V3StageContexts.model_validate(stage_contexts)
 517  
 518  
 519  def stage_context_text(
 520      stage_contexts: V3StageContexts | dict[str, Any],
 521      name: StageContextName,
 522  ) -> str:
 523      """Return one required projection; malformed runtime inputs fail loudly."""
 524      return getattr(_validated_stage_contexts(stage_contexts), name).text
 525  
 526  
 527  def stage_context_manifest(
 528      stage_contexts: V3StageContexts | dict[str, Any],
 529  ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 530      """Compact debug receipt for contexts whose full prompts live in traces."""
 531      contexts = _validated_stage_contexts(stage_contexts)
 532      return {
 533          name: {
 534              "included_sections": list(context.included_sections),
 535              "character_count": len(context.text),
 536              "fingerprint": context.fingerprint,
 537          }
 538          for name, context in (
 539              ("outline", contexts.outline),
 540              ("compose", contexts.compose),
 541              ("audit", contexts.audit),
 542              ("repair_lock", contexts.repair_lock),
 543              ("repair_facts", contexts.repair_facts),
 544          )
 545      }
 546  
 547  
 548  def assemble_v3_instructions(
 549      request: Prompt2BlogV4Request,
 550      packet: WritingPacket,
 551      *,
 552      catalog: EditorialCatalog | None = None,
 553  ) -> V3InstructionSet:
 554      """Build canonical layers and job-specific contexts for one brief.
 555  
 556      The packet is required rather than optional. Two ways to reach the writer
 557      -- one narrow, one from the whole dossier -- is the arrangement where a
 558      failure in the narrow one silently restores the old behaviour, which is
 559      the failure this redesign exists to prevent. A run that wants every fact
 560      says so with `select_everything`, and gets a packet either way.
 561      """
 562      catalog = catalog or load_editorial_catalog()
 563      brief = request.brief
 564      work_order = request.work_order
 565  
 566      form = next((item for item in catalog.forms if item.id == brief.form_id), None)
 567      if form is None:
 568          raise ValueError(f"Unknown article form: {brief.form_id}")
 569  
 570      modules_by_id = {module.id: module for module in catalog.topic_modules}
 571      unknown_modules = [
 572          module_id
 573          for module_id in brief.topic_module_ids
 574          if module_id not in modules_by_id
 575      ]
 576      if unknown_modules:
 577          raise ValueError(f"Unknown topic modules: {sorted(unknown_modules)}")
 578      unknown_tags = [
 579          tag_id
 580          for tag_id in brief.reader.tags
 581          if tag_id not in {tag.id for tag in catalog.audience_tags}
 582      ]
 583      if unknown_tags:
 584          raise ValueError(f"Unknown audience tags: {sorted(unknown_tags)}")
 585  
 586      # Catalog order, not brief order, so two runs with the same modules
 587      # assemble byte-identical instructions.
 588      active_modules = [
 589          module
 590          for module in catalog.topic_modules
 591          if module.id in set(brief.topic_module_ids)
 592      ]
 593      evidence = normalize_evidence(work_order, request.evidence_package)
 594  
 595      layers = [
 596          InstructionLayer(
 597              layer="evidence",
 598              title="VERIFIED EVIDENCE",
 599              body=_evidence_body(evidence),
 600          ),
 601          InstructionLayer(
 602              layer="brief",
 603              title="APPROVED COMMISSION",
 604              body=_brief_body(brief, work_order),
 605          ),
 606          InstructionLayer(
 607              layer="form",
 608              title=f"ARTICLE FORM — {form.label}",
 609              body=form.instructions,
 610          ),
 611          InstructionLayer(
 612              layer="topic_modules",
 613              title="TOPIC MODULES",
 614              body="\n\n".join(module.instructions for module in active_modules)
 615              or "No topic module is active for this brief.",
 616          ),
 617          InstructionLayer(
 618              layer="audience",
 619              title="AUDIENCE GUIDANCE",
 620              body=_audience_body(brief, catalog),
 621          ),
 622          InstructionLayer(
 623              layer="house_style",
 624              title="HOUSE STYLE",
 625              body=catalog.house_rules.instructions,
 626          ),
 627      ]
 628  
 629      form_structure = _form_structure(form.instructions)
 630      brief_body = _brief_body(brief, work_order)
 631      audience_body = _audience_body(brief, catalog)
 632      topic_modules_body = (
 633          "\n\n".join(module.instructions for module in active_modules)
 634          or "No topic module is active for this brief."
 635      )
 636      stage_contexts = V3StageContexts(
 637          outline=_stage_context(
 638              parts=[
 639                  (
 640                      "outline_authority",
 641                      precedence_block(
 642                          "OUTLINE AUTHORITY\nYou are planning, not writing. The "
 643                          "voice below says what kind of piece this is."
 644                      ),
 645                  ),
 646                  # The single largest change in the spec. Compose is obedient:
 647                  # give it a good plan and it writes well, give it an audit and
 648                  # it writes an excellent audit. This stage decides which.
 649                  ("voice", f"THE VOICE YOU ARE WRITING IN\n{catalog.voice.instructions}"),
 650                  ("brief", f"APPROVED BRIEF\n{brief_body}"),
 651                  ("audience", f"AUDIENCE GUIDANCE\n{audience_body}"),
 652                  (
 653                      "form_structure",
 654                      f"ARTICLE FORM STRUCTURE — {form.label}\n{form_structure}",
 655                  ),
 656                  ("facts", _packet_facts_body(packet)),
 657                  (
 658                      "outline_rules",
 659                      "PLANNING RULES\n"
 660                      # A3. "Do not claim a transformation" became a section
 661                      # called Scope limits: a negative instruction is a topic
 662                      # waiting to happen.
 663                      "- No section may take scope, limits, method, evidence or "
 664                      "the state of our research as its subject. The reader came "
 665                      "for the place, not for how we found out about it.\n"
 666                      # A4. Compose is separately required to add an opening and
 667                      # takeaways -- about 165 words nobody counts -- so a plan
 668                      # that budgets the full target overshoots by construction.
 669                      # The reserve is now subtracted before the prompt is built
 670                      # and arrives as SECTION BUDGET: this rule and the template
 671                      # used to give the model two different totals and ask it to
 672                      # reconcile them, which is why run 95a74dce planned 730
 673                      # against a 900 target, twice.
 674                      "- The SECTION BUDGET already excludes the opening and the "
 675                      "closing takeaways, which you do not plan. Budget to it "
 676                      "exactly; do not subtract anything further.\n"
 677                      "- Group sections by subject. One section per research "
 678                      "question is a research plan, not an article.",
 679                  ),
 680              ]
 681          ),
 682          compose=_stage_context(
 683              parts=[
 684                  (
 685                      "compose_authority",
 686                      precedence_block(
 687                          "COMPOSE AUTHORITY\nThe brief says what you are making. "
 688                          "The facts below are the material you may make it from."
 689                      ),
 690                  ),
 691                  # The brief first, and evidence reframed. Evidence still binds
 692                  # the facts; it stops being the reason the article exists,
 693                  # which is what produced a piece about its own research.
 694                  ("voice", f"THE VOICE YOU ARE WRITING IN\n{catalog.voice.instructions}"),
 695                  ("brief", f"WHAT WE ARE MAKING\n{brief_body}"),
 696                  (
 697                      "evidence",
 698                      f"THE FACTS YOU MAY USE\n{_packet_evidence_body(packet)}",
 699                  ),
 700                  ("form", f"ARTICLE FORM — {form.label}\n{form_structure}"),
 701                  ("topic_modules", f"TOPIC MODULES\n{topic_modules_body}"),
 702                  ("audience", f"AUDIENCE GUIDANCE\n{audience_body}"),
 703                  (
 704                      "writing_conventions",
 705                      f"WRITING CONVENTIONS\n{catalog.writing_conventions.instructions}",
 706                  ),
 707                  ("house_style", f"HOUSE STYLE\n{catalog.house_rules.instructions}"),
 708              ]
 709          ),
 710          audit=_stage_context(
 711              parts=[
 712                  (
 713                      "audit_authority",
 714                      precedence_block(
 715                          "AUDIT AUTHORITY\nJudge brief fidelity, form fit, reader "
 716                          "service, and style against this order. Treat the "
 717                          "grounding verdict as final on support."
 718                      ),
 719                  ),
 720                  ("brief", f"APPROVED BRIEF\n{brief_body}"),
 721                  ("support", _packet_support_body(packet)),
 722                  ("form", f"ARTICLE FORM — {form.label}\n{form_structure}"),
 723                  ("audience", f"AUDIENCE GUIDANCE\n{audience_body}"),
 724                  ("house_style", f"HOUSE STYLE\n{catalog.house_rules.instructions}"),
 725              ]
 726          ),
 727          # Finding 03. Repair used to receive the previous draft, a list of
 728          # revisions, and a scope lock -- and was told never to add factual
 729          # material, including researched material. So a revision like "compare
 730          # these restaurants on price" was unsatisfiable whenever the first
 731          # draft happened to leave the price out: the fact was chosen, frozen,
 732          # and sitting in the packet the repair pass could not see. What came
 733          # back was repetition, vague judgement, or an unresolved revision.
 734          #
 735          # It is the same list compose was given, from the same frozen packet.
 736          # The editorial cut still holds: a fact nobody chose is still not
 737          # available, and repair still cannot invent one.
 738          repair_facts=_stage_context(
 739              parts=[
 740                  (
 741                      "facts",
 742                      "THE FACTS AVAILABLE TO THIS REPAIR\n"
 743                      + _packet_evidence_body(packet),
 744                  ),
 745              ]
 746          ),
 747          repair_lock=_stage_context(
 748              parts=[
 749                  (
 750                      "repair_authority",
 751                      "REPAIR AUTHORITY\nExact revisions and unsupported-claim verdicts "
 752                      "control this pass. This lock is immutable.",
 753                  ),
 754                  ("evidence_disposition_policy", EVIDENCE_DISPOSITION_POLICY),
 755                  (
 756                      "scope_style_lock",
 757                      "COMPACT SCOPE AND STYLE LOCK\n"
 758                      + _repair_lock_body(
 759                          brief, work_order, packet, form_label=form.label
 760                      ),
 761                  ),
 762              ]
 763          ),
 764      )
 765  
 766      return V3InstructionSet(
 767          precedence=list(PRECEDENCE),
 768          layers=layers,
 769          stage_contexts=stage_contexts,
 770          instruction_meta={
 771              "schema_version": INSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
 772              "form_id": form.id,
 773              "form_label": form.label,
 774              "source_requirements": list(form.source_requirements),
 775              "topic_module_ids": [module.id for module in active_modules],
 776              "audience_tag_ids": list(brief.reader.tags),
 777              "house_rules_id": catalog.house_rules.id,
 778              "precedence": list(PRECEDENCE),
 779              "brief_fingerprint": brief.brief_fingerprint,
 780              "work_order_fingerprint": work_order.work_order_fingerprint,
 781              "evidence_receipt": evidence.receipt(),
 782              # Resolved once, here, and frozen with the rest of the run's
 783              # instructions. Outline, compose and the deterministic checks all
 784              # read this rather than each resolving the form again -- and a
 785              # resumed leg reads the policy the draft was written under, not
 786              # whatever the form file says today.
 787              "structure_policy": form.structure.model_dump(),
 788          },
 789      )
 790  
 791  
 792  def resolve_structure_policy(
 793      instructions: dict[str, Any] | None,
 794  ) -> FormStructurePolicy:
 795      """The structure policy one run was frozen with.
 796  
 797      Falls back to the old universal shape -- direct answer, three-plus
 798      headings, takeaways -- when a run has no policy recorded, which is every
 799      run started before forms carried one. That is deliberately the pre-change
 800      behaviour rather than a refusal: an old run resumed after this shipped
 801      should finish the article it started.
 802      """
 803      meta = _safe_meta(instructions).get("structure_policy")
 804      if not isinstance(meta, dict) or not meta:
 805          logger.warning(
 806              "No structure policy recorded for this run; using the default shape"
 807          )
 808          return DEFAULT_STRUCTURE_POLICY
 809      return FormStructurePolicy.model_validate(meta)
 810  
 811  
 812  def _safe_meta(instructions: dict[str, Any] | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
 813      if not isinstance(instructions, dict):
 814          return {}
 815      meta = instructions.get("instruction_meta")
 816      return meta if isinstance(meta, dict) else {}
apps/backend/app/features/prompt2blog/api/intake.py
   1  """The HTTP surface for the four intake stages.
   2  
   3  Every handler below is `def`, never `async def`, and that is load bearing.
   4  
   5  FastAPI runs an `async def` handler on the event loop and a `def` handler in a
   6  threadpool. Every route here does blocking work -- ten sequential web searches,
   7  a model call that runs for minutes, SQLite reads -- so declaring them `async`
   8  handed the event loop to one request and froze the entire server for as long as
   9  it took.
  10  
  11  The symptoms did not look like one bug. The Claude status pill hung on
  12  "checking", links did nothing, and the page forgot which run it was on, because
  13  its resume read timed out and the code took silence to mean the run was gone.
  14  All three were requests queued behind a research pass that had the loop.
  15  
  16  If a handler here ever needs `await`, it needs its blocking work moved off the
  17  loop first.
  18  
  19  One route per move the operator can make: type a seed, answer a question, go
  20  back into the grill, approve the brief, plan the research, cut the plan, run
  21  the research. Each
  22  one is a turn -- it loads what the run knows, advances it, writes it back -- so
  23  a page that is reloaded, or reopened tomorrow, asks `GET /intake/{run_id}` and
  24  carries on.
  25  
  26  Every route is staff-guarded because every one of them spends money.
  27  """
  28  
  29  from __future__ import annotations
  30  
  31  import logging
  32  from dataclasses import asdict
  33  from typing import Any
  34
