 101  
 102  def _grounded_call(
 103      prompt: str,
 104      *,
 105      job_id: str,
 106      model_name: str | None = None,
 107      max_tokens: int,
 108      usage_recorder: Any | None,
 109      correlation_id: str | None = None,
 110  ) -> tuple[str, list[str], int | None]:
 111      """A grounded search, counted.
 112  
 113      Grounded search is raw REST: it never passes through the LangChain
 114      adapters the token ledger watches, so every search a run made was
 115      invisible to it. Measured on two real runs, that was 27,207 tokens over
 116      eight searches (b78a9fe8) and 31,992 over seven (76b36468), and the
 117      receipt for both reported zero. The per-run ceiling reads that same total,
 118      so it was guarding a number with the most token-hungry step missing.
 119  
 120      A response that carried no usage block is recorded as a call with no
 121      measurement rather than a call that cost nothing: `record` files a `None`
 122      usage as unmetered, and both real runs had exactly one search like that.
 123      """
 124      from app.shared.model_calls import grounded_text
 125  
 126      if correlation_id is None:
 127          correlation_id = getattr(getattr(usage_recorder, "__self__", None), "run_id", None)
 128  
 129      # Reported here for the first time. These two searches are the most
 130      # token-hungry step in a run and neither has ever reached the dashboard,
 131      # because reporting was wired per call site and these sites were missed.
 132      result = grounded_text(
 133          job_id, prompt, model=model_name, max_tokens=max_tokens, endpoint="grounded",
 134          correlation_id=correlation_id
 135      )
 136      if result is None:
 137          # The call failed rather than returned nothing. There is no successful
 138          # call to record.
 139          return "", [], None
 140      if usage_recorder is not None:
 141          counts = {
 142              "input_tokens": result.input_tokens,
 143              "output_tokens": result.output_tokens,
 144              "total_tokens": result.total_tokens,
 145          }
 146          measured = {key: value for key, value in counts.items() if value is not None}
 147          if measured:
 148              measured["output_token_details"] = {"reasoning": getattr(result, "reasoning_tokens", 0) or 0}
 149              measured["cached_input_tokens"] = getattr(result, "cached_input_tokens", 0) or 0
 150          try:
 151              usage_recorder(
 152                  str(result.model_name or model_name),
 153                  measured or None,
 154              )
 155          except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover -- telemetry only
 156              logger.warning("Grounded search usage record failed: %s", exc)
 157      return result.text, list(result.source_urls), result.total_tokens
 158  
 159  
 160  def _services(run_id: str | None = None) -> IntakeServices:
 161      """The intake's dependencies, continuing `run_id`'s ledger where there is one.
 162  
 163      Built per request. Without the restore each request's tracker held only
 164      its own calls, and writing the ledger under one stage name then replaced
 165      the run's accounting with that request's slice -- see
 166      `dependencies_for_run`.
 167      """
 168      pipeline = (
 169          dependencies_for_run(run_id) if run_id else PipelineDependencies()
 170      )
 171      record_usage = getattr(
 172          getattr(pipeline.llm, "usage_tracker", None), "record", None
 173      )
 174  
 175      def _ground(prompt: str) -> tuple[str, list[str], int | None]:
 176          """Look something up on the one path in this app that reaches the web.
 177  
 178          Search stays off Claude on purpose: its WebSearch denial is a
 179          deliberate security boundary, and research is the most token-hungry
 180          step there is -- spending Claude's budget reading web pages risks
 181          running out during the writing, which is the part that actually needs
 182          it.
 183          """
 184          return _grounded_call(
 185              f"Brief a travel editor on this in a few dense paragraphs. "
 186              f"Facts, reputation, neighbourhoods, what it is known for.\n\n{prompt}",
 187              job_id="p2b.grill_research",
 188              max_tokens=GRILL_RESEARCH_MAX_TOKENS,
 189              usage_recorder=record_usage,
 190              correlation_id=run_id,
 191          )
 192  
 193      def _gather(prompt: str, model_name: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, list[str], int | None]:
 194          """One grounded pass, for research rather than for the grill."""
 195          return _grounded_call(
 196              prompt,
 197              job_id="p2b.research_gather",
 198              max_tokens=GATHER_MAX_TOKENS,
 199              usage_recorder=record_usage,
 200              correlation_id=run_id,
 201          )
 202  
 203      return IntakeServices(
 204          dependencies=GrillDependencies(llm=pipeline.llm, research=_ground),
 205          recorder=pipeline.recorder,
 206          research=ResearchDependencies(
 207              gather=_gather,
 208              structure_llm=pipeline.llm,
 209              # The gateway answers for `p2b.research_structure`; the stage no
 210              # longer carries a model of its own.
 211              structure_model=None,
 212          ),
 213      )
 214  
 215  
 216  def _handle(action, *args, **kwargs) -> Any:
 217      """Turn the intake's own failures into answers a page can act on."""
 218      try:
 219          return action(*args, **kwargs)
 220      except BriefIncomplete as error:
 221          logger.error("Brief incomplete: %s | %s", error.missing, error.raw[:2000])
 222          raise HTTPException(
 223              status_code=502,
 224              detail={
 225                  "error": "brief_incomplete",
 226                  "message": (
 227                      "The brief came back missing "
 228                      + ", ".join(error.missing)
 229                      + ". Nothing you said caused this — try approving again, or "
 230                      "go back to the grill and say more about it."
 231                  ),
 232                  "raw": error.raw[:2000],
 233              },
 234          ) from error
 235      except BriefUnusable as error:
 236          # 502 and a sentence, not a Pydantic traceback. This arrived as
 237          # "1 validation error for ArticleBrief ... must_name entry values must
 238          # be unique", mid-flow, after the grill had been paid for.
 239          logger.error("Brief did not fit its contract: %s | %s", error.reason, error.raw[:2000])
 240          raise HTTPException(
 241              status_code=502,
 242              detail={
 243                  "error": "brief_unusable",
 244                  "message": (
 245                      "The brief came back in a shape the system cannot use "
 246                      "and did not settle on a second try. Nothing you said "
 247                      "caused this — try approving again."
 248                  ),
 249                  "raw": error.reason,
 250              },
 251          ) from error
 252      except ResearchUnusable as error:
 253          logger.error("Dossier did not fit its contract: %s | %s", error.reason, error.raw[:2000])
 254          raise HTTPException(
 255              status_code=502,
 256              detail={
 257                  "error": "research_unusable",
 258                  "message": (
 259                      "The research came back in a shape the system cannot use. "
 260                      "Nothing you said caused this — try researching again."
 261                  ),
 262                  "raw": error.reason,
 263              },
 264          ) from error
 265      except WorkOrderUnusable as error:
 266          logger.error(
 267              "Work order did not fit its contract: %s | %s", error.reason, error.raw[:2000]
 268          )
 269          raise HTTPException(
 270              status_code=502,
 271              detail={
 272                  "error": "work_order_unusable",
 273                  "message": (
 274                      "The research plan came back in a shape the system cannot "
 275                      "use. Nothing you said caused this — try planning again."
 276                  ),
 277                  "raw": error.reason,
 278              },
 279          ) from error
 280      except GrillUnusableResponse as error:
 281          # 502, not 400: nothing the operator typed caused this, and the reply
 282          # travels with it. The first real run died here and left no trace at
 283          # all, which made the one failure that most needed explaining the one
 284          # with no evidence.
 285          logger.error("Grill returned an unusable response: %s", error.raw[:2000])
 286          raise HTTPException(
 287              status_code=502,
 288              detail={
 289                  "error": "grill_unusable_response",
 290                  "message": (
 291                      "The interviewer did not come back with a question. This is "
 292                      "not something you did. Try again."
 293                  ),
 294                  "raw": error.raw[:2000],
 295              },
 296          ) from error
 297      except SelectionRefused as error:
 298          # The operator asked the picker for something it cannot mean. Their
 299          # move, their sentence back, and nothing was changed.
 300          raise HTTPException(
 301              status_code=400,
 302              detail={"error": "selection_refused", "message": str(error)},
 303          ) from error
 304      except RunTokenCeilingReached as error:
 305          # Not a server fault and not a retry: the run is over its ceiling and
 306          # says what it spent.
 307          raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=error.status.as_record()) from error
 308      except PlanTooLargeToFinish as error:
 309          # The same 409 shape, and for the same reason: not a fault, not a
 310          # retry. The difference is that this one is answerable -- the plan is
 311          # still on the screen and the cut is one click away.
 312          raise HTTPException(
 313              status_code=409,
 314              detail={
 315                  "error": "plan_too_large_to_finish",
 316                  "message": error.projection.note,
 317                  "budget_projection": asdict(error.projection),
 318              },
 319          ) from error
 320      except PlanHasNothingWorthReading as error:
 321          # Same 409, same reason, and answerable the same way: the plan is on
 322          # the screen and the box for adding a question is under it. A run with
 323          # no texture question stops at a gate that offers nothing to settle, so
 324          # this is refused before the research rather than discovered after it.
 325          raise HTTPException(
 326              status_code=409,
 327              detail={"error": "plan_has_nothing_worth_reading", "message": str(error)},
 328          ) from error
 329      except ValidationError as error:
 330          # Anything a stage builds and the contracts refuse. Pydantic's own
 331          # message is addressed to a developer and it subclasses ValueError, so
 332          # without this it fell through to the 400 below and reached the
 333          # operator verbatim -- "List should have at least 1 item after
 334          # validation, not 0", mid-flow, twice in one evening.
 335          logger.error("Intake payload failed its contract: %s", error)
 336          raise HTTPException(
 337              status_code=502,
 338              detail={
 339                  "error": "contract_violation",
 340                  "message": (
 341                      "Something came back in a shape the system cannot use. "
 342                      "Nothing you said caused this — try that step again."
 343                  ),
 344                  "raw": "; ".join(
 345                      f"{'.'.join(str(part) for part in item['loc'])}: {item['msg']}"
 346                      for item in error.errors()
 347                  )[:2000],
 348              },
 349          ) from error
 350      except GateAnswerRefused as error:
 351          # The operator asked for something the dossier will not take -- an
 352          # empty answer, or a question research already settled.
 353          raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(error)) from error
 354      except LookupError as error:
 355          raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=str(error)) from error
 356      except ValueError as error:
 357          raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(error)) from error
 358

 363  ) -> JSONResponse:

 423  @router.post("/{run_id}/work-order/cut")
 424  @exclusive_run
 425  def cut_the_work_order(
 426      run_id: str, request: CutRequest, _staff=Depends(require_staff)
 427  ) -> JSONResponse:
 428      """Apply the operator's cut, and hand back what it cost.
 429  
 430      The warnings ride on the response as well as the run, because they are for
 431      the person who just made the decision -- said once, not enforced.
 432      """
 433      outcome = _handle(
 434          apply_cut,
 435          run_id,
 436          _services(run_id),
 437          struck_ids=request.struck_ids,
 438          added_questions=request.added_questions,
 439      )
 440      return JSONResponse({**intake_state(run_id), "cut_warnings": outcome.warnings})

 443  @router.post("/{run_id}/research")
 444  @exclusive_run

 456  class GateAnswerRequest(BaseModel):
 457      requirement_id: str = Field(min_length=1)

 464      # not there. Different from the note above: that one says the figure exists
 465      # and nobody prints it.

 504  @router.post("/{run_id}/gate")
 505  @exclusive_run
 506  def settle_the_gate(
 507      run_id: str, request: GateAnswerRequest, _staff=Depends(require_staff)
 508  ) -> JSONResponse:
 509      """Settle one blocking question without re-buying the research.
 510  
 511      No model call: this is the operator's decision, recorded. The coverage
 512      verdict is re-derived afterwards by the function that blocked, so the page
 513      reads the same answer it would have got from a fresh research pass.
 514      """
 515      chosen = [
 516          request.answer is not None,
 517          request.unpublished_note is not None,
 518          request.nonexistent_note is not None,
 519          request.omit,
 520      ]
 521      if sum(chosen) != 1:
 522          raise HTTPException(
 523              status_code=400,
 524              detail=(
 525                  "Say one of four things: what the answer is, that nobody "
 526                  "publishes it, that the thing is not there, or that the "
 527                  "question should be dropped."
 528              ),
 529          )
 530      _handle(
 531          settle_gate,
 532          run_id,
 533          _services(run_id),
 534          requirement_id=request.requirement_id,
 535          answer=request.answer,
 536          source_url=request.source_url,
 537          unpublished_note=request.unpublished_note,
 538          nonexistent_note=request.nonexistent_note,
 539          omit=request.omit,
 540      )
 541      return JSONResponse(intake_state(run_id))

 665  
 666  @router.post("/{run_id}/write", status_code=202)
 667  @exclusive_run
 668  def start_writing(
 669      run_id: str,
 670      background_tasks: BackgroundTasks,
 671      _staff=Depends(require_staff),
 672  ) -> JSONResponse:
 673      """Hand a settled run to the graph.
 674  
 675      The same run id all the way through: the article is written onto the run
 676      the seed opened, so the receipt covers intake and writing together rather
 677      than splitting one article across two records.
 678  
 679      Refuses when research said no. That is the same gate decided once, not a
 680      second opinion.
 681      """
 682      handoff = _handle(writing_request, run_id)
 683      credential = _prompt2blog_credential_for_run()
 684      # One coherent snapshot: the brief, the dossier and the selection were read
 685      # together above, and the packet built from them is frozen into the runtime
 686      # request here. A resume reads that frozen packet rather than rebuilding
 687      # one from a selection the operator may have edited since.
 688      runtime = _handle(
 689          prepare_v3_runtime_request, handoff.request, handoff.selection
 690      )
 691  
 692      # The run already exists -- it was opened by the seed -- so this records
 693      # what the graph is about to run rather than queueing a new one. That is
 694      # the whole point of starting a run at the seed: one article, one record,
 695      # one receipt covering intake and writing together.
 696      # Continuing the run's ledger, not a fresh one. `record_stage` writes the
 697      # whole ledger at the end of every call, so a recorder built on an empty
 698      # tracker does not merely fail to add -- it ERASES what intake spent.
 699      #
 700      # Measured on run 062c0b86 (2026-09-01): the intake stages had recorded
 701      # 105,098 tokens, this line wrote the `pipeline_input_v3` row at 19:29:14,
 702      # and the run's finished receipt reported 161,897 -- the writing graph
 703      # alone. The ceiling reads that same total.
 704      recorder = dependencies_for_run(run_id).recorder
 705      artifact = v3_run_input_artifact(runtime)
 706      artifact["claude_account_label"] = credential.label if credential else None
 707      recorder.record_stage(run_id, RUN_INPUT_STAGE, artifact)
 708  
 709      background_tasks.add_task(
 710          _run_pipeline_v4_background, run_id, runtime, credential
 711      )
 712      return JSONResponse(
 713          {**intake_state(run_id), "writing": "queued"}, status_code=202
 714      )
apps/backend/app/features/prompt2blog/grill_v4.py
   1  """The interview that replaces the commission form.
   2  
   3  v3 asked an operator to choose between three directions a model wrote from one
   4  typed line. Nothing in that flow ever asked what the article was *for*, and the
   5  audited Lima run passed every measure the system owned while being unreadable.
   6  
   7  A form is a literacy test: it only works if you already know what belongs in
   8  each field. The people using this are travellers, creators and researchers
   9  writing about places they may never have been, not features editors. So the
  10  expertise goes in the system and the operator is asked only about what they
  11  know.
  12  
  13  Five rules, from ADR 0030:
  14  
  15  - G1 Every question carries a recommended answer. Nobody faces a blank.
  16  - G2 It researches before it asks. Anything it can look up, it never asks.
  17       This is what keeps the grill short -- not a question limit.
  18  - G3 One question at a time, each shaped by the last.
  19  - G4 It pushes back when an answer contradicts the seed or an earlier answer.
  20  - G5 It stops at agreement, not at a count.
  21  
  22  The loop lives here and the model calls sit behind `GrillDependencies`, so the
  23  rules above are testable without a network.
  24  """
  25  
  26  from __future__ import annotations
  27  
  28  import json
  29  import logging
  30  from dataclasses import dataclass
  31  from typing import Any, Callable, Protocol
  32  
  33  from .config import (
  34      P2B_V4_GRILL_MAX_LOOKUPS,
  35      P2B_V4_GRILL_TEMPERATURE,
  36  )
  37  from .contracts_v4 import (
  38      BRIEF_MARKERS,
  39      MARKER_KEYS,
  40      GrillOption,
  41      GrillQuestion,
  42      GrillState,
  43      GrillTurn,
  44  )
  45  from .schema_guards import require_non_empty
  46  from .support import _safe_dict, _safe_str, _safe_str_list
  47  
  48  logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  49  
  50  GRILL_STAGE = "stage_v4_grill"
  51  
  52  
  53  def _json_or_repr(payload: Any) -> str:
  54      try:
  55          return json.dumps(payload)
  56      except Exception:  # pragma: no cover -- diagnostics only
  57          return repr(payload)
  58  
  59  # Enough for a dense digest of a city. The helper's own default is 1024, which
  60  # truncates silently -- the Lima dossier was 12,000 characters.
  61  GRILL_RESEARCH_MAX_TOKENS = 4_096
  62  
  63  # What the live grounding path actually runs on. `editor_assist` has grounded
  64  # on this model in production since ADR 0003; the 3.x models are not known to
  65  # work through the REST grounding endpoint, and this is not the place to find
  66  # out.
  67  
  68  
  69  # `question` and `consensus` are both required, and the prompt says to leave
  70  # the unused one empty. Making only `done` required is what broke the first
  71  # real run: `{"done": false}` with nothing else is schema-valid and useless,
  72  # and the model took that gap. A schema that permits what the code refuses is
  73  # a schema that has not been written down properly.
  74  #
  75  # The reverse is a fault too, and this schema had it. `require_non_empty`
  76  # floors every required string at one character, so the same schema that
  77  # tells the model to leave `consensus` empty while asking also declared an
  78  # empty `consensus` invalid. Nothing enforced it until Gemini started being
  79  # sent the schema, and then the first turn of the first real run died on
  80  # `response.consensus: too short`. The state-dependent fields carry an
  81  # explicit `minLength: 0` below.
  82  # Flat on purpose.
  83  #
  84  # This was nested -- `question` as an object carrying `ask`, `recommendation`
  85  # and `pushback` -- and models kept answering flat instead: `question` as the
  86  # question string, with `recommendation` beside it at the top level. Twice in a
  87  # row the reply was a good question with a good recommendation, and it was
  88  # refused for its shape.
  89  #
  90  # There is nothing here worth nesting. A flat object has no structure to get
  91  # wrong, and shape is not worth losing content over.
  92  NEXT_TURN_SCHEMA = require_non_empty({
  93      "type": "object",
  94      "properties": {
  95          "done": {"type": "boolean"},
  96          # Required so the model always accounts for them, but explicitly
  97          # allowed to be empty: which of these carries content depends on the
  98          # turn, and `require_non_empty` would otherwise floor every one of
  99          # them at a character. Asking fills `ask`; finishing fills
 100          # `consensus`; neither is wrong to leave blank in the other state.
 101          # "Exactly one of these is filled" is not a thing a JSON schema can
 102          # say, so `_advance_once` is what refuses a turn that answers with
 103          # nothing -- see the guard that raises on neither question nor
 104          # consensus.
 105          "ask": {"type": "string", "minLength": 0},
 106          "recommendation": {"type": "string", "minLength": 0},
 107          "pushback": {"type": "string"},
 108          "topic": {"type": "string"},
 109          "consensus": {"type": "string", "minLength": 0},
 110          "location": {"type": "string"},
 111          "markers_covered": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
 112          # Empty is the honest answer when the operator's line is genuinely
 113          # ambiguous about what it asks about.
 114          "asks_about": {"type": "string", "minLength": 0},
 115          "options": {
 116              "type": "array",
 117              "items": {
 118                  "type": "object",
 119                  "properties": {
 120                      "text": {"type": "string"},
 121                      "recommended": {"type": "boolean"},
 122                      "group": {"type": "string"},
 123                  },
 124                  "required": ["text", "recommended"],
 125              },
 126          },
 127          "lookup": {"type": "string"},
 128      },
 129      "required": [
 130          "done",
 131          "ask",
 132          "recommendation",
 133          "consensus",
 134          "markers_covered",
 135          "asks_about",
 136      ],
 137  })
 138

 140  class GrillLLM(Protocol):
 141      def invoke_json(
 142          self, *, prompt: str, model_name: str, schema: dict[str, Any], **kwargs: Any
 143      ) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str]: ...
 144  
 145  
 146  @dataclass
 147  class GrillDependencies:
 148      """The two outside things the grill needs, both replaceable in tests."""
 149  
 150      llm: GrillLLM
 151      # Returns (digest, source_urls, total_tokens). Separate from `llm` because
 152      # this one reaches the web and the other does not.
 153      research: Callable[[str], tuple[str, list[str], int | None]]
 154      # Which grill this is. The listicle pipeline runs this same engine and is
 155      # its own job, so it stops reporting itself as `prompt2blog` -- which it
 156      # has done since it borrowed this code.
 157      job_id: str = "p2b.grill"
 158      # An operator's explicit choice. None means the gateway answers for the
 159      # job above, which is what makes the model changeable from the dashboard.
 160      model_name: str | None = None
 161      # What the grill is told before it decides its next move. The five rules in
 162      # this module are about how an interview behaves and hold whatever is being
 163      # commissioned; the wording of the questions is not, and belongs to the
 164      # thing doing the commissioning. A listicle grill passes its own and gets
 165      # the loop, the retry, the lookup budget, the pushback and the stop
 166      # condition unchanged -- which is the whole point of putting it here rather
 167      # than forking the file.
 168      # None means the article interview, whose prompt is defined further down
 169      # this module and so cannot be named as a default here.
 170      build_prompt: Callable[[GrillState], str] | None = None
 171  
 172  
 173  def research_seed(dependencies: GrillDependencies, seed: str) -> tuple[str, list[str], int | None]:
 174      """Look the seed up before asking anything (G2).
 175  
 176      A grill that asks what it could have looked up is a form with extra steps.
 177      Failure is not fatal: an ungrounded grill asks more questions, which is
 178      worse than a grounded one and better than no article.
 179      """
 180      try:
 181          return dependencies.research(seed)
 182      except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover -- network dependent
 183          logger.warning("Grill pre-research failed, continuing ungrounded: %s", exc)
 184          return "", [], None
 185  
 186  
 187  def _lookups_left(state: GrillState) -> int:
 188      return max(0, P2B_V4_GRILL_MAX_LOOKUPS - len(state.lookups))
 189  
 190  
 191  def look_up_mid_interview(
 192      state: GrillState,
 193      dependencies: GrillDependencies,
 194      query: str,
 195  ) -> GrillState:
 196      """Look something up in the middle of the interview, and remember it.
 197  
 198      The seed lookup happens once, before the first question. After that the
 199      grill went blind: by the fourth turn the conversation could have narrowed
 200      to one neighbourhood while the grill was still working from the general
 201      city briefing it pulled at the start.
 202  
 203      That matters because G2 is what keeps the grill short. A grill that cannot
 204      look up what the conversation has moved to is forced back into asking,
 205      which is the form-with-extra-steps failure the interview replaced.
 206  
 207      The budget is consumed whether or not the search comes back. A failed
 208      lookup that cost nothing to retry is a loop: the model would ask for the
 209      same thing again every turn, and the run has no question limit to stop it.
 210      What failed is written into the digest so the next call knows not to wait
 211      for it.
 212      """
 213      try:
 214          digest, urls, _tokens = dependencies.research(query)
 215      except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover -- network dependent
 216          logger.warning("Grill lookup failed for %r: %s", query, exc)
 217          digest, urls = "", []
 218  
 219      body = digest.strip() or "Nothing came back for this."
 220      return state.model_copy(
 221          update={
 222              "research_digest": (
 223                  f"{state.research_digest}\n\n"
 224                  f"--- Looked up mid-interview: {query} ---\n{body}"
 225              ).strip(),
 226              "research_source_urls": [
 227                  *state.research_source_urls,
 228                  *[url for url in urls if url not in state.research_source_urls],
 229              ],
 230              "lookups": [*state.lookups, query],
 231          }
 232      )
 233  
 234  
 235  def _transcript(state: GrillState) -> str:
 236      """The whole conversation, including the grill's own half.
 237  
 238      This used to render the question and the answer and drop the draft answer
 239      the grill wrote. The screen pre-fills the answer box with that draft, so
 240      the most common way to answer is to send it back untouched -- and with the
 241      draft missing from the replay, the grill read its own sentence returning as
 242      a confident, detailed answer from a writer. Run 1b441532 (2026-08-30
 243      15:40Z) agreed after two turns on that basis, having learned nothing.
 244  
 245      A grill that cannot tell "they said it" from "I said it" cannot judge
 246      agreement, so it gets told (ADR 0033).
 247      """
 248      if not state.turns:
 249          return "Nothing asked yet."
 250  
 251      blocks: list[str] = []
 252      for index, turn in enumerate(state.turns, start=1):
 253          lines = [f"Q{index}. You asked: {turn.question.ask}"]
 254          if turn.question.pushback:
 255              lines.append(f"You pushed back: {turn.question.pushback}")
 256          if turn.question.options:
 257              # A question answered by picking is not a draft they let stand.
 258              # Ticking six boxes out of twenty is a decision, and the
 259              # accepted-draft warning below says the opposite -- it tells the
 260              # grill it learned nothing, and a grill that believes it learned
 261              # nothing asks again. A live listicle run asked its angle question
 262              # twice in a row on exactly this, which is the single most
 263              # expensive question in that interview.
 264              offered = len(turn.question.options)
 265              lines.append(f"You offered them {offered} options to choose from.")
 266              lines.append(f"They chose these, and this is SETTLED:\n{turn.answer}")
 267          else:
 268              lines.append(
 269                  f"You drafted this answer for them: {turn.question.recommendation}"
 270              )
 271              if turn.accepted_as_drafted:
 272                  lines.append(
 273                      "They sent your draft back untouched. Those are YOUR words, not "
 274                      "theirs: it means they did not object, and it tells you nothing "
 275                      "you did not already believe."
 276                  )
 277              else:
 278                  lines.append(f"They wrote, in their own words: {turn.answer}")
 279          blocks.append("\n".join(lines))
 280      return "\n\n".join(blocks)
 281  
 282  
 283  def _marker_status(
 284      state: GrillState,
 285      markers: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = BRIEF_MARKERS,
 286  ) -> str:
 287      """What the brief still needs, named in plain English."""
 288      covered = set(state.markers_covered)
 289      return "\n".join(
 290          f"- {marker}: {description} — {'COVERED' if marker in covered else 'still missing'}"
 291          for marker, _, description in markers
 292      )
 293  
 294  
 295  def build_next_turn_prompt(state: GrillState) -> str:
 296      """What the grill is told before it decides its next move."""
 297      asked = len(state.turns)
 298      left = _lookups_left(state)
 299      can_look_up = (
 300          f"""You may look something up before deciding. Set `lookup` to what you
 301  want to know, in plain words, and leave everything else empty -- you will be
 302  asked again with the answer in hand. Use it when the conversation has moved
 303  somewhere your briefing does not cover: they named a neighbourhood, a festival,
 304  a business you know nothing about. Do NOT use it to check something you were
 305  already told, and do NOT use it instead of asking them what only they can say.
 306  You may do this {left} more time(s) this interview."""
 307          if left
 308          else """Your lookup budget is spent for this interview. Work from the
 309  briefing above and ask them; do not set `lookup`."""
 310      )
 311      return f"""You are interviewing a writer about an article they want to commission.
 312  They are a traveller or researcher, not an editor. Do not use editorial jargon.
 313  
 314  THEIR OPENING LINE:
 315  {state.seed}
 316  
 317  WHAT YOU ALREADY LOOKED UP (never ask about anything in here):
 318  {state.research_digest or "Nothing; you could not look anything up."}
 319  
 320  LOOKING SOMETHING UP:
 321  {can_look_up}
 322  
 323  THE INTERVIEW SO FAR:
 324  {_transcript(state)}
 325  
 326  WHAT THE BRIEF STILL NEEDS:
 327  {_marker_status(state)}
 328  
 329  Decide the single most useful next move.
 330  
 331  Output shape (mechanical -- get it right and then forget about it): every
 332  reply carries `ask`, `recommendation`, `consensus`, `markers_covered` and
 333  `asks_about`. When you are asking, fill `ask`, `recommendation` and
 334  `asks_about`, and leave `consensus` empty. When you are done, fill `consensus`
 335  and leave the others empty. `markers_covered` is always the full list of
 336  markers you can now fill.
 337  
 338  Now the part that matters:
 339  - Ask about ONE thing. If you are joining two questions with "and", you are
 340    asking two: keep the one you need first and save the other for next turn.
 341    Only ever ask about something you cannot look up -- what they want, who it
 342    is for, what they personally have, what would make it a failure. Never ask
 343    them to confirm a fact.
 344  - `recommendation` is your best answer to your own question, and it goes
 345    straight into their answer box for them to accept or correct. Three rules,
 346    in order of how badly each one bites.
 347  
 348    STATE THE ANSWER, NOT A SENTENCE ABOUT WHO HOLDS IT. No "you", no "I", no
 349    "I'm guessing", no question mark. Just the answer, the way a good editor
 350    says it out loud.
 351  
 352    Write: "A first-timer's guide with a point of view, not a ranking."
 353    Write: "It fails if it reads like a luxury fine-dining checklist."
 354    Never: "I'm guessing you want to build the piece around your own trip."
 355  
 356    MAKE IT YOUR REAL JUDGMENT. This is the expertise they came for, and a
 357    recommendation is the one place you get to use it. Think about what would
 358    genuinely make the best article, given their line and what you looked up,
 359    and propose that -- specifically, and strongly enough to argue with. A
 360    hedge, a menu of options, or a restatement of their own words is a wasted
 361    turn. Being wrong is fine and easy for them to fix. Being vague hands back
 362    the blank you were meant to fill.
 363  
 364    NEVER INVENT A FACT ABOUT THEIR LIFE. You can judge what the article should
 365    be. You cannot know where they have been, who they know, or what they ate.
 366    For anything only they can answer, do not write them a trip they may never
 367    have taken -- an invented experience they accept becomes first-hand material
 368    that nothing downstream is allowed to check. Recommend the research-led
 369    case, which is both the common one and the safe one, and let them correct it
 370    upward.
 371  
 372    Write: "Nothing first-hand -- this is researched rather than reported."
 373    Never: "I spent a week there in April and ate at the places I write about."
 374  - If an answer contradicts their opening line or an earlier answer, set
 375    `pushback` naming the contradiction, and make the question resolve it.
 376  - Ask about what they HAVE, never about credentials. "Been there, know
 377    someone, have an interview?" is the shape. "Nothing" is a fine answer and
 378    means it is a research-led piece.
 379  - Set `location` to the city AND its country: "Medellin, Colombia", never
 380    "Medellin". Everything downstream searches the web with this, and half the
 381    place names in Latin America exist in several countries. Medellin has a
 382    neighbourhood called Buenos Aires; a bare city name let a search answer about
 383    Argentina. Leave it empty only when their line is genuinely ambiguous about
 384    which place they mean.
 385  - Set `asks_about` to the marker your question is meant to settle. Ask about a
 386    marker that is still missing. NEVER ask about a marker twice: once they have
 387    answered a question, that marker is settled and you move to the next one. If
 388    their answer was thin and you want more, that is a different question about
 389    something else -- rephrasing the same question is how an interview stops
 390    being one.
 391  - `markers_covered` lists every marker you could now fill. Accepting your draft
 392    IS answering: they read it and put their name to it. It is weaker than an
 393    answer they wrote themselves, and that difference is worth noticing -- it
 394    tells you they are letting you drive, so put more into your next
 395    recommendation and be readier to push back. It does NOT mean the marker is
 396    unanswered. A marker you asked about and they responded to is settled.
 397  - Set `done` true and write `consensus` only when every marker is covered. Then
 398    play the whole thing back in plain English, addressed to them, so they can
 399    say "yes" or "no, less about that". You are not counting questions -- you are
 400    filling the brief, and you stop when it is full. {asked} questions asked so
 401    far.
 402  """
 403  
 404  
 405  def _question_from(
 406      payload: dict[str, Any],
 407      fallback_id: str,
 408      marker_keys: tuple[str, ...] = MARKER_KEYS,
 409  ) -> GrillQuestion | None:
 410      """Read the question, however the model chose to arrange it.
 411  
 412      Flat is what the schema asks for and what models actually produce. Nested
 413      under `question` is what an earlier schema asked for, and some will still
 414      do it. A bare `question` string with the recommendation beside it is the
 415      third arrangement seen in the wild.
 416  
 417      All three carry the same words. Refusing one of them throws away a
 418      perfectly good question over punctuation, which is exactly what happened
 419      twice on the first live runs.
 420      """
 421      nested = _safe_dict(payload.get("question"))
 422      question_text = payload.get("question")
 423      flat_ask = question_text if isinstance(question_text, str) else ""
 424  
 425      ask = (
 426          _safe_str(payload.get("ask"))
 427          or _safe_str(nested.get("ask"))
 428          or _safe_str(flat_ask)
 429      )
 430      # A recommendation that is a list of lines rather than a string is what a
 431      # model sends when the answer IS a list -- the angle question, where the
 432      # recommendation is the picked lines. `_safe_str` returns "" for a list, a
 433      # question with no recommendation is refused, and a live run spent a whole
 434      # retry on that. The lines are the answer; joining them loses nothing.
 435      recommendation = (
 436          _safe_str(payload.get("recommendation"))
 437          or _safe_str(nested.get("recommendation"))
 438          or "\n".join(_safe_str_list(payload.get("recommendation")))
 439          or "\n".join(_safe_str_list(nested.get("recommendation")))
 440      )
 441      if not ask or not recommendation:
 442          # A question with no recommendation is a blank box, which is the thing
 443          # this replaces. Reject it rather than showing it.
 444          return None
 445      asks_about = _safe_str(payload.get("asks_about")) or _safe_str(
 446          nested.get("asks_about")
 447      )
 448      return GrillQuestion(
 449          question_id=_safe_str(payload.get("question_id"))
 450          or _safe_str(nested.get("question_id"))
 451          or fallback_id,
 452          topic=_safe_str(payload.get("topic")) or _safe_str(nested.get("topic")) or "next",
 453          ask=ask,
 454          recommendation=recommendation,
 455          pushback=_safe_str(payload.get("pushback")) or _safe_str(nested.get("pushback")),
 456          asks_about=asks_about if asks_about in marker_keys else "",
 457          options=_options_from(payload.get("options") or nested.get("options")),
 458      )
 459  
 460  
 461  def _options_from(raw: Any) -> list[GrillOption]:
 462      """The choices, however the model chose to arrange them.
 463  
 464      Objects are what the schema asks for. A bare list of strings is what a
 465      model that skimmed the schema sends, and it carries the only part that
 466      cannot be reconstructed -- the wording. Refusing it would throw away the
 467      whole answer over its shape, which is the mistake this module has already
 468      made twice.
 469  
 470      A plain string is read as recommended, because a model that sent no flag
 471      sent only the ones it meant.
 472      """
 473      if isinstance(raw, str):
 474          return [
 475              GrillOption(text=text, recommended=True) for text in _safe_str_list(raw)
 476          ]
 477      if not isinstance(raw, list):
 478          return []
 479      options: list[GrillOption] = []
 480      seen: set[str] = set()
 481      for item in raw:
 482          if isinstance(item, str):
 483              text, recommended, group = _safe_str(item), True, ""
 484          elif isinstance(item, dict):
 485              text = _safe_str(item.get("text")) or _safe_str(item.get("angle"))
 486              recommended = item.get("recommended") is True
 487              group = _safe_str(item.get("group"))
 488          else:
 489              continue
 490          # Duplicates are the failure this question exists to avoid: the same
 491          # search offered twice is the same search run twice.
 492          key = text.lower()
 493          if not text or key in seen:
 494              continue
 495          seen.add(key)
 496          options.append(GrillOption(text=text, recommended=recommended, group=group))
 497      return options
 498  
 499  
 500  def _markers_from(
 501      payload: dict[str, Any],
 502      state: GrillState,
 503      marker_keys: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
 504  ) -> list[str]:
 505      """Which brief markers are settled: what the grill claims, plus what the
 506      conversation shows.
 507  
 508      The claim alone is not enough. Run a9959013 (2026-08-30 19:29Z) asked what
 509      would make the article a failure four times, got four usable answers, and
 510      never once marked `fails_if` covered -- because every answer was an
 511      accepted draft and the grill had been told an accepted draft is weak
 512      evidence. It refused to credit its own question, so the checklist never
 513      shrank and it asked again. That is a livelock, not caution.
 514  
 515      So a marker a question was asked about, and answered, counts. Accepting a
 516      draft is answering: the operator read it and endorsed it. The written-vs-
 517      accepted distinction still reaches the grill, and it still shapes how hard
 518      it probes -- it just cannot stall progress any more.
 519  
 520      Unknown names in the claim are dropped rather than refused: a model
 521      inventing a seventh marker has still told us about the six real ones.
 522      """
 523      raw = payload.get("markers_covered")
 524      claimed = {_safe_str(item) for item in raw} if isinstance(raw, list) else set()
 525      answered = {turn.question.asks_about for turn in state.turns}
 526      settled = claimed | answered
 527      keys = marker_keys if marker_keys is not None else state.marker_keys
 528      return [key for key in keys if key in settled]
 529  
 530  
 531  def _consensus_text(raw: Any) -> str:
 532      """The agreement, whether it arrived as prose or as the object it describes.
 533  
 534      The schema asks for a string and the prompt says to play the whole thing
 535      back in plain sentences. Models still send the structured version -- run
 536      a5858d6e (2026-09-04) returned `{"kind": "Pisco Sour bars", "place": "Lima,
 537      Peru", "count": 30, ...}`, which was a complete, correct agreement with
 538      every marker covered.
 539  
 540      `_safe_str` reads a dict as the empty string, so that agreement was
 541      discarded as "done with nothing agreed" and the interview asked two more
 542      questions to arrive back where it already was. Two model calls and forty
 543      seconds, thrown away over the shape of a field whose content was right.
 544  
 545      Rendered rather than refused, for the same reason `_question_from` accepts
 546      three arrangements of a question: the words are what matter and they were
 547      all there.
 548      """
 549      text = _safe_str(raw)
 550      if text:
 551          return text
 552      if isinstance(raw, dict):
 553          lines = []
 554          for key, value in raw.items():
 555              label = str(key).replace("_", " ").strip()
 556              if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
 557                  rendered = "\n".join(f"  - {item}" for item in value if item)
 558                  if rendered:
 559                      lines.append(f"{label}:\n{rendered}")
 560                  continue
 561              if value in (None, "", [], {}):
 562                  continue
 563              lines.append(f"{label}: {value}")
 564          return "\n".join(lines)
 565      if isinstance(raw, (list, tuple)):
 566          return "\n".join(f"- {item}" for item in raw if item)
 567      return ""
 568  
 569  
 570  class GrillUnusableResponse(RuntimeError):
 571      """The grill answered with something it cannot act on.
 572  
 573      Carries the raw response. The first real run died on exactly this and left
 574      nothing behind -- no stage row, no log line -- so the one moment that most
 575      needs explaining was the one moment with no evidence.
 576      """
 577  
 578      def __init__(self, raw: str, state: "GrillState | None" = None) -> None:
 579          super().__init__(
 580              "The grill returned neither a usable question nor a consensus."
 581          )
 582          self.raw = raw
 583          # The state as it stood when this failed, carrying any lookups the
 584          # attempt already paid for. Without it the retry starts from the
 585          # original state, the lookup budget resets, and one turn can spend it
 586          # twice -- measured at six searches against a budget of three.
 587          self.state = state
 588  
 589  
 590  def advance_grill(
 591      state: GrillState,
 592      dependencies: GrillDependencies,
 593  ) -> GrillState:
 594      """Decide the grill's next move from everything it knows.
 595  
 596      Returns a state that is either asking one more question or agreed. The
 597      caller records it; nothing is written here.
 598  
 599      Retried once. The writing stages deliberately do not retry a schema call,
 600      because each attempt there is a full article rewrite -- but this is a flash
 601      model deciding one question, and one unusable reply should not end a run
 602      before it has started.
 603      """
 604      attempts: list[str] = []
 605      # Carried across attempts, so a lookup the first attempt paid for is not
 606      # bought again by the second.
 607      working = state
 608      for attempt in range(2):
 609          try:
 610              return _advance_once(working, dependencies)
 611          except GrillUnusableResponse as error:
 612              attempts.append(error.raw)
 613              if error.state is not None:
 614                  working = error.state
 615              logger.warning(
 616                  "Grill returned an unusable response (attempt %s): %s",
 617                  attempt + 1,
 618                  error.raw[:500],
 619              )
 620      raise GrillUnusableResponse("\n---\n".join(attempts), working)
 621  
 622  
 623  def _advance_once(
 624      state: GrillState,
 625      dependencies: GrillDependencies,
 626  ) -> GrillState:
 627      # `state` is rebound as lookups land, so the enlarged digest and the record
 628      # of what was looked up survive on whatever this returns -- including the
 629      # turn where the grill finally asks its question.
 630      while True:
 631          parsed, raw = dependencies.llm.invoke_json(
 632              job_id=dependencies.job_id,
 633              prompt=(dependencies.build_prompt or build_next_turn_prompt)(state),
 634              model_name=dependencies.model_name,
 635              schema=NEXT_TURN_SCHEMA,
 636              max_tokens=2_048,
 637              temperature=P2B_V4_GRILL_TEMPERATURE,
 638          )
 639          payload = _safe_dict(parsed)
 640          lookup = _safe_str(payload.get("lookup"))
 641          # A lookup is a move, not an answer, so nothing else on the payload is
 642          # read: the model is saying "I need to know this before I decide".
 643          # Bounded by the budget, and the budget is spent even on a failure, so
 644          # this cannot become a turn that never ends.
 645          if lookup and payload.get("done") is not True and _lookups_left(state):
 646              logger.info("Grill looked up %r mid-interview", lookup)
 647              state = look_up_mid_interview(state, dependencies, lookup)
 648              continue
 649          if lookup and not _lookups_left(state):
 650              logger.info(
 651                  "Grill wanted to look up %r with no budget left; asking instead",
 652                  lookup,
 653              )
 654          break
 655      location = _safe_str(payload.get("location")) or state.location
 656      covered = _markers_from(payload, state)
 657  
 658      if payload.get("done") is True:
 659          consensus = _consensus_text(payload.get("consensus"))
 660          missing = [key for key in state.marker_keys if key not in covered]
 661          if consensus and not missing:
 662              return state.model_copy(
 663                  update={
 664                      "status": "agreed",
 665                      "pending": None,
 666                      "consensus": consensus,
 667                      "markers_covered": list(covered),
 668                      "location": location,
 669                  }
 670              )
 671          # Claiming to be done without saying what was agreed is not agreement,
 672          # and neither is being done with the brief still short of what it needs
 673          # (ADR 0033). Either way: keep asking rather than inventing the rest.
 674          logger.warning(
 675              "Grill reported done but is not finished; consensus=%s missing=%s",
 676              bool(consensus),
 677              ", ".join(missing) or "none",
 678          )
 679  
 680      question = _question_from(
 681          payload,
 682          fallback_id=f"q{len(state.turns) + 1}",
 683          marker_keys=state.marker_keys,
 684      )
 685      if question is None:
 686          raise GrillUnusableResponse(raw or _json_or_repr(payload), state)
 687      return state.model_copy(
 688          update={
 689              "status": "asking",
 690              "pending": question,
 691              "markers_covered": list(covered),
 692              "location": location,
 693          }
 694      )
 695  
 696  
 697  def start_grill(
 698      run_id: str,
 699      seed: str,
 700      dependencies: GrillDependencies,
 701      marker_keys: tuple[str, ...] = MARKER_KEYS,
 702  ) -> GrillState:
 703      """Open a grill on one typed line.
 704  
 705      `marker_keys` is what this interview has to settle before it may agree.
 706      It defaults to the article brief's, and is carried on the state from here
 707      so every later turn is judged against the checklist the run opened with.
 708      """
 709      digest, source_urls, _tokens = research_seed(dependencies, seed)
 710      opening = GrillState(
 711          run_id=run_id,
 712          seed=seed,
 713          marker_keys=marker_keys,
 714          research_digest=digest,
 715          research_source_urls=source_urls,
 716          # `pending` is filled by advance_grill; the contract forbids an asking
 717          # state without one, so the opening question is not optional.
 718          status="asking",
 719          pending=GrillQuestion(
 720              question_id="q0",
 721              topic="opening",
 722              ask="placeholder",
 723              recommendation="placeholder",
 724          ),
 725      )
 726      return advance_grill(opening, dependencies)
 727  
 728  
 729  def answer_grill(
 730      state: GrillState,
 731      answer: str,
 732      dependencies: GrillDependencies,
 733  ) -> GrillState:
 734      """Record what the operator typed and decide the next move."""
 735      if state.status != "asking" or state.pending is None:
 736          raise ValueError("This grill is not waiting for an answer.")
 737      cleaned = _safe_str(answer)
 738      if not cleaned:
 739          raise ValueError("An answer cannot be empty; the grill has nothing to act on.")
 740  
 741      answered = state.model_copy(
 742          update={
 743              "turns": [*state.turns, GrillTurn(question=state.pending, answer=cleaned)],
 744              "pending": None,
 745              "status": "asking",
 746          }
 747      )
 748      # model_copy skips validation, which is what lets this half-state exist for
 749      # one line. advance_grill returns a state that validates.
 750      return advance_grill(answered, dependencies)
 751  
 752  
 753  def reopen_grill(state: GrillState, dependencies: GrillDependencies) -> GrillState:
 754      """Go back into the grill after agreement.
 755  
 756      The single exit from every dead end (ADR 0030): a refuted premise, a thin
 757      dossier, or a brief the operator no longer wants all come back here. What
 758      was learned stays in the transcript; the agreement does not.
 759      """
 760      reopened = state.model_copy(update={"status": "asking", "consensus": "", "pending": None})
 761      return advance_grill(reopened, dependencies)
 762  
 763  
 764  def grill_stage_record(state: GrillState) -> dict[str, Any]:
 765      """What one grill turn writes to the run.
 766  
 767      The whole state each time, not a delta. Stage rows upsert on
 768      (run_id, stage) and the grill repeats by design, so the row has to be
 769      readable on its own; per-turn token usage is kept by the ledger under this
 770      stage's attempts.
 771      """
 772      return {
 773          "status": state.status,
 774          "seed": state.seed,
 775          "location": state.location,
 776          "turns_asked": len(state.turns),
 777          "transcript": [
 778              {
 779                  "question_id": turn.question.question_id,
 780                  "topic": turn.question.topic,
 781                  "ask": turn.question.ask,
 782                  "recommendation": turn.question.recommendation,
 783                  "pushback": turn.question.pushback,
 784                  "answer": turn.answer,
 785                  # Whether this was their answer or the grill's draft returned
 786                  # untouched. Recorded because a transcript that cannot show the
 787                  # difference is what let the grill agree with itself.
 788                  "accepted_as_drafted": turn.accepted_as_drafted,
 789              }
 790              for turn in state.turns
 791          ],
 792          "pending": json.loads(state.pending.model_dump_json()) if state.pending else None,
 793          "consensus": state.consensus,
 794          "markers_covered": list(state.markers_covered),
 795          "markers_missing": [
 796              marker for marker in MARKER_KEYS if marker not in state.markers_covered
 797          ],
 798          "research": {
 799              "grounded": bool(state.research_digest),
 800              "source_urls": list(state.research_source_urls),
 801          },
 802      }
apps/backend/app/features/prompt2blog/brief_v4.py
   1  """Turning an agreed grill into the Article Brief.
   2  
   3  The brief is the vision, and the only object in the run that is never consumed:
   4  it rides the whole way and the finished article is judged against it, including
   5  against its `fails_if` line -- the measure the system has never had. Every score
   6  v3 owned said the Lima article passed.
   7  
   8  The model reads the transcript and proposes the structure. It does not get to
   9  invent the operator's own words: a first-hand statement has to be an answer the
  10  operator actually typed, checked here rather than trusted, because first-hand
  11  material is excused from fact-checking by design and a paraphrase of it is an
  12  unverifiable claim nothing downstream can catch.
  13  """
  14  
  15  from __future__ import annotations
  16  
  17  import hashlib
  18  import json
  19  import logging
  20  import re
  21  from typing import Any, get_args
  22  
  23  from pydantic import ValidationError
  24  
  25  from .contracts_v4 import (
  26      BRIEF_MARKERS,
  27      ArticleBrief,
  28      ArticleFormId,
  29      AudienceTagId,
  30      BriefMaterial,
  31      BriefReader,
  32      GrillState,
  33  )
  34  from .editorial_catalog import EditorialCatalog, load_editorial_catalog
  35  from .grill_v4 import GrillDependencies
  36  from .schema_guards import require_non_empty
  37  from .support import _safe_dict, _safe_str, _safe_str_list
  38  
  39  logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  40  
  41  BRIEF_STAGE = "stage_v4_brief"
  42  
  43  # `form_id` carries its vocabulary in the schema rather than in prose. Gemini's
  44  # translator keeps `enum` and drops `minLength`, so an enum is one of the few
  45  # constraints that actually survives the trip -- and a bare string field named
  46  # `form_id`, with fifteen legal values stated nowhere, is what run 90b3f9bc
  47  # (2026-08-30 20:01Z) returned empty.
  48  BRIEF_SCHEMA = require_non_empty({
  49      "type": "object",
  50      "properties": {
  51          "form_id": {"type": "string", "enum": list(get_args(ArticleFormId))},
  52          "topic_module_ids": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
  53          "primary_reader": {"type": "string"},
  54          "reader_tags": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
  55          "reader_question": {"type": "string"},
  56          "outcome": {"type": "string"},
  57          "spine": {"type": "string"},
  58          "must_name": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
  59          "fails_if": {"type": "string"},
  60          "material": {
  61              "type": "array",
  62              "items": {
  63                  "type": "object",
  64                  "properties": {
  65                      "kind": {"type": "string"},
  66                      "quoted_answer": {"type": "string"},
  67                      "note": {"type": "string"},
  68                  },
  69                  "required": ["kind", "quoted_answer"],
  70              },
  71          },
  72      },
  73      "required": [
  74          "form_id",
  75          "primary_reader",
  76          "reader_question",
  77          "outcome",
  78          "spine",
  79          "fails_if",
  80      ],
  81  })
  82  
  83  
  84  def _form_exclusions(catalog: EditorialCatalog) -> str:
  85      """Each form's own "Do not use when" clause, at the moment a form is chosen.
  86  
  87      The forms carry these clauses and nothing has ever read them. Outline and
  88      compose are projected only Reader promise, Required evidence, Allowed
  89      structures and Failure modes, so a form chosen wrongly is invisible from
  90      there on -- and it must stay invisible, because a writer free to depart
  91      from an approved form is the thing approving one prevents.
  92  
  93      So the clause belongs here, where the choice is still being made. Run
  94      95a74dce called a single morning's walk a `destination-guide`, whose clause
  95      reads "Do not use for a single practical problem, a day-by-day plan, or a
  96      ranked list."
  97      """
  98      lines = []
  99      for form in catalog.forms:
 100          body = form.instructions.split("## Do not use when", 1)
 101          if len(body) < 2:
 102              continue
 103          clause = body[1].split("\n## ", 1)[0].strip().replace("\n", " ")
 104          if clause:
 105              lines.append(f"- {form.id}: {clause}")
 106      return "\n".join(lines)
 107  
 108  
 109  def build_brief_prompt(
 110      state: GrillState, *, catalog: EditorialCatalog | None = None
 111  ) -> str:
 112      catalog = catalog or load_editorial_catalog()
 113      form_exclusions = _form_exclusions(catalog)
 114      transcript = "\n\n".join(
 115          f"Q. {turn.question.ask}\nThey said: {turn.answer}" for turn in state.turns
 116      )
 117      return f"""Turn this interview into a commissioning brief.
 118  
 119  THEIR OPENING LINE (provenance only -- it is not a promise to keep):
 120  {state.seed}
 121  
 122  THE INTERVIEW:
 123  {transcript}
 124  
 125  WHAT YOU BOTH AGREED:
 126  {state.consensus}
 127  
 128  Fill the brief from what was actually said. Every field below is required and
 129  must carry a real value -- an empty string is not an answer. Where the
 130  interview did not settle something outright, decide it from what they did say
 131  rather than leaving it blank.
 132  
 133  - `form_id` is the kind of article, chosen from the list the schema allows.
 134    A walk through what a place offers is `destination-guide`; a ranked or
 135    grouped set of picks is `curated-list-best-of`; a day-by-day plan is
 136    `itinerary`; a how-much-does-it-cost piece is `cost-budget-breakdown`.
 137    Each form says what it is NOT for. Read these before choosing, and do not
 138    pick a form whose exclusion describes this piece:
 139  {form_exclusions}
 140  - `primary_reader` is who this is for, in a phrase -- who they are and what
 141    situation they are in, not a demographic bracket.
 142  - `reader_question` is the question in that reader's head, written the way
 143    they would ask it.
 144  - `spine` is the argument the piece is built on, in their words where possible.
 145  - `outcome` is what the reader should do or decide afterwards.
 146  - `fails_if` is what would make this a failure, taken from what they said, not
 147    invented. This is the line the finished article gets judged against.
 148  - `must_name` is only what the piece genuinely has to mention, and it is a
 149    list: one name per entry, never several in one string separated by commas.
 150    A single entry reading "Surquillo market, Miraflores, the municipal ranking"
 151    is three obligations the system can then only measure as one.
 152    Every entry names ONE thing the article must contain. Never write a rule
 153    about every item -- "For each museum named: what it costs" is not a name,
 154    and the writer reads this list as a checklist to satisfy in the prose, so a
 155    rule like that comes back as the same fact repeated in every section. If the
 156    operator wants a detail carried for each item, that belongs in `fails_if`.
 157  - `material` is what they personally have. For each entry, `quoted_answer` must
 158    be an EXACT copy of one of their answers above -- do not summarise, tidy or
 159    merge. `kind` is firsthand, interview, or research.
 160  - If they said they have nothing, return no material. That is a research-led
 161    piece and is completely fine.
 162  - Do not choose `analysis` as the form unless they said they want to make a
 163    case rather than write a guide.
 164  """
 165  
 166  
 167  def _material_from(payload: dict[str, Any], state: GrillState) -> list[BriefMaterial]:
 168      """Keep only material the operator actually typed.
 169  
 170      The model nominates which answers are material and what kind they are. The
 171      words themselves come from the transcript, matched exactly. Anything that
 172      does not match a real answer is dropped and logged: a "first-hand" claim
 173      the operator never made is worse than no material at all, because nothing
 174      downstream will ever check it.
 175  
 176      An answer that became one of the brief's own fields is a commissioning
 177      decision, not evidence, and is dropped too. Run 95a74dce filed six of them
 178      as `interview` -- the reader, the spine, the outcome and the failure line,
 179      1,349 characters of instructions restated as facts. `interview` is the one
 180      kind the evidence policy lets the writer assert with no source ("First-hand
 181      material is the writer's own knowledge: state it directly, as fact"), so
 182      the misfiling hands editorial intent the standing of reported fact. Those
 183      answers already reach every stage as the fields they became.
 184  
 185      The exact-quote check stays exactly as it was. This only removes answers
 186      the brief is already carrying.
 187      """
 188      answers = {turn.answer for turn in state.turns}
 189      # These are the payload's own key names -- BRIEF_SCHEMA keeps
 190      # `primary_reader` at the top level, not nested under a reader object.
 191      commissioned = {
 192          _safe_str(payload.get(key))
 193          for key in ("primary_reader", "reader_question", "outcome", "spine", "fails_if")
 194      }
 195      commissioned.discard("")
 196  
 197      material: list[BriefMaterial] = []
 198      for raw in payload.get("material") or []:
 199          record = _safe_dict(raw)
 200          quoted = _safe_str(record.get("quoted_answer"))
 201          kind = _safe_str(record.get("kind"))
 202          if kind not in {"firsthand", "interview", "research"}:
 203              continue
 204          if quoted not in answers:
 205              logger.warning(
 206                  "Dropping brief material that does not quote a real answer: %r",
 207                  quoted[:80],
 208              )
 209              continue
 210          if quoted in commissioned:
 211              logger.info(
 212                  "Dropping brief material that is a commissioning decision, not "
 213                  "evidence: %r",
 214                  quoted[:80],
 215              )
 216              continue
 217          material.append(
 218              BriefMaterial(kind=kind, statement=quoted, note=_safe_str(record.get("note")))
 219          )
 220      return material
 221  
 222  
 223  # A `must_name` entry that begins "for each" is not a name, it is a rule about
 224  # every item the article names. Narrow on purpose: a bare "Every ..." can open
 225  # a real name ("Every Man Jack bar"), so that form only counts as a rule when
 226  # it also carries the colon that introduces what must be said about each item.
 227  _PER_ITEM_RULE = re.compile(
 228      r"^for\s+(?:each|every)\b|^(?:each|every)\b[^:]*:", re.IGNORECASE
 229  )
 230  
 231  
 232  def _split_per_item_rules(entries: list[str]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
 233      """Separate the names the article must carry from rules about every item.
 234  
 235      `must_name` is a coverage checklist: the writer reads it in the brief and
 236      the audit scores the finished article entry by entry. A rule in that list
 237      is therefore an instruction to repeat something for every item, enforced.
 238  
 239      Run e001d48c was briefed with four such entries -- "For each working
 240      ascensor named: what a visitor pays at the window" and three more -- and
 241      the article printed the fare in six of its seven sections. The writer was
 242      obeying. The same repetition appeared in the first draft and survived
 243      repair unchanged, because nothing in the repair loop was what put it there.
 244  
 245      The rules are not discarded. They move to `fails_if`, which is prose the
 246      writer weighs and the line the article is judged against as a whole, rather
 247      than a list scored one line at a time.
 248      """
 249      names = [item for item in entries if not _PER_ITEM_RULE.match(item.strip())]
 250      rules = [item for item in entries if _PER_ITEM_RULE.match(item.strip())]
 251      return names, rules
 252  
 253  
 254  def _deduped(values: list[str], *, casefold: bool = False) -> list[str]:
 255      """Keep the first of each value, in the order the model gave them.
 256  
 257      Three of the brief's lists carry a uniqueness rule -- `must_name`,
 258      `topic_module_ids` and `reader_tags` -- and the model is told about none of
 259      them. A repeated entry used to take the whole brief down with a Pydantic
 260      error about `must_name` uniqueness, which is a good brief refused over a
 261      duplicated string.
 262  
 263      The contract stays strict, because a brief that names the same thing twice
 264      is genuinely malformed. What changes is that it is handed clean input,
 265      the same way material is filtered before it gets there.
 266      """
 267      seen: set[str] = set()
 268      kept: list[str] = []
 269      for value in values:
 270          key = value.casefold() if casefold else value
 271          if key in seen:
 272              continue
 273          seen.add(key)
 274          kept.append(value)
 275      return kept
 276  
 277  
 278  def _reader_from(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> BriefReader:
 279      """Who this is for, with tags the contract will actually accept.
 280  
 281      `reader_tags` is a closed vocabulary the model is not shown, so an invented
 282      tag is normal and is dropped rather than allowed to take the brief down.
 283      The reader themself is required and is not guessed at here -- an empty one
 284      is caught by the missing-field check with a sentence about it.
 285      """
 286      allowed = set(get_args(AudienceTagId))
 287      tags = _deduped(
 288          [tag for tag in _safe_str_list(payload.get("reader_tags")) if tag in allowed]
 289      )
 290      return BriefReader(
 291          primary_reader=_safe_str(payload.get("primary_reader")), tags=tags
 292      )
 293  
 294  
 295  def brief_fingerprint(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
 296      """A stable id for one brief's contents.
 297  
 298      Content-addressed so the work order and the evidence can each be checked
 299      against the brief they were derived from rather than trusted.
 300      """
 301      canonical = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)
 302      return "bf-" + hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:32]
 303  
 304  
 305  class BriefIncomplete(RuntimeError):
 306      """The brief writer left something out that the brief cannot do without.
 307  
 308      Carries what it did return. A run that fails here has already paid for the
 309      grill, so the operator should get a sentence about what is missing rather
 310      than a Pydantic traceback about string length.
 311      """
 312  
 313      def __init__(self, missing: list[str], raw: str) -> None:
 314          super().__init__(
 315              "The brief came back missing: " + ", ".join(missing) + "."
 316          )
 317          self.missing = missing
 318          self.raw = raw
 319  
 320  
 321  class BriefUnusable(RuntimeError):
 322      """The brief came back complete and still would not assemble.
 323  
 324      A duplicated `must_name` entry reached the operator as a raw Pydantic
 325      error about value uniqueness, mid-flow, after the grill had been paid for.
 326      The contract is right to refuse a malformed brief; what was wrong is that
 327      its complaint was addressed to a developer.
 328  
 329      Carries the reason and the payload, and is retried once -- a duplicate is
 330      the kind of fluke a second attempt usually clears.
 331      """
 332  
 333      def __init__(self, reason: str, raw: str) -> None:
 334          super().__init__(reason)
 335          self.reason = reason
 336          self.raw = raw
 337  
 338  
 339  # What a brief cannot be assembled without. Empty is the failure mode that
 340  # actually happens -- the key is present and the value is "" -- so this checks
 341  # the value, not the key.
 342  #
 343  # Derived from `BRIEF_MARKERS` rather than typed out again: the same six things
 344  # are the grill's stop condition (ADR 0033), and a grill that stops one marker
 345  # short of what the brief demands is a run that dies here having already paid
 346  # for the whole interview.
 347  REQUIRED_BRIEF_FIELDS = tuple(
 348      (field, description) for _, field, description in BRIEF_MARKERS
 349  )
 350  
 351  
 352  def _missing_fields(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
 353      return [
 354          label
 355          for key, label in REQUIRED_BRIEF_FIELDS
 356          if not _safe_str(payload.get(key))
 357      ]
 358  
 359  
 360  def build_brief(
 361      state: GrillState,
 362      dependencies: GrillDependencies,
 363      *,
 364      location: str | None = None,
 365  ) -> ArticleBrief:
 366      """Assemble the brief an agreed grill earned.
 367  
 368      Retried once. The grill has already been paid for by this point, and a
 369      single thin reply should not cost the operator the whole conversation.
 370      """
 371      if state.status != "agreed":
 372          raise ValueError("A brief can only be built from a grill that reached agreement.")
 373  
 374      attempts: list[str] = []
 375      last: BriefIncomplete | None = None
 376      last_unusable: BriefUnusable | None = None
 377      for attempt in range(2):
 378          try:
 379              return _build_brief_once(state, dependencies, location=location)
 380          except BriefIncomplete as error:
 381              attempts.append(error.raw)
 382              logger.warning(
 383                  "Brief came back incomplete (attempt %s), missing %s",
 384                  attempt + 1,
 385                  ", ".join(error.missing),
 386              )
 387              last = error
 388          except BriefUnusable as error:
 389              attempts.append(error.raw)
 390              logger.warning(
 391                  "Brief did not fit its contract (attempt %s): %s",
 392                  attempt + 1,
 393                  error.reason,
 394              )
 395              last_unusable = error
 396      if last is not None:
 397          raise BriefIncomplete(last.missing, "\n---\n".join(attempts))
 398      assert last_unusable is not None
 399      raise BriefUnusable(last_unusable.reason, "\n---\n".join(attempts))
 400  
 401  
 402  def _build_brief_once(
 403      state: GrillState,
 404      dependencies: GrillDependencies,
 405      *,
 406      location: str | None = None,
 407  ) -> ArticleBrief:
 408      parsed, raw = dependencies.llm.invoke_json(
 409              job_id="p2b.brief",
 410          prompt=build_brief_prompt(state),
 411          model_name=dependencies.model_name,
 412          schema=BRIEF_SCHEMA,
 413          max_tokens=2_048,
 414          temperature=0.2,
 415      )
 416      payload = _safe_dict(parsed)
 417  
 418      missing = _missing_fields(payload)
 419      if missing:
 420          # Checked here rather than left to Pydantic, so the operator is told
 421          # what is missing in words instead of being shown a string-length
 422          # validation error for a field they have never heard of.
 423          raise BriefIncomplete(missing, raw or json.dumps(payload))
 424  
 425      resolved_location = _safe_str(location or state.location)
 426      if not resolved_location:
 427          # The brief cannot be built without one, and guessing a place is how an
 428          # article about somewhere else gets written.
 429          raise ValueError("The grill did not settle a location; ask before briefing.")
 430  
 431      must_name, per_item_rules = _split_per_item_rules(
 432          _deduped(_safe_str_list(payload.get("must_name")), casefold=True)
 433      )
 434      fails_if = _safe_str(payload.get("fails_if"))
 435      if per_item_rules:
 436          logger.info(
 437              "Brief moved %s per-item rule(s) out of must_name: %s",
 438              len(per_item_rules),
 439              "; ".join(per_item_rules),
 440          )
 441          fails_if = "\n".join(
 442              (
 443                  fails_if,
 444                  "It also fails on any of these, which are rules about every "
 445                  "item the article names rather than names in their own right:",
 446                  *(f"- {rule}" for rule in per_item_rules),
 447              )
 448          )
 449  
 450      fields: dict[str, Any] = {
 451          "seed": state.seed,
 452          "location": resolved_location,
 453          "form_id": _safe_str(payload.get("form_id")),
 454          "topic_module_ids": _deduped(
 455              _safe_str_list(payload.get("topic_module_ids"))
 456          )[:4],
 457          "reader": _reader_from(payload),
 458          "reader_question": _safe_str(payload.get("reader_question")),
 459          "outcome": _safe_str(payload.get("outcome")),
 460          "spine": _safe_str(payload.get("spine")),
 461          # Casefolded, because that is what the contract compares on.
 462          "must_name": must_name,
 463          "material": _material_from(payload, state),
 464          "fails_if": fails_if,
 465      }
 466      # Fingerprinted over the contents, before the fingerprint is one of them.
 467      fingerprint_source = {
 468          key: (
 469              [item.model_dump(mode="json") for item in value]
 470              if key == "material"
 471              else value.model_dump(mode="json")
 472              if key == "reader"
 473              else value
 474          )
 475          for key, value in fields.items()
 476      }
 477      try:
 478          return ArticleBrief(
 479              brief_fingerprint=brief_fingerprint(fingerprint_source), **fields
 480          )
 481      except ValidationError as error:
 482          raise BriefUnusable(
 483              "; ".join(
 484                  f"{'.'.join(str(part) for part in item['loc']) or 'brief'}: {item['msg']}"
 485                  for item in error.errors()
 486              )
 487              or "the brief did not fit its contract",
 488              json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)[:4000],
