 404  
 405  def load_evidence(run_id: str) -> EvidencePackage:
 406      stored = _stage_data(run_id, RESEARCH_STAGE).get(STATE_KEY)
 407      if not isinstance(stored, dict):
 408          raise LookupError(f"No research for run {run_id}.")
 409      return EvidencePackage.model_validate(stored)
 410  
 411  
 412  def do_research(run_id: str, services: IntakeServices) -> CoverageVerdict:
 413      """Run both research passes and decide whether this can be written.
 414  
 415      The verdict is recorded whether or not it passes. A run that stopped here
 416      should be able to say why without anyone re-running anything.
 417      """
 418      if services.research is None:
 419          raise ValueError("Research is not configured for this run.")
 420      tokens_spent = _run_tokens_spent(run_id)
 421      enforce_run_budget(tokens_spent, stage=RESEARCH_STAGE)
 422  
 423      brief = load_brief(run_id)
 424      work_order = load_work_order(run_id)
 425  
 426      def record_progress(progress: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
 427          services.recorder.record_stage(run_id, PROGRESS_STAGE, progress)
 428  
 429      def check_budget() -> None:
 430          enforce_run_budget(_run_tokens_spent(run_id), stage=RESEARCH_STAGE)
 431  
 432      def save_notes(notes: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
 433          services.recorder.record_stage(run_id, NOTES_STAGE, notes_stage_record(work_order, notes))
 434  
 435      notes = notes_from_record(_stage_data(run_id, NOTES_STAGE), work_order) or {}
 436      outstanding = [
 437          item
 438          for item in work_order.requirements
 439          if not (item.requirement_id in notes and notes[item.requirement_id].text.strip())
 440      ]
 441      # The ceiling asks what this run has already spent. This asks what the
 442      # gathering it is about to do will cost, which is the only part of the sum
 443      # that can still be changed. Counted over the questions still without a
 444      # note, so a resume is not charged again for notes it already paid for.
 445      enforce_plan_fits(len(outstanding), tokens_spent, _run_billed_cost(run_id))
 446      # Asked of the whole plan rather than of what is outstanding, so a resume
 447      # that has already paid for its notes is judged on the same plan it started
 448      # with. A run with no texture question stops at the gate either way; this
 449      # says so while it still costs nothing.
 450      enforce_plan_has_texture(work_order)
 451  
 452      if outstanding:
 453          _open(services, run_id, NOTES_STAGE)
 454          notes = gather_research(
 455              brief, work_order, services.research, record_progress,
 456              kept_notes=notes, checkpoint=save_notes, before_call=check_budget,
 457          )
 458          save_notes(notes)
 459  
 460      record_progress({"phase": "structuring", "done": len(notes), "total": len(notes),
 461                       "last_question_back": ""})
 462      try:
 463          _open(services, run_id, RESEARCH_STAGE)
 464          evidence = structure_research(
 465              work_order, notes, services.research,
 466              kept_batches=_stage_data(run_id, BATCHES_STAGE).get("batches", {}),
 467              checkpoint=lambda batches: services.recorder.record_stage(run_id, BATCHES_STAGE, {"batches": batches}),
 468              before_call=lambda: enforce_run_budget(_run_tokens_spent(run_id), stage=RESEARCH_STAGE),
 469          )
 470      except ResearchUnusable as error:
 471          # The most expensive step in intake. A failure here that leaves nothing
 472          # behind means the next attempt is another guess.
 473          _record(
 474              services,
 475              run_id,
 476              RESEARCH_STAGE,
 477              {
 478                  "status": "failed",
 479                  "reason": error.reason,
 480                  "unusable_response": error.raw[:40000],
 481              },
 482          )
 483          raise
 484      verdict = assess_coverage(work_order, evidence)
 485  
 486      _record(
 487          services,
 488          run_id,
 489          RESEARCH_STAGE,
 490          {
 491              **research_stage_record(evidence, notes),
 492              "coverage": verdict.as_record(),
 493              STATE_KEY: json.loads(evidence.model_dump_json()),
 494          },
 495      )
 496      # One definition of what happens to the choice when the dossier moves, and
 497      # this is the first time it moves. A blocked run selects nothing: ranking
 498      # the evidence of an article nobody reaches is two model calls spent on a
 499      # decision that may not survive the gate.
 500      _resettle_selection(run_id, services, work_order, evidence, verdict)
 501      return verdict
 502  
 503  
 504  def _select_evidence(
 505      run_id: str,
 506      services: IntakeServices,
 507      brief: ArticleBrief,
 508      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
 509      evidence: EvidencePackage,
 510  ) -> Selection:
 511      """Deduplicate and rank, and record where the line starts (#534).
 512  
 513      Recorded apart from the dossier. The evidence stays exactly what research
 514      returned, and which facts the article is written from stays a separate,
 515      reversible editorial record that `writing_request` applies at the hand-off.
 516      """
 517      selection = select_evidence(
 518          brief,
 519          work_order,
 520          evidence,
 521          SelectionDependencies(llm=services.dependencies.llm),
 522          target_word_count=default_target_word_count(),
 523      )
 524      _record(services, run_id, SELECTION_STAGE, selection.as_record())
 525      return selection
 526  
 527  
 528  def _resettle_selection(
 529      run_id: str,
 530      services: IntakeServices,
 531      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
 532      evidence: EvidencePackage,
 533      verdict: CoverageVerdict,
 534  ) -> None:
 535      """Keep the editorial choice pointing at the dossier it is applied to.
 536  
 537      The gate is not the end of research. Answering a question mints a claim,
 538      re-asking one replaces a batch, dropping a venue removes one, and noting a
 539      venue changes what a fact means. Every one of those happens after selection
 540      has run, and every one used to leave the choice describing a dossier that
 541      no longer existed -- which the packet then refused to write from. The venue
 542      check sits directly above the picker on the same screen, so the most
 543      ordinary thing an operator can do would have blocked the article.
 544  
 545      Three cases, and only one of them costs anything:
 546  
 547      A run that still cannot be written is left alone. Ranking the evidence of a
 548      blocked article buys two model calls for a decision nobody reaches, and the
 549      gate may change the dossier again before they do.
 550  
 551      A run that can be written and has never selected gets a real selection. A
 552      run that was ever blocked used to reach the writer with none, and write
 553      from every claim it found -- which is the behaviour #534 exists to end.
 554  
 555      A run that can be written and already has one is rebound: choices carried
 556      by stable id, no model call. A note on a venue says nothing about which
 557      facts this article needs.
 558      """
 559      if not verdict.can_write:
 560          return
 561      brief = load_brief(run_id)
 562      selection = load_selection(run_id)
 563      if selection is None:
 564          _select_evidence(run_id, services, brief, work_order, evidence)
 565          return
 566      rebound, changed = rebind(selection, brief, work_order, evidence)
 567      if changed or rebound.as_record() != selection.as_record():
 568          _record(services, run_id, SELECTION_STAGE, rebound.as_record())
 569  
 570  
 571  def review_selection(run_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 572      """The ranked shortlist, where the line sits, and whether it still holds.
 573  
 574      `available: False` used to mean the run would write from every fact it
 575      found. It no longer does -- the hand-off refuses without a selection --
 576      so the screen has to say that rather than show nothing.
 577      """
 578      selection = load_selection(run_id)
 579      if selection is None:
 580          return {
 581              "available": False,
 582              "claims": [],
 583              "keep_count": 0,
 584              "note": "",
 585              "stale_reason": "",
 586          }
 587      brief = load_brief(run_id)
 588      work_order = load_work_order(run_id)
 589      evidence = load_evidence(run_id)
 590      # Shown as the writer would receive it. The gate persists a rebind at every
 591      # point it changes the dossier; doing it again here means a read cannot
 592      # show a list the hand-off would then quietly reconcile behind the
 593      # operator's back.
 594      selection, changed = rebind(selection, brief, work_order, evidence)
 595      return {
 596          "available": True,
 597          "claims": shortlist(evidence, work_order, selection),
 598          "keep_count": selection.keep_count,
 599          "target_word_count": selection.target_word_count,
 600          "deduped": selection.deduped,
 601          "ranked": selection.ranked,
 602          "note": " ".join(part for part in (selection.note, changed) if part),
 603          # The same sentence the write boundary would refuse with, shown while
 604          # the operator can still do something about it. Empty when the choice
 605          # still describes what it was made from.
 606          "stale_reason": stale_reason(brief, work_order, evidence, selection),
 607          # What is weak about the facts that are actually going to the writer
 608          # (improvement 08). Here rather than at the gate because this is the
 609          # last screen before prose exists and the first one that knows which
 610          # facts were chosen -- a stale price the operator already cut is not
 611          # this article's problem, and reporting it would bury the one that is.
 612          #
 613          # Advisory. Nothing here blocks: the operator can read that the newest
 614          # price is eighteen months old and decide it does not matter, which is
 615          # a judgement no deterministic check is entitled to make for them.
 616          "evidence_health": assess_evidence_health(
 617              brief,
 618              apply_selection(evidence, selection),
 619              today=date.today(),
 620          ).as_record(),
 621      }
 622  
 623  
 624  def settle_selection(
 625      run_id: str,
 626      services: IntakeServices,
 627      *,
 628      keep_count: int | None = None,
 629      rescue: str | None = None,
 630      drop: str | None = None,
 631      clear: str | None = None,
 632  ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 633      """Apply one of the operator's moves and hand the list back."""
 634      selection = load_selection(run_id)
 635      if selection is None:
 636          raise SelectionRefused("Nothing has been selected for this run yet.")
 637      revised = revise(
 638          selection, keep_count=keep_count, rescue=rescue, drop=drop, clear=clear
 639      )
 640      _record(services, run_id, SELECTION_STAGE, revised.as_record())
 641      return review_selection(run_id)
 642  
 643  
 644  def load_selection(run_id: str) -> Selection | None:
 645      """The operator's editorial record, or None when nothing has selected.
 646  
 647      None is not an empty selection. A run whose selection never ran writes from
 648      every fact it found, exactly as it did before this existed.
 649      """
 650      record = _stage_data(run_id, SELECTION_STAGE)
 651      return Selection.from_record(record) if record.get("order") else None
 652  
 653  
 654  def _strike_must_name(
 655      run_id: str, services: IntakeServices, names: list[str]
 656  ) -> ArticleBrief:
 657      """Drop an obligation research has just proved cannot be met.
 658  
 659      Run b29d66b4 asked for the shortlist to be cross-checked against "Lima's
 660      municipal ranking of cevicherias". Research settled it: the ranking does
 661      not exist. `must_name` still carried it, the article named it anyway, and
 662      `must_include_covered` scored true -- the check rewarding the piece for
 663      naming a thing the run had established is not real.
 664  
 665      The operator says which entries to strike. No matcher tries to guess which
 666      `must_name` line a dead question corresponds to: that matcher would be
 667      wrong in both directions and would need its own repair later.
 668  
 669      `brief_fingerprint` is deliberately left alone. It binds the work order and
 670      the evidence to the brief they were derived from, and re-deriving it here
 671      would break both bindings over an operator edit. `omit_requirement` makes
 672      the same choice when it trims a work order, for the same reason.
 673      """
 674      brief = load_brief(run_id)
 675      unwanted = {name.strip().casefold() for name in names if name.strip()}
 676      kept = [item for item in brief.must_name if item.casefold() not in unwanted]
 677      if len(kept) == len(brief.must_name):
 678          raise GateAnswerRefused(
 679              "None of those are on the brief's must-name list."
 680          )
 681      struck = brief.model_copy(update={"must_name": kept})
 682      logger.info(
 683          "Operator struck must_name %s at the research gate",
 684          sorted(unwanted),
 685          extra={"run_id": run_id},
 686      )
 687      _record(
 688          services,
 689          run_id,
 690          BRIEF_STAGE,
 691          {
 692              **brief_stage_record(struck),
 693              "struck_must_name": sorted(unwanted),
 694              STATE_KEY: json.loads(struck.model_dump_json()),
 695          },
 696      )
 697      return struck
 698  
 699  
 700  def settle_gate(
 701      run_id: str,
 702      services: IntakeServices,
 703      *,
 704      requirement_id: str,
 705      answer: str | None = None,
 706      source_url: str | None = None,
 707      unpublished_note: str | None = None,
 708      nonexistent_note: str | None = None,
 709      strike_must_name: list[str] | None = None,
 710      omit: bool = False,
 711  ) -> CoverageVerdict:
 712      """Settle one blocking question without re-buying the research.
 713  
 714      A blocked run had one exit, the grill, which discards everything the
 715      research pass paid for. Run 76b36468 was stopped by a single co-op that
 716      does not publish its price, with six of seven questions answered and ten
 717      web searches already spent.
 718  
 719      No model call. This is the operator's decision, recorded, and the coverage
 720      verdict is then re-derived by the same function that blocked -- not a
 721      second opinion, the same one asked again.
 722      """
 723      work_order = load_work_order(run_id)
 724      evidence = load_evidence(run_id)
 725      notes = _stage_data(run_id, RESEARCH_STAGE).get("notes") or {}
 726  
 727      if strike_must_name:
 728          _strike_must_name(run_id, services, strike_must_name)
 729  
 730      if omit:
 731          evidence, work_order, cost = omit_requirement(
 732              evidence, work_order, requirement_id=requirement_id
 733          )
 734          # The work order changes too, or the coverage check would go on asking
 735          # about a question that no longer exists.
 736          _record(
 737              services,
 738              run_id,
 739              WORK_ORDER_STAGE,
 740              {
 741                  **work_order_stage_record(
 742                      work_order,
 743                      [cost],
 744                      tokens_spent=_run_tokens_spent(run_id),
 745                      target_word_count=default_target_word_count(),
 746                  ),
 747                  STATE_KEY: json.loads(work_order.model_dump_json()),
 748              },
 749          )
 750      elif unpublished_note is not None:
 751          evidence = mark_unpublished(
 752              evidence, requirement_id=requirement_id, note=unpublished_note
 753          )
 754      elif nonexistent_note is not None:
 755          evidence = mark_nonexistent(
 756              evidence, requirement_id=requirement_id, note=nonexistent_note
 757          )
 758      else:
 759          evidence = answer_requirement(
 760              evidence,
 761              requirement_id=requirement_id,
 762              answer=answer or "",
 763              source_url=source_url,
 764          )
 765  
 766      verdict = assess_coverage(work_order, evidence)
 767      _record(
 768          services,
 769          run_id,
 770          RESEARCH_STAGE,
 771          {
 772              **research_stage_record(evidence, notes),
 773              "coverage": verdict.as_record(),
 774              # What the operator settled by hand, kept so a wrong fact in the
 775              # article can be traced to a person rather than blamed on the
 776              # research that never claimed it.
 777              "operator_settled": sorted(
 778                  {
 779                      *(_stage_data(run_id, RESEARCH_STAGE).get("operator_settled") or []),
 780                      requirement_id,
 781                  }
 782              ),
 783              STATE_KEY: json.loads(evidence.model_dump_json()),
 784          },
 785      )
 786      _resettle_selection(run_id, services, work_order, evidence, verdict)
 787      return verdict
 788  
 789  
 790  def reask_question(
 791      run_id: str,
 792      services: IntakeServices,
 793      *,
 794      requirement_id: str,
 795      question: str,
 796  ) -> CoverageVerdict:
 797      """Rewrite one research question and buy one search, not a whole pass.
 798  
 799      Run 76b36468 asked for a community-led project "in Buenos Aires" and got a
 800      garden collective in Argentina; the article is about Medellín, whose Buenos
 801      Aires is a neighbourhood. The answer came back `supported`, so nothing
 802      downstream would have caught it, and the only moves available were to drop
 803      a perfectly good question or research it by hand.
 804  
 805      One search, then one structuring call. The other questions keep the notes
 806      they already paid for -- which is the whole reason the notes are stored per
 807      requirement rather than as one blob.
 808  
 809      The structuring call is not free and is the longest single wait in a run.
 810      It is re-run rather than patched because deduplication and conflict
 811      detection are cross-question by construction: splicing one requirement's
 812      records into a finished dossier would leave the new answer unchecked
 813      against everything already in it.
 814      """
 815      if services.research is None:
 816          raise RuntimeError("Research dependencies are not configured.")
 817  
 818      enforce_run_budget(_run_tokens_spent(run_id), stage=NOTES_STAGE)
 819  
 820      brief = load_brief(run_id)
 821      work_order = load_work_order(run_id)
 822      evidence = load_evidence(run_id)
 823  
 824      evidence, work_order, note = reask_requirement(
 825          evidence, work_order, requirement_id=requirement_id, question=question
 826      )
 827  
 828      # The work order first: if the search or the structuring fails, the run is
 829      # left holding the rewritten question rather than the wording the operator
 830      # already rejected.
 831      _record(
 832          services,
 833          run_id,
 834          WORK_ORDER_STAGE,
 835          {
 836              **work_order_stage_record(
 837                  work_order,
 838                  [note],
 839                  tokens_spent=_run_tokens_spent(run_id),
 840                  target_word_count=default_target_word_count(),
 841              ),
 842              STATE_KEY: json.loads(work_order.model_dump_json()),
 843          },
 844      )
 845  
 846      requirement = next(
 847          item for item in work_order.requirements if item.requirement_id == requirement_id
 848      )
 849      notes = notes_from_record(_stage_data(run_id, NOTES_STAGE), work_order) or {}
 850      _open(services, run_id, NOTES_STAGE)
 851      notes = {
 852          **notes,
 853          requirement_id: gather_one_requirement(brief, requirement, services.research),
 854      }
 855      _record(services, run_id, NOTES_STAGE, notes_stage_record(work_order, notes))
 856  
 857      _open(services, run_id, RESEARCH_STAGE)
 858      try:
 859          evidence = structure_research(
 860              work_order, notes, services.research,
 861              kept_batches=_stage_data(run_id, BATCHES_STAGE).get("batches", {}),
 862              checkpoint=lambda batches: services.recorder.record_stage(run_id, BATCHES_STAGE, {"batches": batches}),
 863              before_call=lambda: enforce_run_budget(_run_tokens_spent(run_id), stage=RESEARCH_STAGE),
 864          )
 865      except ResearchUnusable as error:
 866          _record(
 867              services,
 868              run_id,
 869              RESEARCH_STAGE,
 870              {
 871                  "status": "failed",
 872                  "reason": error.reason,
 873                  "unusable_response": error.raw[:40000],
 874              },
 875          )
 876          raise
 877  
 878      verdict = assess_coverage(work_order, evidence)
 879      _record(
 880          services,
 881          run_id,
 882          RESEARCH_STAGE,
 883          {
 884              **research_stage_record(evidence, notes),
 885              "coverage": verdict.as_record(),
 886              # Every rewrite, in order. A question the article rests on that was
 887              # asked three ways before it answered is worth seeing later.
 888              "reasked": [
 889                  *(_stage_data(run_id, RESEARCH_STAGE).get("reasked") or []),
 890                  note,
 891              ],
 892              STATE_KEY: json.loads(evidence.model_dump_json()),
 893          },
 894      )
 895      _resettle_selection(run_id, services, work_order, evidence, verdict)
 896      return verdict
 897  
 898  
 899  def settle_premise(
 900      run_id: str,
 901      services: IntakeServices,
 902      *,
 903      assumption_id: str,
 904      note: str,
 905  ) -> CoverageVerdict:
 906      """Withdraw an assumption research refuted. The operator's call, recorded.
 907  
 908      No model call. A refuted premise is the one block with no exit: the error
 909      says more research will not clear it, which is true, and leaves the run
 910      permanently unwritable. Run b88081a0 hit it on an assumption bundling a
 911      confirmed park length, a motorway length nobody claimed, and an opinion the
 912      research itself called unconfirmable -- see #526.
 913  
 914      The note is required. Withdrawing an assumption is a claim about the world
 915      the operator is making instead of the research, and a wrong fact in the
 916      finished article has to be traceable to the person who allowed it.
 917      """
 918      if not _safe_str(note):
 919          raise ValueError(
 920              "Say why the assumption is being withdrawn. This is a decision "
 921              "about what is true, and it has to be attributable."
 922          )
 923  
 924      previous_order = load_work_order(run_id)
 925      evidence = load_evidence(run_id)
 926      notes = _stage_data(run_id, RESEARCH_STAGE).get("notes") or {}
 927  
 928      evidence, work_order = strike_assumption(
 929          evidence, previous_order, assumption_id=assumption_id
 930      )
 931      # Withdrawing an assumption does not unmake the facts that were found, so
 932      # the questions that declared it keep their searches. Their notes have to
 933      # be re-stamped against the new work order here, because striking removes
 934      # the assumption from every requirement that named it and so changes those
 935      # requirements' fingerprints. Without this, the notes are read back against
 936      # a plan they no longer match and are silently discarded -- the next
 937      # re-ask then restructures the dossier out of what is left, and questions
 938      # that were answered disappear from it.
 939      #
 940      # Measured on run e001d48c (2026-09-06): striking one assumption three
 941      # questions declared, then re-asking a fourth, cut the dossier from 66
 942      # claims over seven questions to 23 over four, threw away a search that had
 943      # just been bought, and put a run that had passed the gate back behind it.
 944      #
 945      # Read against the plan the notes were gathered under, written under the
 946      # plan that replaces it. `notes_from_record` still refuses notes whose
 947      # question or brief actually changed; this only says that an assumption a
 948      # person deliberately withdrew is not such a change.
 949      kept_notes = notes_from_record(_stage_data(run_id, NOTES_STAGE), previous_order)
 950      if kept_notes:
 951          services.recorder.record_stage(
 952              run_id, NOTES_STAGE, notes_stage_record(work_order, kept_notes)
 953          )
 954      _record(
 955          services,
 956          run_id,
 957          WORK_ORDER_STAGE,
 958          {
 959              **work_order_stage_record(
 960                  work_order,
 961                  [],
 962                  tokens_spent=_run_tokens_spent(run_id),
 963                  target_word_count=default_target_word_count(),
 964              ),
 965              STATE_KEY: json.loads(work_order.model_dump_json()),
 966          },
 967      )
 968  
 969      verdict = assess_coverage(work_order, evidence)
 970      _record(
 971          services,
 972          run_id,
 973          RESEARCH_STAGE,
 974          {
 975              **research_stage_record(evidence, notes),
 976              "coverage": verdict.as_record(),
 977              "struck_assumptions": sorted(
 978                  {
 979                      *(
 980                          _stage_data(run_id, RESEARCH_STAGE).get("struck_assumptions")
 981                          or []
 982                      ),
 983                      assumption_id,
 984                  }
 985              ),
 986              "struck_assumption_notes": {
 987                  **(
 988                      _stage_data(run_id, RESEARCH_STAGE).get("struck_assumption_notes")
 989                      or {}
 990                  ),
 991                  assumption_id: _safe_str(note),
 992              },
 993              # `research_stage_record` writes the summary, not the dossier.
 994              # Omitting this wipes the evidence `load_evidence` reads and costs
 995              # the run everything research paid for -- which is exactly what it
 996              # did to run b88081a0 before this line existed.
 997              STATE_KEY: json.loads(evidence.model_dump_json()),
 998          },
 999      )
1000      _resettle_selection(run_id, services, work_order, evidence, verdict)
1001      return verdict
1002  
1003  
1004  def review_venues(run_id: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
1005      """The places this run would send a reader, for a person to look at."""
1006      return venues_to_check(load_evidence(run_id))
1007  
1008  
1009  def settle_venue(
1010      run_id: str,
1011      services: IntakeServices,
1012      *,
1013      claim_id: str,
1014      drop: bool = False,
1015      dismiss: bool = False,
1016      note: str | None = None,
1017  ) -> CoverageVerdict:
1018      """Record what the operator saw when they looked at a place.
1019  
1020      No model call. Dropping one can put the run back behind the gate, when the
1021      dropped place was a question's only support -- which is correct: an article
1022      must not rest on a claim its operator looked at and rejected. The screen
1023      says so before the click, rather than after it.
1024  
1025      Dismissing costs nothing by design: it is the move for a place that should
1026      never have been on the list, and it leaves the dossier exactly as it was.
1027      """
1028      work_order = load_work_order(run_id)
1029      evidence = load_evidence(run_id)
1030      notes = _stage_data(run_id, RESEARCH_STAGE).get("notes") or {}
1031  
1032      if drop:
1033          evidence = drop_venue(evidence, claim_id=claim_id)
1034      elif dismiss:
1035          evidence = dismiss_venue(evidence, claim_id=claim_id)
1036      else:
1037          evidence = note_venue(evidence, claim_id=claim_id, note=note or "")
1038  
1039      verdict = assess_coverage(work_order, evidence)
1040      _record(
1041          services,
1042          run_id,
1043          RESEARCH_STAGE,
1044          {
1045              **research_stage_record(evidence, notes),
1046              "coverage": verdict.as_record(),
1047              "operator_settled": _stage_data(run_id, RESEARCH_STAGE).get(
1048                  "operator_settled"
1049              )
1050              or [],
1051              STATE_KEY: json.loads(evidence.model_dump_json()),
1052          },
1053      )
1054      _resettle_selection(run_id, services, work_order, evidence, verdict)
1055      return verdict
1056  
1057  
1058  def blocking_questions(run_id: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
1059      """The questions holding this run up, with what research did find.
1060  
1061      The screen needs the question itself, which lives on the work order, next
1062      to the gap, which lives on the evidence. Neither is much use alone.
1063      """
1064      work_order = load_work_order(run_id)
1065      evidence = load_evidence(run_id)
1066      brief = load_brief(run_id)
1067      verdict = assess_coverage(work_order, evidence)
1068      if verdict.can_write:
1069          return []
1070  
1071      questions = {
1072          item.requirement_id: item for item in work_order.requirements
1073      }
1074      found = {item.requirement_id: item for item in evidence.requirements}
1075      claims = {claim.claim_id: claim for claim in evidence.claims}
1076  
1077      blocking: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
1078      for requirement_id in verdict.unsupported_load_bearing:
1079          question = questions.get(requirement_id)
1080          record = found.get(requirement_id)
1081          blocking.append(
1082              {
1083                  "requirement_id": requirement_id,
1084                  "question": question.question if question else requirement_id,
1085                  "kind": question.kind if question else "load_bearing",
1086                  "status": record.status if record else "missing",
1087                  "gap": record.gap if record else "",
1088                  # Why research fell short, and what that implies. A run
1089                  # recorded before causes existed says nothing here, and the
1090                  # screen then shows what it always showed.
1091                  "cause": record.cause if record else "unknown",
1092                  "suggestion": suggested_move(
1093                      record.status if record else "missing",
1094                      record.cause if record else "unknown",
1095                  ),
1096                  # What it did find. A question is rarely a blank: run 76b36468
1097                  # was stopped holding a name, a URL and two founders, missing
1098                  # only a price nobody publishes.
1099                  "found": [
1100                      claims[claim_id].text
1101                      for claim_id in (record.claim_ids if record else [])
1102                      if claim_id in claims
1103                  ],
1104                  # A question that came back `nonexistent` may have a matching
1105                  # obligation on the brief. b29d66b4 proved a municipal ranking
1106                  # does not exist and then named it in the article anyway,
1107                  # because `must_name` still said to. The operator is the one
1108                  # who can say which line that is, so they are shown the list
1109                  # rather than a guess at it.
1110                  "must_name": (
1111                      list(brief.must_name)
1112                      if (record and record.status == "nonexistent")
1113                      else []
1114                  ),
1115              }
1116          )
1117      return blocking
1118  
1119  
1120  @dataclass(frozen=True)
1121  class WritingHandoff:
1122      """Everything the write boundary needs, read in one pass.
1123  
1124      The request and the selection travel together because they are only
1125      meaningful together: the request says what the article is and what was
1126      found, the selection says which of it belongs in this article, and the
1127      packet built from the pair is what the writer sees. Separating them is how
1128      a run ends up writing from a dossier nobody chose.
1129      """
1130  
1131      request: Prompt2BlogV4Request
1132      selection: Selection
1133  
1134  
1135  def writing_request(run_id: str, *, length_id: str = "medium") -> WritingHandoff:
1136      """Assemble what the graph runs from, out of what intake settled.
1137  
1138      Refuses if research said no. The gate is decided once, in one place; this
1139      is not a second opinion, it is the same one enforced at the hand-off.
1140  
1141      Refuses again if nothing has selected. Falling back to every fact was the
1142      old behaviour and it is the wrong failure: the case where the ranking model
1143      fell over looks exactly like the case where a person decided to keep
1144      everything, and only one of those should produce a hundred-fact article. A
1145      run whose selection is missing is a run for a person to look at.
1146      """
1147      brief = load_brief(run_id)
1148      work_order = load_work_order(run_id)
1149      evidence = load_evidence(run_id)
1150  
1151      verdict = assess_coverage(work_order, evidence)
1152      if not verdict.can_write:
1153          raise ValueError(
1154              f"This run cannot be written yet: {verdict.reason}. "
1155              + " ".join(verdict.findings)
1156          )
1157  
1158      selection = load_selection(run_id)
1159      if selection is None:
1160          raise ValueError(
1161              "No facts have been chosen for this run yet, so there is nothing "
1162              "to write from. Run selection again, or keep every fact "
1163              "deliberately."
1164          )
1165      # Belt and braces. The gate rebinds at every point it changes the dossier,
1166      # and if a path is ever added that does not, the cost of missing it should
1167      # be a fact carried across by id rather than a run that cannot be written.
1168      # The refusals that matter -- a different brief, a different work order,
1169      # nothing selected -- are unaffected, because rebinding by id cannot invent
1170      # a choice.
1171      selection, _changed = rebind(selection, brief, work_order, evidence)
1172  
1173      # The one place the editorial cut is applied (#534). Coverage is decided
1174      # above it, on the whole dossier, so a deselected claim can never turn a
1175      # supported question into a gate.
1176      return WritingHandoff(
1177          request=Prompt2BlogV4Request(
1178              brief=brief,
1179              work_order=work_order,
1180              evidence_package=apply_selection(evidence, selection),
1181              profiles=Prompt2BlogWritingProfiles(length_id=length_id),
1182          ),
1183          selection=selection,
1184      )
1185  
1186  
1187  # What the graph's stage names mean to somebody watching. The run row already
1188  # carries the current one; it was simply never shown, so a write looked dead
1189  # for twenty minutes and then a finished article sat unseen for twenty more.
1190  WRITING_STAGE_LABELS = {
1191      "queued": "Getting ready",
1192      "stage_v3_outline": "Planning the sections",
1193      "stage_v3_compose": "Writing the article",
1194      "stage_v3_groundedness": "Checking every claim against the research",
1195      "stage_v3_quality_audit": "Reading it back",
1196      "stage_v3_repair": "Fixing what the audit named",
1197      "stage_v3_quality_settle": "Settling on the best draft",
1198      "stage_v3_title": "Writing the headline",
1199      "stage_v3_finalize": "Finishing up",
1200      "complete": "Done",
1201  }
1202  
1203  # The same, for the stages the operator owns. A run begins at the seed
1204  # (ADR 0031), so a run that never reached the graph is an ordinary run and has
1205  # to be nameable in a list beside the ones that did.
1206  INTAKE_STAGE_LABELS = {
1207      "queued": "Getting ready",
1208      GRILL_STAGE: "In the grill",
1209      BRIEF_STAGE: "Brief written",
1210      WORK_ORDER_STAGE: "Research planned",
1211      NOTES_STAGE: "Searching the web",
1212      RESEARCH_STAGE: "Research done",
1213  }
1214  
1215  RUN_STAGE_LABELS = {**INTAKE_STAGE_LABELS, **WRITING_STAGE_LABELS}
1216  
1217  
1218  # The stages that mean the graph is running or has finished. Everything else on
1219  # a run row -- every `stage_v4_*` intake stage, and `queued` -- belongs to the
1220  # operator, not the writer.
1221  #
1222  # Derived from the topology rather than from the labels above, so a node added
1223  # to the graph cannot be left out of this by forgetting to label it. The
1224  # consequence of forgetting would be the page dropping back to the intake
1225  # screens in the middle of a write, which is the same class of bug this set
1226  # exists to fix.
1227  GRAPH_STAGES = frozenset(V3_NODE_STAGE_NAMES.values()) | {"complete"}
1228  
1229  
1230  def recent_runs(limit: int = 15) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
1231      """The runs this operator could go back to, newest first.
1232  
1233      The page tracked exactly one run, in `localStorage`. Lose that pointer or
1234      start a second article and every earlier run became unreachable from the
1235      interface, even though all of it was on the server -- on 2026-08-31 the
1236      only way back to a live run was a `?run=<uuid>` URL produced by querying
1237      the database by hand.
1238  
1239      Every long step invites the operator to leave the page. That is only safe
1240      if leaving does not depend on one browser's memory surviving.
1241  
1242      Runs that never reached an article are listed too. A run is created when
1243      the seed is typed (ADR 0031), so one that stopped in the grill is an
1244      ordinary run rather than a failure to hide.
1245  
1246      The seed comes from the grill row rather than the run row, which is one
1247      extra read per run. Bounded by `limit` and local, and a run without a
1248      recognisable name is a list nobody can use.
1249      """
1250      rows = get_all_runs(FEATURE_NAME)[:max(0, limit)]
1251      runs: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
1252      for row in rows:
1253          run_id = _safe_str(_safe_dict(row).get("run_id"))
1254          if not run_id:
1255              continue
1256          stage = _safe_str(row.get("stage"))
1257          grill = _stage_data(run_id, GRILL_STAGE)
1258          runs.append(
1259              {
1260                  "run_id": run_id,
1261                  "seed": _safe_str(grill.get("seed")),
1262                  "status": _safe_str(row.get("status")),
1263                  "stage": stage,
1264                  "stage_label": RUN_STAGE_LABELS.get(stage, stage),
1265                  "updated_at": _safe_str(row.get("updated_at")),
1266              }
1267          )
1268      return runs
1269  
1270  
1271  def writing_state(run_id: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
1272      """What the writer is doing, or what it produced.
1273  
1274      Everything here was already on the run and none of it was ever sent to the
1275      page. `stage` is the live one from the run row, so this answers "is it
1276      working" while the graph runs, and "what did it make" once it stops.
1277      """
1278      status = _safe_dict(read_status(run_id))
1279      if not status:
1280          return None
1281      state = _safe_str(status.get("state"))
1282      stage = _safe_str(status.get("stage"))
1283      # A run is only writing once the graph owns it, and the test has to be a
1284      # whitelist. Intake records its own stages on the same run row -- the run
1285      # is created at the seed (ADR 0031) -- so excluding only "queued" let
1286      # `stage_v4_grill` through, and run 76b36468 answered its first grill
1287      # question behind a screen saying the article was being written.
1288      if stage not in GRAPH_STAGES:
1289          return None
1290  
1291      finalize = _stage_data(run_id, "stage_v3_finalize")
1292      outline = _stage_data(run_id, "stage_v3_outline")
1293      return {
1294          "state": state,
1295          "stage": stage,
1296          "stage_label": WRITING_STAGE_LABELS.get(stage, stage),
1297          "error": _safe_str(status.get("error")) or None,
1298          "updated_at": _safe_str(status.get("updated_at")),
1299          "final_title": _safe_str(finalize.get("final_title")) or None,
1300          "word_count": finalize.get("word_count_estimate"),
1301          "pipeline_status": _safe_str(finalize.get("pipeline_status")) or None,
1302          "readiness_blockers": finalize.get("readiness_blockers") or [],
1303          "constraint_checks": _safe_dict(finalize.get("constraint_checks")),
1304          "outline_warning": (
1305              "The section plan was unusable. The writer structured this article "
1306              "from the Article Brief and selected evidence instead. Review its structure."
1307              if outline.get("accepted") is False else None
1308          ),
1309      }
1310  
1311  
1312  def finished_article(run_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
1313      """The article the run produced, for reading.
1314  
1315      Its own call rather than part of `intake_state`, because the state is
1316      polled every few seconds while the graph runs and the article payload is
1317      several hundred kilobytes. Fetched once, when there is something to read.
1318      """
1319      payload = _stage_data(run_id, "pipeline_v3")
1320      if not payload:
1321          raise LookupError(f"No article written for run {run_id}.")
1322      article = _safe_dict(payload.get("improved_article"))
1323      finalize = _stage_data(run_id, "stage_v4_finalize") or _stage_data(
1324          run_id, "stage_v3_finalize"
1325      )
1326      return {
1327          "run_id": run_id,
1328          "title": _safe_str(finalize.get("final_title")) or _safe_str(article.get("title")),
1329          # The editorial shape, in the words staging labels drafts with. Sent
1330          # so the finished article can be handed to the editor without the
1331          # operator retyping what the brief already settled.
1332          "form_label": _safe_str(_safe_dict(payload.get("form")).get("label")),
1333          "markdown": _safe_str(payload.get("final_markdown"))
1334          or _safe_str(article.get("content")),
1335          "pipeline_status": _safe_str(finalize.get("pipeline_status")) or None,
1336          "readiness_blockers": finalize.get("readiness_blockers") or [],
1337          # `needs_revision` alone cannot say whether repair looked and found
1338          # nothing or was never offered the chance. On run 95a74dce it was the
1339          # second: the budget was spent before the writing graph reached it.
1340          "repair_outcome": _safe_dict(
1341              _stage_data(run_id, "pipeline_v3").get("repair_outcome")
1342          ),
1343          "constraint_checks": _safe_dict(finalize.get("constraint_checks")),
1344          "word_count": finalize.get("word_count_estimate"),
1345      }
1346  
1347  
1348  def polish_prompt(run_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
1349      """The prompt the operator carries to a flagship model, with the article.
1350  
1351      Assembled from what the run already recorded about its own output. It is
1352      generated and never hand edited: operator influence belongs in a control
1353      with its own validated field, or nothing downstream can say what was
1354      actually asked for.
1355      """
1356      article = finished_article(run_id)
1357      quality = _stage_data(run_id, "stage_v3_quality_audit")
1358      audit_problems = [
1359          _safe_str(item)
1360          for item in (quality.get("required_revisions") or [])
1361          if _safe_str(item)
1362      ]
1363      return {
1364          "run_id": run_id,
1365          "prompt": build_polish_prompt(
1366              brief=load_brief(run_id),
1367              article_markdown=article["markdown"],
1368              title=article["title"],
1369              constraint_checks=article["constraint_checks"],
1370              readiness_blockers=article["readiness_blockers"],
1371              audit_problems=audit_problems,
1372          ),
1373      }
1374  
1375  
1376  def writers_evidence(run_id: str) -> EvidencePackage:
1377      """The dossier with the writer's own cut marked on it.
1378  
1379      The stored dossier is what research returned, and every claim on it is
1380      flagged selected: the cut is written into the request the graph runs from
1381      and never back into storage. Anything reading the stored rows therefore
1382      sees a hundred facts the writer supposedly had, which is how the punch list
1383      came to offer facts a person deliberately removed as ordinary omissions --
1384      the last editing aid arguing to refill the article the earlier stages had
1385      carefully reduced.
1386  
1387      The frozen packet is the honest source and not the current selection: it is
1388      what actually reached the writer, so a selection edited after the article
1389      was written cannot make this disagree with the piece it is describing. The
1390      selection is the fallback for a run written before packets were recorded,
1391      and the bare dossier the fallback for one with no selection at all.
1392      """
1393      evidence = load_evidence(run_id)
1394      receipt = _safe_dict(
1395          _stage_data(run_id, "pipeline_v3").get("packet_receipt")
1396      )
1397      reached = [
1398          _safe_str(item) for item in (receipt.get("claim_ids") or []) if _safe_str(item)
1399      ]
1400      if reached:
1401          chosen = set(reached)
1402          return evidence.model_copy(
1403              update={
1404                  "claims": [
1405                      claim.model_copy(update={"selected": claim.claim_id in chosen})
1406                      for claim in evidence.claims
1407                  ]
1408              }
1409          )
1410      if selection := load_selection(run_id):
1411          return apply_selection(evidence, selection)
1412      return evidence
1413  
1414  
1415  def punch_list(run_id: str, services: IntakeServices) -> dict[str, Any]:
1416      """What a person should fix by hand, computed once and kept.
1417  
1418      Read from the run after the first time, because it is a model call over a
1419      finished article and the answer cannot change: nothing downstream of
1420      `finalize` edits the piece. Re-deriving it on every page load would charge
1421      the run again for the same paragraph.
1422  
1423      Not a stage in the graph. The article is written, stamped and stored before
1424      this is asked for, so a failure here loses the notes and not the piece --
1425      which is the whole reason it is allowed to run at all (ADR 0030 keeps the
1426      one gate before writing, and nothing blocks after it).
1427      """
1428      stored = _stage_data(run_id, PUNCH_LIST_STAGE)
1429      if stored.get("items") is not None:
1430          return {"run_id": run_id, **{k: v for k, v in stored.items() if k != STATE_KEY}}
1431  
1432      article = finished_article(run_id)
1433      # Open before the call, like every other stage: usage is filed against
1434      # whichever stage is open when the model answers, and this one used to
1435      # bill to `unattributed` while its own row claimed it cost nothing.
1436      _open(services, run_id, PUNCH_LIST_STAGE)
1437      result = build_punch_list(
1438          brief=load_brief(run_id),
1439          title=article["title"],
1440          article_markdown=article["markdown"],
1441          evidence=writers_evidence(run_id),
1442          llm=services.dependencies.llm,
1443          model_name=services.dependencies.model_name,
1444      )
1445      _record(services, run_id, PUNCH_LIST_STAGE, result)
1446      return {"run_id": run_id, **result}
1447  
1448  
1449  def _research_view(run_id: str, research: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
1450      """The research row as the page needs it, findings included.
1451  
1452      Derived from the stored evidence when the row predates the findings field,
1453      rather than asking the operator to re-run a pass they already paid ten web
1454      searches for. The evidence itself has been on the run the whole time; only
1455      the summary written beside it was thinner.
1456      """
1457      view = {key: value for key, value in research.items() if key != STATE_KEY}
1458      if not view or view.get("findings"):
1459          return view
1460      stored = research.get(STATE_KEY)
1461      if not isinstance(stored, dict):
1462          return view
1463      try:
1464          evidence = EvidencePackage.model_validate(stored)
1465      except ValidationError:
1466          # An older dossier that no longer fits the contract still deserves to
1467          # show its statuses rather than an empty screen.
1468          return view
1469      view["findings"] = research_stage_record(evidence, {})["findings"]
1470      return view
1471  
1472  
1473  def intake_state(run_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
1474      """Where this run stands, for a page that may have been reloaded."""
1475      grill = _stage_data(run_id, GRILL_STAGE)
1476      brief = _stage_data(run_id, BRIEF_STAGE)
1477      work_order = _stage_data(run_id, WORK_ORDER_STAGE)
1478      research = _stage_data(run_id, RESEARCH_STAGE)
1479      grill_state = _safe_dict(grill.get(STATE_KEY))
1480      # A failed brief leaves a row saying so. It is evidence, not progress, so
1481      # the page stays on the grill with the agreement intact and one more
1482      # approve to try.
1483      if _safe_str(brief.get("status")) == "failed":
1484          brief = {}
1485      if _safe_str(work_order.get("status")) == "failed":
1486          work_order = {}
1487      if _safe_str(research.get("status")) == "failed":
1488          research = {}
1489      return {
1490          "run_id": run_id,
1491          "step": (
1492              "research"
1493              if research
1494              else "work_order"
1495              if work_order
1496              else "brief"
1497              if brief
1498              else "grill"
1499              if grill
1500              else "seed"
1501          ),
1502          "grill": {
1503              "status": _safe_str(grill_state.get("status")),
1504              "seed": _safe_str(grill_state.get("seed")),
1505              "turns": grill.get("transcript") or [],
1506              "pending": grill.get("pending"),
1507              "consensus": _safe_str(grill_state.get("consensus")),
1508              # What the brief still needs. The grill stops when this is empty
1509              # (ADR 0033), so it is also the honest answer to "how far along am
1510              # I" -- which a question count never was.
1511              "markers_covered": grill.get("markers_covered") or [],
1512              "markers_missing": grill.get("markers_missing") or [],
1513          }
1514          if grill
1515          else None,
1516          "brief": {key: value for key, value in brief.items() if key != STATE_KEY} or None,
1517          "work_order": {
1518              key: value for key, value in work_order.items() if key != STATE_KEY
1519          }
1520          or None,
1521          "research": _research_view(run_id, research) or None,
1522          # Written as the searches go, so five to ten silent minutes can say
1523          # which question it is on.
1524          "research_progress": _stage_data(run_id, PROGRESS_STAGE) or None,
1525          "writing": writing_state(run_id),
1526      }
apps/backend/app/features/prompt2blog/research_v4.py
   1  """Research, in two passes.
   2  
   3  The rigour here is the best thing in the pipeline and none of it changes:
   4  first-party sources, dated, conflicts surfaced, confidence recorded. What
   5  changes is what we send it looking for, and where it runs.
   6  
   7  **Gather** gets the facts, on the one path in this app that reaches the web.
   8  **Structure** turns them into the evidence records the writing stages read,
   9  with the shape enforced at the transport rather than requested politely.
  10  
  11  Two passes rather than one because they want different things. Gathering wants
  12  a model that can search and will write freely about what it found. Structuring
  13  wants a model that will return exactly the shape asked for and invent nothing —
  14  and asking one model to do both is how a dossier ends up shaped like its own
  15  retrieval log.
  16  
  17  Search stays off Claude on purpose. Its WebSearch denial is a deliberate
  18  security boundary, and research is the most token-hungry step there is:
  19  spending Claude's budget reading web pages risks running out during the
  20  writing, which is the part that actually needs it.
  21  """
  22  
  23  from __future__ import annotations
  24  
  25  import json
  26  import hashlib
  27  import copy
  28  import logging
  29  from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, wait, FIRST_COMPLETED
  30  from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  31  import re
  32  from datetime import date
  33  from typing import Any, Callable, get_args
  34  
  35  from pydantic import ValidationError
  36  
  37  from .contracts_v4 import (
  38      ArticleBrief,
  39      EvidenceConfidence,
  40      EvidenceMaterialType,
  41      PremiseVerdict,
  42      EvidenceRequirementStatus,
  43      EvidenceShortfallCause,
  44      EvidenceSourceType,
  45      EvidencePackage,
  46      Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
  47      WorkOrderRequirement,
  48  )
  49  from .config import P2B_V4_GATHER_CONCURRENCY
  50  from .research_readiness_v3 import PREMISE_CHECK_RULES
  51  from .evidence_conflicts import record_detected_conflicts
  52  from .schema_guards import require_non_empty
  53  from .support import _safe_dict, _safe_str
  54  
  55  logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  56  
  57  RESEARCH_STAGE = "stage_v4_research"
  58  
  59  
  60  class ResearchUnusable(RuntimeError):
  61      """The dossier came back in a shape that cannot be used.
  62  
  63      Research is the most expensive step in intake and the last one before
  64      writing, so a failure here has to leave the payload behind to read. It
  65      previously raised a bare Pydantic error from inside `model_validate` and
  66      wrote no stage row at all.
  67      """
  68  
  69      def __init__(self, reason: str, raw: str) -> None:
  70          super().__init__(reason)
  71          self.reason = reason
  72          self.raw = raw
  73  
  74  
  75  # The contract forbids extra keys, so a leftover alias -- `questions` sitting
  76  # beside the `requirements` it was read into -- is fatal on its own. The reader
  77  # emits exactly what each record declares and nothing else.
  78  EVIDENCE_SOURCE_FIELDS = frozenset(
  79      {"source_id", "title", "publisher", "url", "published_at", "retrieved_at",
  80       "source_type", "material_type", "notes"}
  81  )
  82  EVIDENCE_CLAIM_FIELDS = frozenset(
  83      {
  84          "claim_id",
  85          "text",
  86          "source_ids",
  87          "requirement_ids",
  88          "as_of",
  89          "confidence",
  90          "venue",
  91          "venue_note",
  92          # Operator-set, like `venue_note`. It survives a re-parse of stored
  93          # evidence, so a place already cleared off the list stays cleared.
  94          "venue_dismissed",
  95      }
  96  )
  97  EVIDENCE_REQUIREMENT_FIELDS = frozenset(
  98      {"requirement_id", "status", "claim_ids", "gap", "cause"}
  99  )
 100  EVIDENCE_FINDING_FIELDS = frozenset({"assumption_id", "verdict", "basis", "claim_ids"})
 101  EVIDENCE_CONFLICT_FIELDS = frozenset({"conflict_id", "claim_ids", "summary", "resolution"})
 102  EVIDENCE_GAP_FIELDS = frozenset({"gap_id", "requirement_ids", "summary"})
 103  
 104  
 105  def _only(record: dict[str, Any], fields: frozenset[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
 106      return {key: value for key, value in record.items() if key in fields}
 107  
 108  
 109  def _as_date(value: Any) -> str:
 110      """A plain date, from whatever the model called a date.
 111  
 112      `published_at`, `retrieved_at` and `as_of` are dates, and a model that
 113      writes a full ISO timestamp is refused by the contract: "Datetimes
 114      provided to dates should have zero time". That took down a dossier that
 115      cost ten web searches, over the time of day on one source out of thirteen.
 116  
 117      The date part is the fact. Anything unparseable becomes empty and is
 118      handled by whatever the field's own rule is.
 119      """
 120      text = _safe_str(value)
 121      if not text:
 122          return ""
 123      head = text.replace("/", "-").split("T")[0].split(" ")[0].strip()
 124      try:
 125          return date.fromisoformat(head).isoformat()
 126      except ValueError:
 127          return ""
 128  
 129  
 130  def _web_or_other(material_type: str, url: str, publisher: str) -> str:
 131      """Demote a web/report source that cannot meet the rule for being one."""
 132      if material_type in {"web", "report"} and not (url and publisher):
 133          return "other"
 134      return material_type
 135  
 136  
 137  def _one_of(value: Any, vocabulary: Any, fallback: str) -> str:
 138      """Keep the value when it is one the contract knows, else fall back.
 139  
 140      A closed vocabulary the model is never shown is a vocabulary it will
 141      invent. Falling back is honest -- "other" says we could not classify it --
 142      and it is a great deal better than discarding a dossier that cost ten web
 143      searches over a label.
 144      """
 145      text = _safe_str(value)
 146      return text if text in set(get_args(vocabulary)) else fallback
 147  
 148  
 149  def _first(record: dict[str, Any], *names: str) -> Any:
 150      for name in names:
 151          if name in record and record[name] not in (None, "", []):
 152              return record[name]
 153      return None
 154  
 155  
 156  def _id_list(record: dict[str, Any], *names: str) -> list[str]:
 157      value = _first(record, *names)
 158      if not isinstance(value, list):
 159          return []
 160      return [_safe_str(item) for item in value if _safe_str(item)]
 161  
 162  
 163  def _rows(payload: dict[str, Any], *names: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
 164      value = _first(payload, *names)
 165      return [_safe_dict(item) for item in value] if isinstance(value, list) else []
 166  
 167  
 168  def _source_id_for(row: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
 169      """A stable id for a source the model described but never named.
 170  
 171      Derived from what it did give -- publisher, then title -- so the same
 172      publisher cited by six claims becomes one source rather than six.
 173      """
 174      label = _safe_str(_first(row, "publisher", "site", "title", "name"))
 175      if not label:
 176          return ""
 177      slug = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "_", label.casefold()).strip("_")
 178      return f"s_{slug}"[:60] if slug else ""
 179  
 180  
 181  def _sources_inside_claims(
 182      payload: dict[str, Any],
 183  ) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, list[str]]]:
 184      """Sources the model nested inside each claim instead of listing at the top.
 185  
 186      Run 849ae5aa (2026-09-01) returned thirteen claims, each carrying its
 187      sources as objects -- publisher, source_type, material_type -- and no
 188      top-level `sources` array at all. Every claim therefore cited nothing the
 189      parser could resolve, all thirteen were dropped as unusable, and twelve
 190      answered questions arrived at the gate reading "its supporting claims could
 191      not be used". The dossier was complete. It was shaped differently.
 192  
 193      So the sources are lifted out and given ids, and each claim is handed the
 194      ids of its own. Same principle as every other repair here: a schema exists
 195      so the model knows what to send, not so the parser can reject what arrived.
 196      """
 197      harvested: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
 198      by_claim: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
 199      for row in _rows(payload, "claims"):
 200          claim_id = _safe_str(_first(row, "claim_id", "id"))
 201          if not claim_id:
 202              continue
 203          for entry in _first(row, "sources", "source_ids") or []:
 204              if not isinstance(entry, dict):
 205                  continue
 206              record = _safe_dict(entry)
 207              source_id = _safe_str(_first(record, "source_id", "id")) or _source_id_for(
 208                  record
 209              )
 210              if not source_id:
 211                  continue
 212              harvested.setdefault(
 213                  source_id,
 214                  {
 215                      **record,
 216                      "source_id": source_id,
 217                      "title": _safe_str(_first(record, "title", "name"))
 218                      or _safe_str(_first(record, "publisher", "site"))
 219                      or source_id,
 220                  },
 221              )
 222              ids = by_claim.setdefault(claim_id, [])
 223              if source_id not in ids:
 224                  ids.append(source_id)
 225      return list(harvested.values()), by_claim
 226  
 227  
 228  def _normalised_evidence(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
 229      """Take the dossier the model sent, whatever it named things.
 230  
 231      Three jobs, all of them repairs the contract would otherwise refuse over.
 232  
 233      **Names.** The structure prompt says "question" throughout and the schema
 234      says `requirements`; the same model renamed exactly that list in the work
 235      order an hour earlier. Aliases are read rather than rejected.
 236  
 237      **Dangling references.** A claim citing a source that is not in the list is
 238      dropped from that claim, not fatal to the dossier.
 239  
 240      **The two-way mapping.** The contract requires the claim-to-question links
 241      and the question-to-claim links to agree exactly. That is a consistency
 242      property, not information: a model that says a claim answers q3, while q3
 243      forgets to list it, has told us the same fact once. Both directions are
 244      unioned and written back consistently, so the contract is satisfied by
 245      construction and keeps its guarantee.
 246      """
 247      embedded, embedded_by_claim = _sources_inside_claims(payload)
 248      sources: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
 249      seen_sources: set[str] = set()
 250      # Declared first, so a top-level entry wins over one lifted out of a claim.
 251      for row in [*_rows(payload, "sources"), *embedded]:
 252          source_id = _safe_str(_first(row, "source_id", "id"))
 253          if not source_id or source_id in seen_sources:
 254              continue
 255          seen_sources.add(source_id)
 256          sources.append(
 257              {
 258                  **_only(row, EVIDENCE_SOURCE_FIELDS),
 259                  "source_id": source_id,
 260                  "title": _safe_str(_first(row, "title", "name")) or source_id,
 261                  # Today when the model gave nothing, which is not a guess:
 262                  # these pages were read during this run. Run 849ae5aa
 263                  # (2026-09-01) came back with eleven sources and not one
 264                  # retrieval date, and the whole dossier was refused over a
 265                  # field the parser was in a position to know.
 266                  "retrieved_at": _as_date(
 267                      _first(row, "retrieved_at", "retrieved", "accessed_at")
 268                  )
 269                  or date.today().isoformat(),
 270                  "published_at": _as_date(_first(row, "published_at", "published"))
 271                  or None,
 272                  # Both vocabularies carry an "other" member, which is what
 273                  # makes an invented value survivable. Every source in run
 274                  # 90b3f9bc came back as `research_notes` /
 275                  # `synthesized_research_note` -- one invented vocabulary,
 276                  # applied consistently, because the schema declared plain
 277                  # strings and the prompt listed no values.
 278                  "url": _safe_str(row.get("url")) or None,
 279                  "source_type": _one_of(
 280                      _first(row, "source_type", "type"), EvidenceSourceType, "other"
 281                  ),
 282                  # A source calling itself a web page without a link is not one
 283                  # the contract will accept, and the grounded search path cannot
 284                  # supply per-source URLs -- it returns a dozen opaque redirect
 285                  # blobs per question, which nothing can honestly map onto "How
 286                  # to Peru". Forty-nine of fifty-four sources in run 90b3f9bc
 287                  # came back with a publisher, a title and no URL, and the whole
 288                  # dossier was refused.
 289                  #
 290                  # `other` carries no URL requirement, so a source without one
 291                  # is admitted as what it actually is. The guarantee survives
 292                  # intact: anything still labelled `web` really does have a link.
 293                  "material_type": _web_or_other(
 294                      _one_of(
 295                          _first(row, "material_type", "material"),
 296                          EvidenceMaterialType,
 297                          "other",
 298                      ),
 299                      _safe_str(row.get("url")),
 300                      _safe_str(_first(row, "publisher", "site")),
 301                  ),
 302                  # The contract wants every source to carry a note, and the
 303                  # same run returned eleven sources with none. Said plainly
 304                  # rather than invented: a sentence about what the record does
 305                  # not contain is honest, and a sentence about the world would
 306                  # not be.
 307                  "notes": _id_list(row, "notes")
 308                  or ["No note recorded for this source."],
 309              }
 310          )
 311  
 312      requirements: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
 313      seen_requirements: set[str] = set()
 314      for row in _rows(payload, "requirements", "questions"):
 315          requirement_id = _safe_str(_first(row, "requirement_id", "id", "question_id"))
 316          if not requirement_id or requirement_id in seen_requirements:
 317              continue
 318          seen_requirements.add(requirement_id)
 319          status = _one_of(row.get("status"), EvidenceRequirementStatus, "partial")
 320          gap = _safe_str(row.get("gap"))
 321          requirements.append(
 322              {
 323                  **_only(row, EVIDENCE_REQUIREMENT_FIELDS),
 324                  "requirement_id": requirement_id,
 325                  "status": status,
 326                  # Read under its aliases here, because the union below reads
 327                  # this dict and not the raw row -- and the field allowlist has
 328                  # already stripped whatever the model called it. Run 849ae5aa
 329                  # said `claims`, so every question arrived linked to nothing,
 330                  # every claim was dropped for answering nothing, and a complete
 331                  # dossier reached the gate with twelve empty questions.
 332                  "claim_ids": _id_list(row, "claim_ids", "claims"),
 333                  # A cause we cannot read is `unknown`, which the gate treats as
 334                  # "no suggestion" rather than as a wrong one.
 335                  "cause": _one_of(
 336                      _first(row, "cause", "shortfall_cause", "reason"),
 337                      EvidenceShortfallCause,
 338                      "unknown",
 339                  ),
 340                  # The contract insists an unsettled question describes its gap,
 341                  # and a status we had to guess at has one by definition.
 342                  "gap": ""
 343                  if status == "supported"
 344                  else gap or "The dossier did not say what is missing here.",
 345              }
 346          )
 347  
 348      claims: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
 349      seen_claims: set[str] = set()
 350      # What each claim asked for, kept aside because both lists below are
 351      # filtered here and `requirement_ids` is rewritten again by the union.
 352      # Without this a dropped claim can only be counted, never explained.
 353      cited: dict[str, tuple[list[str], list[str]]] = {}
 354      for row in _rows(payload, "claims"):
 355          claim_id = _safe_str(_first(row, "claim_id", "id"))
 356          text = _safe_str(_first(row, "text", "statement", "claim"))
 357          if not claim_id or not text or claim_id in seen_claims:
 358              continue
 359          seen_claims.add(claim_id)
 360          cited[claim_id] = (
 361              _id_list(row, "source_ids", "sources"),
 362              _id_list(row, "requirement_ids", "question_ids", "questions"),
 363          )
 364          claims.append(
 365              {
 366                  **_only(row, EVIDENCE_CLAIM_FIELDS),
 367                  "claim_id": claim_id,
 368                  "text": text,
 369                  # Declared ids first, and the ones minted from this claim's
 370                  # own nested sources when none of the declared ones resolve --
 371                  # a claim citing "s1" against a dossier that never listed a
 372                  # top-level source has told us nothing, while the objects
 373                  # hanging off it name a real publisher.
 374                  "source_ids": [
 375                      item
 376                      for item in _id_list(row, "source_ids", "sources")
 377                      if item in seen_sources
 378                  ]
 379                  or [
 380                      item
 381                      for item in embedded_by_claim.get(claim_id, [])
 382                      if item in seen_sources
 383                  ],
 384                  "requirement_ids": [
 385                      item
 386                      for item in _id_list(
 387                          row, "requirement_ids", "question_ids", "questions"
 388                      )
 389                      if item in seen_requirements
 390                  ],
 391                  "confidence": _one_of(row.get("confidence"), EvidenceConfidence, "low"),
 392                  "as_of": _as_date(row.get("as_of")) or None,
 393              }
 394          )
 395  
 396      # Union both directions, then write both sides from the union.
 397      links: dict[str, set[str]] = {rid: set() for rid in seen_requirements}
 398      for claim in claims:
 399          for requirement_id in claim["requirement_ids"]:
 400              links[requirement_id].add(claim["claim_id"])
 401      for row in requirements:
 402          for claim_id in _id_list(row, "claim_ids", "claims"):
 403              if claim_id in seen_claims:
 404                  links[row["requirement_id"]].add(claim_id)
 405      for claim in claims:
 406          claim["requirement_ids"] = sorted(
 407              rid for rid, ids in links.items() if claim["claim_id"] in ids
 408          )
 409  
 410      # Filtering a dangling reference can empty a list the contract requires to
 411      # hold at least one entry, so the repair would itself become the failure.
 412      # A claim citing no surviving source, or answering no surviving question,
 413      # is unusable to every stage downstream: drop the claim, not the dossier.
 414      kept = [
 415          claim
 416          for claim in claims
 417          if claim["source_ids"] and claim["requirement_ids"]
 418      ]
 419      if len(kept) != len(claims):
 420          # Name what was lost. A count alone cannot tell a claim that cited a
 421          # source the model never declared from one that answered a question in
 422          # another batch, and those want opposite fixes. The dropped claim is
 423          # gone from every stored artefact by the time anyone looks.
 424          for claim in claims:
 425              if claim["source_ids"] and claim["requirement_ids"]:
 426                  continue
 427              claim_sources, claim_requirements = cited.get(claim["claim_id"], ([], []))
 428              logger.warning(
 429                  "Dropped claim %s: cited sources %s, kept %s; "
 430                  "cited questions %s, kept %s",
 431                  claim["claim_id"],
 432                  sorted(claim_sources) or "none",
 433                  sorted(claim["source_ids"]) or "none",
 434                  sorted(claim_requirements) or "none",
 435                  sorted(claim["requirement_ids"]) or "none",
 436              )
 437          logger.warning(
 438              "Dropped %s claim(s) with no usable source or question",
 439              len(claims) - len(kept),
 440          )
 441          claims = kept
 442          # Everything downstream filters against this set, so it has to shrink
 443          # with the claims -- a premise finding still pointing at a dropped
 444          # claim fails the contract exactly as a dangling reference would.
 445          seen_claims = {claim["claim_id"] for claim in claims}
 446          for requirement_id in links:
 447              links[requirement_id] &= seen_claims
 448  
 449      for row in requirements:
 450          row["claim_ids"] = sorted(links[row["requirement_id"]])
 451          # A question whose every claim was dropped is no longer supported by
 452          # anything, and the contract refuses that pairing outright.
 453          if row["status"] == "supported" and not row["claim_ids"]:
 454              row["status"] = "partial"
 455              row["gap"] = row.get("gap") or "Its supporting claims could not be used."
 456  
 457      findings = []
 458      seen_findings: set[str] = set()
 459      for row in _rows(payload, "premise_findings", "premises", "premise"):
 460          assumption_id = _safe_str(_first(row, "assumption_id", "id"))
 461          if not assumption_id or assumption_id in seen_findings:
 462              continue
 463          seen_findings.add(assumption_id)
 464          findings.append(
 465              {
 466                  **_only(row, EVIDENCE_FINDING_FIELDS),
 467                  "assumption_id": assumption_id,
 468                  "verdict": _one_of(row.get("verdict"), PremiseVerdict, "unverified"),
 469                  "claim_ids": [
 470                      item for item in _id_list(row, "claim_ids", "claims")
 471                      if item in seen_claims
 472                  ],
 473              }
 474          )
 475  
 476      conflicts = []
 477      seen_conflicts: set[str] = set()
 478      for row in _rows(payload, "conflicts"):
 479          conflict_id = _safe_str(_first(row, "conflict_id", "id"))
 480          ids = [c for c in dict.fromkeys(_id_list(row, "claim_ids", "claims")) if c in seen_claims]
 481          # Two claims are what makes a conflict a conflict, and eleven of them
 482          # arrived with none that matched a real claim. A conflict nothing can
 483          # point at is unusable to every stage downstream; dropping it costs a
 484          # note, where refusing it costs ten web searches.
 485          if not conflict_id or conflict_id in seen_conflicts or len(ids) < 2:
 486              continue
 487          seen_conflicts.add(conflict_id)
 488          conflicts.append(
 489              {
 490                  **_only(row, EVIDENCE_CONFLICT_FIELDS),
 491                  "conflict_id": conflict_id,
 492                  "claim_ids": ids,
 493              }
 494          )
 495  
 496      gaps = []
 497      seen_gaps: set[str] = set()
 498      for row in _rows(payload, "gaps"):
 499          gap_id = _safe_str(_first(row, "gap_id", "id"))
 500          ids = [
 501              r for r in dict.fromkeys(_id_list(row, "requirement_ids", "requirements"))
 502              if r in seen_requirements
 503          ]
 504          if not gap_id or gap_id in seen_gaps or not ids:
 505              continue
 506          seen_gaps.add(gap_id)
 507          gaps.append(
 508              {
 509                  **_only(row, EVIDENCE_GAP_FIELDS),
 510                  "gap_id": gap_id,
 511                  "requirement_ids": ids,
 512              }
 513          )
 514  
 515      return {
 516          "sources": sources,
 517          "claims": claims,
 518          "requirements": requirements,
 519          "premise_findings": findings,
 520          "conflicts": conflicts,
 521          "gaps": gaps,
 522      }

 525  # The Lima dossier was 12,000 characters. The helper's own default is 1024,
 526  # which truncates without saying so.
 527  GATHER_MAX_TOKENS = 8_192
 528  STRUCTURE_MAX_TOKENS = 16_384
 529  
 530  # A few questions' worth. Ignored on the Claude CLI, which takes no output
 531  # cap, and honoured on Gemini.
 532  ONE_QUESTION_MAX_TOKENS = 8_192
 533  
 534  # How many questions go into one structuring call.
 535  #
 536  # The whole dossier in one call stopped converging: a schema failure anywhere
 537  # in one large object throws all of it away and it is silently regenerated,
 538  # and on 2026-09-02 three attempts died at 600s, 600s and 1200s.
 539  #
 540  # One question per call fixed that and cost four times as much. Measured on
 541  # run 86cfad32: twelve calls, 345,315 input tokens against 86,892 for the
 542  # single call it replaced. Every CLI call carries about 28,000 tokens of the
 543  # tool's own prefix -- 18,132 of it showed up as cached from the second call
 544  # onwards -- and that overhead is per call, not per question. Twelve calls pay
 545  # it twelve times.
 546  #
 547  # Four is the middle: three calls on an eleven question plan rather than
 548  # twelve, each object small enough to come back first time, and a failure
 549  # costs a third of the questions instead of all of them.
 550  STRUCTURE_BATCH_SIZE = 4
