 554  EVIDENCE_SCHEMA = require_non_empty({
 555      "type": "object",
 556      "properties": {
 557          "sources": {
 558              "type": "array",
 559              "items": {
 560                  "type": "object",
 561                  "properties": {
 562                      "source_id": {"type": "string"},
 563                      "title": {"type": "string"},
 564                      "publisher": {"type": "string"},
 565                      "url": {"type": "string"},
 566                      "published_at": {"type": "string"},
 567                      "retrieved_at": {"type": "string"},
 568                      "source_type": {
 569                          "type": "string",
 570                          "enum": list(get_args(EvidenceSourceType)),
 571                      },
 572                      "material_type": {
 573                          "type": "string",
 574                          "enum": list(get_args(EvidenceMaterialType)),
 575                      },
 576                      "notes": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
 577                  },
 578                  "required": ["source_id", "title", "retrieved_at", "source_type", "material_type", "notes"],
 579              },
 580          },
 581          "claims": {
 582              "type": "array",
 583              "items": {
 584                  "type": "object",
 585                  "properties": {
 586                      "claim_id": {"type": "string"},
 587                      "text": {"type": "string"},
 588                      "source_ids": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
 589                      "requirement_ids": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
 590                      "as_of": {"type": "string"},
 591                      "confidence": {
 592                          "type": "string",
 593                          "enum": list(get_args(EvidenceConfidence)),
 594                      },
 595                      "venue": {"type": "string"},
 596                  },
 597                  "required": ["claim_id", "text", "source_ids", "requirement_ids", "confidence"],
 598              },
 599          },
 600          "requirements": {
 601              "type": "array",
 602              "items": {
 603                  "type": "object",
 604                  "properties": {
 605                      "requirement_id": {"type": "string"},
 606                      "status": {
 607                          "type": "string",
 608                          "enum": list(get_args(EvidenceRequirementStatus)),
 609                      },

 620          # Declared with their fields, because an array of unspecified objects
 621          # is an array nothing fills. Every stored run -- 062c0b86, 90b3f9bc,

 623          # conflicts and gaps all empty, on prompts that asked for each of them
 624          # in as many words. The model was not ignoring the instruction; the

 695  
 696  def _fingerprint(value: Any) -> str:
 697      return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()
 698  
 699  
 700  def requirement_fingerprint(work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder, requirement: WorkOrderRequirement) -> str:
 701      """What this question was asked under, so a changed context cannot reuse it.
 702  
 703      Only the assumptions this question actually rests on. Fingerprinting the
 704      whole premise meant withdrawing one misread assumption threw away every
 705      saved search in the run, including searches for questions that never
 706      depended on it -- run b88081a0 lost eighteen. An assumption a question does
 707      not declare cannot have changed what its answer means.
 708      """
 709      depends_on = set(requirement.assumption_ids)
 710      return _fingerprint({
 711          "brief": work_order.brief_fingerprint,
 712          "subject": work_order.primary_subject,
 713          "scope": work_order.scope.model_dump(mode="json"),
 714          "premise": [
 715              item.model_dump(mode="json")
 716              for item in work_order.premise
 717              if item.assumption_id in depends_on
 718          ],
 719          "requirement": requirement.model_dump(mode="json", exclude={"search_group"}),
 720      })
 721  
 722  
 723  def notes_stage_record(
 724      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
 725      notes: dict[str, GatheredNotes],
 726  ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 727      """The raw gather, kept so a failure downstream is not re-bought.
 728  
 729      Persist after each completed search. Per-question fingerprints include
 730      brief, scope, and premise so cuts retain unrelated work while a changed
 731      question or changed editorial context cannot reuse stale answers.
 732      """
 733      return {
 734          "work_order_fingerprint": work_order.work_order_fingerprint,
 735          "requirement_fingerprints": {item.requirement_id: requirement_fingerprint(work_order, item) for item in work_order.requirements if item.requirement_id in notes},
 736          "notes": {
 737              requirement_id: {
 738                  "text": item.text,
 739                  "source_urls": list(item.source_urls),
 740                  "tokens": item.tokens,
 741              }
 742              for requirement_id, item in notes.items()
 743          },
 744      }
 745  
 746  
 747  def notes_from_record(
 748      record: dict[str, Any],
 749      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
 750  ) -> dict[str, GatheredNotes] | None:
 751      """The kept notes, when they answer this exact plan. Otherwise nothing."""
 752      fingerprints = record.get("requirement_fingerprints", {})
 753      if not fingerprints and record.get("work_order_fingerprint") != work_order.work_order_fingerprint:
 754          return None
 755      stored = record.get("notes")
 756      if not isinstance(stored, dict) or not stored:
 757          return None
 758      notes: dict[str, GatheredNotes] = {}
 759      for requirement in work_order.requirements:
 760          requirement_id = requirement.requirement_id
 761          if requirement_id not in stored:
 762              continue
 763          if fingerprints and fingerprints.get(requirement_id) != requirement_fingerprint(work_order, requirement):
 764              continue
 765          raw = stored[requirement_id]
 766          item = _safe_dict(raw)
 767          notes[_safe_str(requirement_id)] = GatheredNotes(
 768              text=_safe_str(item.get("text")),
 769              source_urls=[_safe_str(url) for url in (item.get("source_urls") or [])],
 770              tokens=item.get("tokens") if isinstance(item.get("tokens"), int) else None,
 771          )
 772      return notes
 773  
 774  
 775  def _precision_brief(precision: str) -> str:
 776      """What the article needs, and what that does not license.
 777  
 778      A loosened target says how exact the ARTICLE must be. It never says how
 779      freely the model may estimate. "Under 55 minutes for the full line, five
 780      intermediate stops, so allow about half an hour" is built from published
 781      numbers and shows its working. "About 25 minutes" is arithmetic printed as
 782      fact, and a reader cannot tell it from the S/3.20 fare beside it.
 783      """
 784      if precision == "approximate":
 785          return (
 786              "A range or an order of magnitude is what the article needs. If "
 787              "nobody publishes the precise figure, say so, then give the "
 788              "bounded answer and show the published numbers you bounded it "
 789              "with -- that is a complete answer, not a partial one.\n"
 790              "This is not permission to estimate. Never derive a number and "
 791              "state it as a found fact. A figure with its working shown is an "
 792              "answer; a figure you calculated and presented bare is a "
 793              "fabrication a reader cannot tell from a real one."
 794          )
 795      return (
 796          "The article needs the actual figure, because a reader acts on it. If "
 797          "nobody publishes it, say so plainly and say where you looked, rather "
 798          "than approximating it."
 799      )
 800  
 801  
 802  def build_gather_prompt(
 803      brief: ArticleBrief,
 804      requirement: WorkOrderRequirement,
 805  ) -> str:
 806      """Ask for one question's answer, and everything around it.
 807  
 808      Deliberately asks for more than the question. "Guided circuits six days a
 809      week" and "a pre-Inca pyramid you can stand on at night" came from the same
 810      source, and only the first survived -- a research pass that answers the
 811      question and nothing else produces a dossier that is correct and unusable.
 812      """
 813      return f"""Research one question for a travel article about {brief.location}.
 814  
 815  EVERYTHING BELOW IS IN {brief.location}. If a place named in the question also
 816  exists somewhere else in the world, it is the one in {brief.location} that is
 817  meant. Answering about the other one is worse than not answering: it comes back
 818  looking like a found fact and nothing downstream can tell.
 819  
 820  THE QUESTION
 821  {requirement.question}
 822  
 823  HOW EXACT THE ARTICLE NEEDS THIS
 824  {_precision_brief(requirement.precision)}
 825  
 826  Answer it as fully as you can, with sources. Then keep going:
 827  
 828  - Give the specifics. Prices with their currency and the date they were true.
 829    Opening hours with the days. Names of places, dishes, streets, people.
 830  - Say who published each thing you found, and when. Prefer official and
 831    first-party sources for anything that changes.
 832  - Where sources disagree, say so and say which you would believe. Never average
 833    them into a number nobody published.
 834  - If nobody has published an answer, say that plainly and say where you looked.
 835    That is a finding, not a failure.
 836  - Include what you noticed while looking that a reader would find interesting
 837    even though nobody asked: what a place is actually like, what surprises
 838    people, what the thing next door is. Do not discard it because it was not the
 839    question.
 840  """
 841  
 842  
 843  # Namespace and asset URLs scraped out of page markup, which grounded search
 844  # returns alongside the real ones. `http://www.w3.org/2000/svg` is not a source.
 845  NON_SOURCE_URL_MARKERS = ("w3.org", "schema.org", "/favicon", ".svg", ".css", ".js")
 846  
 847  
 848  def _citable(urls: list[str]) -> list[str]:
 849      return [
 850          url
 851          for url in urls
 852          if url and not any(marker in url for marker in NON_SOURCE_URL_MARKERS)
 853      ]
 854  
 855  
 856  STRUCTURE_RULES = """Rules:
 857  - Every claim cites at least one source and at least one question it answers.
 858    Every question lists the claims that answer it. The two must agree.
 859  - A source needs a publisher and a URL when it is a web page or a report.
 860  - Every source carries a `source_type` and a `material_type`, and both come
 861    from fixed lists. `source_type` is one of: official, reporting, specialist,
 862    firsthand, other. `material_type` is one of: web, report, transcript,
 863    interview-responses, first-person-notes, evaluation-notes, other. A page you
 864    read on the web is `reporting` and `web`. Use `other` when nothing fits --
 865    do not invent a label.
 866  - `confidence` on a claim is one of: high, medium, low. An answer that is
 867    genuinely a range is still `supported` at `medium` or `low`; it does not
 868    become `partial` for being approximate.
 869  - Judge each question against what it says it `needs`, not against its wording.
 870    A question marked `approximate` is `supported` by a bounded answer that shows
 871    the published numbers behind it -- "the full 16-mile line runs about 55
 872    minutes at peak and this segment passes five stops" answers "roughly how
 873    long" completely, and marking it `partial` because no one publishes the exact
 874    minute blocks a run over a number the article never needed. A question marked
 875    `exact` is not settled by a range.
 876  - Set `venue` only on a claim that sends a reader to a place whose survival is
 877    genuinely in doubt: an independent tour operator, a small guesthouse, one
 878    restaurant, a bar, a family business, a tour run by a few people. Put the
 879    name of the place there and nothing else. A person looks these up before the
 880    article recommends them, and they are looking for one thing -- whether it is
 881    still going.
 882    Leave it empty in all three of these cases:
 883    - The claim is only a fact: an elevation, a visitor count, a date.
 884    - Nobody doubts the place is still there: a chain, a plaza, a park, a metro
 885      station, a cathedral, a museum that has been open for decades. Asking about
 886      one of these is a question the person can never learn anything from, and it
 887      buries the two or three worth their time.
 888    - The claim names the place as evidence rather than as a destination.
 889      "Parque Kennedy is surrounded by McDonald's, Starbucks and KFC" names three
 890      venues and sends a reader to none of them -- it describes what an area has
 891      become, and that is a good sentence to write. Tag the place the article
 892      points at, never the place it merely mentions.
 893    Most claims should have no venue. On a run with nineteen claims, three or
 894    four is a normal count, and a list with every fact in it is a list nobody
 895    reads.
 896  - A `conflict` records two or more claims that disagree, and must list their
 897    claim ids. If you cannot name at least two claims in conflict, it is not a
 898    conflict -- leave it out.
 899  - `status` per question: `supported`, `partial`, `missing`, or `unpublished`.
 900    Use `unpublished` when the notes establish that nobody publishes the answer,
 901    and say where was checked in `gap`. That is different from not having looked.
 902  - Anything with a status other than `supported` must describe the gap.
 903  - On anything other than `supported`, set `cause` to why you fell short. A
 904    person reads this to decide what to do about it, so pick the one that is
 905    actually true rather than the one that sounds least like a failure:
 906    - `not_published` -- you checked a source and it does not print the figure.
 907    - `does_not_exist` -- the thing the question assumes exists is not there, and
 908      you can say what is there instead. "No genuine 4-star hotel within five
 909      blocks; the nearest is the Sheraton at 1.4 km" is this. Only use it when
 910      your claims show what you found instead. If you simply did not find
 911      anything, that is `nothing_found`, not this.
 912    - `question_too_precise` -- you found near-miss figures but not the exact one
 913      the question demanded, because nobody publishes it to that precision.
 914    - `answered_something_else` -- what came back is about a different place,
 915      period or subject than was asked.
 916    - `nothing_found` -- nothing relevant came back at all.
 917  - Record a `premise_findings` verdict for every assumption above: `confirmed`,
 918    `refuted`, or `unverified`, with the basis.
 919  - Where the notes say sources disagree, record a conflict rather than picking
 920    silently. The notes rarely use the word "conflict". A section headed
 921    "Discrepancies", a figure called an outlier, a sentence saying one source is
 922    inconsistent with the others, or two numbers you are about to write into two
 923    claims that do not agree -- each of those is a conflict, and each has to be
 924    recorded as one. Two claims answering the same question with figures that
 925    disagree, and no conflict naming them, is the failure this is here to stop.
 926  - Where the notes weigh the disagreement and say which figure to prefer, put
 927    that in the conflict's `resolution`, in their reasoning. A conflict recorded
 928    without it leaves the writer choosing between two numbers with nothing to
 929    choose on. Leave `resolution` empty when the notes do not settle it: an
 930    unresolved conflict is a question for a person, and inventing a resolution
 931    takes it away from them.
 932  - Keep records concise: source metadata once per URL, short source IDs, and
 933    one claim per distinct fact. Do not copy the research narrative into records.
 934    A source's notes should contain only a caveat needed to interpret it.
 935  - Keep the interesting detail. A note that puts a reader somewhere belongs in a
 936    claim as much as a price does; do not drop it for not being a number."""
 937  
 938  
 939  def build_structure_prompt(
 940      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
 941      notes: dict[str, GatheredNotes],
 942  ) -> str:
 943      """Turn free notes into evidence records. Records nothing new."""
 944      questions = "\n".join(
 945          f"- {item.requirement_id} [{item.kind}] [needs: {item.precision}] "
 946          f"{item.question}"
 947          for item in work_order.requirements
 948      )
 949      gathered = "\n\n".join(
 950          f"=== {requirement_id} ===\n{note.text}\n"
 951          f"Sources seen: {', '.join(_citable(note.source_urls)) or 'none recorded'}"
 952          for requirement_id, note in notes.items()
 953      )
 954      premise = (
 955          "\n".join(f"- {item.assumption_id}: {item.statement}" for item in work_order.premise)
 956          or "- None declared."
 957      )
 958      return f"""Turn research notes into evidence records. Add nothing that is not in the notes.
 959  
 960  THE QUESTIONS
 961  {questions}
 962  
 963  WHAT WAS ASSUMED WITHOUT BEING CHECKED
 964  {premise}
 965  
 966  THE NOTES
 967  {gathered}
 968  
 969  {STRUCTURE_RULES}
 970  """
 971  
 972  
 973  PROGRESS_STAGE = "stage_v4_research_progress"
 974  
 975  
 976  def gather_one_requirement(
 977      brief: ArticleBrief,
 978      requirement: WorkOrderRequirement,
 979      dependencies: ResearchDependencies,
 980  ) -> GatheredNotes:
 981      """One question, one grounded pass. Never raises.
 982  
 983      A hole is survivable and a dead run is not, so a failed search comes back
 984      empty rather than taking the other searches down with it.
 985  
 986      Module level rather than a closure inside `gather_research`, because the
 987      gate re-asks exactly one rewritten question (#446) and re-running the whole
 988      pass to do it would re-buy every search that was already right.
 989      """
 990      prompt = build_gather_prompt(brief, requirement)
 991      try:
 992          # None, not a model: the gather job names itself and the gateway
 993          # answers. The argument stays so the callable's shape is unchanged.
 994          text, urls, tokens = dependencies.gather(prompt, None)
 995      except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover -- network dependent
 996          logger.warning("Gather failed for %s: %s", requirement.requirement_id, exc)
 997          text, urls, tokens = "", [], None
 998      return GatheredNotes(
 999          text=_safe_str(text), source_urls=list(urls or []), tokens=tokens
1000      )
1001  
1002  
1003  def gather_requirement_group(
1004      brief: ArticleBrief, requirements: list[WorkOrderRequirement], dependencies: ResearchDependencies,
1005  ) -> dict[str, GatheredNotes]:
1006      if len(requirements) == 1:
1007          item = requirements[0]
1008          return {item.requirement_id: gather_one_requirement(brief, item, dependencies)}
1009      prompt = (
1010          "Research these related questions together using shared sources. "
1011          "Keep each question's precision and scope. Return concise cited facts under "
1012          "each question ID; explicitly say when a question could not be answered. "
1013          "Do not repeat the same background or source description.\n\n"
1014          + "\n\n".join(f"QUESTION {item.requirement_id}\n{build_gather_prompt(brief, item)}" for item in requirements)
1015      )
1016      try:
1017          text, urls, tokens = dependencies.gather(prompt, None)
1018      except Exception as exc:
1019          logger.warning("Grouped research failed: %s", exc)
1020          text, urls, tokens = "", [], None
1021      # All questions retain the original cited response; attribution happens in
1022      # structuring. Only one note carries call tokens so totals do not multiply.
1023      return {item.requirement_id: GatheredNotes(_safe_str(text), list(urls or []), tokens if index == 0 else None)
1024              for index, item in enumerate(requirements)}
1025  
1026  
1027  def gather_research(
1028      brief: ArticleBrief,
1029      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
1030      dependencies: ResearchDependencies,
1031      on_progress: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], None] | None = None,
1032      *,
1033      kept_notes: dict[str, GatheredNotes] | None = None,
1034      checkpoint: Callable[[dict[str, GatheredNotes]], None] | None = None,
1035      before_call: Callable[[], None] | None = None,
1036  ) -> dict[str, GatheredNotes]:
1037      """Bounded concurrent searches, sharing retrieval for related questions.
1038  
1039      Texture is researched to the identical standard: a scene we cannot source
1040      is still cut, so it has to be sourced like anything else.
1041  
1042      The work order may group related questions; each request holds at most
1043      four, while coverage still judges every question separately. Complete
1044      results are checkpointed before another request is dispatched. An error
1045      stops new submissions but lets in-flight work finish and be saved.
1046  
1047      Bounded at `P2B_V4_GATHER_CONCURRENCY`, because grounded-search rate limits
1048      are unknown and the number of questions is set by the work order rather
1049      than by us.
1050  
1051      `on_progress` reports **completions**, not position: it fires once when the
1052      searches start and once each time one comes back. It cannot say what is
1053      being searched now, because several are, so it names the last question to
1054      come back instead.
1055      """
1056      requirements = list(work_order.requirements)
1057      total = len(requirements)
1058  
1059      def _emit(phase: str, done: int, last_question_back: str) -> None:
1060          if on_progress is None:
1061              return
1062          try:
1063              on_progress(
1064                  {
1065                      "phase": phase,
1066                      "done": done,
1067                      "total": total,
1068                      "last_question_back": last_question_back,
1069                  }
1070              )
1071          except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover -- telemetry only
1072              logger.warning("Research progress write failed: %s", exc)
1073  
1074      gathered = {key: note for key, note in (kept_notes or {}).items() if note.text.strip()}
1075      missing = [item for item in requirements if item.requirement_id not in gathered]
1076      grouped: dict[str, list[WorkOrderRequirement]] = {}
1077      for item in missing:
1078          grouped.setdefault(item.search_group or f"single:{item.requirement_id}", []).append(item)
1079      groups = [items[start:start + STRUCTURE_BATCH_SIZE] for items in grouped.values()
1080                for start in range(0, len(items), STRUCTURE_BATCH_SIZE)]
1081      if missing:
1082          _emit("gathering", len(gathered), "")
1083          workers = max(1, min(P2B_V4_GATHER_CONCURRENCY, len(groups)))
1084          remaining = iter(groups)
1085          with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as pool:
1086              pending = {}
1087              stopped: Exception | None = None
1088              while True:
1089                  while stopped is None and len(pending) < workers:
1090                      requirement = next(remaining, None)
1091                      if requirement is None:
1092                          break
1093                      try:
1094                          if before_call:
1095                              before_call()
1096                      except Exception as error:
1097                          stopped = error
1098                          break
1099                      pending[pool.submit(gather_requirement_group, brief, requirement, dependencies)] = requirement
1100                  if not pending:
1101                      break
1102                  completed, _ = wait(pending, return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED)
1103                  for future in completed:
1104                      requirement = pending.pop(future)
1105                      try:
1106                          gathered.update(future.result())
1107                          if checkpoint:
1108                              checkpoint(dict(gathered))
1109                      except Exception as error:
1110                          stopped = error
1111                      _emit("gathering", len(gathered), requirement[-1].question)
1112              if stopped is not None:
1113                  raise stopped
1114  
1115      # Rebuilt in work-order order rather than completion order, so the notes,
1116      # the structure prompt built from them and anything diffing two runs do not
1117      # change shape with the weather.
1118      notes = {
1119          requirement.requirement_id: gathered[requirement.requirement_id]
1120          for requirement in requirements
1121          if requirement.requirement_id in gathered
1122      }
1123  
1124      # Structuring has its own progress phase after the last search.
1125      _emit("structuring", total, "")
1126      return notes
1127  
1128  
1129  def _reconcile_premise_findings(
1130      package: EvidencePackage, work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder
1131  ) -> EvidencePackage:
1132      """Every declared assumption gets a verdict, even when research gave none.
1133  
1134      Run b29d66b4 declared three premises, including one that was provably
1135      false, and came back with `premise_findings: []`. So `refuted_assumptions`
1136      was empty -- which reads as "nothing was refuted" when the truth is
1137      "nothing was checked", and the rule that stops a run on a refuted premise
1138      could never fire.
1139  
1140      This is the same hazard `groundedness` already guards: `checked` is read
1141      before `grounded`, because an outage that degrades to "fine" is worse than
1142      one that says it did not run. A missing verdict becomes `unverified` with
1143      a basis that says plainly nobody answered, so the operator meets it at the
1144      gate rather than never.
1145      """
1146      declared = [item.assumption_id for item in work_order.premise]
1147      if not declared:
1148          return package
1149      answered = {finding.assumption_id for finding in package.premise_findings}
1150      missing = [item for item in declared if item not in answered]
1151      if not missing:
1152          return package
1153  
1154      logger.warning(
1155          "Prompt2Blog research returned no premise verdict for %s", missing
1156      )
1157      payload = package.model_dump(mode="json")
1158      payload["premise_findings"] = [
1159          *payload.get("premise_findings", []),
1160          *(
1161              {
1162                  "assumption_id": assumption_id,
1163                  "verdict": "unverified",
1164                  "basis": (
1165                      "The research step returned no verdict for this premise. "
1166                      "It was declared and never answered, which is not the same "
1167                      "as having been checked and left open."
1168                  ),
1169                  "claim_ids": [],
1170              }
1171              for assumption_id in missing
1172          ),
1173      ]
1174      return EvidencePackage.model_validate(payload)
1175  
1176  
1177  BATCH_SCHEMA = require_non_empty({
1178      "type": "object",
1179      "properties": {
1180          "sources": EVIDENCE_SCHEMA["properties"]["sources"],
1181          "claims": EVIDENCE_SCHEMA["properties"]["claims"],
1182          "requirements": EVIDENCE_SCHEMA["properties"]["requirements"],
1183          "gaps": EVIDENCE_SCHEMA["properties"]["gaps"],
1184      },
1185      "required": ["sources", "claims", "requirements"],
1186  })
1187  
1188  PREMISE_SCHEMA = require_non_empty({
1189      "type": "object",
1190      "properties": {
1191          "premise_findings": EVIDENCE_SCHEMA["properties"]["premise_findings"],
1192          "conflicts": EVIDENCE_SCHEMA["properties"]["conflicts"],
1193      },
1194      "required": ["premise_findings"],
1195  })
1196  
1197  
1198  # The shape `_batch_source_table` mints. A value matching it is a stand-in
1199  # for a link, never a fact about the source.
1200  _HANDLE = re.compile(r"URL\d+")
1201  
1202  
1203  def _batch_source_table(
1204      requirements: list[WorkOrderRequirement], notes: dict[str, GatheredNotes],
1205  ) -> dict[str, str]:
1206      """Keep opaque grounding redirect URLs out of generated JSON (#499).
1207  
1208      The model copies short handles; the application restores exact URLs.
1209      Includes URLs embedded in prose as well as the grounding metadata.
1210      """
1211      urls: set[str] = set()
1212      for item in requirements:
1213          if item.requirement_id not in notes:
1214              continue
1215          note = notes[item.requirement_id]
1216          urls.update(_citable(note.source_urls))
1217          urls.update(match.rstrip(".,;:") for match in re.findall(r'https?://[^\s<>"\]\)\}]+', note.text))
1218      return {f"URL{index}": url for index, url in enumerate(sorted(urls), start=1)}
1219  
1220  
1221  def _compact_batch_notes(
1222      requirements: list[WorkOrderRequirement], notes: dict[str, GatheredNotes],
1223  ) -> dict[str, GatheredNotes]:
1224      table = _batch_source_table(requirements, notes)
1225      replacements = sorted(table.items(), key=lambda pair: len(pair[1]), reverse=True)
1226      compact = {}
1227      for item in requirements:
1228          if item.requirement_id not in notes:
1229              continue
1230          note = notes[item.requirement_id]
1231          text = note.text
1232          for handle, url in replacements:
1233              text = text.replace(url, handle)
1234          compact[item.requirement_id] = GatheredNotes(
1235              text, [handle for handle, url in table.items() if url in note.source_urls], note.tokens,
1236          )
1237      return compact
1238  
1239  
1240  def build_batch_prompt(
1241      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
1242      requirements: list[WorkOrderRequirement],
1243      notes: dict[str, GatheredNotes],
1244  ) -> str:
1245      """Structure a few questions' notes. The same rules, a fraction of the work.
1246  
1247      The dossier used to be built in a single call: every note in, one large
1248      object out. On the Claude CLI that generated three to four times what it
1249      delivered -- 32,060 and 39,139 billed tokens against a 36 KB record --
1250      because a schema failure anywhere in the object throws all of it away and
1251      it is silently produced again. On 2026-09-02 it stopped converging and
1252      three attempts died, at 600s, 600s and 1200s.
1253  
1254      A handful of questions at a time is small enough to come back first time,
1255      and a failure costs a third of the plan instead of the whole run.
1256      """
1257      notes = _compact_batch_notes(requirements, notes)
1258      listed = "\n".join(
1259          f"- {item.requirement_id} [{item.kind}] [needs: {item.precision}] "
1260          f"{item.question}"
1261          for item in requirements
1262      )
1263      shared_notes: dict[str, tuple[list[str], GatheredNotes]] = {}
1264      for item in requirements:
1265          if item.requirement_id not in notes:
1266              continue
1267          note = notes[item.requirement_id]
1268          key = _fingerprint({"text": note.text, "urls": note.source_urls})
1269          if key not in shared_notes:
1270              shared_notes[key] = ([], note)
1271          shared_notes[key][0].append(item.requirement_id)
1272      gathered = "\n\n".join(
1273          f"=== {', '.join(question_ids)} ===\n{note.text}\n"
1274          f"Sources seen: {', '.join(_citable(note.source_urls)) or 'none recorded'}"
1275          for question_ids, note in shared_notes.values()
1276      )
1277      ids = ", ".join(item.requirement_id for item in requirements)
1278      return f"""Turn these questions' research notes into evidence records. Add nothing that is not in the notes.
1279  
1280  THE QUESTIONS
1281  {listed}
1282  
1283  THE NOTES
1284  {gathered}
1285  
1286  URL1, URL2, etc. are exact source references. Copy the relevant handle into
1287  source.url. The application restores the original URL. Never expand a handle
1288  or invent a URL. Use short source_id values; the URL handle is not a claim.
1289  
1290  {STRUCTURE_RULES}
1291  - One claim per distinct fact. Do not split a fact across several claims, and
1292    do not repeat the same fact once per source that mentions it: a claim cites
1293    all of its sources. Two or three claims answer most questions well, and a
1294    question with ten is the same answer written out at length.
1295  
1296  Return records for these questions only: {ids}. Every claim lists at least one
1297  of them in its requirement_ids, and the requirements array holds one entry for
1298  each."""
1299  
1300  
1301  def build_premise_prompt(
1302      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder, claims: list[dict[str, Any]]
1303  ) -> str:
1304      """Settle the premise, and name conflicts that span two questions.
1305  
1306      The only two jobs a per-question pass cannot do, so they get one small
1307      call of their own that sees the claim texts and nothing else.
1308      """
1309      premise = (
1310          "\n".join(
1311              f"- {item.assumption_id}: {item.statement}" for item in work_order.premise
1312          )
1313          or "- None declared."
1314      )
1315      listed = "\n".join(
1316          f"- [{claim['claim_id']}] {claim['text']}" for claim in claims
1317      ) or "- Nothing was established."
1318      return f"""Settle what the plan assumed, against what research found.
1319  
1320  WHAT WAS ASSUMED WITHOUT BEING CHECKED
1321  {premise}
1322  
1323  WHAT RESEARCH ESTABLISHED
1324  {listed}
1325  
1326  {PREMISE_CHECK_RULES}
1327  
1328  Also record a `conflict` for any two claims above that disagree with each
1329  other, listing their claim ids and summarising the disagreement. A conflict
1330  records two or more claims that disagree; if you cannot name at least two, it
1331  is not a conflict. Where the notes settled which side is right, put that in
1332  `resolution`, and leave it empty when they did not: an unresolved conflict is
1333  a question for a person, and inventing a resolution takes it away from them.
1334  
1335  Return premise_findings for every assumption above, and conflicts, and nothing
1336  else."""
1337  
1338  
1339  def _namespaced(payload: dict[str, Any], requirement_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
1340      """Prefix this call's ids so eleven calls cannot collide.
1341  
1342      Two questions answered separately both produce a claim called `c1`. The
1343      prefix is applied to the ids and to every reference to them, so the
1344      contract's link checks still hold after the merge.
1345      """
1346      tag = f"{requirement_id}:"
1347      sources = _rows(payload, "sources")
1348      claims = _rows(payload, "claims")
1349      for source in sources:
1350          source["source_id"] = f"{tag}{_safe_str(source.get('source_id'))}"
1351      for claim in claims:
1352          claim["claim_id"] = f"{tag}{_safe_str(claim.get('claim_id'))}"
1353          claim["source_ids"] = [
1354              f"{tag}{item}" for item in _id_list(claim, "source_ids")
1355          ]
1356      for requirement in _rows(payload, "requirements"):
1357          requirement["claim_ids"] = [
1358              f"{tag}{item}" for item in _id_list(requirement, "claim_ids")
1359          ]
1360      for gap in _rows(payload, "gaps"):
1361          gap.setdefault("gap_id", f"{tag}gap")
1362          gap["gap_id"] = f"{tag}{_safe_str(gap.get('gap_id'))}"
1363      return {
1364          "sources": sources,
1365          "claims": claims,
1366          "requirements": _rows(payload, "requirements"),
1367          "gaps": _rows(payload, "gaps"),
1368      }
1369  
1370  
1371  def _merge_sources(parts: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[str, str]]:
1372      """One entry per real source, and a map from every id that meant it.
1373  
1374      The same page answers three questions and is described three times, once
1375      per call. Merged on url, then on title, because a dossier listing the same
1376      site under three ids is not wrong so much as unreadable.
1377      """
1378      merged: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
1379      by_key: dict[str, str] = {}
1380      remap: dict[str, str] = {}
1381      for part in parts:
1382          for source in part["sources"]:
1383              key = (
1384                  _safe_str(source.get("url")).strip().rstrip("/").lower()
1385                  or _safe_str(source.get("title")).strip().lower()
1386              )
1387              source_id = _safe_str(source.get("source_id"))
1388              if key and key in by_key:
1389                  remap[source_id] = by_key[key]
1390                  continue
1391              merged.append(source)
1392              if key:
1393                  by_key[key] = source_id
1394              remap[source_id] = source_id
1395      return merged, remap
1396  
1397  
1398  def assemble_evidence(
1399      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
1400      payload: dict[str, Any],
1401      *,
1402      reconcile_premises: bool = True,
1403  ) -> EvidencePackage:
1404      """Normalise what the model sent, then hold it to the contract.
1405  
1406      Separate from the calls that produce it, because what arrives is repaired
1407      the same way whether it came back in one piece or eleven.
1408  
1409      `reconcile_premises=False` is for a single batch. A premise verdict is
1410      about the whole dossier and a batch sees four questions, so `BATCH_SCHEMA`
1411      has no `premise_findings` and `build_batch_prompt` asks for none. Judging a
1412      batch against the declared premises therefore finds every one of them
1413      missing, every time, on runs where nothing is wrong -- and the warning that
1414      says "nobody checked your premises" is the same warning either way. The
1415      reconciliation belongs where the whole dossier exists, after
1416      `_settle_premise` has run.
1417      """
1418      payload = _normalised_evidence(_safe_dict(payload))
1419      payload["schema_version"] = 4
1420      payload["work_order_fingerprint"] = work_order.work_order_fingerprint
1421      try:
1422          package = record_detected_conflicts(EvidencePackage.model_validate(payload))
1423          return _reconcile_premise_findings(package, work_order) if reconcile_premises else package
1424      except ValidationError as error:
1425          raise ResearchUnusable(
1426              "; ".join(
1427                  f"{'.'.join(str(part) for part in item['loc']) or 'dossier'}: {item['msg']}"
1428                  for item in error.errors()
1429              )
1430              or "the dossier did not fit its contract",
1431              json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)[:40000],
1432          ) from error
1433  
1434  
1435  def _structure_batch(
1436      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
1437      requirements: list[WorkOrderRequirement],
1438      notes: dict[str, GatheredNotes],
1439      dependencies: ResearchDependencies,
1440  ) -> dict[str, Any]:
1441      """A few questions structured together. Never raises.
1442  
1443      A batch whose structuring fails comes back recorded as unanswered, with a
1444      gap saying so, because the alternative is one bad call taking the other
1445      eight down with it. The operator meets it at the gate like any other hole.
1446      """
1447      ids = [item.requirement_id for item in requirements]
1448      try:
1449          parsed, _raw = dependencies.structure_llm.invoke_json(
1450              job_id="p2b.research_structure",
1451              prompt=build_batch_prompt(work_order, requirements, notes),
1452              model_name=dependencies.structure_model,
1453              schema=BATCH_SCHEMA,
1454              max_tokens=ONE_QUESTION_MAX_TOKENS,
1455              temperature=0.0,
1456          )
1457          parsed = copy.deepcopy(_safe_dict(parsed))
1458          source_table = _batch_source_table(requirements, notes)
1459          unresolved: list[str] = []
1460          for source in _rows(parsed, "sources"):
1461              given = source.get("url")
1462              resolved = source_table.get(given, given)
1463              # A handle it never saw, or a bare host it typed from memory. Both
1464              # mean this source was not retrieved, and "not a valid URL" from the
1465              # model further down does not say which value caused it.
1466              if isinstance(resolved, str) and resolved and not resolved.startswith(
1467                  ("http://", "https://")
1468              ):
1469                  unresolved.append(resolved)
1470              source["url"] = resolved
1471              # The model reads `URL7` where a link used to be and reasonably
1472              # uses it as the source's name too. Restoring only the url left 429
1473              # of 543 titles in run 95a74dce reading "URL1", "URL2" -- a
1474              # bibliography with no identifying information in it at all. A
1475              # handle is never a title; say so rather than shipping one.
1476              if _HANDLE.fullmatch(_safe_str(source.get("title"))):
1477                  source["title"] = "Untitled source"
1478          if unresolved:
1479              raise ResearchUnusable(
1480                  "Structuring returned source URLs that are not links: "
1481                  + ", ".join(sorted(set(unresolved))[:5]),
1482                  _raw,
1483              )
1484          part = _namespaced(parsed, ids[0])
1485          package = assemble_evidence(work_order, part, reconcile_premises=False)
1486          answered = {item.requirement_id for item in package.requirements}
1487          unanswered = set(ids) - answered
1488          if unanswered:
1489              raise ResearchUnusable(
1490                  "Structuring did not answer "
1491                  + ", ".join(sorted(unanswered)),
1492                  _raw,
1493              )
1494          # An extra answer is not a failure. Notes are gathered per search
1495          # group and a batch is a slice of one, so the notes in front of the
1496          # model routinely cover questions this batch did not ask about, and it
1497          # answers what it was given -- correctly.
1498          #
1499          # This was set equality. Run bogota-replan-0906 asked about four
1500          # rideshare questions, got all four right plus `req_rideshare_time_usaquen`
1501          # from the same group, and had the whole batch recorded `missing` /
1502          # `nothing_found`; the TransMilenio batch went the same way on
1503          # `req_transmilenio_time_chapinero`. Eight correct, paid-for answers
1504          # thrown away, the gate blocked, and the operator told to answer
1505          # questions by hand whose answers were sitting in the notes. Retrying
1506          # reproduced it exactly, because nothing about it was random.
1507          #
1508          # Extras are dropped rather than kept: every requirement is in exactly
1509          # one batch, so the one this answered early is recorded by its own
1510          # batch, and keeping it here would file the same requirement twice.
1511          extra = answered - set(ids)
1512          if extra:
1513              logger.info(
1514                  "Structuring answered %s beyond the batch it was asked about; "
1515                  "kept the %s requested and left those to their own batch",
1516                  ", ".join(sorted(extra)),
1517                  len(ids),
1518              )
1519              record = package.model_dump(mode="json")
1520              record["requirements"] = [
1521                  item for item in record["requirements"]
1522                  if item["requirement_id"] in set(ids)
1523              ]
1524              return record
1525          return package.model_dump(mode="json")
1526      except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- one hole beats the whole plan
1527          logger.warning("Structuring failed for %s: %s", ", ".join(ids), exc)
1528          return {
1529              "_retryable": True,
1530              "sources": [],
1531              "claims": [],
1532              "requirements": [
1533                  {
1534                      "requirement_id": requirement_id,
1535                      "status": "missing",
1536                      "cause": "nothing_found",
1537                      "gap": (
1538                          "The research notes for this question could not be "
1539                          "turned into records. The notes are kept, so this is "
1540                          "one call to retry rather than a lost search."
1541                      ),
1542                      "claim_ids": [],
1543                  }
1544                  for requirement_id in ids
1545              ],
1546              "gaps": [],
1547          }
1548  
1549  
1550  def _settle_premise(
1551      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
1552      claims: list[dict[str, Any]],
1553      dependencies: ResearchDependencies,
1554  ) -> dict[str, Any]:
1555      """The two jobs a per-question pass cannot do. Never raises.
1556  
1557      A premise verdict is about the whole dossier, and a conflict between two
1558      questions is invisible to a call that sees one. `_reconcile_premise_findings`
1559      fills in anything missing afterwards, so a failure here degrades rather
1560      than blocks.
1561      """
1562      if not work_order.premise and len(claims) < 2:
1563          return {"premise_findings": [], "conflicts": []}
1564      try:
1565          parsed, _raw = dependencies.structure_llm.invoke_json(
1566              job_id="p2b.research_structure",
1567              prompt=build_premise_prompt(work_order, claims),
1568              model_name=dependencies.structure_model,
1569              schema=PREMISE_SCHEMA,
1570              max_tokens=ONE_QUESTION_MAX_TOKENS,
1571              temperature=0.0,
1572          )
1573      except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
1574          logger.warning("Premise pass failed: %s", exc)
1575          return {"premise_findings": [], "conflicts": [], "_retryable": True}
1576      payload = _safe_dict(parsed)
1577      return {
1578          "premise_findings": _rows(
1579              payload, "premise_findings", "premise", "assumptions", "findings"
1580          ),
1581          "conflicts": _rows(payload, "conflicts", "conflict"),
1582      }
1583  
1584  
1585  def structure_research(
1586      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
1587      notes: dict[str, GatheredNotes],
1588      dependencies: ResearchDependencies,
1589      *,
1590      kept_batches: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
1591      checkpoint: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], None] | None = None,
1592      before_call: Callable[[], None] | None = None,
1593  ) -> EvidencePackage:
1594      """Turn the notes into the evidence package the writing stages read.
1595  
1596      A few questions per call, then one small call for the premise and any
1597      conflict that spans two of them.
1598  
1599      It used to be a single call: every note in, the whole dossier out. On the
1600      Claude CLI that generated three to four times what it delivered, because a
1601      schema failure anywhere in one large object throws all of it away and it is
1602      silently produced again. On 2026-09-02 it stopped converging and took three
1603      attempts down with it, at 600s, 600s and 1200s, on a plan smaller than the
1604      one that had worked the day before. The CLI takes no output cap -- it
1605      accepts `max_tokens` and drops it -- so nothing bounded what that call
1606      could spend.
1607  
1608      Smaller calls are not a workaround for that. They are the shape that makes
1609      a failure cost one question instead of the run.
1610      """
1611      requirements = [
1612          item for item in work_order.requirements if item.requirement_id in notes
1613      ]
1614      batches = [
1615          requirements[start : start + STRUCTURE_BATCH_SIZE]
1616          for start in range(0, len(requirements), STRUCTURE_BATCH_SIZE)
1617      ]
1618      cache = copy.deepcopy(kept_batches or {})
1619      parts = []
1620      batch_keys: list[str] = []
1621      for batch in batches:
1622          prompt = build_batch_prompt(work_order, batch, notes)
1623          key = _fingerprint({"prompt": prompt, "sources": _batch_source_table(batch, notes), "schema": BATCH_SCHEMA, "version": 2})
1624          batch_keys.append(key)
1625          if key not in cache:
1626              if before_call:
1627                  before_call()
1628              part = _structure_batch(work_order, batch, notes, dependencies)
1629              if not part.get("_retryable"):
1630                  cache[key] = part
1631              # Persist usage even when this paid response was unusable.
1632              if checkpoint:
1633                  checkpoint(copy.deepcopy(cache))
1634          else:
1635              part = cache[key]
1636          parts.append(copy.deepcopy(part))
1637  
1638      sources, remap = _merge_sources(parts)
1639      claims = [claim for part in parts for claim in part["claims"]]
1640      for claim in claims:
1641          claim["source_ids"] = sorted(
1642              {remap.get(item, item) for item in _id_list(claim, "source_ids")}
1643          )
1644      premise_key = _fingerprint({"prompt": build_premise_prompt(work_order, claims), "schema": PREMISE_SCHEMA, "version": 1})
1645      if premise_key in cache:
1646          settled = cache[premise_key]
1647      else:
1648          if before_call:
1649              before_call()
1650          settled = _settle_premise(work_order, claims, dependencies)
1651          if not settled.get("_retryable"):
1652              cache[premise_key] = settled
1653  
1654      # A cut question, an edited one or a re-gathered note all change the key
1655      # its batch answers under, and nothing will ever hit the old entry again.
1656      # Dropping them here is what stops the saved cache growing with every cut.
1657      live = set(batch_keys) | {premise_key}
1658      cache = {key: value for key, value in cache.items() if key in live}
1659      if checkpoint:
1660          checkpoint(copy.deepcopy(cache))
1661  
1662      return assemble_evidence(
1663          work_order,
1664          {
1665              "sources": sources,
1666              "claims": claims,
1667              "requirements": [
1668                  item for part in parts for item in part["requirements"]
1669              ],
1670              "gaps": [gap for part in parts for gap in part["gaps"]],
1671              "premise_findings": settled["premise_findings"],
1672              "conflicts": settled["conflicts"],
1673          },
1674      )
1675  
1676  
1677  def run_research(
1678      brief: ArticleBrief,
1679      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
1680      dependencies: ResearchDependencies,
1681      on_progress: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], None] | None = None,
1682      notes: dict[str, GatheredNotes] | None = None,
1683  ) -> tuple[EvidencePackage, dict[str, GatheredNotes]]:
1684      """Both passes. Returns the evidence and the notes it came from.
1685  
1686      `notes` skips the gathering when a previous attempt already paid for it.
1687      """
1688      if notes is None:
1689          notes = gather_research(brief, work_order, dependencies, on_progress)
1690      return structure_research(work_order, notes, dependencies), notes
1691  
1692  
1693  def research_stage_record(
1694      evidence: EvidencePackage,
1695      notes: dict[str, GatheredNotes],
1696  ) -> dict[str, Any]:
1697      """What the run keeps about the research it paid for."""
1698      return {
1699          "work_order_fingerprint": evidence.work_order_fingerprint,
1700          "source_count": len(evidence.sources),
1701          "claim_count": len(evidence.claims),
1702          "requirement_status": {
1703              item.requirement_id: item.status for item in evidence.requirements
1704          },
1705          # What research actually found, per question. The screen used to show
1706          # "q3 — partly answered" and nothing else, which tells the operator
1707          # neither what was asked nor what came back, and leaves the one
1708          # decision they have to make unmakeable.
1709          "findings": {
1710              item.requirement_id: {
1711                  "status": item.status,
1712                  "gap": item.gap,
1713                  "claims": [
1714                      {
1715                          "claim_id": claim.claim_id,
1716                          "text": claim.text,
1717                          "confidence": claim.confidence,
1718                          "venue": claim.venue,
1719                          "venue_note": claim.venue_note,
1720                          "sources": [
1721                              {
1722                                  "title": source.title,
1723                                  "url": str(source.url) if source.url else "",
1724                                  "source_type": source.source_type,
1725                              }
1726                              for source in evidence.sources
1727                              if source.source_id in claim.source_ids
1728                          ],
1729                      }
1730                      for claim in evidence.claims
1731                      if item.requirement_id in claim.requirement_ids
1732                  ],
1733              }
1734              for item in evidence.requirements
1735          },
1736          "conflicts": [item.summary for item in evidence.conflicts],
1737          "gathered": {
1738              requirement_id: {
1739                  "characters": len(note.text),
1740                  "source_urls": note.source_urls,
1741                  "tokens": note.tokens,
1742              }
1743              for requirement_id, note in notes.items()
1744          },
1745      }
apps/backend/app/features/prompt2blog/coverage_v4.py
   1  """Is this dossier enough to write from, and is any of it worth reading?
   2  
   3  Two questions, and v3 only ever asked the first.
   4  
   5  The audited Lima run passed every check the system owned. Its research was
   6  clean: first-party sources, dated, conflicts surfaced. It was also unusable --
   7  no food, in one of the great food cities on earth -- because all three of its
   8  questions existed to prove the premise, so all three answers proved it. Nothing
   9  downstream noticed, because nothing downstream was looking.
  10  
  11  So a dossier with nothing a reader would enjoy is reported as a real gap, the
  12  same way a missing fact is. And this is the one gate in the whole pipeline that
  13  blocks: writing is the most expensive step, writing well on thin material is
  14  not possible, and a gate before writing saves money where a gate after writing
  15  only hides work already paid for.
  16  
  17  The exit is the grill. That is not a fallback -- it is the door the refuted
  18  premise has not had since the direction cards were deleted.
  19  """
  20  
  21  from __future__ import annotations
  22  
  23  from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  24  from typing import Any
  25  
  26  from .contracts_v4 import EvidencePackage, Prompt2BlogWorkOrder
  27  
  28  # A claim that could only have come from someone looking: a texture answer, a
  29  # scene, something specific enough to put a reader somewhere. Counted rather
  30  # than judged, because the alternative is another model call to ask a model
  31  # whether it was interesting.
  32  ENJOYABLE_STATUSES = {"supported", "partial"}
  33  
  34  # The statuses that settle a load-bearing question rather than block on it.
  35  #
  36  # `unpublished` and `nonexistent` are findings, not failures, and both are
  37  # publishable sentences: nobody prints Lima's customs times, and there is no
  38  # 4-star hotel within five blocks of the Plaza Mayor. Neither is a hole in the
  39  # article -- they are things the article can say. What they are not is texture,
  40  # which is why they stay out of ENJOYABLE_STATUSES above: a dossier answering
  41  # every question with an absence still has nothing a reader would enjoy.
  42  SETTLED_STATUSES = {"supported", "unpublished", "nonexistent"}
  43  
  44  
  45  @dataclass
  46  class CoverageVerdict:
  47      """Whether this run may write, and what is missing if not."""
  48  
  49      can_write: bool
  50      unsupported_load_bearing: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
  51      refuted_assumptions: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
  52      has_texture: bool = True
  53      findings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
  54  
  55      @property
  56      def reason(self) -> str:
  57          if self.can_write:
  58              return "ready_to_write"
  59          if self.refuted_assumptions:
  60              # More research cannot clear this. The article was commissioned
  61              # about something that is not so.
  62              return "premise_refuted"
  63          if self.unsupported_load_bearing:
  64              return "load_bearing_unanswered"
  65          return "nothing_worth_reading"
  66  
  67      def as_record(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
  68          return {
  69              "can_write": self.can_write,
  70              "reason": self.reason,
  71              "unsupported_load_bearing": list(self.unsupported_load_bearing),
  72              "refuted_assumptions": list(self.refuted_assumptions),
  73              "has_texture": self.has_texture,
  74              "findings": list(self.findings),
  75          }
  76  
  77  
  78  def assess_coverage(
  79      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
  80      evidence: EvidencePackage,
  81  ) -> CoverageVerdict:
  82      """Decide whether this dossier can carry the piece."""
  83      status_by_id = {item.requirement_id: item.status for item in evidence.requirements}
  84      kind_by_id = {item.requirement_id: item.kind for item in work_order.requirements}
  85  
  86      unsupported = sorted(
  87          requirement_id
  88          for requirement_id, kind in kind_by_id.items()
  89          if kind == "load_bearing"
  90          and status_by_id.get(requirement_id) not in SETTLED_STATUSES
  91      )
  92      refuted = sorted(
  93          finding.assumption_id
  94          for finding in evidence.premise_findings
  95          if finding.verdict == "refuted"
  96      )
  97  
  98      texture_ids = {
  99          requirement_id
 100          for requirement_id, kind in kind_by_id.items()
 101          if kind == "texture"
 102      }
 103      answered_texture = {
 104          requirement_id
 105          for requirement_id in texture_ids
 106          if status_by_id.get(requirement_id) in ENJOYABLE_STATUSES
 107      }
 108      # No texture questions at all still counts as thin: a work order with
 109      # nothing but proof produces a dossier with nothing but proof, which is
 110      # exactly what happened to Lima.
 111      has_texture = bool(answered_texture)
 112  
 113      findings: list[str] = []
 114      for requirement_id in unsupported:
 115          findings.append(
 116              f"{requirement_id} is load-bearing and unanswered "
 117              f"({status_by_id.get(requirement_id, 'missing')})."
 118          )
 119      for assumption_id in refuted:
 120          findings.append(
 121              f"{assumption_id} was assumed and turned out not to be so. "
 122              "More research will not change that."
 123          )
 124      if not has_texture:
 125          findings.append(
 126              "Nothing here would be a pleasure to read. Every answer proves "
 127              "something and none of it puts a reader anywhere."
 128          )
 129  
 130      return CoverageVerdict(
 131          can_write=not unsupported and not refuted and has_texture,
 132          unsupported_load_bearing=unsupported,
 133          refuted_assumptions=refuted,
 134          has_texture=has_texture,
 135          findings=findings,
 136      )
apps/backend/app/features/prompt2blog/selection_v4.py
   1  """Which facts the article is written from (#534).
   2  
   3  Research finds around a hundred facts. Until now nothing decided which of them
   4  the article needed, and the writer received all of them.
   5  
   6  Run 9e66bf84, the Lima chifa article, 1,155 words:
   7  
   8      105 claims, 110 sources, from 13 requirements
   9      the outline assigned  102 of 105 claims across 6 sections
  10      compose received      105 of 105
  11  
  12  The outline did not select. It distributed -- it found a home for almost
  13  everything and called that a plan. One 200-word section was given 56 claims,
  14  which is three and a half words per claim, and there is no sentence you can
  15  write at that density except a list. The article read like a database because
  16  it was one.
  17  
  18  Three passes stand between research and the outline.
  19  
  20  **Deduplicate.** A model groups claims that are the same fact and names which
  21  one survives. It never writes new claim text: a merged claim composed by a
  22  model is prose asserting a fact, and a drifted date or price inside one would
  23  pass groundedness, because groundedness checks the draft against the claim and
  24  the claim is the thing that moved. Every survivor is verbatim what research
  25  returned, and it inherits the sources and questions of everything merged into
  26  it, so nothing loses its provenance.
  27  
  28  **Rank.** A model orders the survivors by how much they matter to *this* brief
  29  -- the reader question, the promise, and `fails_if`. Not by general interest: a
  30  fact can be true, well sourced and irrelevant here.
  31  
  32  **A person picks.** The operator sees the ranked list with a line drawn where
  33  the keep-set ends, moves the line, and rescues or drops individual claims. That
  34  step is the point and not a fallback. A model dropping a fact the article
  35  needed is a silent loss the operator discovers by reading a worse article; a
  36  person dropping it is a decision they made and can undo.
  37  
  38  Nothing here deletes. Selection is a flag on the claim, so groundedness and the
  39  readiness follow-up keep reading the whole dossier, a deselected claim leaves
  40  the writer's desk and never the record, and a question it supports stays
  41  supported. Deselecting is an editorial choice and must never become a coverage
  42  failure.
  43  
  44  Both model calls degrade rather than fail. When either comes back unusable the
  45  run keeps every claim, exactly as it behaved before this existed, and the
  46  record says which pass fell over -- an article written from all the evidence is
  47  worse than one written from the right quarter of it, and both are better than
  48  no article.
  49  """
  50  
  51  from __future__ import annotations
  52  
  53  import logging
  54  import re
  55  from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  56  from typing import Any
  57  
  58  from .contracts_v4 import ArticleBrief, EvidencePackage, Prompt2BlogWorkOrder
  59  from .schema_guards import require_non_empty
  60  from .support import _safe_dict, _safe_int, _safe_str
  61  
  62  logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  63  
  64  SELECTION_STAGE = "stage_v4_selection"
  65  
  66  # How many facts a hundred words of prose can carry and still be prose.
  67  #
  68  # Run 9e66bf84 ran at nine per hundred words across the article and 28 per
  69  # hundred in its worst section. Two is the density of writing that explains,
  70  # compares and decides rather than lists: a fact gets a clause of its own and
  71  # room for what it means. A 900-word article keeps around eighteen.
  72  #
  73  # Not a hard cap. It sets where the line starts; the operator moves it.
  74  CLAIMS_PER_HUNDRED_WORDS = 2.0
  75  
  76  # Below this the cut is not an editorial judgement, it is an empty article.
  77  # A short piece with a big dossier should still keep enough to write from.
  78  MIN_KEPT_CLAIMS = 8
  79  
  80  # How much of the keep-set is held for colour rather than proof.
  81  #
  82  # Ranking against the brief means ranking against the reader question, the
  83  # outcome and `fails_if`. Every one of those is a question about usefulness, so
  84  # a fact whose only job is to make a place feel like a place loses to a price
  85  # band every time. It is not that the ranker is wrong; it is that it was asked
  86  # one question and answered it.
  87  #
  88  # Measured on the ceviche run 8a7e9aa4: 23 texture claims in the dossier, two
  89  # selected. The best line in the whole run -- Canta Rana's dining room is
  90  # bare-bones and covered in football flags because the owner is Argentine --
  91  # ranked 59th of 151 and was cut. The article that came out was accurate,
  92  # useful and had nothing in it anybody would repeat to a friend.
  93  #
  94  # A fifth, because texture is seasoning. A piece that is one-fifth colour reads
  95  # as written by a person; one that is half colour has stopped answering the
  96  # question it was commissioned to answer.
  97  TEXTURE_SHARE = 0.2
  98  
  99  # One call each, and they read the same claim texts the writer would have. The
 100  # ceiling is generous because the input scales with the dossier.
 101  DEDUPE_MAX_TOKENS = 8_000
 102  RANK_MAX_TOKENS = 8_000
 103  
 104  
 105  def texture_claim_ids(
 106      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder, evidence: EvidencePackage
 107  ) -> set[str]:
 108      """Claims whose only job is colour.
 109  
 110      A claim that also answers a load-bearing question is doing load-bearing
 111      work, whatever else it does, so only claims serving texture questions
 112      exclusively are counted here. The work order already draws this line and
 113      coverage already refuses a run with no texture answered; selection was the
 114      one stage that could not see it.
 115      """
 116      kinds = {item.requirement_id: item.kind for item in work_order.requirements}
 117      return {
 118          claim.claim_id
 119          for claim in evidence.claims
 120          if claim.requirement_ids
 121          and all(kinds.get(item) == "texture" for item in claim.requirement_ids)
 122      }
 123  
 124  
 125  def article_fact_budget(target_word_count: int) -> int:
 126      """How many facts an article this long has room for, before any dossier.
 127  
 128      Split out of `target_claim_count` because the number is needed twice, at
 129      opposite ends of the run. Selection needs it against a dossier it can
 130      count. The research planner needs it before a single question has been
 131      asked, and there is nothing to count yet -- which is exactly the gap that
 132      let run e23257c0 buy 57 questions, find 431 facts, and hand the writer the
 133      same eighteen a 15-question run handed it.
 134  
 135      Two definitions of "how many facts fit" would drift, and the one the
 136      planner reads would be the one nobody checked.
 137      """
 138      return max(
 139          MIN_KEPT_CLAIMS,
 140          int(round(max(0, target_word_count) * CLAIMS_PER_HUNDRED_WORDS / 100)),
 141      )
 142  
 143  
 144  def target_claim_count(target_word_count: int, available: int) -> int:
 145      """Where the cut line starts, from the length the article is aiming at.
 146  
 147      Derived rather than fixed, so it scales: a 2,500-word piece is allowed more
 148      facts than a 400-word one, and the same constant explains both.
 149      """
 150      if available <= MIN_KEPT_CLAIMS:
 151          return available
 152      return min(available, article_fact_budget(target_word_count))
 153  
 154  
 155  DEDUPE_SCHEMA = require_non_empty({
 156      "type": "object",
 157      "properties": {
 158          "groups": {
 159              "type": "array",
 160              "items": {
 161                  "type": "object",
 162                  "properties": {
 163                      "keep": {"type": "string"},
 164                      "same_as": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
 165                      "why": {"type": "string"},
 166                  },
 167                  "required": ["keep", "same_as"],
 168              },
 169          },
 170      },
 171      "required": ["groups"],
 172  })
 173  
 174  FOLD_SCHEMA = require_non_empty({
 175      "type": "object",
 176      "properties": {
 177          "groups": {
 178              "type": "array",
 179              "items": {
 180                  "type": "object",
 181                  "properties": {
 182                      "general": {"type": "string"},
 183                      "restatements": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
 184                      "attribute": {"type": "string"},
 185                  },
 186                  "required": ["general", "restatements"],
 187              },
 188          },
 189      },
 190      "required": ["groups"],
 191  })
 192  
 193  FOLD_MAX_TOKENS = 8_000
 194  
 195  # What a fact is for in the finished piece. Editorial roles, and deliberately
 196  # not the work order's question kinds: a load-bearing question can produce a
 197  # fact whose job in the article is colour, and a texture question can produce
 198  # the one price the reader needs.
 199  #
 200  # They travel to the outline, which groups its sections on them, and to the
 201  # picker, which shows the operator what each fact is doing. Nothing gates on
 202  # them: a role is a description, and a wrong one costs a fact its heading, not
 203  # its place in the article.
 204  PACKET_ROLES = ("backbone", "practical", "texture")
 205  
 206  RANK_SCHEMA = require_non_empty({
 207      "type": "object",
 208      "properties": {
 209          "ranked": {
 210              "type": "array",
 211              "items": {
 212                  "type": "object",
 213                  "properties": {
 214                      "claim_id": {"type": "string"},
 215                      "why": {"type": "string"},
 216                      # Not required, and deliberately not an enum. The shape
 217                      # check runs over the whole response after generation and
 218                      # raises on the first value outside an enum, so one row
 219                      # labelled `vibes` would throw away the entire ranking --
 220                      # and an unranked list keeps every fact, which is the
 221                      # failure this module exists to prevent. The allowed values
 222                      # are in the prompt, and `_rank` discards anything else.
 223                      # A description for a person and a heading for the outline
 224                      # is not worth an article's worth of facts.
 225                      "role": {"type": "string"},
 226                  },
 227                  "required": ["claim_id"],
 228              },
 229          },
 230      },
 231      "required": ["ranked"],
 232  })
 233  
 234  
 235  def handles(claims: list[Any]) -> tuple[dict[str, str], dict[str, str]]:
 236      """Short names for the prompt, and the map back to real claim ids.
 237  
 238      Claim ids are namespaced by the question that produced them, so they run to
 239      76 characters -- `req_neighbourhood_chifa_characteristics:ncc_18`. Asked to
 240      copy a hundred of those, a model shortens them: the first real ranking came
 241      back correctly ordered, with good reasoning, and every id rewritten to
 242      `ncc_18` or invented outright as `clm_titi_name`. Not one of 102 matched,
 243      and the ranking was thrown away.
 244  
 245      This is #499 again -- a model copies a short handle and the application
 246      restores the real value -- and the same answer works. The handle carries no
 247      meaning, so there is nothing in it to abbreviate.
 248      """
 249      to_handle = {claim.claim_id: f"f{index}" for index, claim in enumerate(claims, 1)}
 250      return to_handle, {handle: real for real, handle in to_handle.items()}
 251  
 252  
 253  def build_dedupe_prompt(evidence: EvidencePackage) -> str:
 254      """Group the claims that are the same fact. Nothing else."""
 255      to_handle, _ = handles(list(evidence.claims))
 256      claims = "\n".join(
 257          f"- {to_handle[claim.claim_id]} | {claim.text}" for claim in evidence.claims
 258      )
 259      return f"""\
 260  You are grouping research findings that say the same thing.
 261  
 262  The dossier below was gathered by several separate searches, so the same fact
 263  often arrives more than once in different words. Your only job is to say which
 264  claims are the same fact.
 265  
 266  CLAIMS
 267  {claims}
 268  
 269  Return strict JSON only:
 270  {{"groups": [{{"keep": "f1", "same_as": ["f7"], "why": "string"}}]}}
 271  
 272  Rules:
 273  - Only group claims asserting THE SAME FACT. Different wording, different
 274    ordering, or a different level of politeness is the same fact.
 275  - `keep` is the claim that states it best: the most specific, the most precise
 276    figure, the clearest sentence. You are choosing a survivor, not writing one.
 277    Never invent or rewrite claim text.
 278  - A SUMMARY AND ITS DETAILS ARE NOT DUPLICATES. "Seven dishes define the
 279    cuisine" and a claim describing one of those seven dishes are two different
 280    facts at two levels of zoom. Both may be worth keeping and that is not your
 281    decision. Leave them alone.
 282  - A general statement and a specific one are not duplicates. "Prices are low"
 283    and "a plate costs 15 soles" are different facts.
 284  - Two claims about different places, dates, times, prices, hours or people are
 285    never the same fact, however similar the sentence. Two opening times that
 286    differ by fifteen minutes are a disagreement, not a repetition.
 287  - Return only groups that actually contain a duplicate. A claim with no
 288    duplicate does not need a group of its own.
 289  - Use the labels above exactly as written (f1, f2, ...). Never invent a
 290    label, never shorten one, and never use any other name for a claim.
 291  - Every label you return must be one of the labels above, and no label may
 292    appear twice anywhere in your answer.
 293  """
 294  
 295  
 296  def build_fold_prompt(claims: list[Any]) -> str:
 297      """Group one fact restated item by item, and name the claim that covers all of it."""
 298      to_handle, _ = handles(claims)
 299      listed = "\n".join(f"- {to_handle[claim.claim_id]} | {claim.text}" for claim in claims)
 300      return f"""\
 301  You are finding one fact that the dossier states over and over, once per item.
 302  
 303  Research asks about each place separately, so a fare that is the same
 304  everywhere arrives as one claim per place. To a reader that is a single
 305  sentence. To the writer it looks like fifteen separate things to say, and the
 306  article ends up saying the fare fifteen times.
 307  
 308  CLAIMS
 309  {listed}
 310  
 311  Return strict JSON only:
 312  {{"groups": [{{"general": "f1", "restatements": ["f7"], "attribute": "fare"}}]}}
 313  
 314  Rules:
 315  - A group is ONE attribute, at ONE value, stated for several different items.
 316    "The fare is 200 across the network" with "Barón is 200", "Cordillera is
 317    200", "El Peral is 200" is a group. The general claim goes in `general` and
 318    the item-by-item ones go in `restatements`.
 319  - `general` MUST be a claim that already covers every item in the group. It is
 320    the claim a reader would accept on its own. If no claim in the dossier states
 321    the general case, DO NOT make a group: picking one item to stand for the rest
 322    would delete the others from the article.
 323  - A DIFFERENT VALUE IS NEVER A RESTATEMENT. If one item costs 300 where the
 324    rest cost 200, that item is the exception the reader needs most. Leave it
 325    out of the group and leave it alone.
 326  - Group only what is genuinely the same attribute. A fare and an opening time
 327    are two attributes, however alike the sentences look.
 328  - Never invent or rewrite claim text. You are naming which claim covers the
 329    others, not writing one.
 330  - Use the labels above exactly as written (f1, f2, ...). Never invent a label
 331    and never use a label twice anywhere in your answer.
 332  """
 333  
 334  
 335  def build_rank_prompt(
 336      brief: ArticleBrief,
 337      work_order: Prompt2BlogWorkOrder,
 338      claims: list[Any],
 339  ) -> str:
 340      """Order what survived by how much this particular article needs it."""
 341      to_handle, _ = handles(claims)
 342      listed = "\n".join(f"- {to_handle[claim.claim_id]} | {claim.text}" for claim in claims)
 343      return f"""\
 344  You are deciding which facts an article actually needs.
 345  
 346  Below is the brief the article was commissioned against, and the facts research
 347  found. Order the facts by how much THIS article needs them.
 348  
 349  THE ARTICLE
 350  Primary subject: {work_order.primary_subject}
 351  Core reader question: {brief.reader_question}
 352  The promise to keep: {brief.outcome}
 353  Spine: {brief.spine}
 354  Primary reader: {brief.reader.primary_reader}
 355  This piece fails if: {brief.fails_if}
 356  The seed it grew from: {brief.seed}
 357  
 358  THE FACTS
 359  {listed}
 360  
 361  Return strict JSON only:
 362  {{"ranked": [{{"claim_id": "f1", "why": "string", "role": "backbone"}}]}}
 363  
 364  Rules:
 365  - Most needed first. The fact the article cannot be written without goes at the
 366    top; the one it loses nothing by omitting goes at the bottom.
 367  - `role` says what this fact is FOR in the finished piece. Exactly one of:
 368      backbone  — the piece argues from it. Take it away and the spine does not
 369                  stand up: the thing that makes the case, establishes the
 370                  claim, or explains why any of this is so.
 371      practical — the reader acts on it. A price, an opening hour, an address, a
 372                  journey time, a booking rule; anything that changes what they
 373                  do next.
 374      texture   — it makes the place real. A named thing, an odd detail,
 375                  something a person did. It proves nothing and the piece is
 376                  worse without it.
