   3  P2B_V3_OUTLINE_PROMPT = """\
   4  You are a commissioning editor planning an article before it is written.
   5  
   6  Goal:
   7  Plan the sections that answer the approved brief using only the verified
   8  evidence records. Plan the structure only. Do not write the article.
   9  
  10  Return strict JSON only:
  11  {{
  12    "working_title": "string",
  13    "direct_answer_focus": "string",
  14    "sections": [
  15      {{
  16        "heading": "string",
  17        "reader_payoff": "string",
  18        "claim_ids": ["string"],
  19        "target_words": 0
  20      }}
  21    ],
  22    "takeaway_focus": "string",
  23    "brief_alignment": "string",
  24    "unsupported_requirements": ["string"]
  25  }}
  26  
  27  Rules:
  28  {structure_rules}
  29  - Headings must be specific and distinct. No generic "Introduction" or
  30    "Conclusion" headings.
  31  - Every section must earn its place. Two sections may not promise the reader
  32    the same thing; if they do, they are one section, or one of them has no
  33    reason to exist.
  34  - Every section must name the claim_ids it rests on, using IDs from the facts
  35    below. Never cite a claim that is not there: what you are shown is the whole
  36    desk, and a fact outside it is one a person decided this article does not
  37    need.
  38  - You are not obliged to place every fact. A section carrying more facts than
  39    it has words for is a list, not a section. Leave out what the piece is
  40    better without.
  41  - The primary subject controls the article. A context-only reference may
  42    calibrate a fact inside a section; it may never be what a section is about,
  43    and it may never appear as a heading subject.
  44  - Only an approved comparator may share comparison scope, and only when the
  45    scope mode allows it.
  46  - If the brief asks for something the evidence cannot support, list it in
  47    unsupported_requirements instead of planning a section that would need an
  48    invented fact.
  49  - target_words across all sections should total roughly the SECTION BUDGET
  50    below, which is already the target minus the opening and takeaways you
  51    do not plan. Do not subtract anything yourself.
  52  - brief_alignment must explain in one or two sentences how this structure
  53    answers the core reader question for the primary subject.
  54  
  55  {instructions}
  56  
  57  TARGET WORD COUNT (the whole article):
  58  {target_word_count}
  59  
  60  SECTION BUDGET (what your sections must total):
  61  {section_budget}
  62  """

  64  P2B_V3_COMPOSE_PROMPT = """\
  65  You are an expert editor writing a publish-ready article from verified evidence.
  66  
  67  Goal:
  68  Write the article the approved brief describes, using only the evidence
  69  records supplied.
  70  
  71  Return strict JSON only:
  72  {{
  73    "improved_title": "string",
  74    "improved_content": "string",
  75    "brief_alignment_summary": "string",
  76    "improvements_applied": ["string"],
  77    "remaining_gaps": ["string"]
  78  }}
  79  
  80  Hard rules:
  81  - Every figure, date, rule, price, duration, capacity, and named entity must
  82    trace to a fact you were given. Preserve its dates, units, geography, and
  83    the limits it states. General background a well-informed writer would state
  84    without looking it up needs no fact behind it, and it is also not where this
  85    article's value is.
  86  - Keep a limit that changes what the reader should do -- an as-of date, a
  87    season, a route only some operators run. Drop confidence language that
  88    changes nothing: no "it seems", no "arguably", no grading your own certainty.
  89  - Never invent a bridge fact, scene, quotation, experience, statistic, price,
  90    consensus, or practical detail. Follow the EVIDENCE DISPOSITION POLICY in
  91    the compose context exactly.
  92  - The evidence records are internal working material. Never cite them in the
  93    article: no claim IDs, no source IDs, no "(Source 1)", no numbered
  94    references of any kind. The reader cannot see them.
  95  - Never name the outlet, publication, site, or report a fact came from, and
  96    never attribute by its position in the records. Name an actor or institution
  97    only when it is part of the story itself -- the ministry that set a fare, the
  98    museum that publishes a price -- not because it is where the fact was found.
  99  - Keep the approved form, primary subject, scope mode, and reference roles. A
 100    context-only reference may calibrate a fact; it may never become a
 101    co-subject, a recurring section, a ranking, or a verdict.
 102  - Answer the core reader question and deliver the stated reader outcome.
 103  - Keep to the brief's spine, and name everything under must_name.
 104  - improved_content must not contain a `#` H1.
 105  {structure_rules}
 106  - Follow the STYLE DIRECTIVE exactly. Tone, length, and brand voice are
 107    requirements, not suggestions.
 108  - You are not obliged to use every fact you were given. A section that names
 109    ten things and judges none of them is a directory; three details you explain
 110    are worth more than ten you list, and the reader can only act on the ones you
 111    explained. Where the plan marks a fact as colour and droppable, dropping it
 112    is a decision you are allowed to make. What you may never drop is an
 113    obligation under must_name, or a limit that changes what the reader should
 114    do.
 115  - The "Room to work" line under a section is advice and never a maximum. One
 116    complicated fact can need more explaining than five simple ones, so the count
 117    cannot decide anything for you; it is there because you cannot otherwise see
 118    how much room the plan left you.
 119  - Follow the SECTION PLAN when one is provided: use its headings, in order, and
 120    hold each section to roughly its word budget. Depart from it only where the
 121    evidence makes a planned section unsupportable. Record that departure in
 122    remaining_gaps; never narrate missing research to the reader.
 123  - Write to the TARGET WORD COUNT below. The section budgets are how that total
 124    is spent, not a smaller target: half the count is unfinished, not short.
 125  
 126  TARGET WORD COUNT:
 127  {target_word_count}
 128  
 129  SECTION PLAN:
 130  {outline}
 131  
 132  {instructions}
 133  
 134  SEO-SAFE RULES:
 135  {seo_guideline}
 136  
 137  STYLE DIRECTIVE (REQUIRED):
 138  {style_directive}
 139  """

 142  P2B_V3_GROUNDEDNESS_PROMPT = """You are a fact-grounding checker for travel articles.
 143  
 144  Goal:
 145  Find statements in the draft that the evidence records do not support.
 146  
 147  Return strict JSON only:
 148  {{
 149    "grounded": true,
 150    "assessment": "string",
 151    "unsupported_claims": [
 152      {{
 153        "claim": "string",
 154        "reason": "string",
 155        "severity": "high|low"
 156      }}
 157    ]
 158  }}
 159  
 160  What counts as unsupported:
 161  - Any figure, date, rule, price, duration, capacity, or named entity that no
 162    claim in the records states.
 163  - A claim stated more confidently, more recently, or more broadly than the
 164    record it rests on. Check attribution, as-of dates, geography, units, and
 165    stated uncertainty against the record itself.
 166  - A conflict resolved in the prose that the records leave unresolved.
 167  - Safety, health, legal, or entry guidance the records do not establish.
 168  - Superlatives and rankings presented as fact.
 169  
 170  What does NOT count:
 171  - General background a well-informed writer would state without a source.
 172  - Uncertainty or qualification that the evidence record itself states.
 173  - Restatement or paraphrase of something a record does say.
 174  - Advice framed as judgement rather than fact.
 175  - Anything the SUPPLIED MATERIAL below covers, within the scope it states.
 176  
 177  First-hand material:
 178  The writer was given the material below by the person commissioning the
 179  article. It is their own experience, stated in their own words. It is not a
 180  web source and it was never sent to research, so no evidence record will
 181  mention it. Treat it as support, at the scope it states and no wider.
 182  - A statement resting on supplied material is supported, including a
 183    paraphrase that keeps its scope. "I waited 45 minutes on my visit" supports
 184    "the wait ran about forty-five minutes on a recent visit".
 185  - A statement that widens it into a general rule is NOT supported. The same
 186    material does not support "everyone waits 45 minutes" or "expect a
 187    45-minute wait".
 188  - Supplied material is experience, not a verified fact. Do not treat it as
 189    confirming, correcting, or overriding an evidence record. Where the two
 190    disagree, say so in `assessment`; do not resolve it and do not raise a
 191    claim purely because they differ.
 192  
 193  Rules:
 194  - severity is "high" when a reader could be misled into a booking, spending,
 195    legal, or safety decision. Otherwise "low".
 196  - Quote the claim as it appears in the draft.
 197  - grounded is true only when there are no high-severity unsupported claims.
 198  - `grounded: false` requires at least one high-severity entry saying why.
 199  - severity is exactly "high" or "low". No other value is accepted.
 200  - `assessment` is always a non-empty sentence, including when nothing is
 201    unsupported.
 202  - Do not rewrite the article.
 203  
 204  {evidence_disposition_policy}
 205  
 206  EVIDENCE RECORDS:
 207  {evidence_records}
 208  
 209  SUPPLIED MATERIAL (first-hand, from the commissioner):
 210  {supplied_material}
 211  
 212  DRAFT TITLE:
 213  {rewritten_title}
 214  
 215  DRAFT CONTENT:
 216  {rewritten_content}
 217  """

 219  P2B_V3_QUALITY_AUDIT_PROMPT = """You are a quality auditor for commissioned articles.
 220  
 221  Goal:
 222  Score the draft on brief fidelity, evidence discipline, form fit, and
 223  reader utility — and on whether it delivers the article the working title
 224  promised.
 225  
 226  Return strict JSON only:
 227  {{
 228    "overall_score": 1,
 229    "guideline_coverage_score": 1,
 230    "informativeness_score": 1,
 231    "originality_score": 1,
 232    "brief_adherence_score": 1,
 233    "seo_score": 1,
 234    "too_close_to_source": false,
 235    "word_count_estimate": 0,
 236    "constraint_checks": {{
 237      "audience_match": false,
 238      "tone_match": false
 239    }},
 240    "fails_if_quote": "string",
 241    "fails_if_why": "string",
 242    "unresolved_payoffs": [
 243      {{"heading": "string", "why": "string"}}
 244    ],
 245    "required_revisions": ["string"],
 246    "quality_summary": "string"
 247  }}
 248  
 249  Scoring rubric — overall_score estimates how much work a human editor still
 250  has to do before this article is publishable, not how many rules it obeyed:
 251  - 9-10: an exceptional starting draft. What remains is personalisation and a
 252    proofread. Nothing needs restructuring, no section needs re-researching, and
 253    no section has to be rewritten before it is useful to a reader.
 254  - 7-8: acceptable with edits. The structure holds, but at least one section
 255    needs rewriting, or leaves a decision it raised unresolved.
 256  - <=6: requires hard rewrite.
 257  
 258  Rules:
 259  - required_revisions must be specific and actionable.
 260  - Treat these as failures, not style notes: the article drifts from the
 261    approved form; a context-only reference organizes a section or earns a
 262    verdict; the core reader question goes unanswered; an exclusion is broken; a
 263    statement outruns the evidence record behind it.
 264  - guideline_coverage_score is fidelity to the approved brief and its
 265    article form.
 266  - The line under "The promise to keep" is what the reader was promised, and
 267    has not read the article yet. Judge the draft against that promise, not only
 268    against the brief. A brief can drift from the seed it came from, and a
 269    draft that follows a drifted brief faithfully is still the wrong
 270    article: "Where to eat in Lima right now" that names no restaurant, dish,
 271    price, or neighborhood has failed, however cleanly it executes its form.
 272    Where the draft answers a narrower or different question than the title
 273    promises, say so in required_revisions, name what the reader came for and did
 274    not get, and cap overall_score at 5.
 275  - originality_score is not a measure of tidiness. Wire copy is tidy. Score it
 276    on whether a person would choose to read this over the search results it was
 277    built from.
 278  - Mark too_close_to_source=true when phrasing or structure tracks an evidence
 279    record too closely.
 280  - Judge only audience_match and tone_match. Word count, paragraph length, CTA,
 281    and keyword presence are measured deterministically outside this prompt, so
 282    do not report them.
 283  - The line under "This piece fails if" is the operator's own definition of
 284    failure for this piece, written in their words before anything was
 285    researched. It is the one criterion nobody else can supply.
 286    Do not answer whether the draft avoids it. Answer with evidence:
 287    fails_if_quote is the sentence copied out of the draft, word for word, that
 288    walks into that line, and fails_if_why is one line saying how it does. If
 289    the draft does not walk into it, fails_if_quote is an empty string and
 290    fails_if_why says why the line does not apply. Copy the sentence exactly;
 291    the quote is checked against the draft, and a sentence that is not in it
 292    tells us the answer cannot be relied on.
 293    A quoted sentence also belongs in required_revisions, and it weighs on
 294    brief_adherence_score and overall_score the way any other failure of the
 295    brief does.
 296    Two runs walked into their own line and reported otherwise. 849ae5aa was
 297    told the piece fails if it "describes the projects in the present tense when
 298    nobody has confirmed they are still running", opened with "Hundreds of fog
 299    nets built in Lima are standing and functioning in 2026", and passed.
 300    b29d66b4 was told it fails if it walks the stalls one after another and
 301    never says which to go to, wrote a section this audit itself called an
 302    inventory, and still answered that the failure was avoided.
 303  - The line is freehand and it is not a gate. A sentence you cannot apply is a
 304    sentence you leave alone: return an empty quote and say so rather than
 305    inventing a reading of it.
 306  - Score honestly. A draft that merely avoids mistakes is a 7, not a 9. Being
 307    grounded, complete, and constraint-compliant is the floor this scale starts
 308    from, not what earns the top of it.
 309  - SECTION PROMISES below is what the plan said each section would leave the
 310    reader with. It is not yours to re-decide; your job is whether the draft
 311    delivered it. For every promise that the prose does not keep, add an entry
 312    to unresolved_payoffs naming that heading and one line on what is missing --
 313    what the reader was going to be able to decide, or understand, or have
 314    answered, and still cannot. Quote or paraphrase the specific gap; "does not
 315    fully deliver" is not an answer anybody can act on.
 316    A section that lays out options without saying what separates them -- what
 317    each is better and worse for, and who should choose which -- has covered its
 318    requirement without keeping its promise. Every unresolved payoff also
 319    belongs in required_revisions, and unresolved payoffs weigh on
 320    overall_score: a draft that leaves any of them open cannot score above 8.
 321    Where the promises list says none were recorded, return an empty
 322    unresolved_payoffs rather than inventing the promises you would have made.
 323  - A fact catalog is not coverage. Prose that walks a list of named items with
 324    their prices, hours, or figures attached, in sequence, without comparison or
 325    judgement, reads as a directory rather than an article. It can be entirely
 326    accurate and still leave the reader to do the work. Where a substantial
 327    section reads this way, cap overall_score at 7 and say which section and what
 328    comparison is missing.
 329  - The closing takeaways are scored on whether they compress the decisions the
 330    article supported. Takeaways that restate the body, or that surface a
 331    leftover fact the article never built on, cap overall_score at 8.
 332  - MEASURED CHECKS below are counted outside this prompt and are not opinions.
 333    While any of them is false, overall_score may not exceed 6, and the failure
 334    must appear in required_revisions. Length is a band with two edges: a draft
 335    at a third of its target length is not publishable, and neither is one that
 336    overruns the band. Never infer which way a length check missed -- when
 337    target_word_count_met is FAIL, `word_count_verdict` states the direction and
 338    the size of the miss, and your required_revisions must say the same thing it
 339    does.
 340  
 341  {instructions}
 342  
 343  STYLE DIRECTIVE (REQUIRED):
 344  {style_directive}
 345  
 346  GROUNDING VERDICT (authoritative on factual support):
 347  {grounding_verdict}
 348  
 349  MEASURED CHECKS (counted, not judged):
 350  {measured_checks}
 351  
 352  SECTION PROMISES (what the plan said each section would give the reader):
 353  {section_promises}
 354  
 355  DRAFT TITLE:
 356  {rewritten_title}
 357  
 358  DRAFT CONTENT:
 359  {rewritten_content}
 360  """
 361  
 362  P2B_V3_REPAIR_PROMPT = """You are running a repair pass on a commissioned article.
 363  
 364  Goal:
 365  Fix what the auditor flagged, by replacing only the sections that need it.
 366  
 367  Return strict JSON only:
 368  {{
 369    "improved_title": "string",
 370    "sections": [
 371      {{
 372        "section_id": "string",
 373        "text_hash": "string",
 374        "heading": "string",
 375        "content": "string",
 376        "claim_ids": ["string"]
 377      }}
 378    ],
 379    "brief_alignment_summary": "string",
 380    "improvements_applied": ["string"],
 381    "remaining_gaps": ["string"]
 382  }}
 383  
 384  How editing works here:
 385  - The article is listed below as a SECTION MAP. Return an entry only for a
 386    section you are actually changing. Every section you do not return is kept
 387    exactly as it is; you do not need to repeat it, and repeating it unchanged
 388    only risks damaging it.
 389  - Copy `section_id` and `text_hash` from the map exactly. An entry whose id is
 390    unknown, whose hash does not match, or which names the same section twice is
 391    discarded, and the section keeps its current text.
 392  - `content` is the full replacement body for that section, without its `##`
 393    heading line. `heading` changes the heading; omit it to keep the current one.
 394    The opening block has no heading — leave `heading` empty for it.
 395  - You cannot add a section, delete one, or reorder them. That is a planning
 396    decision and this pass does not hold the plan. Change length inside the
 397    sections that exist. `content` may not contain a `##` or `#` line of its own
 398    and `heading` may not span lines; an entry that does is discarded.
 399  - Only the sections under SECTIONS YOU MAY CHANGE are yours to change.
 400  - A revision that needs several sections moved together must return all of
 401    them. Do not fix half of a structural problem.
 402  
 403  Facts:
 404  - THE FACTS AVAILABLE below are the facts a person chose for this article.
 405    You may use any of them, including ones the first draft left out — that is
 406    the point of this list. Using a fact the draft omitted is not inventing one.
 407  - For every entry, `claim_ids` names the facts you added to that section which
 408    were not already in it. An id that is not on the list is rejected with the
 409    section.
 410  - You may not use anything else. No fact from anywhere but that list, and no
 411    detail you are filling in from your own knowledge.
 412  - Preserve every limitation attached to a fact you use. A caveat is what makes
 413    the fact true; dropping it turns a correct sentence into a confident wrong
 414    one, and nothing downstream can put it back.
 415  - Naming a claim id does not license a sentence that says more than the claim
 416    does. The draft is checked against the evidence again after this pass.
 417  
 418  Rules:
 419  - Resolve each required revision directly.
 420  - A revision that states a length change gives the direction and the number of
 421    words. Move that way. Never lengthen a draft asked to be cut, or cut one
 422    asked to be lengthened.
 423  - Do not change the brief: not the form, the primary subject, the scope mode,
 424    the reference roles, the approved scope, or the exclusions.
 425  - Apply the EVIDENCE DISPOSITION POLICY in the repair lock exactly, including
 426    deletion of every assertion under UNSUPPORTED CLAIMS. Delete them; never
 427    hedge, attribute, or label them.
 428  - Never promote a context-only reference, add a comparator, or broaden scope to
 429    satisfy a revision.
 430  - Never cite evidence records in the prose: no claim IDs, no source IDs, no
 431    numbered references, and no naming the outlet or publication a fact came
 432    from. An actor or institution in the story may be named; the reporter of it
 433    may not.
 434  
 435  REQUIRED REVISIONS:
 436  {required_revisions}
 437  
 438  UNSUPPORTED CLAIMS:
 439  {unsupported_claims}
 440  
 441  SECTIONS CONTAINING A FLAGGED CLAIM:
 442  {flagged_sections}
 443  
 444  SECTION MAP:
 445  {section_map}
 446  
 447  SECTIONS YOU MAY CHANGE:
 448  An entry for any other section is discarded and that section keeps its current
 449  text. This list is what the required revisions and the flagged claims actually
 450  point at; it is not a judgement about the rest of the draft.
 451  {editable_sections}
 452  
 453  PREVIOUS TITLE:
 454  {previous_title}
 455  
 456  PREVIOUS CONTENT:
 457  {previous_content}
 458  
 459  {facts}
 460  
 461  {instructions}
 462  
 463  STYLE DIRECTIVE (REQUIRED):
 464  {style_directive}
 465  """
apps/backend/app/features/prompt2blog/stages/v3/groundedness.py
   1  from __future__ import annotations
   2  
   3  from typing import Any
   4  
   5  from ...dependencies import PipelineDependencies
   6  from ...graph.state import Prompt2BlogV3GraphState
   7  from ...grounding_service import check_grounding
   8  from ...instructions_v3 import EVIDENCE_DISPOSITION_POLICY
   9  from ...observability import _append_stage_trace
  10  from ...packet_v4 import supplied_material_text
  11  from ...prompts.editorial_v3 import P2B_V3_GROUNDEDNESS_PROMPT
  12  
  13  def check_v3_groundedness(
  14      state: Prompt2BlogV3GraphState,
  15      dependencies: PipelineDependencies,
  16      *,
  17      stage: str,
  18      rewrite: dict[str, Any],
  19  ) -> dict[str, Any]:
  20      """Compare one draft against the exact evidence records.
  21  
  22      V2 compared a draft with cleaned source prose, which had already lost
  23      publisher, date, and qualification. V3 compares it with the records
  24      themselves, so an overstated date or a widened claim is visible.
  25  
  26      The checker also reads the first-hand material the writer was given
  27      (finding 01). Without it the two halves of the run were looking at
  28      different desks: compose could legitimately use "I waited 45 minutes" from
  29      the brief, and the checker, seeing no record of it, could only call it
  30      invented -- after which repair is instructed to delete it.
  31  
  32      The call, the one retry and the refusal of an unreadable verdict now live
  33      in `grounding_service`, so the post-writing editor can have the same
  34      judgement without running this stage for its side effects. What is left
  35      here is the side effects: this stage's prompt, its trace rows, its stage
  36      row.
  37      """
  38      run_id = state["run_id"]
  39      prompt = P2B_V3_GROUNDEDNESS_PROMPT.format(
  40          evidence_disposition_policy=EVIDENCE_DISPOSITION_POLICY,
  41          evidence_records=state["evidence"]["records_text"],
  42          supplied_material=supplied_material_text(state.get("packet")),
  43          rewritten_title=rewrite["improved_title"],
  44          rewritten_content=rewrite["improved_content"],
  45      )
  46      groundedness_model = state.get("groundedness_model")
  47  
  48      outcome = check_grounding(
  49          llm=dependencies.llm,
  50          prompt=prompt,
  51          job_id="p2b.groundedness",
  52          model_name=groundedness_model,
  53      )
  54  
  55      for record in outcome.attempts:
  56          _append_stage_trace(
  57              state["trace"],
  58              state["include_debug"],
  59              stage=stage,
  60              model_name=groundedness_model,
  61              input_payload=(
  62                  {"attempt": record.attempt} if record.raw_response or record.parsed
  63                  else None
  64              ),
  65              prompt=record.prompt,
  66              raw_response=record.raw_response or None,
  67              parsed=record.parsed,
  68              error=record.error or None,
  69              output=(
  70                  outcome.verdict
  71                  if record is outcome.attempts[-1] and not record.error
  72                  else None
  73              ),
  74          )
  75  
  76      groundedness = outcome.verdict
  77      if outcome.rejected:
  78          groundedness = {**groundedness, "rejected_responses": outcome.rejected}
  79  
  80      dependencies.recorder.record_stage(
  81          run_id,
  82          stage,
  83          {"groundedness": groundedness, "raw_response": outcome.raw_response},
  84      )
  85      return groundedness
  86  
  87  
  88  def run_v3_groundedness_stage(
  89      state: Prompt2BlogV3GraphState,
  90      dependencies: PipelineDependencies,
  91  ) -> dict[str, Any]:
  92      stage = "stage_v3_groundedness"
  93      dependencies.recorder.start_stage(state["run_id"], stage)
  94      groundedness = check_v3_groundedness(
  95          state,
  96          dependencies,
  97          stage=stage,
  98          rewrite=state["rewrite"],
  99      )
 100      return {"current_stage": stage, "groundedness": groundedness}

  17  # Share of secondary keywords that must appear before the check passes.
  18  SECONDARY_KEYWORD_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD = 0.6
  19  
  20  # must_include items are hard requirements, so the bar is near-total. The
  21  # per-item test is fuzzy (an item is a phrase, not a keyword), hence not 1.0.
  22  MUST_INCLUDE_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD = 0.9

  24  # The audit rubric calls 7-8 "acceptable with edits" and <=6 "requires a hard
  25  # rewrite". Repair therefore fires below 7, not at or below it.
  26  REPAIR_SCORE_THRESHOLD = 7

  29  # threshold, so a gap in the response is never itself a repair trigger.

  32  # The constraint checks an article must satisfy to ship. This is the single
  33  # list; `_should_run_repair` spends an attempt when one of these fails, and
  34  # `policies.evaluate_readiness` refuses to mark the run ready while one still
  35  # fails. Keeping both on the same tuple is what stops the gate that decides
  36  # "try again" and the gate that decides "ship it" from disagreeing -- finalize
  37  # used to check three of these and ignore the rest.
  38  #
  39  # `paragraph_length_met` is deliberately absent: it is a soft stylistic
  40  # preference, it never triggered repair, and promoting it to a blocker would
  41  # fail runs that nothing in the pipeline is able to fix.
  42  #
  43  # `target_word_count_met` was removed for the same reason plus a worse one
  44  # (#432, A16). A 4% overage is not a failure any editor would recognise, and
  45  # on the Lima run one four-word overage both capped the score below threshold
  46  # and raised a separate constraint failure -- the same miss counted twice, and
  47  # it bought a full regeneration of 1,041 words to trim forty.
  48  #
  49  # The measurement stays. A large miss is a symptom worth reporting, and
  50  # `word_count_severity` below says which kind of miss it is; it is simply no
  51  # longer a gate.
  52  HARD_CONSTRAINT_CHECK_KEYS = (
  53      "cta_present",
  54      "primary_keyword_present",
  55      "secondary_keywords_present",
  56      "must_include_covered",
  57      "claims_grounded",
  58  )
  59  
  60  # Keys `_build_constraint_checks` returns that are measurements, not pass/fail
  61  # verdicts. Every site that merges computed checks over the auditor's own
  62  # `constraint_checks` has to drop these, or a count lands in a dict whose
  63  # other values are booleans and reads as a check that failed. The sites used
  64  # to each carry their own filter -- one by name, one by `_coverage` suffix --
  65  # which meant a new measurement leaked into whichever list was not updated.
  66  CONSTRAINT_MEASUREMENT_KEYS = frozenset(
  67      {
  68          "word_count_severity",
  69          "word_count_estimate",
  70          "word_count_delta",
  71          "word_count_direction",
  72          "word_count_target_min",
  73          "word_count_target_max",
  74          "secondary_keyword_coverage",
  75          "must_include_coverage",
  76          # Sentence spread is measured and never gated. Every one of these has
  77          # to be listed or a count lands among booleans and reads as a check
  78          # that failed.
  79          "sentence_count",
  80          "sentence_mean_words",
  81          "sentence_stdev_words",
  82          "sentence_widest_band_share",
  83          "sentences_over_25_words",
  84          "sentences_under_8_words",
  85          "sentence_variety_note",
  86          # Repetition is measured and never gated, same as sentence spread.
  87          "repeated_sentence_pairs",
  88          "repeated_sentence_overlap",
  89          "repeated_sentence_note",
  90          # Sentence openings, same rule: reported so an operator can look at the
  91          # passage, never gated. A walking guide legitimately repeats place
  92          # names and a threshold here would fight the form.
  93          "opening_proper_noun_share",
  94          "opening_longest_same_kind_run",
  95          "opening_run_example",
  96          "opening_kinds",
  97      }
  98  )

 101  # The auditor is told "overall_score may not exceed 6" while a measured check
 102  # is failing, and it does not reliably obey: the Medellin run returned 10 with
 103  # a failing check in the same prompt. Asking a model to cap its own score is a
 104  # request; this is the enforcement. Only deterministic booleans count here --
 105  # the auditor's own `audience_match` / `tone_match` judgements are editorial
 106  # opinion and must not silently cap a score.
 107  MEASURED_CHECK_SCORE_CEILING = 6
 108  
 109  
 110  def enforce_measured_check_ceiling(
 111      quality: dict[str, Any], computed_checks: dict[str, Any]
 112  ) -> list[str]:
 113      """Clamp `overall_score` while any measured check is failing.
 114  
 115      Returns the failing check names so callers can report them.
 116      """
 117      failed = sorted(
 118          key
 119          for key, value in computed_checks.items()
 120          if isinstance(value, bool) and value is False
 121      )
 122      if failed:
 123          current = _safe_int(
 124              quality.get("overall_score"), default=MEASURED_CHECK_SCORE_CEILING
 125          )
 126          quality["overall_score"] = min(current, MEASURED_CHECK_SCORE_CEILING)
 127      return failed
 128  
 129  
 130  def _extract_narrative_focus(writing_brief: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
 131      editorial = _safe_str(writing_brief.get("editorial_instructions"))
 132      if editorial:
 133          return editorial
 134      goal = _safe_str(writing_brief.get("goal"))
 135      if goal:
 136          return goal
 137      # `perspective` is still read so briefs posted to the runtime endpoint
 138      # before the rename keep resolving.
 139      destination = _safe_str(writing_brief.get("destination_context")) or _safe_str(
 140          writing_brief.get("perspective")
 141      )
 142      return destination or "No additional narrative focus provided."
 143  
 144  
 145  # A brief asking for "flights to Lima" is satisfied by prose saying "flight to
 146  # Lima". Raw substring matching failed those, which drove keyword checks false
 147  # and bought a full repair rewrite for a plural.
 148  def _canonical_tokens(value: str) -> list[str]:
 149      tokens: list[str] = []
 150      for token in _tokenize_words(value):
 151          token = token.removesuffix("'s").rstrip("'")
 152          if len(token) > 4 and token.endswith(("ses", "xes", "zes", "ches", "shes")):
 153              token = token[:-2]
 154          elif len(token) > 3 and token.endswith("s"):
 155              token = token[:-1]
 156          if token:
 157              tokens.append(token)
 158      return tokens
 159  
 160  
 161  def _contains_phrase(text: str, phrase: str) -> bool:
 162      phrase_tokens = _canonical_tokens(phrase)
 163      if not phrase_tokens:
 164          return True
 165  
 166      text_tokens = _canonical_tokens(text)
 167      window = len(phrase_tokens)
 168      for start in range(len(text_tokens) - window + 1):
 169          if text_tokens[start : start + window] == phrase_tokens:
 170              return True
 171      return False
 172  
 173  
 174  # The width of the band that counts as "the same length". Five words apart is
 175  # close enough that a reader hears the same beat twice.
 176  SENTENCE_BAND_WIDTH = 5
 177  # Above this share of an article inside one band, the prose reads as metered.
 178  # The first article this pipeline produced sat at 0.57.
 179  SENTENCE_CLUSTER_SHARE = 0.45
 180  
 181  
 182  # Abbreviations whose full stop does not end a sentence. Without these a
 183  # splitter cuts "9:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m." into three, which is how one count of
 184  # the same article reached 68 units and another 59 -- and why no number from
 185  # either was worth reporting.
 186  _ABBREVIATIONS = (
 187      "a.m.",
 188      "p.m.",
 189      "e.g.",
 190      "i.e.",
 191      "etc.",
 192      "vs.",
 193      "approx.",
 194      "St.",
 195      "Mt.",
 196      "Av.",
 197      "No.",
 198  )
 199  
 200  
 201  def _sentences(content: str) -> list[str]:
 202      """Every sentence of prose, headings and list markers excluded.
 203  
 204      One splitter, shared by everything that counts sentences, because two
 205      splitters produce two different articles' worth of numbers from the same
 206      text and neither can be argued with.
 207      """
 208      body = "\n".join(
 209          line for line in content.splitlines() if not line.lstrip().startswith("#")
 210      )
 211      guarded = body
 212      for index, abbreviation in enumerate(_ABBREVIATIONS):
 213          guarded = guarded.replace(abbreviation, f"\x00{index}\x00")
 214      parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", guarded)
 215      sentences = []
 216      for part in parts:
 217          for index, abbreviation in enumerate(_ABBREVIATIONS):
 218              part = part.replace(f"\x00{index}\x00", abbreviation)
 219          part = part.strip().lstrip("*-\u2022 ").strip()
 220          if len(part) > 3:
 221              sentences.append(part)
 222      return sentences
 223  
 224  
 225  def _sentence_lengths(content: str) -> list[int]:
 226      """Word counts for every sentence of prose, headings excluded.
 227  
 228      A heading is not a sentence and counting it drags the numbers toward the
 229      short end of an article that is merely well sectioned.
 230      """
 231      return [len(_tokenize_words(part)) for part in _sentences(content)]
 232  
 233  
 234  def measure_sentence_openings(content: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 235      """How many sentences begin the same way. Reported, never gated.
 236  
 237      Run 95a74dce's article kept every surface anti-AI check at zero -- no em
 238      dashes, no stock phrasing, no brochure adjectives -- and still read as a
 239      machine wrote it, because almost every sentence opened by naming a place.
 240      Four in a row were `[Park name], [description]`. A human writer tires of
 241      their own rhythm; a model does not, and nothing here was counting.
 242  
 243      Deliberately not a threshold. A walking guide legitimately repeats place
 244      names, and an earlier "85% of sentences" figure came from an unspecified
 245      splitter that another splitter disagreed with. This reports the share and
 246      the longest run, and quotes the run so a person can look at the actual
 247      passage and decide.
 248      """
 249      sentences = _sentences(content)
 250      if not sentences:
 251          return {
 252              "opening_proper_noun_share": 0.0,
 253              "opening_longest_same_kind_run": 0,
 254              "opening_run_example": "",
 255              "opening_kinds": {},
 256          }
 257  
 258      kinds = [_opening_kind(sentence) for sentence in sentences]
 259      longest = current = 1
 260      longest_end = 0
 261      for index in range(1, len(kinds)):
 262          if kinds[index] == kinds[index - 1] == "proper_noun":
 263              current += 1
 264              if current > longest:
 265                  longest, longest_end = current, index
 266          else:
 267              current = 1
 268      example = ""
 269      if longest > 1:
 270          window = sentences[longest_end - longest + 1 : longest_end + 1]
 271          example = " ".join(window)[:400]
 272  
 273      counts: dict[str, int] = {}
 274      for kind in kinds:
 275          counts[kind] = counts.get(kind, 0) + 1
 276      return {
 277          "opening_proper_noun_share": round(
 278              counts.get("proper_noun", 0) / len(sentences), 3
 279          ),
 280          "opening_longest_same_kind_run": longest if longest > 1 else 0,
 281          "opening_run_example": example,
 282          "opening_kinds": counts,
 283      }
 284  
 285  
 286  _OPENING_FUNCTION_WORDS = {
 287      "the", "a", "an", "this", "that", "these", "those", "it", "its", "they",
 288      "there", "here", "you", "your", "we", "our", "i", "he", "she", "his", "her",
 289      "if", "when", "while", "after", "before", "from", "at", "on", "in", "for",
 290      "to", "by", "with", "about", "further", "continuing", "starting", "walking",
 291      "most", "many", "some", "several", "both", "each", "every", "no", "not",
 292      "and", "but", "or", "so", "because", "although", "though", "since",
 293  }
 294  
 295  
 296  def _opening_kind(sentence: str) -> str:
 297      """What kind of word a sentence starts with.
 298  
 299      A capitalised first word is not evidence of anything -- every sentence has
 300      one. A proper noun opener is a capitalised word that is not a function word
 301      and not a bare pronoun, which is what "Parque Bernales offers..." is and
 302      "The path continues..." is not.
 303      """
 304      words = sentence.split()
 305      if not words:
 306          return "other"
 307      first = words[0].strip("\"'\u201c\u2018([")
 308      lowered = first.casefold().strip(".,;:")
 309      if not first:
 310          return "other"
 311      if lowered in _OPENING_FUNCTION_WORDS:
 312          return "function_word"
 313      if first[0].isdigit():
 314          return "number"
 315      if first[0].isupper():
 316          return "proper_noun"
 317      return "other"
 318  
 319  
 320  def measure_sentence_spread(content: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 321      """How varied the sentences are. Reported, never gated.
 322  
 323      The first article the v4 pipeline wrote averaged 11.3 words with 57% of its
 324      seventy five sentences inside a five word band and exactly one past 25. It
 325      read as accurate and mechanical, and nothing in the run said so, because
 326      nothing was counting. Once prose exists nothing blocks (ADR 0030), so this
 327      is a number the operator reads and acts on, not a gate.
 328  
 329      `sentence_widest_band_share` is the share of sentences inside the most
 330      crowded five word window. High is bad: it is the metronome, measured.
 331      """
 332      lengths = _sentence_lengths(content)
 333      if not lengths:
 334          return {
 335              "sentence_count": 0,
 336              "sentence_mean_words": 0.0,
 337              "sentence_stdev_words": 0.0,
 338              "sentence_widest_band_share": 0.0,
 339              "sentences_over_25_words": 0,
 340              "sentences_under_8_words": 0,
 341              "sentence_variety_note": "",
 342          }
 343  
 344      mean = statistics.mean(lengths)
 345      stdev = statistics.pstdev(lengths) if len(lengths) > 1 else 0.0
 346      busiest = max(
 347          sum(1 for length in lengths if start <= length < start + SENTENCE_BAND_WIDTH)
 348          for start in range(min(lengths), max(lengths) + 1)
 349      )
 350      share = busiest / len(lengths)
 351      long_ones = sum(1 for length in lengths if length > 25)
 352      short_ones = sum(1 for length in lengths if length < 8)
 353  
 354      note = ""
 355      if share >= SENTENCE_CLUSTER_SHARE or (long_ones == 0 and len(lengths) >= 20):
 356          note = (
 357              f"{round(share * 100)}% of sentences sit within {SENTENCE_BAND_WIDTH} "
 358              f"words of each other and {long_ones} run past 25. The prose will "
 359              "read as metered. Joining related facts into longer sentences is "
 360              "the fix; nothing here blocks."
 361          )
 362  
 363      return {
 364          "sentence_count": len(lengths),
 365          "sentence_mean_words": round(mean, 1),
 366          "sentence_stdev_words": round(stdev, 1),
 367          "sentence_widest_band_share": round(share, 3),
 368          "sentences_over_25_words": long_ones,
 369          "sentences_under_8_words": short_ones,
 370          "sentence_variety_note": note,
 371      }
 372  
 373  
 374  # Two sentences this close are the same sentence written twice. Set high on
 375  # purpose: a piece is allowed to restate its spine, and the cost of a wrong
 376  # accusation is an operator who stops reading these notes.
 377  #
 378  # Tuned against the twenty four stored articles rather than picked. Two fire:
 379  # 849ae5aa at 0.61, and a restaurant run whose five pairs each state the same
 380  # booking terms in two sections. The nearest thing below the line is 0.44 --
 381  # a stay-length figure given in the opening and again in its own section,
 382  # which is an article restating its spine and not a duplicate. The gap
 383  # between 0.58 and 0.44 is where this sits.
 384  REPEATED_SENTENCE_OVERLAP = 0.5
 385  # Below this many content words a sentence has too little of its own to
 386  # compare. "The nets are maintained by volunteers" shares almost everything
 387  # with any other short sentence about the nets.
 388  REPEATED_SENTENCE_MIN_WORDS = 7
 389  
 390  # Words that carry no subject of their own. A pair whose overlap is built out
 391  # of these is not a repetition.
 392  _FUNCTION_WORDS = frozenset(
 393      """a about above across after all also although among an and another any are
 394      around as at back be because been before being below between both but by
 395      came can come could did do does doing down during each either else even
 396      ever every few for from further get given go goes going got had has have
 397      having he her here hers herself him himself his how however if in inside
 398      into is it its itself just like made make many may me might more most much
 399      must my near need no nor not now of off on once one only onto or other our
 400      out over own per rather said same see seen several shall she should since
 401      so some still such than that the their theirs them themselves then there
 402      these they this those though through to too under until up upon us use
 403      used very was way we well were what when where whether which while who
 404      whom whose why will with within without would yet you your yours""".split()
 405  )
 406  
 407  
 408  def _content_words(sentence: str) -> set[str]:
 409      """What a sentence is about, minus the names it happens to share.
 410  
 411      A shared proper noun is not a duplicate: "Villa Maria del Triunfo" in six
 412      sentences is an article staying on its subject. Capitalised words after
 413      the first are dropped for that reason, along with the function words that
 414      every sentence carries.
 415      """
 416      names = {
 417          token.lower().strip(".,;:!?\u2019's")
 418          for token in sentence.split()[1:]
 419          if token[:1].isupper()
 420      }
 421      return {
 422          token
 423          for token in _canonical_tokens(sentence)
 424          if token not in _FUNCTION_WORDS and token not in names and len(token) > 2
 425      }
 426  
 427  
 428  # A bullet, a takeaway and an FAQ answer restate the body on purpose. Reading
 429  # those as duplicates would fire on every article with a takeaways block,
 430  # which is the wrong refusal this check cannot afford to make. Compare running
 431  # prose against running prose.
 432  _NOT_RUNNING_PROSE = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:>|[-*+]\s|\d+[.)]\s)")
 433  
 434  
 435  def _sections(content: str) -> list[list[str]]:
 436      """Prose sentences, grouped by the heading they sit under."""
 437      sections: list[list[str]] = [[]]
 438      for line in content.splitlines():
 439          if line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
 440              sections.append([])
 441              continue
 442          if _NOT_RUNNING_PROSE.match(line):
 443              continue
 444          sections[-1].append(line)
 445      grouped: list[list[str]] = []
 446      for block in sections:
 447          body = "\n".join(block).strip()
 448          if not body:
 449              continue
 450          grouped.append(
 451              [
 452                  part.strip()
 453                  for part in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", body)
 454                  if len(part.strip()) > 3
 455              ]
 456          )
 457      return grouped
 458  
 459  
 460  def measure_repetition(content: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 461      """The same sentence said twice, in two different sections.
 462  
 463      Run 849ae5aa opened with "over 600 collectors were built historically in
 464      the district of Villa Maria del Triunfo, currently, hundreds of these nets
 465      are actively maintained and functioning across Lima as a whole" and, two
 466      paragraphs later under its own heading, said it again almost word for
 467      word. In an 845 word article that is a noticeable share of the piece spent
 468      saying one thing twice, and nothing noticed: the run was stamped
 469      ready_for_staging with no blockers, and the post-hoc punch list caught it
 470      after the article was finished.
 471  
 472      A comparison, not a judgement, so it cannot invent anything. Advisory on
 473      the same reasoning as the bundled-question check: it is a heuristic, the
 474      operator is reading the article anyway, and a wrong refusal is worse than
 475      a missed duplicate. Nothing blocks after writing (ADR 0030).
 476      """
 477      sections = [
 478          [
 479              (sentence, _content_words(sentence))
 480              for sentence in section
 481              if len(_content_words(sentence)) >= REPEATED_SENTENCE_MIN_WORDS
 482          ]
 483          for section in _sections(content)
 484      ]
 485  
 486      worst = 0.0
 487      worst_pair: tuple[str, str] | None = None
 488      pairs = 0
 489      for index, section in enumerate(sections):
 490          for other in sections[index + 1 :]:
 491              for sentence, words in section:
 492                  for candidate, candidate_words in other:
 493                      overlap = len(words & candidate_words) / len(
 494                          words | candidate_words
 495                      )
 496                      if overlap < REPEATED_SENTENCE_OVERLAP:
 497                          continue
 498                      pairs += 1
 499                      if overlap > worst:
 500                          worst = overlap
 501                          worst_pair = (sentence, candidate)
 502  
 503      note = ""
 504      if worst_pair:
 505          note = (
 506              f"Two sentences in different sections share "
 507              f"{round(worst * 100)}% of their content words: "
 508              f"\u201c{_shorten(worst_pair[0])}\u201d and "
 509              f"\u201c{_shorten(worst_pair[1])}\u201d. Deliberate restatement "
 510              "is allowed and this does not block; where it is not deliberate, "
 511              "one of them is paying for words the article needs elsewhere."
 512          )
 513  
 514      return {
 515          "repeated_sentence_pairs": pairs,
 516          "repeated_sentence_overlap": round(worst, 3),
 517          "repeated_sentence_note": note,
 518      }
 519  
 520  
 521  def _shorten(sentence: str, limit: int = 90) -> str:
 522      collapsed = " ".join(sentence.split())
 523      if len(collapsed) <= limit:
 524          return collapsed
 525      return f"{collapsed[:limit].rstrip()}..."
 526  
 527  
 528  def _estimate_paragraph_sentence_average(content: str) -> float:
 529      # Headings are not paragraphs. They used to be counted as one-sentence
 530      # blocks, so every `##` dragged the average down and a well-sectioned
 531      # article measured far shorter than it reads -- which is exactly the
 532      # article the length profiles ask for.
 533      paragraphs = [
 534          block.strip()
 535          for block in re.split(r"\n\s*\n", content)
 536          if block.strip() and not block.lstrip().startswith("#")
 537      ]
 538      if not paragraphs:
 539          return 0.0
 540  
 541      sentence_counts = []
 542      for paragraph in paragraphs:
 543          count = len(re.findall(r"[.!?](?:\s|$)", paragraph))
 544          sentence_counts.append(max(1, count))
 545  
 546      return sum(sentence_counts) / max(1, len(sentence_counts))
 547  
 548  
 549  def _keyword_overlap_ratio(reference: str, text: str) -> float:
 550      ref_tokens = {token for token in _tokenize_words(reference) if len(token) > 3}
 551      if not ref_tokens:
 552          return 1.0
 553  
 554      content_tokens = set(_tokenize_words(text))
 555      overlap = ref_tokens & content_tokens
 556      return len(overlap) / len(ref_tokens)
 557  
 558  
 559  def _build_constraint_checks(
 560      title: str,
 561      content: str,
 562      writing_brief: dict[str, Any],
 563  ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 564      combined = f"{title}\n\n{content}".strip()
 565      word_count = len(_tokenize_words(content))
 566  
 567      formatting = writing_brief.get("formatting") or {}
 568      paragraph_length_pref = _safe_str(formatting.get("paragraph_length"))
 569      target_word_count = _safe_int(formatting.get("target_word_count"), default=0)
 570  
 571      # The check carries which way it missed, not just that it missed. As a bare
 572      # boolean it told the auditor "wrong length" and left the direction to be
 573      # guessed; on the Lima restaurant run the guess was "too short" against a
 574      # draft 363 words over the ceiling, and both repair passes made the article
 575      # longer still. `word_count_delta` is the distance outside the accepted
 576      # band, signed: positive is over the ceiling, negative is under the floor.
 577      target_word_count_met = True
 578      word_count_delta = 0
 579      word_count_direction = "within"
 580      word_count_target_min = 0
 581      word_count_target_max = 0
 582      if target_word_count > 0:
 583          tolerance = max(100, int(target_word_count * 0.1))
 584          word_count_target_min = target_word_count - tolerance
 585          word_count_target_max = target_word_count + tolerance
 586          if word_count < word_count_target_min:
 587              word_count_delta = word_count - word_count_target_min
 588              word_count_direction = "under"
 589          elif word_count > word_count_target_max:
 590              word_count_delta = word_count - word_count_target_max
 591              word_count_direction = "over"
 592          target_word_count_met = word_count_direction == "within"
 593  
 594      # How badly, not just whether. A handful of words either way is editing; a
 595      # third of the article missing is a symptom of thin research and should be
 596      # reported as one rather than as a length problem.
 597      word_count_severity = _severity(
 598          word_count_delta, word_count_target_min, word_count_target_max
 599      )
 600  
 601      avg_sentences = _estimate_paragraph_sentence_average(content)
 602      paragraph_length_met = True
 603      if paragraph_length_pref.lower().startswith("short"):
 604          paragraph_length_met = avg_sentences <= 2.5
 605      elif paragraph_length_pref.lower().startswith("medium"):
 606          paragraph_length_met = 2.5 <= avg_sentences <= 5.5
 607      elif paragraph_length_pref.lower().startswith("long"):
 608          # Bounded on both sides. This used to be `>= 5.0`, which is unbounded
 609          # above and turned the gate into a hard requirement for wall-of-text
 610          # paragraphs -- against the long profile's own instruction to keep
 611          # structure scannable. Length comes from more sections, not longer
 612          # blocks, so an article that stays readable must not fail the check.
 613          paragraph_length_met = 3.0 <= avg_sentences <= 6.5
 614  
 615      cta = _safe_str(writing_brief.get("call_to_action"))
 616      cta_present = _keyword_overlap_ratio(cta, combined) >= 0.35 if cta else True
 617  
 618      seo = writing_brief.get("seo") or {}
 619      primary_keyword = _safe_str(seo.get("primary_keyword"))
 620      primary_keyword_present = _contains_phrase(combined, primary_keyword)
 621  
 622      secondary_raw = seo.get("secondary_keywords")
 623      secondary_keywords: list[str] = []
 624      if isinstance(secondary_raw, list):
 625          secondary_keywords = [
 626              _safe_str(item) for item in secondary_raw if _safe_str(item)
 627          ]
 628  
 629      # Requiring every secondary keyword verbatim made the check fail on almost
 630      # any realistic keyword set, and repair is told to satisfy it "naturally" --
 631      # which is a direct instruction to keyword-stuff against the SEO guidance.
 632      secondary_keyword_coverage = 1.0
 633      if secondary_keywords:
 634          matched = sum(1 for kw in secondary_keywords if _contains_phrase(combined, kw))
 635          secondary_keyword_coverage = matched / len(secondary_keywords)
 636      secondary_keywords_present = (
 637          secondary_keyword_coverage >= SECONDARY_KEYWORD_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD
 638      )
 639  
 640      # must_include items are user-stated hard requirements. Nothing used to
 641      # verify them, so "must mention visa-on-arrival" was silently droppable.
 642      must_include = [
 643          _safe_str(item)
 644          for item in (writing_brief.get("must_include") or [])
 645          if _safe_str(item)
 646      ]
 647      must_include_coverage = 1.0
 648      if must_include:
 649          matched = sum(
 650              1 for item in must_include if _keyword_overlap_ratio(item, combined) >= 0.6
 651          )
 652          must_include_coverage = matched / len(must_include)
 653  
 654      # audience_match and tone_match are deliberately absent. They are semantic
 655      # judgements and belong to the quality auditor; the token-overlap heuristic
 656      # that used to compute them here overrode the model on the two questions it
 657      # is actually good at. See _audit_rewrite.
 658      return {
 659          "must_include_covered": must_include_coverage >= MUST_INCLUDE_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD,
 660          "must_include_coverage": round(must_include_coverage, 3),
 661          "target_word_count_met": target_word_count_met,
 662          "word_count_delta": word_count_delta,
 663          "word_count_direction": word_count_direction,
 664          "word_count_target_min": word_count_target_min,
 665          "word_count_target_max": word_count_target_max,
 666          "paragraph_length_met": paragraph_length_met,
 667          "cta_present": cta_present,
 668          "primary_keyword_present": primary_keyword_present,
 669          "secondary_keywords_present": secondary_keywords_present,
 670          "secondary_keyword_coverage": round(secondary_keyword_coverage, 3),
 671          "word_count_estimate": word_count,
 672          "word_count_severity": word_count_severity,
 673          **measure_sentence_spread(content),
 674          **measure_sentence_openings(content),
 675          **measure_repetition(content),
 676      }
 677  
 678  
 679  # Above this share of the target, a length miss stops being an edit and starts
 680  # being a symptom -- usually of thin research rather than of bad writing.
 681  LARGE_LENGTH_MISS_RATIO = 0.15
 682  
 683  
 684  def _severity(delta: int, lower: int, upper: int) -> str:
 685      """How badly a draft missed its band: `within`, `slight`, or `large`."""
 686      if not delta:
 687          return "within"
 688      target = (lower + upper) / 2 if upper > 0 else 0
 689      if target <= 0:
 690          return "slight"
 691      return "large" if abs(delta) / target > LARGE_LENGTH_MISS_RATIO else "slight"
 692  
 693  
 694  def word_count_revision_instruction(checks: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
 695      """The length revision, stated in words, or None when the length is fine.
 696  
 697      Repair used to receive whatever sentence the auditor wrote about length.
 698      The auditor was reading a boolean, so it could only guess a direction, and
 699      a wrong guess costs a full writing-model call plus the minutes it takes.
 700      This sentence is computed from the same counts the check is, so it cannot
 701      disagree with the check that triggered it.
 702      """
 703      if _safe_bool(checks.get("target_word_count_met"), default=True):
 704          return None
 705      direction = _safe_str(checks.get("word_count_direction"))
 706      delta = _safe_int(checks.get("word_count_delta"), default=0)
 707      word_count = _safe_int(checks.get("word_count_estimate"), default=0)
 708      lower = _safe_int(checks.get("word_count_target_min"), default=0)
 709      upper = _safe_int(checks.get("word_count_target_max"), default=0)
 710      if direction not in {"over", "under"} or not delta or upper <= 0:
 711          return None
 712  
 713      # A handful of words either way is not worth a writing-model call. The Lima
 714      # run spent 11,119 output tokens regenerating 1,041 words to trim forty,
 715      # and the keep-best safety net that caught the worse result afterwards is
 716      # not the bug -- needing one was.
 717      #
 718      # Derived here rather than read off the checks so this function stays
 719      # self-sufficient: it already has everything the judgement needs, and a
 720      # caller that assembles checks by hand should not be able to lose the
 721      # threshold by omitting a key.
 722      if _severity(delta, lower, upper) != "large":
 723          return None
 724  
 725      # Rounded to the nearest ten. A writer asked for "363 words" treats the
 726      # number as a target to hit exactly and pads or truncates to reach it.
 727      amount = max(10, abs(delta) // 10 * 10)
 728      band = f"{lower}-{upper} words"
 729      if direction == "over":
 730          return (
 731              f"Length: the draft is {word_count} words, roughly {abs(delta)} over the "
 732              f"{band} required for this article. Cut about {amount} words. Tighten "
 733              "prose, remove repetition and merge overlapping passages. Do not drop "
 734              "a required subject, a section, or a sourced fact to make the count."
 735          )
 736      return (
 737          f"Length: the draft is {word_count} words, roughly {abs(delta)} under the "
 738          f"{band} required for this article. Add about {amount} words by developing "
 739          "material the draft already covers. Never add a fact the evidence records "
 740          "do not contain, and do not pad with restatement."
 741      )
 742  
 743  
 744  # Words that mark a revision as being about how long the article is. Used to
 745  # drop the auditor's own length sentence when the deterministic one exists:
 746  # two length instructions in one list can point opposite ways, and that is the
 747  # bug this whole path was built to remove.
 748  _LENGTH_REVISION_TERMS = (
 749      "word count",
 750      "word target",
 751      "length",
 752      "expand",
 753      "lengthen",
 754      "shorten",
 755      "trim",
 756      "condense",
 757      "too short",
 758      "too long",
 759      "target_word_count",
 760  )
 761  
 762  
 763  def drop_length_revisions(revisions: list[str]) -> list[str]:
 764      """Remove revisions about length, keeping everything else in order.
 765  
 766      Only called when a computed length instruction is taking their place. The
 767      auditor is shown the direction now, but being shown it is not the same as
 768      obeying it, and a list holding both "cut about 360 words" and "expand the
 769      draft" leaves the repair model to pick. It picked wrong once already.
 770      """
 771      return [
 772          revision
 773          for revision in revisions
 774          if not any(term in revision.lower() for term in _LENGTH_REVISION_TERMS)
 775      ]
 776  
 777  
 778  def _sanitize_coverage(parsed: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
 779      missing_sections_raw = parsed.get("missing_sections")
 780      missing_sections: list[str] = []
 781      if isinstance(missing_sections_raw, list):
 782          missing_sections = [
 783              _safe_str(item) for item in missing_sections_raw if _safe_str(item)
 784          ]
 785  
 786      return {
 787          "coverage_sufficient": _safe_bool(
 788              parsed.get("coverage_sufficient"), default=False
 789          ),
 790          "analysis": _safe_str(parsed.get("analysis"))
 791          or "Coverage analysis not provided.",
 792          "missing_sections": missing_sections,
 793      }
 794  
 795  
 796  def _sanitize_rewrite(
 797      parsed: dict[str, Any],
 798      *,
 799      fallback_title: str,
 800      fallback_content: str,
 801  ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 802      improvements_raw = parsed.get("improvements_applied")
 803      improvements = []
 804      if isinstance(improvements_raw, list):
 805          improvements = [_safe_str(item) for item in improvements_raw if _safe_str(item)]
 806  
 807      remaining_raw = parsed.get("remaining_gaps")
 808      remaining = []
 809      if isinstance(remaining_raw, list):
 810          remaining = [_safe_str(item) for item in remaining_raw if _safe_str(item)]
 811  
 812      improved_title = _clean_title(_safe_str(parsed.get("improved_title")))
 813      improved_content = _safe_str(parsed.get("improved_content"))
 814      # The source blocks handed to compose are labelled "Source 1:", "Source 2:"
 815      # so the model can tell them apart, and it cited them back into the prose.
 816      # The prompts now forbid that; this is the half that does not rely on the
 817      # model having listened.
 818      improved_title, title_citations = strip_source_citations(improved_title)
 819      improved_content, content_citations = strip_source_citations(improved_content)
 820  
 821      return {
 822          "improved_title": improved_title or _clean_title(fallback_title),
 823          "improved_content": improved_content or fallback_content,
 824          "guideline_alignment_summary": _safe_str(
 825              parsed.get("guideline_alignment_summary")
 826          )
 827          or "Guideline alignment summary not provided.",
 828          "improvements_applied": improvements,
 829          "remaining_gaps": remaining,
 830          "source_citations_removed": title_citations + content_citations,
 831      }
 832  
 833  
 834  def _sanitize_quality(parsed: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
 835      required_revisions_raw = parsed.get("required_revisions")
 836      required_revisions = []
 837      if isinstance(required_revisions_raw, list):
 838          required_revisions = [
 839              _safe_str(item) for item in required_revisions_raw if _safe_str(item)
 840          ]
 841  
 842      # Only the semantic checks are read from the auditor. Word count, paragraph
 843      # length, CTA and keyword presence are measured deterministically in
 844      # _build_constraint_checks and overwrite anything the model claims, so the
 845      # prompt no longer asks for them.
 846      checks_raw = _safe_dict(parsed.get("constraint_checks"))
 847      checks = {
 848          "audience_match": _safe_bool(checks_raw.get("audience_match"), default=True),
 849          "tone_match": _safe_bool(checks_raw.get("tone_match"), default=True),
 850      }
 851  
 852      # Promises the plan made that the draft did not keep (improvement 01).
 853      # Each needs a heading and a reason: an entry naming neither is an
 854      # accusation nobody can act on, and repair would spend a call on it.
 855      unresolved_payoffs = []
 856      for item in parsed.get("unresolved_payoffs") or []:
 857          record = _safe_dict(item)
 858          heading = _safe_str(record.get("heading"))
 859          why = _safe_str(record.get("why"))
 860          if heading and why:
 861              unresolved_payoffs.append({"heading": heading, "why": why})
 862  
 863      # A missing or unparseable score used to default to 6, which sits below the
 864      # repair threshold -- so a malformed audit response silently bought a full
 865      # article rewrite. Absent scores now default to neutral and are reported as
 866      # incomplete, and _should_run_repair ignores the score signal entirely when
 867      # the audit did not actually produce one.
 868      audit_complete = _safe_int(parsed.get("overall_score"), default=0) > 0
 869  
 870      def _score(key: str) -> int:
 871          return max(
 872              1, min(10, _safe_int(parsed.get(key), default=NEUTRAL_QUALITY_SCORE))
 873          )
 874  
 875      return {
 876          "audit_complete": audit_complete,
 877          "overall_score": _score("overall_score"),
 878          "guideline_coverage_score": _score("guideline_coverage_score"),
 879          "informativeness_score": _score("informativeness_score"),
 880          "originality_score": _score("originality_score"),
 881          "brief_adherence_score": _score("brief_adherence_score"),
 882          "seo_score": _score("seo_score"),
 883          "too_close_to_source": _safe_bool(
 884              parsed.get("too_close_to_source"), default=False
 885          ),
 886          "word_count_estimate": max(
 887              0, _safe_int(parsed.get("word_count_estimate"), default=0)
 888          ),
 889          "constraint_checks": checks,
 890          # Evidence, not a verdict. `evaluate_fails_if` turns it into one by
 891          # checking the quote is really in the draft; a boolean asked for
 892          # directly was answered "avoided" on a draft the same response called
 893          # an inventory (run b29d66b4).
 894          "fails_if_quote": _safe_str(parsed.get("fails_if_quote")),
 895          "fails_if_why": _safe_str(parsed.get("fails_if_why")),
 896          # Kept as its own list as well as folded into the revisions. "How many
 897          # promises did this draft leave open" is the measure improvement 01
 898          # asks to track, and it is not recoverable from a flat list of
 899          # revision sentences.
 900          "unresolved_payoffs": unresolved_payoffs,
 901          "required_revisions": required_revisions,
 902          "quality_summary": _safe_str(parsed.get("quality_summary"))
 903          or "Quality summary not provided.",
 904      }
 905  
 906  
 907  class GroundednessMalformed(ValueError):
 908      """The checker answered, but not with a verdict anyone can read.
 909  
 910      Raised rather than normalised. The whole point of finding 02 is that a
 911      response nobody can read used to arrive downstream wearing a pass: `{}`
 912      became `checked: true, grounded: true`, and an article nothing had checked
 913      carried the stamp of one that had.
 914      """
 915  
 916  
 917  # The only two severities the prompt offers. A third value means the response
 918  # was not written against the contract, and guessing which one it meant is how
 919  # a high-severity finding becomes a low one.
 920  _GROUNDEDNESS_SEVERITIES = ("high", "low")
 921  
 922  
 923  def _groundedness_claims(parsed: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
 924      """Read the findings list, or refuse the whole response.
 925  
 926      One unreadable entry refuses everything. A findings list is a set of
 927      reasons a draft should not ship, and silently dropping the entry that
 928      could not be parsed shortens exactly that list.
 929      """
 930      claims_raw = parsed.get("unsupported_claims")
 931      if not isinstance(claims_raw, list):
 932          raise GroundednessMalformed("unsupported_claims is not a list")
 933  
 934      claims: list[dict[str, str]] = []
 935      for item in claims_raw:
 936          if not isinstance(item, dict):
 937              raise GroundednessMalformed("a finding is not an object")
 938          claim = _safe_str(item.get("claim"))
 939          if not claim:
 940              raise GroundednessMalformed("a finding names no claim")
 941          severity = _safe_str(item.get("severity")).lower()
 942          if severity not in _GROUNDEDNESS_SEVERITIES:
 943              raise GroundednessMalformed(f"unknown severity: {severity or 'missing'}")
 944          claims.append(
 945              {
 946                  "claim": claim,
 947                  "reason": _safe_str(item.get("reason")) or "Reason not stated.",
 948                  "severity": severity,
 949              }
 950          )
 951      return claims
 952  
 953  
 954  def _sanitize_groundedness(parsed: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
 955      """Read the grounding check, or refuse it.
 956  
 957      The audit scored `too_close_to_source`, the plagiarism direction. Nothing
 958      checked the opposite direction: claims in the draft that the sources do not
 959      support. For travel content -- visa rules, prices, safety guidance -- that
 960      is the more consequential failure.
 961  
 962      Every field the verdict rests on is required, because the alternative is
 963      the finding-02 behaviour: absence read as agreement. A response that fails
 964      any of these is a `GroundednessMalformed`, and the stage turns that into
 965      `unchecked` -- which readiness already treats as a blocker -- rather than
 966      into a pass.
 967  
 968      One normalisation survives, in the safe direction only: a response that
 969      says `grounded: true` while naming a high-severity finding is trusted on
 970      the finding. That keeps the finding on the record for repair to act on,
 971      and it cannot manufacture a pass. The other direction -- `grounded: false`
 972      with nothing to point at -- is refused, because a fail nobody can act on
 973      and a pass are the same thing by the time repair reads it.
 974      """
 975      if not isinstance(parsed, dict) or not parsed:
 976          raise GroundednessMalformed("empty response")
 977  
 978      grounded_raw = parsed.get("grounded")
 979      if not isinstance(grounded_raw, bool):
 980          raise GroundednessMalformed("grounded is not a boolean")
 981  
 982      assessment = _safe_str(parsed.get("assessment"))
 983      if not assessment:
 984          raise GroundednessMalformed("assessment is missing")
 985  
 986      claims = _groundedness_claims(parsed)
 987      high_severity = [claim for claim in claims if claim["severity"] == "high"]
 988      if not grounded_raw and not high_severity:
 989          raise GroundednessMalformed(
 990              "grounded is false but no high-severity claim explains why"
 991          )
 992  
 993      grounded = not high_severity
 994      return {
 995          "checked": True,
 996          "grounded": grounded,
 997          "status": "supported" if grounded else "unsupported",
 998          "assessment": assessment,
 999          "unsupported_claims": claims,
1000          "high_severity_count": len(high_severity),
1001      }
1002  
1003  
1004  def unchecked_groundedness(reason: str = "") -> dict[str, Any]:
1005      """Result used when the grounding check could not run, or could not be read.
1006  
1007      Treated as grounded so a checker outage degrades the signal rather than
1008      blocking the run, but recorded as unchecked so it is visible -- and
1009      readiness reads `checked`, so an unchecked draft is never called verified.
1010  
1011      `reason` says which of the two happened. "The provider failed" and "the
1012      provider answered with something unreadable" are different problems with
1013      different fixes, and the row that only says `checked: false` cannot tell
1014      them apart.
1015      """
1016      return {
1017          "checked": False,
1018          "grounded": True,
1019          "status": "unchecked",
1020          "assessment": "Grounding check did not run."
1021          if not reason
1022          else f"Grounding could not be completed: {reason}",
1023          "unchecked_reason": reason,
1024          "unsupported_claims": [],
1025          "high_severity_count": 0,
1026      }
1027  
1028  
1029  def looks_truncated(content: str, *, max_output_tokens: int) -> bool:
1030      """Did the model stop, or did the transport cut it off? (#432, A17)
1031  
1032      Output is capped, and a response that hit the cap is a transport failure,
1033      not a writing one. Repairing it as though the writer chose to stop early
1034      asks the wrong model to fix the wrong thing -- and the fix for a cap is a
1035      higher cap or a shorter plan, neither of which repair can do.
1036  
1037      Judged on two signals together, because either alone is noisy: the text is
1038      close to what the cap allows, and it does not end like finished prose.
1039      """
1040      if not content or max_output_tokens <= 0:
1041          return False
1042      # Four characters to a token, near enough to spot a ceiling.
1043      near_cap = len(content) >= max_output_tokens * 4 * 0.92
1044      stripped = content.rstrip()
1045      ends_cleanly = stripped.endswith((".", "!", "?", '"', "'", ")", "`"))
1046      return near_cap and not ends_cleanly
1047  
1048  
1049  # How much of a quoted sentence has to be found in the draft before the quote
1050  # counts as real. Not an exact match: a model that drops a comma or repairs a
1051  # dash has still located the sentence, and losing a true finding to punctuation
1052  # would be the worst way to fail.
1053  QUOTE_MATCH_THRESHOLD = 0.6
1054  # An auditor quoting the problem often quotes more than one sentence of it.
1055  QUOTE_MATCH_MAX_SENTENCES = 3
1056  
1057  
1058  def evaluate_fails_if(quality: dict[str, Any], content: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
1059      """Turn the auditor's quote into a verdict, or into a visible shrug.
1060  
1061      Three outcomes, and the third is the point:
1062  
1063      - No quote: the auditor says the draft does not walk into its failure
1064        line, and there is nothing to check.
1065      - A quote found in the draft: the failure is real and named, and the
1066        sentence is on the record for repair to work from.
1067      - A quote that is not in the draft: the answer cannot be relied on. It
1068        does not become a failure -- inventing one from an unverifiable quote is
1069        the same sin in the other direction -- but it is recorded as unjudged
1070        rather than banked as a pass.
1071      """
1072      quote = _safe_str(quality.get("fails_if_quote"))
1073      if not quote:
1074          return {
1075              "quote": "",
1076              "why": _safe_str(quality.get("fails_if_why")),
1077              "verdict": "avoided",
1078              "matched": "",
1079              "match_score": 0.0,
1080          }
1081  
1082      wanted = _content_words(quote)
1083      best, score = "", 0.0
1084      if wanted:
1085          # Windows of up to three consecutive sentences, because an auditor
1086          # quoting the problem often quotes two sentences of it. Scored against
1087          # a single sentence, a two sentence quote can never match anything and
1088          # a true finding is thrown away for spanning a full stop.
1089          for section in _sections(content):
1090              for start in range(len(section)):
1091                  for width in range(1, QUOTE_MATCH_MAX_SENTENCES + 1):
1092                      window = section[start : start + width]
1093                      if len(window) < width:
1094                          break
1095                      words = _content_words(" ".join(window))
1096                      if not words:
1097                          continue
1098                      overlap = len(wanted & words) / len(wanted)
1099                      if overlap > score:
1100                          best, score = " ".join(window), overlap
1101  
1102      found = score >= QUOTE_MATCH_THRESHOLD
1103      return {
1104          "quote": quote,
1105          "why": _safe_str(quality.get("fails_if_why")),
1106          "verdict": "walks_into_it" if found else "unjudged",
1107          "matched": best if found else "",
1108          "match_score": round(score, 3),
1109      }
1110  
1111  
1112  def _should_run_repair(quality: dict[str, Any], checks: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
1113      # Only trust the score when the auditor actually returned one.
1114      if _safe_bool(quality.get("audit_complete"), default=True):
1115          if quality.get("overall_score", NEUTRAL_QUALITY_SCORE) < REPAIR_SCORE_THRESHOLD:
1116              return True
1117      if _safe_bool(quality.get("too_close_to_source"), default=False):
1118          return True
1119  
1120      for key in HARD_CONSTRAINT_CHECK_KEYS:
1121          if not _safe_bool(checks.get(key), default=True):
1122              return True
1123  
1124      return False
