  45  # The measurements are deterministic and cheap, so they run before the audit
  46  # call rather than after it. The Lima food article scored 9/10 on every axis
  47  # while `target_word_count_met` was false at 388 words against a 1400 target:
  48  # the auditor could not have known, because the checks it was being scored
  49  # beside were merged into its answer after it had given one.
  50  #
  51  # The later Lima restaurant run failed the same check from the other side --
  52  # 1903 words against a 1260-1540 band -- and the auditor, reading a bare
  53  # boolean, wrote "expand the draft". Both repair passes obeyed and both were
  54  # discarded by keep-best. Hence the direction travels with the check.
  55  def _measured_checks_block(checks: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
  56      reported = {key: value for key, value in checks.items() if isinstance(value, bool)}
  57      if not reported:
  58          return "None measured."
  59      lines = [
  60          f"- {key}: {'pass' if value else 'FAIL'}"
  61          for key, value in sorted(reported.items())
  62      ]
  63      word_count = checks.get("word_count_estimate")
  64      if word_count is not None:
  65          lines.append(f"- word_count_estimate: {word_count}")
  66      # A failed length check without its direction is a coin flip for the
  67      # auditor, and it called the Lima run wrong: it read "too short" off a
  68      # draft 363 words over the ceiling and told repair to expand.
  69      if checks.get("target_word_count_met") is False:
  70          direction = checks.get("word_count_direction")
  71          delta = checks.get("word_count_delta")
  72          lower = checks.get("word_count_target_min")
  73          upper = checks.get("word_count_target_max")
  74          if direction in {"over", "under"} and delta:
  75              lines.append(
  76                  f"- word_count_verdict: {direction.upper()} the required "
  77                  f"{lower}-{upper} word band by {abs(int(delta))} words"
  78              )
  79      return "\n".join(lines)
  80

  82  def _audit_v3_rewrite(
  83      state: Prompt2BlogV3GraphState,
  84      dependencies: PipelineDependencies,
  85      rewrite: dict[str, Any],
  86  ) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any], str, str, dict[str, Any]]:
  87      computed_checks = _build_constraint_checks(
  88          rewrite["improved_title"],
  89          rewrite["improved_content"],
  90          v3_constraint_brief(state["brief"], state["option_context"]),
  91      )
  92      groundedness = state.get("groundedness") or unchecked_groundedness()
  93      prompt = P2B_V3_QUALITY_AUDIT_PROMPT.format(
  94          instructions=stage_context_text(state["stage_contexts"], "audit"),
  95          style_directive=_format_style_directive(state["option_context"]),
  96          grounding_verdict=_json(groundedness),
  97          measured_checks=_measured_checks_block(computed_checks),
  98          # What the plan promised, so the auditor compares the draft against a
  99          # written commitment instead of against whatever it would have planned
 100          # (improvement 01).
 101          section_promises=format_payoff_promises(_safe_dict(state.get("outline"))),
 102          rewritten_title=rewrite["improved_title"],
 103          rewritten_content=rewrite["improved_content"],
 104      )
 105      parsed, raw_response = dependencies.llm.invoke_json(
 106          job_id="p2b.audit",
 107          prompt=prompt,
 108          max_tokens=1536,
 109          temperature=0.05,
 110          model_name=state["audit_model"],
 111      )
 112      quality = _sanitize_quality(parsed)
 113      # A promise the draft did not keep is a revision request, whether or not
 114      # the auditor also wrote one. Repair reads `required_revisions` and nothing
 115      # else, so an unresolved payoff that stayed in its own list would be
 116      # recorded and never acted on.
 117      for unresolved in quality["unresolved_payoffs"]:
 118          instruction = (
 119              f"The section \"{unresolved['heading']}\" does not deliver what "
 120              f"the plan promised the reader: {unresolved['why']}"
 121          )
 122          if not any(unresolved["heading"] in item for item in quality["required_revisions"]):
 123              quality["required_revisions"].append(instruction)
 124      # The auditor answered with a quote; this is where that becomes a verdict.
 125      fails_if = evaluate_fails_if(quality, rewrite["improved_content"])
 126      quality["fails_if_check"] = fails_if
 127      quality["fails_if_avoided"] = fails_if["verdict"] != "walks_into_it"
 128      if fails_if["verdict"] == "walks_into_it":
 129          # Repair reads required_revisions, so the sentence has to be in there
 130          # whether or not the auditor remembered to put it there.
 131          revision = (
 132              f"The draft walks into the line the brief says it fails on. "
 133              f"Rewrite this sentence: \"{fails_if['matched']}\". "
 134              f"{fails_if['why']}".strip()
 135          )
 136          if not any(
 137              fails_if["matched"][:40] in item for item in quality["required_revisions"]
 138          ):
 139              quality["required_revisions"] = [
 140                  revision,
 141                  *quality["required_revisions"],
 142              ]
 143      quality_checks = {
 144          **quality.get("constraint_checks", {}),
 145          **{
 146              key: value
 147              for key, value in computed_checks.items()
 148              if key not in CONSTRAINT_MEASUREMENT_KEYS
 149          },
 150          "claims_grounded": groundedness["grounded"],
 151      }
 152      quality["constraint_checks"] = quality_checks
 153      # The prompt asks the auditor to cap itself at 6 while a measured check is
 154      # failing. The Medellin run returned 10 anyway. Enforce it here, where the
 155      # measurements are facts rather than a request.
 156      enforce_measured_check_ceiling(quality, computed_checks)
 157      quality["word_count_estimate"] = computed_checks["word_count_estimate"]
 158      # Repair reads this to state the length revision in words. It travels on
 159      # `quality` rather than in `constraint_checks`, which holds only verdicts.
 160      quality["word_count_check"] = {
 161          key: computed_checks[key]
 162          for key in (
 163              "target_word_count_met",
 164              "word_count_estimate",
 165              "word_count_delta",
 166              "word_count_direction",
 167              "word_count_target_min",
 168              "word_count_target_max",
 169          )
 170      }
 171      quality["secondary_keyword_coverage"] = computed_checks[
 172          "secondary_keyword_coverage"
 173      ]
 174      quality["groundedness"] = groundedness
 175      return quality, quality_checks, prompt, raw_response, parsed

 178  def run_v3_quality_audit_stage(
 179      state: Prompt2BlogV3GraphState,
 180      dependencies: PipelineDependencies,
 181  ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 182      stage = "stage_v3_quality_audit"
 183      run_id = state["run_id"]
 184      attempt = state.get("repair_attempts", 0)
 185      dependencies.recorder.start_stage(run_id, stage)
 186  
 187      rewrite = state["rewrite"]
 188      quality, checks, prompt, raw_response, parsed = _audit_v3_rewrite(
 189          state,
 190          dependencies,
 191          rewrite,
 192      )
 193  
 194      updates: dict[str, Any] = {
 195          "current_stage": stage,
 196          "quality": quality,
 197          "quality_checks": checks,
 198          # Read after the audit call, so the gate below judges the spend the run
 199          # has actually reached rather than the one it had before this stage.
 200          "tokens_spent": run_tokens_spent(dependencies.llm),
 201          # What the run has actually billed. The repair decision reads this;
 202          # tokens stay for the runaway ceiling and the receipt.
 203          "billed_cost_usd": run_billed_cost_usd(dependencies.llm),
 204      }
 205      if is_better_quality(quality, state.get("best_quality")):
 206          updates["best_rewrite"] = rewrite
 207          updates["best_quality"] = quality
 208          updates["best_quality_checks"] = checks
 209  
 210      # The same call the graph's conditional edge makes, on the same state, run
 211      # here only to record it. The audit is where the operator's "what is wrong
 212      # and what has this cost" answer belongs; the edge itself keeps no history.
 213      decision = decide_repair({**state, **updates})
 214      updates["repair_decision"] = decision.as_dict()
 215  
 216      dependencies.recorder.record_stage(
 217          run_id,
 218          stage,
 219          {
 220              "quality": quality,
 221              "raw_response": raw_response,
 222              "attempt": attempt,
 223              "repair_decision": decision.as_dict(),
 224          },
 225      )
 226      _append_stage_trace(
 227          state["trace"],
 228          state["include_debug"],
 229          stage=stage,
 230          model_name=state["audit_model"],
 231          input_payload={"attempt": attempt},
 232          prompt=prompt,
 233          raw_response=raw_response,
 234          parsed=parsed,
 235          output={"quality": quality, "repair_decision": decision.as_dict()},
 236      )
 237      return updates

 240  def _packet_claim_ids(state: Prompt2BlogV3GraphState) -> set[str]:
 241      packet = state.get("packet") or {}
 242      return {
 243          _safe_str(fact.get("claim_id"))
 244          for fact in (packet.get("facts") or [])
 245          if isinstance(fact, dict) and _safe_str(fact.get("claim_id"))
 246      }

 248  
 249  def _screen_section_edits(
 250      raw_sections: Any,
 251      *,
 252      allowed_claim_ids: set[str],
 253  ) -> tuple[Any, list[dict[str, str]]]:
 254      """Drop edits that cite a fact this article was not written from.
 255  
 256      Finding 03 gives repair the packet and permission to use it. The boundary
 257      that makes that safe is that the packet is the whole permission: an id
 258      from the wider dossier names a fact a person deliberately cut, and an id
 259      that names nothing at all is a fact the model supplied itself.
 260  
 261      An id is not proof the sentence means what the claim means -- grounding
 262      runs again on the assembled article for that. This only refuses the ones
 263      that cannot be checked at all.
 264      """
 265      if not isinstance(raw_sections, list):
 266          # Handed straight on rather than flattened to an empty list, so the
 267          # edit report says the response was the wrong shape instead of
 268          # reporting a repair that proposed nothing.
 269          return raw_sections, []
 270      kept: list[Any] = []
 271      rejected: list[dict[str, str]] = []
 272      for raw in raw_sections:
 273          record = _safe_dict(raw)
 274          cited = [
 275              _safe_str(item)
 276              for item in (record.get("claim_ids") or [])
 277              if _safe_str(item)
 278          ]
 279          unknown = sorted(set(cited) - allowed_claim_ids)
 280          if unknown:
 281              rejected.append(
 282                  {
 283                      "section_id": _safe_str(record.get("section_id")) or "(missing)",
 284                      "reason": f"cites facts outside the packet: {', '.join(unknown)}",
 285                  }
 286              )
 287              continue
 288          kept.append(raw)
 289      return kept, rejected

 292  def run_v3_repair_stage(
 293      state: Prompt2BlogV3GraphState,
 294      dependencies: PipelineDependencies,
 295  ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 296      """Repair the sections the auditor named, and only those.
 297  
 298      Two findings meet here. Repair no longer returns a whole article (06): it
 299      returns replacements for named sections, and the code applies them to the
 300      original document, so prose nobody complained about is the original bytes
 301      rather than a promise. And it can now reach the facts a person chose for
 302      this article (03), including the ones the first draft left out, which is
 303      what makes a revision like "support the comparison" answerable at all.
 304  
 305      The draft it produces is re-grounded and re-audited exactly as before.
 306      """
 307      stage = "stage_v3_repair"
 308      run_id = state["run_id"]
 309      rewrite = state["rewrite"]
 310      quality = state["quality"]
 311      attempt = state.get("repair_attempts", 0) + 1
 312      dependencies.recorder.start_stage(run_id, stage)
 313  
 314      groundedness = state.get("groundedness") or unchecked_groundedness()
 315      required_revisions = list(quality.get("required_revisions", []))
 316      # First, and computed rather than written by the auditor: a length miss is
 317      # the one revision the auditor cannot get wrong twice, because the counts
 318      # that failed the check are the counts that phrase the instruction.
 319      #
 320      # The auditor's own length sentence is dropped rather than kept alongside
 321      # it. The auditor is shown the direction now, but a list carrying both
 322      # "cut about 360 words" and "expand the draft" would leave repair to pick
 323      # between them, which is the original bug wearing a smaller hat.
 324      length_revision = word_count_revision_instruction(
 325          quality.get("word_count_check") or {}
 326      )
 327      if length_revision:
 328          required_revisions = [
 329              length_revision,
 330              *drop_length_revisions(required_revisions),
 331          ]
 332      unsupported_claims = list(groundedness["unsupported_claims"])
 333  
 334      previous_content = rewrite["improved_content"]
 335      sections = segment_article(previous_content)
 336      flagged = locate_claims(sections, unsupported_claims)
 337      # Worked out before the call, not after it. The claim-id screen refuses an
 338      # edit resting on a fact this article was not written from; nothing refused
 339      # an edit to a paragraph nobody complained about, so a pass asked to fix
 340      # one section could rewrite the opening and be applied for it.
 341      targets = resolve_repair_targets(
 342          sections=sections,
 343          required_revisions=required_revisions,
 344          flagged=flagged,
 345          article_wide=[length_revision] if length_revision else [],
 346      )
 347  
 348      prompt = P2B_V3_REPAIR_PROMPT.format(
 349          required_revisions=_json(required_revisions),
 350          unsupported_claims=_json(unsupported_claims),
 351          flagged_sections=_json(flagged) if flagged else "None located by quote.",
 352          section_map=section_manifest(sections),
 353          # The same list the screen enforces, so repair is not refused for
 354          # doing what it was asked.
 355          editable_sections=targets_block(targets, sections),
 356          previous_title=rewrite["improved_title"],
 357          previous_content=previous_content,
 358          facts=stage_context_text(state["stage_contexts"], "repair_facts")
 359          or "THE FACTS AVAILABLE TO THIS REPAIR\n- None recorded for this run.",
 360          instructions=stage_context_text(state["stage_contexts"], "repair_lock"),
 361          style_directive=_format_style_directive(state["option_context"]),
 362      )
 363      # Repair rewrites prose, so it runs on a prose model -- the writer's,
 364      # unless the route named a different one.
 365      #
 366      # Worth being separable from the draft: the two are not the same job. The
 367      # draft writes into an open space; repair is handed a list of required
 368      # revisions and has to satisfy them without breaking the rest, which is the
 369      # kind of work more reasoning effort actually pays for. It is also the
 370      # cheaper place to spend it, because it only runs on a draft that failed.
 371      repair_model = state.get("repair_model") or state["writing_model"]
 372      parsed, raw_response = dependencies.llm.invoke_json(
 373          job_id="p2b.repair",
 374          prompt=prompt,
 375          max_tokens=6144,
 376          temperature=0.1,
 377          model_name=repair_model,
 378          schema=REPAIR_SECTIONS_SCHEMA,
 379      )
 380      parsed_dict = _safe_dict(parsed)
 381      screened, cited_rejections = _screen_section_edits(
 382          parsed_dict.get("sections"),
 383          allowed_claim_ids=_packet_claim_ids(state),
 384      )
 385      screened, scope_rejections = screen_against_targets(screened, targets)
 386      edit = apply_section_replacements(previous_content, screened)
 387      edit_report = {
 388          **edit.as_dict(),
 389          "rejected": [
 390              *edit.as_dict()["rejected"],
 391              *cited_rejections,
 392              *scope_rejections,
 393          ],
 394          "section_count": len(sections),
 395          # On the record whether or not anything was refused. A pass that was
 396          # allowed the whole document because no revision could be located is
 397          # not describable afterwards as a targeted one.
 398          "targets": targets.as_dict(),
 399      }
 400  
 401      repaired = _sanitize_rewrite(
 402          {
 403              **parsed_dict,
 404              "improved_content": edit.content,
 405          },
 406          fallback_title=rewrite["improved_title"],
 407          fallback_content=previous_content,
 408      )
 409      # Which sections moved, from the applied edits rather than from a diff.
 410      # A pass that changed nothing is now a visible outcome instead of a draft
 411      # that looks repaired.
 412      touched = sections_changed(previous_content, repaired["improved_content"])
 413      # And the style cleanup edits sections too (finding 05), on the same model
 414      # that just wrote the text: this is another pass over it, not a separate
 415      # judgement. It is given the repair lock, so the caveats a repaired
 416      # sentence is carrying are visible to the pass tidying it.
 417      repaired["improved_content"], style_report = clean_up_style(
 418          repaired["improved_content"],
 419          dependencies=dependencies,
 420          job_id="p2b.repair",
 421          model_name=repair_model,
 422          max_tokens=4096,
 423          context="prompt2blog v3 repair",
 424          guard=stage_context_text(state["stage_contexts"], "repair_lock"),
 425      )
 426      _append_stage_trace(
 427          state["trace"],
 428          state["include_debug"],
 429          stage=stage,
 430          model_name=repair_model,
 431          input_payload={
 432              "attempt": attempt,
 433              "sections_touched": touched,
 434              "section_edits": edit_report,
 435              "style_cleanup": style_report,
 436          },
 437          prompt=prompt,
 438          raw_response=raw_response,
 439          parsed=parsed,
 440          output={"rewrite": repaired},
 441      )
 442      dependencies.recorder.record_stage(
 443          run_id,
 444          stage,
 445          {
 446              "repair_applied": edit.changed,
 447              "attempt": attempt,
 448              "rewrite": repaired,
 449              "required_revisions": required_revisions,
 450              "unsupported_claims": unsupported_claims,
 451              "section_edits": edit_report,
 452              "style_cleanup": style_report,
 453              "raw_response": raw_response,
 454          },
 455      )
 456      return {
 457          "current_stage": stage,
 458          # False when every proposed edit was refused. The run still continues
 459          # -- the existing draft is intact and saveable -- but the receipt does
 460          # not claim a repair that did not happen.
 461          "repair_applied": edit.changed,
 462          "repair_attempts": attempt,
 463          "rewrite": repaired,
 464      }
 465  
 466  
 467  def run_v3_quality_settle_stage(
 468      state: Prompt2BlogV3GraphState,
 469      dependencies: PipelineDependencies,
 470  ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 471      """Settle on the best-scoring draft the repair loop produced."""
 472      stage = "stage_v3_quality_settle"
 473      run_id = state["run_id"]
 474      dependencies.recorder.start_stage(run_id, stage)
 475  
 476      best_rewrite = state.get("best_rewrite") or state["rewrite"]
 477      best_quality = state.get("best_quality") or state["quality"]
 478      best_checks = state.get("best_quality_checks") or state["quality_checks"]
 479      rolled_back = best_rewrite is not state["rewrite"]
 480  
 481      settlement = {
 482          "repair_attempts": state.get("repair_attempts", 0),
 483          "repair_applied": state.get("repair_applied", False),
 484          "reverted_to_earlier_draft": rolled_back,
 485          "final_overall_score": best_quality.get("overall_score"),
 486          "last_overall_score": state["quality"].get("overall_score"),
 487          # Why the loop stopped here rather than repairing again. A settle that
 488          # came of an exhausted budget and one that came of a passing draft are
 489          # the same row without it.
 490          "repair_decision": state.get("repair_decision"),
 491      }
 492      dependencies.recorder.record_stage(run_id, stage, settlement)
 493      _append_stage_trace(
 494          state["trace"],
 495          state["include_debug"],
 496          stage=stage,
 497          output=settlement,
 498      )
 499      return {
 500          "current_stage": stage,
 501          "rewrite": best_rewrite,
 502          "quality": best_quality,
 503          "quality_checks": best_checks,
 504          # The grounding verdict travels with the draft it describes.
 505          "groundedness": best_quality.get("groundedness") or state["groundedness"],
 506      }
apps/backend/app/features/prompt2blog/stages/v3/repair_targets.py
   1  """Which sections repair is allowed to touch, decided before it is asked.
   2  
   3  Finding: `_screen_section_edits` refuses an edit that cites a fact outside the
   4  packet, and that is the only thing it refuses. Scope was left entirely to the
   5  prompt -- "change length inside the sections that exist", "resolve each
   6  required revision directly" -- and a pass that came back with a rewritten
   7  opening nobody complained about had its edit applied, because the opening's id
   8  was real and its hash was current.
   9  
  10  So the targets are worked out first, from what the audit and the grounding
  11  check actually named, and enforced in code afterwards. The prompt is told the
  12  same list, so repair is not being refused for doing what it was asked.
  13  
  14  Everything here is deterministic. Resolving a revision to a section by asking
  15  a model would be a second call on the stage that already costs the most, and
  16  it would put the scope decision back inside a response nobody can check.
  17  """
  18  
  19  from __future__ import annotations
  20  
  21  import re
  22  from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  23  from typing import Any
  24  
  25  from ...content.sections import ArticleSection
  26  from ...support import _safe_str
  27  
  28  # A revision quoting the draft is the common case and the reliable one: the
  29  # auditor is told to quote the sentence it objects to, and a quote can be
  30  # looked up rather than interpreted.
  31  _QUOTED = re.compile(r"[\"“”'‘’]([^\"“”\n]{8,200})[\"“”'‘’]")
  32  
  33  
  34  
  35  @dataclass(frozen=True)
  36  class RepairTargets:
  37      """The sections repair may change, and how that was decided."""
  38  
  39      allowed: frozenset[str]
  40      # "targeted" -- every revision resolved to named sections.
  41      # "article_wide" -- a revision that legitimately covers the whole draft.
  42      # "unresolved" -- nothing resolved, so the scope is not known.
  43      scope: str
  44      resolved: dict[str, list[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)
  45      unresolved: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
  46  
  47      def permits(self, section_id: str) -> bool:
  48          return section_id in self.allowed
  49  
  50      def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
  51          return {
  52              "scope": self.scope,
  53              "allowed_section_ids": sorted(self.allowed),
  54              "resolved_revisions": {
  55                  revision: list(ids) for revision, ids in self.resolved.items()
  56              },
  57              "unresolved_revisions": list(self.unresolved),
  58          }
  59  
  60  
  61  def _normalise(text: str) -> str:
  62      return " ".join(text.split()).casefold()
  63  
  64  
  65  def _sections_named_by(
  66      revision: str, sections: list[ArticleSection]
  67  ) -> list[str]:
  68      """The sections a revision points at, by quoted prose or by heading."""
  69      text = _normalise(revision)
  70      found: list[str] = []
  71      quotes = [_normalise(match.group(1)) for match in _QUOTED.finditer(revision)]
  72      for section in sections:
  73          haystack = _normalise(f"{section.heading} {section.body}")
  74          heading = _normalise(section.heading)
  75          hit = any(quote and quote in haystack for quote in quotes)
  76          # A heading has to be worth matching on. "Getting there" names a
  77          # section; a two-letter heading would match half the sentences in the
  78          # language and hand repair the whole document.
  79          if not hit and len(heading) >= 6 and heading in text:
  80              hit = True
  81          if hit:
  82              found.append(section.section_id)
  83      return found
  84  
  85  
  86  def resolve_repair_targets(
  87      *,
  88      sections: list[ArticleSection],
  89      required_revisions: list[str],
  90      flagged: dict[str, list[str]],
  91      article_wide: list[str] | None = None,
  92  ) -> RepairTargets:
  93      """Work out which sections this repair pass is for.
  94  
  95      `article_wide` names the revisions the caller already knows cover the whole
  96      draft -- in practice the length instruction, which this pipeline computes
  97      itself from the counts that failed the check. Passed in rather than
  98      recognised from its wording: the one revision whose meaning the code is
  99      certain of is the one the code wrote, and matching an auditor's prose for
 100      words like "throughout" would be guessing about the rest.
 101  
 102      `flagged` is what `locate_claims` found: sections holding a claim the
 103      grounding check called unsupported. Those are targets by definition -- the
 104      policy is to delete the assertion, and the section holding it is where.
 105  
 106      When nothing resolves, every section is allowed and the scope is recorded
 107      as `unresolved`. That is a deliberate choice over refusing the pass: an
 108      audit can raise a real problem with the whole draft -- it never answers
 109      what the reader came for -- that no quote and no heading will locate, and
 110      a repair that refuses those is a repair that only ever fixes the easy half.
 111      What it must not do is happen quietly, so the reason is on the run's
 112      record and the pass is not describable afterwards as targeted.
 113      """
 114      every = frozenset(section.section_id for section in sections)
 115      allowed: set[str] = set(flagged)
 116      resolved: dict[str, list[str]] = {
 117          section_id: ["a claim the grounding check refused"]
 118          for section_id in sorted(flagged)
 119      }
 120      unresolved: list[str] = []
 121      wide = {_normalise(item) for item in (article_wide or []) if _safe_str(item)}
 122      covers_everything = False
 123  
 124      for revision in required_revisions:
 125          text = _safe_str(revision)
 126          if not text:
 127              continue
 128          if _normalise(text) in wide:
 129              covers_everything = True
 130              resolved[text] = sorted(every)
 131              continue
 132          named = _sections_named_by(text, sections)
 133          if named:
 134              allowed.update(named)
 135              resolved[text] = named
 136          else:
 137              unresolved.append(text)
 138  
 139      if covers_everything:
 140          return RepairTargets(
 141              allowed=every,
 142              scope="article_wide",
 143              resolved=resolved,
 144              unresolved=unresolved,
 145          )
 146      if allowed:
 147          return RepairTargets(
 148              allowed=frozenset(allowed),
 149              scope="targeted",
 150              resolved=resolved,
 151              unresolved=unresolved,
 152          )
 153      return RepairTargets(
 154          allowed=every,
 155          scope="unresolved",
 156          resolved=resolved,
 157          unresolved=unresolved,
 158      )
 159  
 160  
 161  def screen_against_targets(
 162      raw_sections: Any, targets: RepairTargets
 163  ) -> tuple[Any, list[dict[str, str]]]:
 164      """Drop edits to sections this pass was not for.
 165  
 166      Runs beside the claim-id screen rather than replacing it. They refuse
 167      different things: that one refuses an edit resting on a fact the article
 168      was not written from, this one refuses an edit to a paragraph nobody
 169      complained about, and an edit can be either without being the other.
 170      """
 171      if not isinstance(raw_sections, list):
 172          return raw_sections, []
 173      kept: list[Any] = []
 174      rejected: list[dict[str, str]] = []
 175      for raw in raw_sections:
 176          section_id = _safe_str(
 177              raw.get("section_id") if isinstance(raw, dict) else ""
 178          )
 179          if not targets.permits(section_id):
 180              rejected.append(
 181                  {
 182                      "section_id": section_id or "(missing)",
 183                      "reason": (
 184                          "outside the sections this repair was for "
 185                          f"({targets.scope})"
 186                      ),
 187                  }
 188              )
 189              continue
 190          kept.append(raw)
 191      return kept, rejected
 192  
 193  
 194  def targets_block(targets: RepairTargets, sections: list[ArticleSection]) -> str:
 195      """What repair is told it may change, in the words of the section map."""
 196      if targets.scope == "article_wide":
 197          return (
 198              "Every section. A required revision changes the whole draft's "
 199              "length, which cannot be done inside one paragraph."
 200          )
 201      if targets.scope == "unresolved":
 202          return (
 203              "Every section. No revision named a particular one, so the scope "
 204              "of this pass could not be narrowed -- change as little as the "
 205              "revisions allow."
 206          )
 207      headings = {
 208          section.section_id: section.heading or "(opening)" for section in sections
 209      }
 210      lines = [
 211          f"- {section_id} {headings.get(section_id, '')}".rstrip()
 212          for section_id in sorted(targets.allowed)
 213      ]
 214      return "\n".join(lines) or "- (none)"
apps/backend/app/features/prompt2blog/policies.py
   1  """Pure gate decisions for the Prompt2Blog quality loop.
   2  
   3  These functions decide whether a draft is good enough, whether another repair
   4  attempt is worth spending, and whether a stage's output is an improvement on
   5  what it replaced. They hold no I/O and no prompt construction.
   6  """
   7  
   8  from __future__ import annotations
   9  
  10  import re
  11  from dataclasses import dataclass
  12  from typing import Any
  13  
  14  from .config import (
  15      P2B_AUGMENTATION_MIN_RETENTION_RATIO,
  16      P2B_REPAIR_ESTIMATED_TOKENS,
  17      P2B_REPAIR_MAX_ATTEMPTS,
  18      P2B_REPAIR_ESTIMATED_COST_USD,
  19      P2B_RUN_COST_BUDGET_USD,
  20      P2B_RUN_TOKEN_BUDGET,
  21  )
  22  from .quality import (
  23      HARD_CONSTRAINT_CHECK_KEYS,
  24      REPAIR_SCORE_THRESHOLD,
  25      _should_run_repair,
  26  )
  27  from .support import _safe_bool, _safe_dict, _safe_int, _safe_str, _tokenize_words
  28  
  29  
  30  @dataclass(frozen=True)
  31  class ReadinessVerdict:
  32      """Whether a finished run may be handed to staging, and why not if not."""
  33  
  34      ready: bool
  35      blockers: tuple[str, ...]
  36  
  37      def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
  38          return {"ready": self.ready, "blockers": list(self.blockers)}
  39  
  40  
  41  def evaluate_readiness(
  42      *,
  43      quality: dict[str, Any],
  44      checks: dict[str, Any],
  45      groundedness: dict[str, Any],
  46  ) -> ReadinessVerdict:
  47      """Decide whether a settled run is ready for staging.
  48  
  49      Finalize used to ask three questions -- word count, primary keyword,
  50      `groundedness["grounded"]` -- and shipped anything that answered yes. A
  51      4/10 article whose repair attempts had all failed still came back
  52      `ready_for_staging`, and so did a run whose grounding check had crashed,
  53      because the unchecked result reports `grounded: True` so that a checker
  54      outage degrades the run instead of blocking it.
  55  
  56      The blocker set is deliberately the repair loop's own trigger conditions
  57      plus the two failures repair cannot clear (an audit that produced no score,
  58      and a grounding check that never ran). Blocking on anything repair does not
  59      try to fix would mark runs `needs_revision` that the pipeline had no way of
  60      rescuing.
  61      """
  62      quality = _safe_dict(quality)
  63      checks = _safe_dict(checks)
  64      groundedness = _safe_dict(groundedness)
  65      blockers: list[str] = []
  66  
  67      # Absent rather than present is the safe default here. `unchecked_groundedness`
  68      # sets `checked: False, grounded: True`; reading `grounded` alone treats a
  69      # crashed checker as a pass.
  70      if not _safe_bool(groundedness.get("checked"), default=False):
  71          blockers.append("groundedness_unchecked")
  72      elif not _safe_bool(groundedness.get("grounded"), default=False):
  73          blockers.append("claims_ungrounded")
  74  
  75      if not _safe_bool(quality.get("audit_complete"), default=False):
  76          blockers.append("audit_incomplete")
  77      elif (
  78          _safe_int(quality.get("overall_score"), default=0) < REPAIR_SCORE_THRESHOLD
  79      ):
  80          blockers.append("quality_score_below_threshold")
  81  
  82      if _safe_bool(quality.get("too_close_to_source"), default=False):
  83          blockers.append("too_close_to_source")
  84  
  85      for key in HARD_CONSTRAINT_CHECK_KEYS:
  86          if not _safe_bool(checks.get(key), default=True):
  87              blockers.append(key)
  88  
  89      return ReadinessVerdict(ready=not blockers, blockers=tuple(blockers))
  90  
  91  
  92  def _length_distance(quality: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
  93      """How far outside its band a draft is, in words. Zero when inside.
  94  
  95      Keep-best used to compare pass/fail and nothing else, so a repaired draft
  96      four words over its ceiling and the original forty-one over looked
  97      identical -- the comparison called it a tie and the settle node restored
  98      the worse one. A tie on everything measurable is broken by which draft is
  99      actually closer.
 100      """
 101      checks = _safe_dict(_safe_dict(quality).get("constraint_checks"))
 102      return abs(_safe_int(checks.get("word_count_delta"), default=0))
 103  
 104  
 105  def _quality_rank(quality: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int]:
 106      """Rank a draft for keep-best comparison, validity before quality.
 107  
 108      Ranking on score alone let an unsafe draft win. A repair pass that fixed
 109      an invented visa fee but scored 8 lost to the ungrounded original scoring
 110      9, and the settle node restored the ungrounded one.
 111  
 112      So the ordering is: grounded first, then how many readiness blockers the
 113      draft carries, then the auditor's scores, and last -- only as a tie-break
 114      -- how far the draft is from its length band. The blocker count is read
 115      from `evaluate_readiness`, the same function finalize ships on, so a draft
 116      cannot rank first and then be refused at the gate for a reason ranking
 117      never looked at.
 118  
 119      Length is last on purpose. It is no longer a gate (#432, A16), and
 120      promoting it above the auditor's judgement would let a draft win for being
 121      the right size while being worse to read.
 122      """
 123      quality = _safe_dict(quality)
 124      groundedness = _safe_dict(quality.get("groundedness"))
 125      verdict = evaluate_readiness(
 126          quality=quality,
 127          checks=_safe_dict(quality.get("constraint_checks")),
 128          groundedness=groundedness,
 129      )
 130      grounded = _safe_bool(groundedness.get("checked"), default=False) and _safe_bool(
 131          groundedness.get("grounded"), default=False
 132      )
 133      return (
 134          1 if grounded else 0,
 135          -len(verdict.blockers),
 136          _safe_int(quality.get("overall_score"), default=0),
 137          _safe_int(quality.get("guideline_coverage_score"), default=0),
 138          -_length_distance(quality),
 139      )
 140  
 141  
 142  def is_better_quality(
 143      candidate: dict[str, Any],
 144      incumbent: dict[str, Any] | None,
 145  ) -> bool:
 146      """True when ``candidate`` should replace ``incumbent`` as the best draft.
 147  
 148      Repair used to overwrite the draft unconditionally, so a repair pass that
 149      scored worse than the draft it replaced still shipped. Ranking then ran on
 150      scores alone, so a safer draft could still lose to a higher-scoring unsafe
 151      one; see `_quality_rank`.
 152      """
 153      if not incumbent:
 154          return True
 155      return _quality_rank(candidate) > _quality_rank(incumbent)
 156  
 157  
 158  @dataclass(frozen=True)
 159  class RepairDecision:
 160      """Whether to spend a repair attempt, and everything that decided it.
 161  
 162      The gate used to answer with a bare "repair"/"settle" string, so a run that
 163      stopped short left no record of why: an operator reading a `needs_revision`
 164      article could not tell a draft the auditor had passed on from one the
 165      pipeline refused to keep paying for. The reason, the problems found, and
 166      the spend at the moment of the decision all travel together.
 167      """
 168  
 169      route: str
 170      reason: str
 171      problems: tuple[str, ...]
 172      attempts_used: int
 173      attempts_allowed: int
 174      tokens_spent: int | None
 175      tokens_per_attempt: int
 176      token_budget: int
 177      # What the run actually billed, and what one more attempt bills. Kept
 178      # beside the token figures rather than replacing them: tokens still say
 179      # whether a run is running away, money says whether it is worth continuing.
 180      billed_cost_usd: float | None = None
 181      cost_per_attempt: float = 0.0
 182      cost_budget_usd: float = 0.0
 183  
 184      def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
 185          return {
 186              "route": self.route,
 187              "reason": self.reason,
 188              "problems": list(self.problems),
 189              "attempts_used": self.attempts_used,
 190              "attempts_allowed": self.attempts_allowed,
 191              "tokens_spent": self.tokens_spent,
 192              "billed_cost_usd": self.billed_cost_usd,
 193              "cost_per_attempt": self.cost_per_attempt,
 194              "cost_budget_usd": self.cost_budget_usd,
 195              "tokens_per_attempt": self.tokens_per_attempt,
 196              "token_budget": self.token_budget,
 197          }
 198  
 199  
 200  def decide_repair(state: dict[str, Any]) -> RepairDecision:
 201      """Decide whether another repair attempt is worth spending.
 202  
 203      Three refusals, in the order they are cheapest to establish:
 204  
 205      1. The draft is good enough -- nothing to repair.
 206      2. The attempt allowance is used up. One automatic attempt, not two: the
 207         second was buying score points at a whole extra repair chain's price.
 208      3. The run has spent so much already that the next attempt would carry it
 209         past `P2B_RUN_COST_BUDGET_USD`. Refusing here is what makes a bad run's
 210         cost predictable instead of open-ended.
 211  
 212      That third check is in money, and only money that was billed. It used to be
 213      in tokens, which treated a Gemini Flash token and a subscription Claude
 214      token as the same currency -- and on both runs that finished, two thirds of
 215      the tokens were Claude drawing plan allowance rather than billing anything.
 216      Both were refused their repair while having spent $0.37. One shipped a
 217      wrong opening time and the other shipped six words over its word cap and
 218      was scored 6 for it; each was one repair call from being right.
 219  
 220      A run with no cost tracker (every test double) skips only the third check;
 221      it behaves exactly as it did before the budget existed.
 222      """
 223      quality = _safe_dict(state.get("quality"))
 224      checks = _safe_dict(state.get("quality_checks"))
 225      attempts = _safe_int(state.get("repair_attempts"), default=0)
 226      tokens_spent = state.get("tokens_spent")
 227      tokens_spent = (
 228          _safe_int(tokens_spent, default=0) if isinstance(tokens_spent, int) else None
 229      )
 230      cost_spent = state.get("billed_cost_usd")
 231      cost_spent = float(cost_spent) if isinstance(cost_spent, (int, float)) else None
 232      problems = evaluate_readiness(
 233          quality=quality,
 234          checks=checks,
 235          groundedness=_safe_dict(quality.get("groundedness")),
 236      ).blockers
 237  
 238      def verdict(route: str, reason: str) -> RepairDecision:
 239          return RepairDecision(
 240              route=route,
 241              reason=reason,
 242              problems=problems,
 243              attempts_used=attempts,
 244              attempts_allowed=P2B_REPAIR_MAX_ATTEMPTS,
 245              tokens_spent=tokens_spent,
 246              tokens_per_attempt=P2B_REPAIR_ESTIMATED_TOKENS,
 247              token_budget=P2B_RUN_TOKEN_BUDGET,
 248              billed_cost_usd=cost_spent,
 249              cost_per_attempt=P2B_REPAIR_ESTIMATED_COST_USD,
 250              cost_budget_usd=P2B_RUN_COST_BUDGET_USD,
 251          )
 252  
 253      if not _should_run_repair(quality, checks):
 254          return verdict("settle", "draft_passed_audit")
 255      if attempts >= P2B_REPAIR_MAX_ATTEMPTS:
 256          return verdict("settle", "attempt_limit_reached")
 257      if (
 258          cost_spent is not None
 259          and cost_spent + P2B_REPAIR_ESTIMATED_COST_USD > P2B_RUN_COST_BUDGET_USD
 260      ):
 261          return verdict("settle", "cost_budget_reached")
 262      return verdict("repair", "repairable_problems_found")
 263  
 264  
 265  def route_quality_gate(state: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
 266      """Decide whether to spend another repair attempt or settle on the best
 267      draft seen so far."""
 268      return decide_repair(state).route
 269  
 270  
 271  def _count_section_headings(content: str) -> int:
 272      return len(re.findall(r"(?m)^\s{0,3}#{2,6}\s+\S", _safe_str(content)))
 273  
 274  
 275  def evaluate_augmentation(
 276      *,
 277      original_content: str,
 278      augmented_content: str,
 279  ) -> tuple[bool, dict[str, Any]]:
 280      """Decide whether augmented content may replace the draft it augmented.
 281  
 282      Editorial augmentation is additive by contract: it inserts callouts and
 283      boxes into an existing article. Content that comes back materially shorter,
 284      or that has lost the article's section structure, is a regression rather
 285      than an augmentation and is rolled back.
 286      """
 287      original_words = len(_tokenize_words(original_content))
 288      augmented_words = len(_tokenize_words(augmented_content))
 289      original_headings = _count_section_headings(original_content)
 290      augmented_headings = _count_section_headings(augmented_content)
 291  
 292      retention_ratio = 1.0
 293      if original_words:
 294          retention_ratio = augmented_words / original_words
 295  
 296      checks = {
 297          "content_present": bool(_safe_str(augmented_content)),
 298          "retained_length": retention_ratio >= P2B_AUGMENTATION_MIN_RETENTION_RATIO,
 299          "retained_headings": augmented_headings >= original_headings,
 300      }
 301      diagnostics = {
 302          **checks,
 303          "retention_ratio": round(retention_ratio, 3),
 304          "original_word_count": original_words,
 305          "augmented_word_count": augmented_words,
 306          "original_heading_count": original_headings,
 307          "augmented_heading_count": augmented_headings,
 308      }
 309      return all(checks.values()), diagnostics
apps/backend/app/shared/prompts/anti_ai_tells.py
   1  """Anti-AI-tells voice guideline appended to prose-producing prompts.
   2  
   3  Two variants are defined; current usage:
   4  
   5  - ANTI_AI_TELLS_BLURB: appended for single-paragraph blurbs. In
   6    `editor_assist/listicle_writer.py` for listicle blurbs, gated per-category via
   7    `_voice_rules_block` (dining pilot from ADR 0003, extended to accommodations,
   8    attractions, and nightlife per ADR 0004). Also appended unconditionally to the
   9    itinerary stop-blurb day composer (`compose_itinerary_day_blurbs`) per ADR
  10    0021. Single-type listicle intros, key_location blurbs, and other listicle
  11    field types remain on the legacy path.
  12  
  13  - ANTI_AI_TELLS_FULL: wired into the itinerary intro composer
  14    (`compose_itinerary_intro`) per ADR 0021, and since extended to the other
  15    article-body composers: youtube2blog (compose, supplement, quality improve,
  16    SEO enrich, deep-expand, listicle rewrite, editorial augmentation), url2blog
  17    (rewrite/repair, length expansion, fact repair, editorial augmentation),
  18    prompt2blog (supplement, compose, repair, editorial augmentation), and the
  19    editor_assist block-rewrite. Anti-AI outputs are validated with
  20    `app.shared.text.validate_anti_ai_tells_markdown` and get one targeted repair
  21    retry instead of automatic dash-to-comma normalization.
  22  
  23  The blurb variant drops rhythm / summary / paragraph-structure rules that do
  24  not apply to a single 90-140 word paragraph.
  25  
  26  Both are written to be appended *after* any per-article-type guideline, with the
  27  precedence statement asserting they override conflicting instructions above.
  28  
  29  Two families in `_BANNED_CONSTRUCTIONS` are named as shapes rather than listed
  30  as strings (ADR 0030). A literal list only catches the variants someone thought
  31  to write down; naming the shape catches the ones they did not. Do not expand
  32  either family back into individual entries.
  33  """
  34  
  35  PRECEDENCE_HEADER = (
  36      "VOICE RULES (override any conflicting instruction above — if an earlier "
  37      "guideline asks for a quality these rules forbid, follow these rules)"
  38  )
  39  
  40  
  41  _BANNED_CONSTRUCTIONS = """\
  42  Banned constructions. Two shapes account for most of these. Learn the shape, \
  43  not the list: a variant is banned even when it is not written out below.
  44  
  45  THE CONTRASTIVE PIVOT — defining a thing by what it is not, or balancing it \
  46  against a counter-claim in the same breath. "It's not just X, it's Y." "More \
  47  than just a [noun]." "A working kitchen rather than a monument." "Not X, but \
  48  Y." "More X than Y." Bare "X, not Y" where Y is abstract or metaphorical ("its \
  49  own cuisine, not a hyphenated footnote"). "Feels both X and Y." "Deceptively \
  50  simple." The shape itself is the tell — rewording the metaphor does not fix \
  51  it. State the thing directly and drop the negation.
  52  
  53  THE KICKER THAT IMPLIES A PAYOFF — a closer that gestures at a reason instead \
  54  of giving it, leaving the reader to fill in the blank. "The line forms early \
  55  for a reason." "The seating to chase." "Lower-key than the price suggests." \
  56  "...which is why the 1pm seating fills first." "Special-occasion territory." \
  57  State the actual reason, name the thing plainly, or cut the sentence.
  58  
  59  Also banned, individually:
  60  - "quietly [adjective]" (quietly radical, quietly confident, quietly stunning)
  61  - "what happens when X meets Y" or "where X meets Y" or "the space between X and Y" — any phrasing that names an abstract interaction between two ingredients, techniques, or cultures instead of describing the result. Describe the result, not the interaction.
  62  - "in a world where..."
  63  - "the [noun] is [verb]-ing" sweeping openers (the city is changing, the menu is evolving)
  64  - "a masterclass in"
  65  - "punches above its weight"
  66  - "the kind of [noun] that..."
  67  - "effortlessly [adjective]"
  68  - "the most X you can Y" or "the X-est you can Y" superlative-of-experience ("the tightest fish you can eat in the city"). The shape sounds writerly and commits to nothing concrete. State what the place actually does, or cut the claim.
  69  - "set the bar," "raise the bar," "move the needle"
  70  - "speaks volumes," "speaks to"
  71  - "at its core," "at the heart of"
  72  - "testament to"
  73  - Compound mood adjectives of the form "[noun]-forward" or "[noun]-led" used to describe a room or program ("art-forward," "produce-forward"). Name the thing instead.
  74  - Strained-clever metaphors that sound good on first read and empty on second ("earn its seat at the table," "writes its own chapter"). If you cannot say the thing literally, do not say it figuratively.
  75  - Two-clause aphoristic closer with abstract nouns — short balanced clauses joined by semicolon, "and," or a comma, with both clauses ending in an abstract or metaphorical noun ("The room is the draw, and the food is the proof."). The parallel-with-abstract-noun shape is a strong signal even when each clause would be fine alone. Cut the symmetry or rewrite as two sentences with different shapes.
  76  - Clipped imperative sign-offs as a closer, whether they end the paragraph or trail a compound sentence as the second clause ("Book weeks out, ideally more." / "Go hungry."). Covers Book, Reserve, Order, Skip, Arrive, Sit, Come, Bring, Go, Stay, Treat. Either fold the practical note into a full sentence earlier, or drop it.
  77  - Any sentence ending in a tidy summary that restates the paragraph."""
  78  
  79  _BANNED_PERSONIFICATIONS = """\
  80  Banned personifications. Menus do not move, dance, weave, sing, or whisper. \
  81  Rooms do not breathe. Flavors do not converse. Dishes do not "do the talking," \
  82  "carry the conversation," "speak for themselves," "make the case," or "argue." \
  83  Food is not an orator. Cut all of these."""
  84  
  85  _SUPERLATIVE_WITHOUT_ANCHOR = """\
  86  Banned superlatives without anchors. Do not write "the smartest / sharpest / \
  87  finest / deepest / tightest / cleanest / leanest / most thoughtful / most \
  88  considered / most committed [wine list, sake program, cellar, beverage \
  89  program, by-the-glass, tasting menu, room, kitchen, pairing, cocktail \
  90  program]" without immediately naming the specific feature that earns the \
  91  claim. "Runs one of the smartest wine and sake programs on the continent" is \
  92  empty unless the next clause names the producers stocked, the by-the-glass \
  93  policy, the markup, the format, or a named sommelier choice. If the source \
  94  material does not support a specific anchor, drop the superlative and \
  95  describe the program with a concrete noun instead. Vague evaluative \
  96  superlatives are the structural opposite of editorial judgment — they sound \
  97  confident and commit to nothing."""
  98  
  99  
 100  _BANNED_HEDGES = """\
 101  Banned hedges and softeners. Cut: arguably, perhaps, somewhat, rather, quite, \
 102  fairly, genuinely, truly, really, simply, just, of course, indeed. Cut "it's \
 103  worth noting that," "it's important to remember," and any meta-commentary \
 104  about the writing itself."""
 105  
 106  # Every phrase the shared validator rejects has to be named here, or a writer
 107  # is judged against a rule it was never given (see
 108  # test_every_phrase_the_validator_rejects_is_named_in_the_prompt). That
 109  # coupling, not verbosity, is why this block is long: it is a phrase list with
 110  # prose around it. Restructured into four named moves rather than shortened.
 111  _BANNED_DISCLAIMERS = """\
 112  Banned disclaimers. Never write about the enquiry. The reader is here for the \
 113  place, not for how we found out about it. State what you know as a plain fact \
 114  and stop: "Customs took twenty five minutes" is the whole sentence. Do not \
 115  caveat a fact, attribute it defensively, date it as a shield, or explain how \
 116  it was established.
 117  
 118  Four moves are banned, in every wording.
 119  
 120  1. Telling the reader how much to trust a claim. Cut: "based on my own experience," "anecdotally," "at the time of writing," "your experience may vary," "this is one traveller's experience," "this is not an average," and any sentence whose job is to tell the reader how much to trust the previous one.
 121  
 122  2. Narrating a gap. Cut: "no official figures exist for," "there is no public data on," "figures could not be verified," "does not publish," "has not disclosed," "is not public information," "is not publicly available," "could not be confirmed." Where research could not establish something, write around it: never narrate the gap. Write what the subject does do, or say nothing.
 123  
 124  3. Letting the vocabulary of the research onto the page. No "sampled" booking flows or menus, no "data points," no "sample size," no "evidence records," and no grading your own confidence in a number ("an estimate rather than a guaranteed bill"). Give the number plainly or leave it out.
 125  
 126  4. Putting a publication between you and the claim. Cut: "sources report," "travel sources," "outlets anticipate," "one outlet," "the publication noted," "the report cited," "according to," "reports suggest." A named person or institution who acts in the story stays; the outlet that wrote it up does not.
 127  
 128  This bans hedging, not first person. In a piece written in first person, "I \
 129  waited twenty five minutes at customs" is the fact, told plainly, and it \
 130  stays. A date or a season belongs in the prose when the reader needs it to \
 131  act — a closure, a season, a change to the place itself — never as armour \
 132  around a claim. Accuracy is settled before the writing starts; it is not the \
 133  reader's problem."""
 134  
 135  _BANNED_ADJ_STACKING = """\
 136  Banned adjective stacking. No three-adjective lists ("warm, unfussy, and \
 137  inviting"). Pick one adjective and make it earn its place, or replace the \
 138  adjective with a noun or verb that shows the same thing."""
 139  
 140  _DICTION = """\
 141  Diction rules. Prefer short Anglo-Saxon words over Latinate ones — "use" not \
 142  "utilize," "show" not "demonstrate," "about" not "regarding." Cut "leverage," \
 143  "curate," "craft" (as a verb), "elevate," "showcase," "highlight," "navigate" \
 144  (when not literal)."""
 145  
 146  _NO_DASH_SUBSTITUTION = """\
 147  No em dashes, and no substitutes for them. A comma-bracketed aside is an em \
 148  dash in disguise: if you would have written "X — Y — Z", do not write "X, Y, \
 149  Z" instead. Asides like "arguing, convincingly, that" or "the room is warm, \
 150  and quietly so, throughout" get rewritten as one sentence with a subordinate \
 151  clause, or as two shorter sentences, or dropped. Reach for the subordinate \
 152  clause first: "the room is warm throughout, which is what makes the terrace \
 153  worth booking" keeps the thought whole and needs no dash. Splitting is the \
 154  last resort, not the house style. None of this bans long sentences: commas \
 155  joining clauses are correct and wanted, and what is banned is a comma standing \
 156  in for a dash around an aside. A spaced hyphen is the same dash in another hat \
 157  and reads as a typewriter artefact.
 158  
 159  Ration hyphenated compounds: roughly one per 200 words, so about four or five \
 160  in a full article. It is a budget and not a ban. Spend it where the hyphen is \
 161  the word rather than a shortcut — "stir-fried" is what the dish is, and \
 162  "cooked quickly in a wok" is a worse sentence written to dodge a rule. What \
 163  the budget exists to stop is the stack: "a well-known, family-run spot near \
 164  two-bedroom apartments on a long-stay visa" is one of the clearest signals the \
 165  text was generated, and every one of those is a modifier that could have been \
 166  a phrase. Rephrase those: "apartments with two bedrooms", "a visa for long \
 167  stays", "a spot the family runs, and people know it". Dates and measures are \
 168  the usual offenders and count the same — "19th-century", "six-month", \
 169  "10-kilometer". Proper names are free: "Aix-en-Provence" costs nothing."""
 170  
 171  _VOICE = """\
 172  Voice rules. Write from a single point of view with an opinion. If the writing \
 173  could have been produced by a committee that has never been to the place, \
 174  rewrite it. Take a side. Risk being wrong. AI prose is recognizable partly \
 175  because it never commits — every claim is balanced against its counter-claim \
 176  within the same sentence."""
 177  
 178  _SPECIFICITY_SOFTENED = """\
 179  Specificity rules. Every paragraph should contain at least one of: a proper \
 180  noun beyond the subject, a number, a named dish or object, a date or year, a \
 181  direct quote, or a physical detail that could only come from being there (a \
 182  smell, a texture, an awkward moment, a small failure) — IF the source \
 183  material supports it. Do not invent facts to satisfy this rule. If the source \
 184  is thin on anchors, prefer a shorter paragraph or merge with an adjacent one \
 185  rather than inventing a dish name, price, year, or quote. Generalizations \
 186  without anchors are the strongest AI signal, but fabricated anchors are worse."""
 187  
 188  # The trigger used to read "if three sentences in a row are 15-25 words". A
 189  # real article came back averaging 11.3 words with 57% of its sentences inside
 190  # a five word band, so the condition never fired once: it was written to catch
 191  # clustering at medium length and the piece clustered short. The rule watched
 192  # one wall of a room with two doors. The blurb version below already had the
 193  # better shape, and this now matches it.
 194  _RHYTHM = """\
 195  Rhythm rules. Vary sentence length aggressively. Clustering at ANY length is \
 196  the failure: sentences all sitting between 9 and 14 words read as generated \
 197  just as surely as all sitting between 15 and 25. Every section carries at \
 198  least one sentence under 8 words and at least one over 25, and three in a row \
 199  within five words of each other means the next one breaks the pattern hard.
 200  
 201  Length comes from subordination, not punctuation. Join clauses with because, \
 202  which, while, after, so that, and with relative pronouns. Where one fact \
 203  explains another, carry both in one sentence instead of lining them up one per \
 204  full stop.
 205  
 206  Parallel structure ("A and B, C and D") is fine once per paragraph, never \
 207  twice. Do not end paragraphs with a balanced two-clause summary line."""
 208  
 209  _SUMMARY_PATTERNS = """\
 210  Banned summary patterns. Do not open with a thesis sentence and close with a \
 211  restated thesis. Do not write "in conclusion," "ultimately," "all in all," or \
 212  any equivalent. End on a concrete detail or a specific recommendation, not a \
 213  sweeping verdict."""
 214  
 215  _BLURB_TRIADS = """\
 216  Triad rule. The rule of three (three nouns, three phrases, three clauses joined \
 217  "A, B, and C") may appear at most once in the blurb. Two triads in adjacent \
 218  sentences is the strongest single AI signal in this format — if you find \
 219  yourself writing a second one, collapse it to two items or split it into \
 220  separate sentences with different shapes."""
 221  
 222  _BLURB_RHYTHM = """\
 223  Blurb rhythm. The paragraph must contain at least one sentence under 10 words \
 224  and at least one over 25. If every sentence lands in the 14-22 word range, the \
 225  paragraph reads as AI. Do not close with a one-line afterthought; the final \
 226  sentence should carry as much weight as the lead."""
 227  
 228  _BLURB_NO_UNIFORM_KICKERS = """\
 229  Cadence rule. Do not end every sentence on a kicker — a small twist, a clever \
 230  inversion, a noun-phrase punchline, or a metaphorical aside. At least one \
 231  sentence in the blurb must be a flat factual statement that ends without any \
 232  twist at all (a date, a location, a fact, a number). The "clause, then kicker" \
 233  shape repeated across every sentence is the structural signature of AI prose, \
 234  even when each individual kicker would be fine in isolation. Vary how \
 235  sentences end, not just how long they are."""
 236  
 237  _FINAL_TEST = """\
 238  Final test. Read the draft as if aloud. If it sounds like every other piece of \
 239  competent writing on the internet, it is AI prose. The fix is almost always \
 240  more specificity and less symmetry."""
 241  
 242  
 243  ANTI_AI_TELLS_FULL = "\n\n".join(
 244      [
 245          PRECEDENCE_HEADER,
 246          _BANNED_CONSTRUCTIONS,
 247          _BANNED_PERSONIFICATIONS,
 248          _NO_DASH_SUBSTITUTION,
 249          _RHYTHM,
 250          _SPECIFICITY_SOFTENED,
 251          _BANNED_HEDGES,
 252          _BANNED_DISCLAIMERS,
 253          _SUMMARY_PATTERNS,
 254          _BANNED_ADJ_STACKING,
 255          _SUPERLATIVE_WITHOUT_ANCHOR,
 256          _DICTION,
 257          _VOICE,
 258          _FINAL_TEST,
 259      ]
 260  )
 261  
 262  
 263  ANTI_AI_TELLS_BLURB = "\n\n".join(
 264      [

 266          _BANNED_CONSTRUCTIONS,
 267          _BANNED_PERSONIFICATIONS,
 268          _NO_DASH_SUBSTITUTION,
 269          _BLURB_TRIADS,

 272          _SPECIFICITY_SOFTENED,
 273          _BANNED_HEDGES,
