   1  """What a person should fix by hand, once the article exists.
   2  
   3  A run ends with an article, a readiness stamp and some measurements, and
   4  nothing that says what to actually do about it. The gap was found by accident
   5  on 2026-09-01: after run 062c0b86 the owner asked what I thought of the output,
   6  and the resulting read -- what works, what is missing, what is buried -- was
   7  more useful than any mechanical check the run already produces. It named things
   8  no measurement in the system can see.
   9  
  10  So: a short ranked list of specific, placeable edits, for a person to spend
  11  twenty minutes on. Not for another model to rewrite the piece, and not to make
  12  the pipeline more perfect. `polish_v4` already assembles the paste-into-a-
  13  chatbot path; this is the other branch, where the operator edits it themselves.
  14  
  15  **The hard part is that it must never supply the missing fact.**
  16  
  17  Run 062c0b86 was titled "Lima Has a Pyramid Older Than the Inca Empire" and the
  18  article never gives a date. The tempting note is "add a sentence saying it
  19  dates to around 400 AD" -- a number invented at the last possible moment, after
  20  every evidence check in the pipeline has already run, entering the article
  21  through the one door with no guard on it.
  22  
  23  Three things stop that here:
  24  
  25  1. Every item is one of two kinds, and says which. **You have this already**
  26     cites claims from the dossier, and the quoted text is looked up from the
  27     dossier rather than taken from the model, so it cannot be misquoted. **Nobody
  28     established this** says what is missing and nothing more.
  29  2. An item claiming the run has something, that cites nothing the dossier
  30     contains, is demoted to "nobody established this". The safe direction is
  31     never asserting the run holds a fact it does not.
  32  3. No note may contain a number the run does not already have. Every figure in
  33     the punch list must appear in the article or in the dossier. "Around 400 AD"
  34     appears in neither, so the note carrying it is dropped.
  35  
  36  It is not a gate, not a score, and not a rewrite. It runs after the article is
  37  finished and stored, so a failure here loses the notes and not the piece.
  38  """
  39  
  40  from __future__ import annotations
  41  
  42  import logging
  43  import re
  44  from typing import Any
  45  
  46  from .contracts_v4 import ArticleBrief, EvidencePackage
  47  from .support import _safe_dict, _safe_str
  48  
  49  logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  50  
  51  PUNCH_LIST_STAGE = "stage_v4_punch_list"
  52  PUNCH_LIST_MAX_TOKENS = 4000
  53  
  54  # Six items a person will act on beats thirty they will scroll past.
  55  MAX_ITEMS = 6
  56  
  57  ITEM_KINDS = ("add_sentence", "add_paragraph", "move", "rephrase", "cut")
  58  
  59  # What the operator is told about where each item's fact would come from.
  60  HAVE_IT = "have_it"
  61  NOT_ESTABLISHED = "not_established"
  62  
  63  _NUMBER = re.compile(r"\d[\d,.]*")
  64  _HEADING = re.compile(r"^#{1,6}\s+(.+?)\s*$", re.MULTILINE)
  65  # A word that is capitalised without starting a sentence: a name, a place, a
  66  # brand. Long enough to be distinctive rather than "The" or "And".
  67  _PROPER = re.compile(r"(?<![.!?]\s)(?<!^)\b([A-Z][\w'’-]{3,})\b", re.MULTILINE)
  68  
  69  
  70  def _numbers(text: str) -> set[str]:
  71      """Every figure in a piece of text, comparable across its own formatting.
  72  
  73      "16,000" and "16000" are the same number written twice, and a note that
  74      reformatted one would otherwise read as introducing a new one.
  75      """
  76      found = set()
  77      for raw in _NUMBER.findall(text or ""):
  78          cleaned = raw.rstrip(".,")
  79          if not cleaned:
  80              continue
  81          found.add(cleaned)
  82          found.add(cleaned.replace(",", ""))
  83      return found
  84  
  85  
  86  def _proper_nouns(text: str) -> set[str]:
  87      return {match.casefold() for match in _PROPER.findall(text or "")}
  88  
  89  
  90  def article_headings(markdown: str) -> list[str]:
  91      """The headings an item is allowed to point at.
  92  
  93      "In the introduction" is not a place. A note the operator cannot put their
  94      finger on is a note they will not act on.
  95      """
  96      return [heading.strip() for heading in _HEADING.findall(markdown or "") if heading.strip()]
  97  
  98  
  99  def unused_claims(
 100      evidence: EvidencePackage,
 101      article_markdown: str,
 102      *,
 103      reserve: bool = False,
 104  ) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
 105      """Claims the run researched, graded and then did not use.
 106  
 107      Fully deterministic, which is the point: these are the items that can be
 108      raised without any risk of inventing something, because the fact was
 109      researched, checked and graded before the writing started.
 110  
 111      A claim counts as used when any figure or name in it appears in the
 112      article. Deliberately generous -- one match is enough -- because telling an
 113      operator they left something out when they did not is worse than staying
 114      quiet about one they did.
 115  
 116      `reserve` splits the two kinds of unused. A fact the writer had and did not
 117      place is an ordinary miss and the safest item on the list. A fact a person
 118      deliberately cut before the writing started is not a miss at all: raising
 119      it as one asks the operator to undo their own decision at the last step,
 120      which is the editing aid refilling the article the earlier stages carefully
 121      reduced.
 122      """
 123      article_numbers = _numbers(article_markdown)
 124      article_names = _proper_nouns(article_markdown)
 125      missed: list[dict[str, str]] = []
 126      for claim in evidence.claims:
 127          if claim.merged_into or claim.selected == reserve:
 128              continue
 129          figures = _numbers(claim.text)
 130          names = _proper_nouns(claim.text)
 131          if not figures and not names:
 132              # Nothing distinctive enough to look for. Saying "this claim is
 133              # unused" on a guess is exactly the kind of noise that gets a list
 134              # ignored.
 135              continue
 136          if figures & article_numbers or names & article_names:
 137              continue
 138          missed.append({"claim_id": claim.claim_id, "text": claim.text})
 139      return missed
 140  
 141  
 142  def numbers_the_run_does_not_have(
 143      text: str,
 144      *,
 145      article_markdown: str,
 146      evidence: EvidencePackage,
 147  ) -> list[str]:
 148      """Figures in a note that appear nowhere in the run's own material.
 149  
 150      The guard on the one door with no other guard on it. A note may repeat a
 151      number the article has, or one the dossier established and the article
 152      dropped. A number from neither was invented while writing the note, which
 153      is the failure this whole module is shaped around avoiding.
 154      """
 155      known = _numbers(article_markdown)
 156      for claim in evidence.claims:
 157          known |= _numbers(claim.text)
 158      for requirement in evidence.requirements:
 159          known |= _numbers(requirement.gap)
 160      return sorted(figure for figure in _numbers(text) if figure not in known)
 161  
 162  
 163  PUNCH_LIST_SCHEMA = {
 164      "type": "object",
 165      "properties": {
 166          "items": {
 167              "type": "array",
 168              "items": {
 169                  "type": "object",
 170                  "properties": {
 171                      "kind": {"type": "string", "enum": list(ITEM_KINDS)},
 172                      "heading": {"type": "string"},
 173                      "where": {"type": "string"},
 174                      "note": {"type": "string"},
 175                      "needs": {"type": "string", "enum": [HAVE_IT, NOT_ESTABLISHED]},
 176                      "claim_ids": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
 177                  },
 178                  "required": ["kind", "heading", "note", "needs"],
 179              },
 180          }
 181      },
 182      "required": ["items"],
 183  }
 184  
 185  
 186  def build_punch_list_prompt(
 187      *,
 188      brief: ArticleBrief,
 189      title: str,
 190      article_markdown: str,
 191      evidence: EvidencePackage,
 192      unused: list[dict[str, str]],
 193      reserved: list[dict[str, str]],
 194  ) -> str:
 195      """Ask for the read a person would give it, with the run's own material."""
 196      headings = "\n".join(f"- {heading}" for heading in article_headings(article_markdown))
 197      dossier = (
 198          "\n".join(
 199              f"- [{claim.claim_id}] {claim.text}"
 200              for claim in evidence.claims
 201              if claim.selected and not claim.merged_into
 202          )
 203          or "- Nothing. Every item you raise is the second kind."
 204      )
 205      never_used = (
 206          "\n".join(f"- [{item['claim_id']}] {item['text']}" for item in unused)
 207          or "- None. Everything the writer had reached the piece in some form."
 208      )
 209      in_reserve = (
 210          "\n".join(f"- [{item['claim_id']}] {item['text']}" for item in reserved)
 211          or "- None. Nothing was held back."
 212      )
 213      return f"""Read this finished article the way an editor would, and list what one
 214  person should fix by hand in twenty minutes.
 215  
 216  Not a rewrite. Not a score. Somebody else is going to open this article and
 217  make these edits themselves, so every item has to be small, specific, and
 218  somewhere they can put their finger on.
 219  
 220  WHAT THIS ARTICLE IS FOR
 221  Reader: {brief.reader.primary_reader}
 222  Their question: {brief.reader_question}
 223  What it should make them do: {brief.outcome}
 224  What it is built on: {brief.spine}
 225  
 226  IT FAILS IF: {brief.fails_if}
 227  
 228  That line defines failure for this specific piece and nothing in this system
 229  has ever read it. Read it now. If the article is drifting toward it, that is
 230  your first item.
 231  
 232  THE HEADLINE IT WILL BE PUBLISHED UNDER
 233  {title}
 234  
 235  Whatever that line asserts is a promise to a reader who clicked it. If it names
 236  an age, a number, a superlative, a first or an oldest, and the article does not
 237  answer it, that is an item -- and check the dossier below before you decide
 238  which kind it is.
 239  
 240  THE HEADINGS YOU MAY POINT AT
 241  {headings or "- The article has no headings."}
 242  
 243  WHAT THE WRITER HAD
 244  A person chose these facts for this article before it was written. Research
 245  found more; the rest is below, and it is not work the article forgot.
 246  {dossier}
 247  
 248  CHOSEN AND NEVER USED
 249  These were on the writer's desk and did not make the article. They are the
 250  safest items on the list: the article can use them today.
 251  {never_used}
 252  
 253  IN RESERVE
 254  Research found these and a person decided this article does not need them.
 255  Raising one is a change of scope, not a missed fact. Only do it when leaving it
 256  out actually costs the reader something -- and say so in those terms, so
 257  whoever reads your note is making the same decision again rather than
 258  discovering it was made for them.
 259  {in_reserve}
 260  
 261  THE ARTICLE
 262  {article_markdown}
 263  
 264  WHAT TO RETURN
 265  
 266  At most {MAX_ITEMS} items, best first. Six a person will act on beats thirty
 267  they will scroll past. Most of the value is rearranging and re-pointing what
 268  the article already earned, so most items should need no new information at
 269  all.
 270  
 271  Each item has:
 272  - `kind`: one of add_sentence, add_paragraph, move, rephrase, cut.
 273  - `heading`: exactly one of the headings listed above, copied as written. Use
 274    the heading the edit happens in, not the one it moves to.
 275  - `where`: a few words quoted from the article so the person can find the spot.
 276  - `note`: one line, in the reader's terms. What is wrong and what to do. Not
 277    "improve flow" -- say what a reader experiences and what fixes it.
 278  - `needs`: `{HAVE_IT}` or `{NOT_ESTABLISHED}`.
 279  - `claim_ids`: on a `{HAVE_IT}` item, the dossier claims that answer it.
 280  
 281  THE RULE THAT MATTERS MOST
 282  
 283  `{HAVE_IT}` means the dossier above already contains the fact and the article
 284  did not use it. Name the claim ids. Do not retype the fact; it will be quoted
 285  from the dossier.
 286  
 287  `{NOT_ESTABLISHED}` means nothing in the dossier answers it. Say what is
 288  missing and that it needs looking up. **Never state the value.** If the
 289  headline promises an age and no research established one, the item is "the
 290  headline promises an age, the research never established one, you need a date
 291  before this headline is honest" -- and nothing more. Writing a plausible date
 292  here would put an invented fact into a published article through the only step
 293  with nothing checking it.
 294  
 295  Any figure you write must already appear in the article or in the dossier. A
 296  note carrying a number from neither will be thrown away.
 297  
 298  WHAT AN ABSENCE IS FOR
 299  
 300  Some claims in the dossier record what the research could not establish: that
 301  nobody publishes a figure, that a list does not exist, that a price is not
 302  posted anywhere. Those are internal. They never become a reader-facing
 303  sentence, and an article that leaves them out has done the right thing rather
 304  than missed something.
 305  
 306  Never ask for one to be stated. "State clearly that repeated searches returned
 307  no official published ranking" is not an edit anyone may make: the house rules
 308  refuse a sentence that announces what the research could not find, so an
 309  operator who followed it would write a sentence the pipeline rejects. If an
 310  absence matters, the item is to cut or rewrite whatever the article built on
 311  top of it, in terms of what the article does know.
 312  """
 313  
 314  
 315  def _items_in(payload: Any) -> list[Any]:
 316      """The list of edits, under whichever shape the read came back in.
 317  
 318      Run 849ae5aa returned a bare array of four good items -- including the one
 319      that caught the article's own rainfall contradiction -- against a schema
 320      asking for `{"items": [...]}`. All four were thrown away, and the operator
 321      got an empty list on an article with real problems in it.
 322  
 323      Same lesson the evidence parser has learned three times: a schema exists so
 324      the model knows what to send, not so the parser can reject what arrived.
 325      """
 326      if isinstance(payload, list):
 327          return payload
 328      record = _safe_dict(payload)
 329      for name in ("items", "edits", "notes", "punch_list", "fixes"):
 330          value = record.get(name)
 331          if isinstance(value, list):
 332              return value
 333      return []
 334  
 335  
 336  def _valid_items(
 337      payload: Any,
 338      *,
 339      article_markdown: str,
 340      evidence: EvidencePackage,
 341  ) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], list[str]]:
 342      """The items that survive their own rules, and what was dropped.
 343  
 344      Degrade rather than fail: a run whose notes came back half usable gives the
 345      operator the usable half. Nothing here can stop or endanger the article,
 346      which is already written and stored by the time this is asked for.
 347      """
 348      headings = article_headings(article_markdown)
 349      by_heading = {heading.casefold(): heading for heading in headings}
 350      claims = {claim.claim_id: claim.text for claim in evidence.claims}
 351      # Facts a person cut before the writing started. An item resting on one is
 352      # a scope change and is labelled as such rather than dropped: the operator
 353      # may well want it, and they are entitled to know they are reversing their
 354      # own decision rather than filling a hole.
 355      reserve = {
 356          claim.claim_id for claim in evidence.claims if not claim.selected
 357      }
 358  
 359      items: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
 360      dropped: list[str] = []
 361      for raw in _items_in(payload):
 362          record = _safe_dict(raw)
 363          note = _safe_str(record.get("note"))
 364          kind = _safe_str(record.get("kind"))
 365          if not note or kind not in ITEM_KINDS:
 366              dropped.append("an item with no note or no kind")
 367              continue
 368  
 369          invented = numbers_the_run_does_not_have(
 370              note, article_markdown=article_markdown, evidence=evidence
 371          )
 372          if invented:
 373              # The guard doing its job. Logged loudly because a model reaching
 374              # for a number at this stage is the failure mode this module was
 375              # built around, and it should be visible when it happens.
 376              logger.warning(
 377                  "Dropped a punch list item carrying figures the run does not "
 378                  "have: %s",
 379                  ", ".join(invented),
 380              )
 381              dropped.append(
 382                  f"an item that introduced a figure the run does not have "
 383                  f"({', '.join(invented)})"
 384              )
 385              continue
 386  
 387          cited = [
 388              claim_id
 389              for claim_id in (record.get("claim_ids") or [])
 390              if _safe_str(claim_id) in claims
 391          ]
 392          needs = _safe_str(record.get("needs"))
 393          # A claim of "you have this already" that cites nothing the dossier
 394          # contains is demoted rather than trusted. Telling someone the research
 395          # covered something it did not is how a fact gets written from memory.
 396          if needs != HAVE_IT or not cited:
 397              needs = NOT_ESTABLISHED
 398              cited = []
 399  
 400          heading = by_heading.get(_safe_str(record.get("heading")).casefold(), "")
 401          items.append(
 402              {
 403                  "kind": kind,
 404                  # Empty when the model named a heading the article does not
 405                  # have. The item still reads; it just points at the piece as a
 406                  # whole.
 407                  "heading": heading,
 408                  "where": _safe_str(record.get("where")),
 409                  "note": note,
 410                  "needs": needs,
 411                  # Quoted from the dossier, never from the model, so an item
 412                  # cannot misstate the fact it is pointing at.
 413                  "have": [{"claim_id": claim_id, "text": claims[claim_id]} for claim_id in cited],
 414                  "scope_change": any(claim_id in reserve for claim_id in cited),
 415              }
 416          )
 417          if len(items) == MAX_ITEMS:
 418              break
 419      return items, dropped
 420  
 421  
 422  def build_punch_list(
 423      *,
 424      brief: ArticleBrief,
 425      title: str,
 426      article_markdown: str,
 427      evidence: EvidencePackage,
 428      llm: Any,
 429      model_name: str | None,
 430  ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 431      """One model call over a finished article, plus the checks that are free."""
 432      unused = unused_claims(evidence, article_markdown)
 433      reserved = unused_claims(evidence, article_markdown, reserve=True)
 434      parsed, _raw = llm.invoke_json(
 435              job_id="p2b.notes",
 436          prompt=build_punch_list_prompt(
 437              brief=brief,
 438              title=title,
 439              article_markdown=article_markdown,
 440              evidence=evidence,
 441              unused=unused,
 442              reserved=reserved,
 443          ),
 444          model_name=model_name,
 445          schema=PUNCH_LIST_SCHEMA,
 446          max_tokens=PUNCH_LIST_MAX_TOKENS,
 447          temperature=0.0,
 448      )
 449      items, dropped = _valid_items(
 450          parsed,
 451          article_markdown=article_markdown,
 452          evidence=evidence,
 453      )
 454      return {
 455          "items": items,
 456          # Kept beside the list because it is the deterministic half and it
 457          # stands on its own: these were researched, graded, and never used,
 458          # whatever the model did or did not say about them.
 459          "researched_and_unused": unused,
 460          # Named apart, and never merged into the list above. An operator
 461          # scanning one list cannot tell a fact the writer missed from a fact
 462          # they themselves cut, and the second one is not a defect.
 463          "in_reserve": reserved,
 464          "dropped": dropped,
 465      }
apps/backend/app/features/prompt2blog/llm.py
   1  from __future__ import annotations
   2  
   3  import json
   4  import logging
   5  from typing import Any, Protocol
   6  
   7  from app.shared.api_usage import observe_external_call, provider_for_llm
   8  from app.shared.model_calls import resolve
   9  from utils import get_vertex_llm, parse_json_response
  10  from .pricing import MEASURED_COST_KEY
  11  from .support import _safe_str
  12  
  13  logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  14  
  15  
  16  class UsageRecorder(Protocol):
  17      """Where a finished call's tokens go.
  18  
  19      ``requested_model`` is keyword-only and optional so that a caller which
  20      does not know what was asked for -- a test double, mostly -- stays valid.
  21      """
  22  
  23      def __call__(
  24          self,
  25          model_name: str,
  26          raw_usage: Any,
  27          *,
  28          requested_model: str | None = None,
  29      ) -> None: ...
  30  
  31  # What the dashboard's API-usage monitor called this work before jobs existed:
  32  # one feature for all thirteen Prompt2Blog stages, and for the listicle grill
  33  # too, because it borrows this pipeline's code. Kept as the fallback for a
  34  # caller that has not named its job yet, so nothing reports as nothing.
  35  #
  36  # The run id is not available here, so calls are correlated by run at the
  37  # stage level instead -- see `pricing.py` for the per-run ledger that does
  38  # know it.
  39  USAGE_FEATURE = "prompt2blog"
  40  
  41  
  42  def _resolved_model(job_id: str | None, model_name: str | None) -> str:
  43      """The model a call will run on.
  44  
  45      With a job, the gateway decides and ``model_name`` is an operator's
  46      explicit choice from the stack they picked -- which still wins. Without
  47      one, this is a caller that has not been migrated yet.
  48      """
  49      if job_id:
  50          return resolve(job_id, model_name)
  51      if model_name:
  52          return model_name
  53      raise ValueError(
  54          "A model call must name either a job or a model. Naming a job is the "
  55          "one that lets the dashboard change it."
  56      )
  57  
  58  
  59  def _warn_on_substitution(
  60      job_id: str | None, resolved_model: str, reported_model: str
  61  ) -> None:
  62      """Say out loud that the job did not get the model it named.
  63  
  64      The Claude paths substitute a Gemini model when neither is switched on, and
  65      that rewrite used to leave no trace anywhere a person looks: the ledger
  66      recorded the model that answered, so a run configured to write on Claude
  67      read back as a run that was always meant to be Gemini.
  68      """
  69      if resolved_model == reported_model:
  70          return
  71      logger.warning(
  72          "%s asked for '%s' and was served by '%s'.",
  73          job_id or USAGE_FEATURE,
  74          resolved_model,
  75          reported_model,
  76      )
  77  
  78  
  79  def _invoke_text_llm(
  80      *,
  81      prompt: str,
  82      max_tokens: int,
  83      temperature: float,
  84      model_name: str | None,
  85      usage_recorder: UsageRecorder | None = None,
  86      job_id: str | None = None,
  87      correlation_id: str | None = None,
  88  ) -> str:
  89      resolved_model = _resolved_model(job_id, model_name)
  90      # get_vertex_llm routes claude-* models to the Anthropic API.
  91      llm = get_vertex_llm(
  92          temperature=temperature,
  93          max_tokens=max_tokens,
  94          model_name=resolved_model,
  95      )
  96      reported_model = str(getattr(llm, "model_name", resolved_model))
  97      _warn_on_substitution(job_id, resolved_model, reported_model)
  98      # The observation wraps the provider call and nothing else, so the duration
  99      # is the call's and a raised exception is recorded as a failed call before
 100      # it reaches the stage that catches it.
 101      with observe_external_call(
 102          provider=provider_for_llm(llm, reported_model),
 103          feature=job_id or USAGE_FEATURE,
 104          model=reported_model,
 105          correlation_id=correlation_id,
 106          endpoint="invoke_text",
 107      ) as observed:
 108          result = llm.invoke(prompt)
 109          # Reading the usage metadata is pure attribute access on the object the
 110          # call just filled in, so it belongs inside. Handing it to the run
 111          # ledger does not: a recorder that raised would otherwise be reported
 112          # as a failed provider call, which it is not.
 113          usage = _usage_with_measured_cost(llm)
 114          observed.record_usage(usage)
 115      if usage_recorder is not None:
 116          usage_recorder(reported_model, usage, requested_model=resolved_model)
 117      text = _safe_str(result)
 118      if not text:
 119          raise RuntimeError("LLM returned empty response")
 120      return text
 121  
 122  
 123  def _usage_with_measured_cost(llm: Any) -> Any:
 124      """Token counts, plus a per-call price when the provider reported one.
 125  
 126      Only the subscription CLI does; Vertex and the Anthropic API report tokens
 127      and leave costing to the rate table. Folded into the usage dict rather than
 128      threaded through a new recorder argument, so every existing recorder --
 129      including the test doubles that take exactly two positionals -- keeps
 130      working untouched.
 131      """
 132      usage = getattr(llm, "last_usage_metadata", None)
 133      cost = getattr(llm, "last_cost_usd", None)
 134      if cost is None or not isinstance(usage, dict):
 135          return usage
 136      return {**usage, MEASURED_COST_KEY: cost}
 137  
 138  
 139  # The parse error names what went wrong, so the excerpt only has to show the
 140  # shape of the failure -- a fenced block, a preamble, a truncation. Sending
 141  # more of the bad output costs input tokens and invites the model to anchor on
 142  # text it has already been told is wrong.
 143  JSON_RETRY_EXCERPT_CHARS = 1_200
 144  
 145  
 146  def _invoke_schema_json_llm(
 147      *,
 148      prompt: str,
 149      max_tokens: int,
 150      temperature: float,
 151      model_name: str | None,
 152      schema: dict[str, Any],
 153      usage_recorder: UsageRecorder | None = None,
 154      job_id: str | None = None,
 155      correlation_id: str | None = None,
 156  ) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str] | None:
 157      """One validated call, or None if this provider cannot make one.
 158  
 159      Capability is asked of the object the factory returned rather than inferred
 160      from the model name, so the question is "can this thing enforce a schema"
 161      and not "do I believe this name is served by something that can". A
 162      provider without the method falls through to asking in prose.
 163  
 164      There is no retry here on purpose. The retry loop below exists because a
 165      model asked in prose can return something unparseable; a validated call
 166      either produced a conforming object or failed for a reason that asking
 167      again three times would not fix -- and each of those attempts is a full
 168      article rewrite on the writer model.
 169      """
 170      resolved_model = _resolved_model(job_id, model_name)
 171      llm = get_vertex_llm(
 172          temperature=temperature,
 173          max_tokens=max_tokens,
 174          model_name=resolved_model,
 175      )
 176      invoke_json = getattr(llm, "invoke_json", None)
 177      if not callable(invoke_json):
 178          return None
 179  
 180      reported_model = str(getattr(llm, "model_name", resolved_model))
 181      _warn_on_substitution(job_id, resolved_model, reported_model)
 182      with observe_external_call(
 183          provider=provider_for_llm(llm, reported_model),
 184          feature=job_id or USAGE_FEATURE,
 185          model=reported_model,
 186          correlation_id=correlation_id,
 187          endpoint="invoke_json",
 188      ) as observed:
 189          options = {"input_schema": schema, "max_tokens": max_tokens}
 190          if job_id == "p2b.research_structure" and reported_model == "gemini-2.5-flash":
 191              options["thinking_budget"] = 0
 192          try:
 193              parsed = invoke_json(prompt, **options)
 194          finally:
 195              usage = _usage_with_measured_cost(llm)
 196              observed.record_usage(usage)
 197              if usage_recorder is not None and usage is not None:
 198                  usage_recorder(
 199                      reported_model, usage, requested_model=resolved_model
 200                  )
 201      if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
 202          raise RuntimeError("Schema-validated LLM response was not an object")
 203      # The trace wants the raw response the stage saw. There was no prose reply
 204      # to record, so this is the validated object rendered back -- honest about
 205      # what happened rather than an empty string in the trace.
 206      return parsed, json.dumps(parsed, ensure_ascii=False)
 207  
 208  
 209  def _invoke_json_llm(
 210      *,
 211      prompt: str,
 212      max_tokens: int,
 213      temperature: float,
 214      model_name: str | None,
 215      schema: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
 216      usage_recorder: UsageRecorder | None = None,
 217      job_id: str | None = None,
 218      correlation_id: str | None = None,
 219  ) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str]:
 220      if schema is not None:
 221          validated = _invoke_schema_json_llm(
 222              prompt=prompt,
 223              max_tokens=max_tokens,
 224              temperature=temperature,
 225              model_name=model_name,
 226              schema=schema,
 227              usage_recorder=usage_recorder,
 228              job_id=job_id,
 229              correlation_id=correlation_id,
 230          )
 231          if validated is not None:
 232              return validated
 233  
 234      if schema is not None:
 235          prompt += "\nREQUIRED JSON SCHEMA:\n" + json.dumps(schema)
 236  
 237      strict_prompt = (
 238          f"{prompt}\n\n"
 239          "CRITICAL OUTPUT RULE:\n"
 240          "Return ONLY one valid JSON object.\n"
 241          "No prose, no markdown, no code fences."
 242      )
 243  
 244      current_prompt = strict_prompt
 245      last_error = "Unknown JSON parse failure"
 246      last_response = ""
 247  
 248      # The retry below is for output that could not be parsed, and nothing else.
 249      # `_invoke_text_llm` raises outside the inner `try`, so a provider fault --
 250      # an exhausted account above all -- leaves this loop on the first attempt
 251      # rather than paying for two more calls that cannot succeed. Keep it that
 252      # way: widening the `except` to cover the invoke would re-introduce exactly
 253      # the wasted calls this loop's shape prevents.
 254  
 255      for attempt in range(1, 4):
 256          raw_response = _invoke_text_llm(
 257              prompt=current_prompt,
 258              max_tokens=max_tokens,
 259              temperature=temperature if attempt == 1 else 0.0,
 260              model_name=model_name,
 261              usage_recorder=usage_recorder,
 262              job_id=job_id,
 263              correlation_id=correlation_id,
 264          )
 265          last_response = raw_response
 266  
 267          try:
 268              parsed = parse_json_response(raw_response)
 269              return parsed, raw_response
 270          except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
 271              last_error = str(exc)
 272              logger.warning(
 273                  "Prompt2Blog JSON parse failed (attempt %d): %s",
 274                  attempt,
 275                  last_error,
 276              )
 277              # The retry used to send only the truncated bad output. That
 278              # discarded the task, the source material and the schema, so the
 279              # model was asked to re-emit a full article as JSON while no
 280              # longer able to see the article -- and the two paid retries after
 281              # a compose failure could not have succeeded on their own terms.
 282              # The instructions come back, and the parse error goes with them:
 283              # naming what was wrong is worth more than a longer sample of the
 284              # output that was wrong.
 285              current_prompt = (
 286                  f"{strict_prompt}\n\n"
 287                  "RETRY NOTICE\n"
 288                  "Your previous response to this exact task could not be parsed "
 289                  f"as JSON: {last_error}\n"
 290                  "Return the same content again as one strict JSON object. "
 291                  "No markdown fences, no commentary, no text before or after "
 292                  "the object.\n\n"
 293                  "Start of the unparseable response, for reference only:\n"
 294                  f"{raw_response[:JSON_RETRY_EXCERPT_CHARS]}"
 295              )
 296  
 297      raise RuntimeError(
 298          "Failed to parse JSON LLM response: "
 299          f"{last_error}. Preview: {last_response[:240]}"
 300      )

   1  from __future__ import annotations

   6  
   7  # The models these stages run on moved to the gateway's registry, where the
   8  # dashboard can change them without a code edit. What was worth saying about
   9  # each choice is worth saying there, so the reasoning went with the values:
  10  # compose and repair earn the stronger model, the small structured calls do
  11  # not, and the grill is the cheapest thing in the pipeline to make good
  12  # because every later stage inherits what it decides.
  13  #
  14  # The temperature stayed. It is a property of the call, not of the model.
  15  
  16  # Higher than the pipeline default. The grill is judgement, not extraction: at
  17  # a low temperature it proposes the safe question rather than the useful one,
  18  # and the whole value of the interview is the sharp question nobody expected.

  52  
  53  # Repair used to be a single unconditional pass whose result was never
  54  # re-gated. It is now a bounded loop back through the audit.
  55  #
  56  # One automatic attempt, not two. A repair pass is not one call: it rewrites
  57  # the whole article on the writing model, runs the anti-AI enforcement pass,
  58  # then re-runs grounding and the audit. On the measured Lima run that chain
  59  # cost 85,012 tokens -- 35% of the whole run -- and a second attempt would
  60  # have bought a point or two of score for the same price again. A draft the
  61  # first repair could not rescue goes back as `needs_revision` instead.
  62  P2B_REPAIR_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 1
  63  
  64  # What one repair attempt is assumed to cost, measured off the Lima run
  65  # (repair + anti-AI enforcement + groundedness + re-audit).
  66  P2B_REPAIR_ESTIMATED_TOKENS = 90_000
  67  
  68  # The ceiling a run may reach *before* an attempt is spent. Attempts are
  69  # refused once `tokens_spent + P2B_REPAIR_ESTIMATED_TOKENS` would pass it, so
  70  # an unusually expensive run stops paying for rescue attempts instead of
  71  # doubling down. Set above the Lima run's pre-repair spend (~158k) on purpose:
  72  # the first repair on a normal run must still be affordable.
  73  #
  74  # RE-DERIVED, 2026-09-02, from the two runs that have complete accounting.
  75  # Everything before PR #455 recorded zero for the intake leg, so the earlier
  76  # number was set against receipts that omitted intake and every grounded
  77  # search. Measured properly:
  78  #
  79  #   a2066506:  9 questions, 133,882 research tokens, 260,586 pre-repair
  80  #   b29d66b4: 14 questions, 206,507 research tokens, 370,114 pre-repair
  81  #
  82  # Both were refused their one repair against the old 320,000, on drafts
  83  # scoring 5 and 6 with actionable revisions waiting. The repair path had
  84  # never once been affordable since the accounting was fixed, which is
  85  # arithmetic rather than two unlucky runs: research costs about 14,800 a
  86  # question, writing about 134,000, and a repair 90,000, so 320,000 left room
  87  # for roughly three questions.
  88  #
  89  # 425,000 grants the repair up to about eleven questions, which covers the
  90  # normal size. The ladder, projected from those rates rather than from any one
  91  # run's receipt:
  92  #
  93  #   380,000 -> repair affordable to ~8 questions
  94  #   400,000 -> ~9 to 10
  95  #   425,000 -> ~11          <- set here
  96  #   470,000 -> 14, the size that broke b29d66b4
  97  #
  98  # A fourteen question plan still will not fit, and `budget_projection` says so
  99  # at the cut step while the plan can still be changed, rather than at the
 100  # settle node when the money is already spent.
 101  #
 102  # Do not set this from a single run's actual pre-repair spend. a2066506
 103  # finished at 260,586, which suggests 350,000 is enough for nine questions --
 104  # but its writing leg was 89,707, the cheapest of six, against a median of
 105  # 134,000. The projection uses the median, which is the honest basis for a
 106  # plan nobody has run yet.
 107  #
 108  # P2B_REPAIR_ESTIMATED_TOKENS above is still untested: no run has repaired
 109  # since the accounting was fixed, so 90,000 remains a measurement of a repair
 110  # nobody has watched. Re-derive it the first time one actually runs.
 111  P2B_RUN_TOKEN_BUDGET = 425_000
 112  
 113  # What one more repair attempt may cost, and what the run may spend before it
 114  # stops being worth one. In money, because a token is not a unit of cost.
 115  #
 116  # The token budget above treated a Gemini Flash token and a subscription Claude
 117  # token as the same currency. On the two runs that finished, two thirds of the
 118  # tokens were Claude drawing plan allowance -- free -- and both runs were
 119  # refused their repair. Chifa 3750891f shipped with a wrong opening time; the
 120  # ceviche run shipped six words over its word cap and scored 6 for it. Each
 121  # would have been a single repair call away, and each run had billed $0.37.
 122  #
 123  #   chifa   3750891f: $0.36 billed, $2.29 notional, 802,018 tokens
 124  #   ceviche 8a7e9aa4: $0.38 billed, $1.97 notional, 692,544 tokens
 125  #
 126  # So $2.00 is five times what a whole run bills, and a repair is a rounding
 127  # error against it. Set from measurement rather than from a round number, and
 128  # it is deliberately generous: the failure this replaces was a budget too tight
 129  # to fix a typo.
 130  P2B_RUN_COST_BUDGET_USD = 2.00
 131  
 132  # What a repair attempt bills. Both stored repairs were Claude, so they billed
 133  # nothing at all; this is the Gemini groundedness and audit re-run that follows
 134  # one. Re-derive it the first time a repair runs on a paid model.
 135  P2B_REPAIR_ESTIMATED_COST_USD = 0.10
 136  
 137  # The hard ceiling. Distinct from P2B_RUN_TOKEN_BUDGET above, which only asks
 138  # whether one more *rescue* is affordable: this asks whether the run may
 139  # continue at all, and refuses when it may not.
 140  #
 141  # v3 did not need one. Its first model call was the outline, and everything
 142  # before it happened in a browser on the operator's own chatbot subscription.
 143  # v4 moves the grill and both research passes in-app, and neither has an upper
 144  # bound by construction -- the grill stops at agreement rather than at a
 145  # question count (ADR 0030), and research is grounded web search. A bug that
 146  # asks forty questions should cost a known amount and then stop.
 147  #
 148  # It exists for runaway, not for costly, and it was set at twice the token
 149  # budget back when affordability was also measured in tokens. That basis is
 150  # gone -- affordability is `P2B_RUN_COST_BUDGET_USD` now -- and the old number
 151  # was firing on runs that were working:
 152  #
 153  #   chifa   3750891f: 802,018 tokens, $0.36 billed, finished
 154  #   ceviche 8a7e9aa4: 692,544 tokens, $0.38 billed, died at `quality_settle`
 155  #     -- the last node, after the article was written and audited, on the step
 156  #     that only picks which draft to keep.
 157  #
 158  # So the number is now set against what a working run actually costs rather
 159  # than against another budget: roughly two and a half times the longest one
 160  # observed. A bug that asks forty questions still stops. A run that merely has
 161  # a lot to say does not.
 162  #
 163  # It stays denominated in tokens on purpose. Money answers whether a run is
 164  # worth continuing; tokens answer whether it has stopped terminating, and a
 165  # loop on a cheap model is still a loop.
 166  P2B_RUN_TOKEN_CEILING = 2_000_000
 167  
 168  # How many times the grill may look something up *during* the interview, on
 169  # top of the one lookup it always makes on the seed.
 170  #
 171  # G2 (ADR 0030) is what keeps the grill short: anything it can look up, it
 172  # never asks. It looked the seed up once and then went blind, so by the fourth
 173  # turn the conversation could be about one neighbourhood while the grill was
 174  # still working from a general city briefing -- and a grill that cannot look up
 175  # where the conversation went is forced back into asking, which is the
 176  # form-with-extra-steps failure the interview replaced (ADR 0033).
 177  #
 178  # Bounded because the grill stops at agreement rather than at a question count,
 179  # so it has no upper bound on turns by construction and would have none on
 180  # searches either. Three is enough to follow a conversation that narrows twice
 181  # and still cheap beside a run: a grounded search measured 3-5k tokens on runs
 182  # b78a9fe8 and 76b36468.
 183  #
 184  # This number is only enforceable because the receipt now counts grounded
 185  # search at all (#440). Before that, adding searches here would have been
 186  # spending against a ceiling that could not see them.
 187  P2B_V4_GRILL_MAX_LOOKUPS = 3
 188  
 189  # How many grounded searches research may have in flight at once.
 190  #
 191  # One question per search, and nothing in question four depends on question
 192  # three, so the sequential loop was only ever the simplest thing to write. On
 193  # run 76b36468 it cost roughly six minutes of a twenty-and-a-half minute
 194  # research pass; concurrently that is about the slowest single search.
 195  #
 196  # Bounded rather than unbounded because the grounded-search rate limits are
 197  # unknown and a run fans out as many searches as the work order has questions.
 198  # Four is a deliberate first guess: enough to collapse most of the wait, small
 199  # enough that a rate limit shows up as slow rather than as a wall of failures.
 200  # Lower it here if searches start coming back empty.
 201  P2B_V4_GATHER_CONCURRENCY = 4
 202  
 203  # How many times one run may be resumed after a failure. A resume costs the
 204  # stages that had not run yet, so a stage that fails for a reason resuming
 205  # cannot fix -- a commission the model keeps refusing, a permanently dead
 206  # credential -- would otherwise let an operator buy the same tail repeatedly.
 207  # Three is enough for a provider blip, a reconnect, and one more.
 208  P2B_RESUME_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3
 209  
 210  # Editorial augmentation may only add to a draft. If the returned content drops
 211  # below this share of the pre-augmentation word count, or loses section
 212  # headings, the stage is rolled back rather than shipped.
 213  P2B_AUGMENTATION_MIN_RETENTION_RATIO = 0.9
 214  
 215  PROMPT2BLOG_CREATIVITY_LEVELS = {"low", "medium", "high"}
 216  
 217  # creativity_level used to be rendered as the literal string "Creativity level:
 218  # medium" inside an instructions blob while every prose call ran at a hardcoded
 219  # temperature, so the control did nothing. It now sets the sampling temperature
 220  # for the stages that actually write prose.
 221  PROMPT2BLOG_CREATIVITY_TEMPERATURES = {"low": 0.05, "medium": 0.2, "high": 0.45}
 222  
 223  PROMPT2BLOG_DEFAULT_COMPOSE_TEMPERATURE = PROMPT2BLOG_CREATIVITY_TEMPERATURES["medium"]
 224  
 225  PROMPT2BLOG_CLEANUP_MODE = "ai_always_aggressive_v1"
 226  
 227  PROMPT2BLOG_CLEANUP_CHUNKING_CHAR_THRESHOLD = 18_000
 228  
 229  PROMPT2BLOG_CLEANUP_CHUNK_TARGET_CHARS = 12_000
 230  
 231  PROMPT2BLOG_CLEANUP_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 8_192
 232  
 233  PROMPT2BLOG_CLEANUP_MAX_REMOVED_BLOCKS = 10
 234  
 235  PROMPT2BLOG_CLEANUP_REMOVED_EXCERPT_CHARS = 220
 236  
 237  PROMPT2BLOG_GUIDELINE_FILE_ALIASES = {
 238      "opinionpiece": "opinionpieces",
 239      "interview": "interviewarticles",
 240      "comparisonarticle": "comparisonarticleavsb",
 241  }
 242  
 243  PROMPT2BLOG_TITLE_FILE_ALIASES = {
