 245  }
apps/backend/app/features/prompt2blog/polish_v4.py
   1  """The prompt the operator carries to a flagship model, with the article.
   2  
   3  The run already knows everything wrong with what it wrote: the measured
   4  constraint checks, the sentence spread, the readiness blockers, the problems
   5  the audit named. All of it is recorded where nobody reads it. This assembles it
   6  into something a person pastes into Claude or ChatGPT along with the finished
   7  piece.
   8  
   9  Two decisions shape it.
  10  
  11  **It carries the brief, not only the complaints.** A model told "the sentences
  12  are too uniform" smooths the prose and quietly drifts the piece. A model told
  13  what the article is for, who reads it, and the line that defines failure fixes
  14  the flatness while protecting what the article is. The `fails_if` line is the
  15  whole point of the brief and it goes in every time.
  16  
  17  **It carries the house rules that are easy to break by accident.** The em dash
  18  ban and the hyphenated compound ban are deliberate, and a chatbot asked to
  19  improve rhythm will reach for an em dash within a sentence or two. Telling it
  20  not to is cheaper than reading the result and finding out.
  21  
  22  **And it has to say how to lengthen a sentence, not only what it cannot use.**
  23  Asked to vary the rhythm and forbidden the dash in the same breath, a model has
  24  one tool left: the full stop. A version of the Medellin article came back from
  25  an outside model with 65 sentences where the pipeline wrote 54, a spread of 5.0
  26  where the pipeline had 7.7, and **zero** sentences over 25 words where the
  27  pipeline had six. Every cut landed on a subordinate clause -- "667 people per
  28  day, *which* falls far short of" became two sentences -- which is exactly the
  29  joint the rhythm fix in `2bd89fb1` had just added.
  30  
  31  Not proven to have come from this prompt: the operator had also been editing by
  32  hand. But the failure matches the prompt's shape precisely, and it is the same
  33  trap `anti_ai_tells.py` had before that commit, where the only escape offered
  34  from an aside was "split it". So the wording here now mirrors what those rules
  35  settled on: length comes from subordination, and splitting is the last resort
  36  rather than the house style.
  37  
  38  It is generated, never hand edited. Operator influence belongs in a control
  39  carrying its own validated field; typed text into a generated prompt leaves
  40  nothing downstream able to say what was actually asked for.
  41  """
  42  
  43  from __future__ import annotations
  44  
  45  from typing import Any
  46  
  47  from .contracts_v4 import ArticleBrief
  48  from .support import _safe_dict, _safe_str
  49  
  50  # Below this, the prose is varied enough that saying so would be noise.
  51  SPREAD_WORTH_MENTIONING = 0.45
  52  
  53  # One sentence past 25 words for every this-many sentences, as a floor.
  54  #
  55  # Crowding alone missed the failure it most needed to catch. Run 062c0b86
  56  # (2026-09-01) came back with 64 sentences, 2 of them past 25 words and 16
  57  # under 8, and a crowding share of 0.36 -- comfortably under the threshold, so
  58  # nothing was said. The prose was choppy: three sentences in the whole article
  59  # used a subordinating clause.
  60  #
  61  # That is the metric and the fault coming apart. Adding very short sentences
  62  # widens the distribution and *improves* the crowding number while making the
  63  # writing worse, so an article can chop its way to a passing score.
  64  #
  65  # Derived rather than tuned. `anti_ai_tells` already requires every section to
  66  # carry at least one sentence over 25 words; a section runs 7 to 10 sentences,
  67  # so one in fifteen is a floor well below what the house rules already demand,
  68  # and it is not a number picked to fit three articles. It separates them
  69  # correctly all the same: Lima 1-in-75 and Huaca 1-in-32 both fire, Medellin
  70  # 1-in-9 stays quiet, and Medellin is the one that read well.
  71  LONG_SENTENCE_AT_LEAST_EVERY = 15
  72  
  73  
  74  def _measured_problems(checks: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
  75      """What the run measured about its own prose, as instructions.
  76  
  77      Only what is actually wrong. A clean article should produce a short prompt,
  78      not a long one with every measurement in it.
  79      """
  80      problems: list[str] = []
  81  
  82      share = checks.get("sentence_widest_band_share")
  83      count = checks.get("sentence_count")
  84      if isinstance(share, (int, float)) and isinstance(count, int) and count:
  85          long_ones = checks.get("sentences_over_25_words") or 0
  86          short_ones = checks.get("sentences_under_8_words") or 0
  87          crowded = share >= SPREAD_WORTH_MENTIONING
  88          starved = long_ones * LONG_SENTENCE_AT_LEAST_EVERY < count
  89          if crowded or starved:
  90              # Named for the faults that actually fired, and both when both
  91              # did. Telling a choppy article its sentences "sit within five
  92              # words of each other" describes something that is not wrong with
  93              # it, and an instruction opening on a wrong diagnosis is easy to
  94              # dismiss. Picking one when both are true has the same problem in
  95              # the other direction, so neither is dropped.
  96              if crowded and starved:
  97                  fault = (
  98                      f"The sentences are too uniform and too short. "
  99                      f"{round(share * 100)}% of the {count} sentences sit "
 100                      f"within five words of each other, only {long_ones} run "
 101                      f"past 25 words, and {short_ones} are under 8."
 102                  )
 103              elif starved:
 104                  fault = (
 105                      f"The sentences are too short and too alike. Only "
 106                      f"{long_ones} of {count} run past 25 words and "
 107                      f"{short_ones} are under 8, so the article moves in short "
 108                      "steps with nothing carrying two ideas at once."
 109                  )
 110              else:
 111                  fault = (
 112                      f"The sentences are too uniform. {round(share * 100)}% of "
 113                      f"the {count} sentences sit within five words of each "
 114                      f"other, and {long_ones} run past 25 words."
 115                  )
 116              problems.append(
 117                  f"{fault} Fix this by joining, never by splitting: where one "
 118                  "fact explains another, carry both in one sentence using "
 119                  "because, which, while, after or so that, and let short "
 120                  "sentences land the points. Length comes from subordination. "
 121                  "Cutting a long sentence in two makes this measurement worse, "
 122                  "not better, and cutting content is never the fix."
 123              )
 124  
 125      if checks.get("target_word_count_met") is False:
 126          direction = _safe_str(checks.get("word_count_direction"))
 127          delta = checks.get("word_count_delta")
 128          if direction and isinstance(delta, int) and delta:
 129              problems.append(
 130                  f"The article is {abs(delta)} words {direction} the agreed "
 131                  "length. Fix it by editing, never by inventing facts."
 132              )
 133  
 134      if checks.get("paragraph_length_met") is False:
 135          problems.append("The paragraphs are the wrong length for this piece.")
 136  
 137      return problems
 138  
 139  
 140  def build_polish_prompt(
 141      *,
 142      brief: ArticleBrief,
 143      article_markdown: str,
 144      title: str,
 145      constraint_checks: dict[str, Any],
 146      readiness_blockers: list[str],
 147      audit_problems: list[str] | None = None,
 148  ) -> str:
 149      """One prompt, ready to paste. Returns the whole thing including the article."""
 150      checks = _safe_dict(constraint_checks)
 151      problems = _measured_problems(checks)
 152      problems += [_safe_str(item) for item in readiness_blockers if _safe_str(item)]
 153      problems += [_safe_str(item) for item in (audit_problems or []) if _safe_str(item)]
 154  
 155      numbered = (
 156          "\n".join(f"{index}. {problem}" for index, problem in enumerate(problems, 1))
 157          or "1. Nothing measurable is wrong with it. Improve the prose only where "
 158          "you can do so without touching a fact."
 159      )
 160  
 161      material = (
 162          "\n".join(f"- [{item.kind}] {item.statement}" for item in brief.material)
 163          or "- Nothing first hand. This is researched rather than reported."
 164      )
 165      must_name = "\n".join(f"- {item}" for item in brief.must_name) or "- Nothing named."
 166  
 167      return f"""You are editing a finished article. Fix what is listed and change nothing else.
 168  
 169  WHAT THIS ARTICLE IS FOR
 170  Reader: {brief.reader.primary_reader}
 171  Their question: {brief.reader_question}
 172  What it should make them do: {brief.outcome}
 173  What it is built on: {brief.spine}
 174  It must name:
 175  {must_name}
 176  What the writer actually has:
 177  {material}
 178  
 179  IT FAILS IF: {brief.fails_if}
 180  
 181  That last line is the test. An edit that fixes the list below and moves the
 182  article toward that failure has made things worse, not better.
 183  
 184  WHAT TO FIX
 185  {numbered}
 186  
 187  RULES YOU MUST NOT BREAK
 188  - No em dashes, and no substitutes. A comma bracketed aside is an em dash in
 189    disguise. This is deliberate: em dashes now read as a sign of AI writing and
 190    this publication does not use them.
 191    This is not a reason to reach for a full stop. The replacement for a dash is
 192    a subordinate clause, not two sentences: "the room is warm throughout, which
 193    is what makes the terrace worth booking" keeps the thought whole and needs no
 194    dash. Long sentences are wanted, and commas joining clauses are correct. What
 195    is banned is a comma standing in for a dash around an aside.
 196  - Ration hyphenated compounds: about one per 200 words. Keep the one that is
 197    the word itself, "stir-fried" over "cooked quickly in a wok". Rephrase the
 198    stacked modifiers around it: "a visa for long stays", never "a long-stay
 199    visa". Dates and measures count too, "19th-century" and "six-month" with the
 200    rest. Proper names are free.
 201  - Invent nothing. No new places, prices, dates, dishes, names or numbers, and
 202    no adjective that implies a fact the article does not already carry. If a
 203    sentence cannot be improved without a fact you do not have, leave it alone.
 204  - Every fact you keep stays exactly as it is: the figure, the date, the unit,
 205    the proper noun, and any qualification attached to it. A caveat is what makes
 206    a sentence true, so it is never the thing you cut to make room.
 207  - You may drop a nonessential detail when a sentence is carrying more than it
 208    can say well. "Keep every fact" is what produced the density this pass exists
 209    to relieve: a paragraph holding six facts in forty words is a list, and the
 210    fix is to let one of them go, not to smooth the joins between them. Drop the
 211    one the reader loses least by, and never a figure the article's argument
 212    rests on.
 213  - Keep the headings and the section order.
 214  - Do not add a conclusion, a summary, or a line telling the reader what they
 215    just read.
 216  
 217  Return the complete edited article as markdown, and nothing else. No preamble,
 218  no notes on what you changed, no list of edits.
 219  
 220  TITLE: {title}
 221  
 222  ARTICLE
 223  {article_markdown}
 224  """
apps/backend/app/features/prompt2blog/section_edit_v4.py
   1  """One section, one asked-for improvement, shown before it is applied.
   2  
   3  Improvement 07. An editor reading a finished draft can see that one paragraph
   4  hedges where it should choose, and the only tools available were to rewrite it
   5  by hand or to re-run the article. Repair is not that tool: it is driven by an
   6  audit, it fires once per run inside a token budget, and it decides for itself
   7  what to change.
   8  
   9  So: pick a section, pick one of a few things to ask for, read the proposal
  10  beside the original, and apply it or throw it away. Everything about the
  11  mechanism is borrowed from the repair work in #547 -- addressed sections, text
  12  hashes, replacements applied in code -- because that machinery already refuses
  13  the two failures that matter, an edit written against an older draft and an
  14  edit that touches prose nobody asked about.
  15  
  16  Three things this is not
  17  ------------------------
  18  It is not a gate. Nothing runs it, nothing waits for it, and a run that never
  19  uses it is unaffected.
  20  
  21  It is not allowed to bring new facts. The edit is shown the frozen packet --
  22  the same facts the writer had -- and nothing else. A request the evidence
  23  cannot support comes back as a refusal with a reason, because the failure mode
  24  of an editor asking for a stronger recommendation is a model inventing the
  25  thing that would make it stronger.
  26  
  27  And it is not trusted. The proposal is checked for figures that appear neither
  28  in the original nor anywhere in the packet before a person is shown it, and the
  29  person still has to press apply.
  30  """
  31  
  32  from __future__ import annotations
  33  
  34  import uuid
  35  from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  36  from typing import Any
  37  
  38  from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
  39  
  40  from .article_memory import build_article_memory
  41  from .content.sections import ArticleSection, segment_article
  42  from .dependencies import PipelineDependencies
  43  from .edit_review import EditReview
  44  from .provenance import _figures
  45  from .support import _safe_dict, _safe_str
  46  
  47  # Bumped when a stored edit history stops meaning what this code reads.
  48  SECTION_EDIT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1
  49  
  50  # Where an article's edit history lives. Its own row: these are an operator's
  51  # later work on a finished run, and writing them into the pipeline artifact
  52  # would rewrite the record of what the pipeline itself produced.
  53  SECTION_EDIT_STAGE = "stage_v4_section_edits"
  54  
  55  
  56  # The things an editor actually asks for, as opposed to a free-text box.
  57  #
  58  # A free-text box was the obvious design and it is the wrong one. "Make this
  59  # better" is a request only a model with an opinion can satisfy, and the
  60  # opinion it reaches for is the house style of the internet. Each of these
  61  # names a specific defect and says what fixing it may not cost.
  62  @dataclass(frozen=True)
  63  class EditAction:
  64      action_id: str
  65      label: str
  66      instruction: str
  67  
  68  
  69  EDIT_ACTIONS: tuple[EditAction, ...] = (
  70      EditAction(
  71          action_id="clarify_recommendation",
  72          label="Make the recommendation clearer",
  73          instruction=(
  74              "This section lays out options without saying what separates them. "
  75              "Say which suits whom and on what basis, using only the facts "
  76              "supplied. If the facts do not support choosing between them, say "
  77              "so in `could_not_do` and leave the section alone -- do not invent "
  78              "the difference that would make a recommendation possible."
  79          ),
  80      ),
  81      EditAction(
  82          action_id="shorten",
  83          label="Say it in fewer words",
  84          instruction=(
  85              "Cut the words this section does not need. Every figure, date, "
  86              "qualification and named place in the original must still be there "
  87              "afterwards: shortening is removing padding, never removing the "
  88              "limits that change what a reader should do."
  89          ),
  90      ),
  91      EditAction(
  92          action_id="reduce_repetition",
  93          label="Stop it repeating itself",
  94          instruction=(
  95              "This section explains the same thing more than once, or lists "
  96              "items whose descriptions run to the same shape. Say each thing "
  97              "once and vary what the sentences do. Losing a fact is not "
  98              "de-duplication."
  99          ),
 100      ),
 101      EditAction(
 102          action_id="strengthen_comparison",
 103          label="Make the comparison do more work",
 104          instruction=(
 105              "This section names things without comparing them. Say what each "
 106              "is better and worse for, from the supplied facts only. Where the "
 107              "facts support no comparison on some axis, leave that axis out "
 108              "rather than asserting one."
 109          ),
 110      ),
 111      EditAction(
 112          action_id="explain_the_detail",
 113          label="Explain a detail instead of listing more",
 114          instruction=(
 115              "This section stacks facts without saying what any of them mean. "
 116              "Keep the two or three that carry the point and explain their "
 117              "significance; the rest may go. Anything under the article's "
 118              "must_name obligations stays."
 119          ),
 120      ),
 121  )
 122  
 123  EDIT_ACTIONS_BY_ID = {action.action_id: action for action in EDIT_ACTIONS}
 124  
 125  
 126  SECTION_EDIT_SCHEMA: dict[str, Any] = {
 127      "type": "object",
 128      "required": ["revised"],
 129      "properties": {
 130          "revised": {"type": "string"},
 131          "heading": {"type": "string"},
 132          "what_changed": {"type": "string"},
 133          # The refusal has to be as easy to return as the rewrite, or a model
 134          # asked for something impossible writes something instead.
 135          "could_not_do": {"type": "string"},
 136      },
 137  }
 138  
 139  
 140  P2B_SECTION_EDIT_PROMPT = """\
 141  You are editing one section of a finished article, at an editor's request.
 142  
 143  Return strict JSON only:
 144  {{
 145    "revised": "string",
 146    "what_changed": "string",
 147    "could_not_do": "string"
 148  }}
 149  
 150  What you were asked to do:
 151  {instruction}
 152  
 153  Hard rules:
 154  - Change this section and nothing else. You are not shown the rest of the
 155    article and you are not editing it.
 156  - Every figure, date, price, duration and named place in `revised` must appear
 157    either in the ORIGINAL SECTION below or in the FACTS AVAILABLE. You may not
 158    introduce one from anywhere else, and you may not make a figure more precise,
 159    more recent, or more general than the fact it comes from.
 160  - Keep the limits that change what a reader should do -- an as-of date, a
 161    season, a route only some operators run. Drop only hedging that changes
 162    nothing.
 163  - Never cite the facts. No claim IDs, no source names, no "(Source 1)". The
 164    reader cannot see them.
 165  - If what you were asked for cannot be done with the facts available, put the
 166    reason in `could_not_do` and return the original text unchanged in `revised`.
 167    That is a correct answer. Writing something that only looks like what was
 168    asked for is not.
 169  - `what_changed` is one sentence, for a person deciding whether to keep this.
 170  
 171  WHAT THE REST OF THE ARTICLE ALREADY DOES (navigation, not evidence):
 172  This is here so you do not explain a second time what another section has
 173  already explained, and do not recommend something the article has already
 174  decided against. It is quoted from the draft, not summarised. It is NOT a
 175  source of facts: every figure and date you write must still come from the
 176  ORIGINAL SECTION or the FACTS AVAILABLE, and a number that appears only here
 177  is a number you may not use.
 178  {memory}
 179  
 180  THE ARTICLE THIS SECTION BELONGS TO:
 181  {brief}
 182  
 183  FACTS AVAILABLE (the only facts you may use):
 184  {facts}
 185  
 186  ORIGINAL SECTION:
 187  {original}
 188  """
 189  
 190  
 191  def _facts_block(packet: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
 192      """The frozen packet, as the writer received it.
 193  
 194      Whole rather than narrowed to the section. Narrowing would need a guess at
 195      which facts this section rests on, and a guess that guessed wrong would
 196      withhold the fact the editor is asking to have explained.
 197      """
 198      lines: list[str] = []
 199      for fact in packet.get("facts") or []:
 200          record = _safe_dict(fact)
 201          text = _safe_str(record.get("text"))
 202          if not text:
 203              continue
 204          as_of = _safe_str(record.get("as_of"))
 205          note = _safe_str(record.get("operator_note"))
 206          suffix = "".join(
 207              part
 208              for part in (
 209                  f" (as of {as_of})" if as_of else "",
 210                  f" [you noted: {note}]" if note else "",
 211              )
 212          )
 213          lines.append(f"- {text}{suffix}")
 214      for note in packet.get("notes") or []:
 215          text = _safe_str(_safe_dict(note).get("text"))
 216          if text:
 217              lines.append(f"- LIMIT: {text}")
 218      for material in packet.get("supplied_material") or []:
 219          statement = _safe_str(_safe_dict(material).get("statement"))
 220          if statement:
 221              lines.append(f"- YOUR OWN NOTE, verbatim: {statement}")
 222      return "\n".join(lines) or "No facts were recorded for this article."
 223  
 224  
 225  def _brief_block(brief: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
 226      record = _safe_dict(brief)
 227      parts = [
 228          f"Headline: {_safe_str(record.get('seed'))}",
 229          f"Reader: {_safe_str(_safe_dict(record.get('reader')).get('primary_reader'))}",
 230          f"Their question: {_safe_str(record.get('reader_question'))}",
 231          f"What they should be able to do: {_safe_str(record.get('outcome'))}",
 232          f"It fails if: {_safe_str(record.get('fails_if'))}",
 233      ]
 234      must_name = [name for name in (record.get("must_name") or []) if _safe_str(name)]
 235      if must_name:
 236          parts.append(f"Must name: {', '.join(must_name)}")
 237      return "\n".join(parts)
 238  
 239  
 240  class EditProposal(BaseModel):
 241      """A change offered, not made."""
 242  
 243      schema_version: int = SECTION_EDIT_SCHEMA_VERSION
 244      run_id: str
 245      # This proposal, once, forever. A double-click and a retried request send
 246      # the same object twice; the second arrives against a revision the first
 247      # advanced past, and without an id that reads as a conflict and sends an
 248      # editor to re-read prose that already says what they wanted.
 249      edit_id: str = ""
 250      # Which version of the whole article this was read from. The section hash
 251      # says the paragraph has not moved; this says the document has not, which
 252      # is the difference between refusing an edit to prose that changed and
 253      # refusing a write that would discard someone else's accepted edit
 254      # elsewhere in the same draft.
 255      base_revision: int = -1
 256      section_id: str
 257      heading: str = ""
 258      action_id: str
 259      # What the section said when this was proposed. `apply` refuses if it has
 260      # moved since, so a proposal read on one screen cannot land on another.
 261      text_hash: str
 262      original: str
 263      revised: str
 264      what_changed: str = ""
 265      could_not_do: str = ""
 266      # Figures in the proposal that are in neither the original nor the packet.
 267      # Deterministic, cheap, and the exact shape of one failure this invites: an
 268      # editor asks for a stronger recommendation and gets a number that would
 269      # make one.
 270      #
 271      # A warning aid, and no longer the whole factual review. It compares sets
 272      # of tokens, so swapping two prices the packet already contains is
 273      # invisible to it -- which is what `review` is for.
 274      introduced_figures: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
 275      # What a checker made of the candidate, read against the frozen packet in
 276      # the article it sits in. `None` on a refusal or a no-op, where there is no
 277      # new prose to judge.
 278      review: EditReview | None = None
 279  
 280      @property
 281      def changed(self) -> bool:
 282          return self.revised.strip() != self.original.strip()
 283  
 284  
 285  def _packet_figures(packet: dict[str, Any]) -> set[str]:
 286      """Every figure the model was shown, which is not the same as every fact.
 287  
 288      This has to cover exactly what `_facts_block` puts in the prompt. It used
 289      to read `text` and `statement` only, while the prompt also carries each
 290      fact's as-of date, the operator's note on it, and the limit notes -- so a
 291      model that correctly wrote "as of March 2026" had 2026 reported as a figure
 292      it invented.
 293  
 294      Found on the first live call this code ever made, against a brief whose
 295      `fails_if` was "quotes a fare without saying when it was true". The model
 296      did the right thing and the guard called it an invention. A warning that
 297      fires on correct work is worse than no warning: it is the one an editor
 298      learns to click past.
 299      """
 300      parts: list[str] = []
 301      for fact in packet.get("facts") or []:
 302          record = _safe_dict(fact)
 303          parts.extend(
 304              (
 305                  _safe_str(record.get("text")),
 306                  _safe_str(record.get("as_of")),
 307                  _safe_str(record.get("operator_note")),
 308              )
 309          )
 310      for note in packet.get("notes") or []:
 311          parts.append(_safe_str(_safe_dict(note).get("text")))
 312      for item in packet.get("supplied_material") or []:
 313          parts.append(_safe_str(_safe_dict(item).get("statement")))
 314      return _figures(" ".join(part for part in parts if part))
 315  
 316  
 317  def find_section(content: str, section_id: str) -> ArticleSection | None:
 318      for section in segment_article(content):
 319          if section.section_id == section_id:
 320              return section
 321      return None
 322  
 323  
 324  def propose_section_edit(
 325      *,
 326      run_id: str,
 327      content: str,
 328      section_id: str,
 329      action_id: str,
 330      brief: dict[str, Any],
 331      packet: dict[str, Any],
 332      dependencies: PipelineDependencies,
 333      base_revision: int = -1,
 334      model_name: str | None = None,
 335      outline: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
 336  ) -> EditProposal:
 337      """Ask for one change to one section. Nothing is written.
 338  
 339      Raises rather than guessing when the section or the action is not one this
 340      draft has: an editor who clicked something that no longer exists should be
 341      told, not handed an edit to a different paragraph.
 342      """
 343      action = EDIT_ACTIONS_BY_ID.get(action_id)
 344      if action is None:
 345          raise ValueError(f"Unknown edit action '{action_id}'")
 346      section = find_section(content, section_id)
 347      if section is None:
 348          raise ValueError(f"This draft has no section '{section_id}'")
 349  
 350      original = section.render()
 351      # Rebuilt from the draft as it is now, so an edit accepted a minute ago is
 352      # already part of what the next one is told (improvement 03). Free and
 353      # deterministic, which is why refreshing it costs nothing to do every time
 354      # rather than being cached and going stale.
 355      memory = build_article_memory(content, outline)
 356      prompt = P2B_SECTION_EDIT_PROMPT.format(
 357          instruction=action.instruction,
 358          memory=memory.for_prompt(excluding=section_id)
 359          or "This article has no other sections.",
 360          brief=_brief_block(brief),
 361          facts=_facts_block(packet),
 362          original=original,
 363      )
 364      parsed, _raw = dependencies.llm.invoke_json(
 365          job_id="p2b.section_edit",
 366          prompt=prompt,
 367          max_tokens=2048,
 368          temperature=0.2,
 369          model_name=model_name,
 370          schema=SECTION_EDIT_SCHEMA,
 371      )
 372      record = _safe_dict(parsed)
 373      revised = _safe_str(record.get("revised")).strip()
 374      could_not_do = _safe_str(record.get("could_not_do")).strip()
 375      if not revised:
 376          # An empty body is far more likely to be a truncated response than a
 377          # considered cut, and this pass may not delete a section in any case.
 378          revised = original
 379          could_not_do = could_not_do or "The edit came back empty, so nothing changed."
 380      if could_not_do:
 381          # A refusal and a replacement are different answers, and a response
 382          # that gives both has not answered. The prompt asks for the original
 383          # back verbatim alongside `could_not_do`; what came back on the probe
 384          # was "Cannot support this" beside prose carrying a $999 nobody had
 385          # ever seen, and the screen offered it as an ordinary proposal because
 386          # the text differed from the original.
 387          #
 388          # Normalised here rather than shown with a warning. An advisory
 389          # finding is something a person may knowingly accept; there is nothing
 390          # to accept in a change the model has just said it could not make.
 391          revised = original
 392  
 393      introduced = sorted(
 394          _figures(revised) - _figures(original) - _packet_figures(packet)
 395      )
 396      return EditProposal(
 397          run_id=run_id,
 398          edit_id=uuid.uuid4().hex,
 399          base_revision=base_revision,
 400          section_id=section_id,
 401          heading=section.heading,
 402          action_id=action_id,
 403          text_hash=section.text_hash,
 404          original=original,
 405          revised=revised,
 406          what_changed=_safe_str(record.get("what_changed")),
 407          could_not_do=could_not_do,
 408          introduced_figures=introduced,
 409      )
 410  
 411  
 412  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 413  # Applying, and taking it back
 414  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 415  
 416  
 417  class AppliedEdit(BaseModel):
 418      """One applied edit, and the whole draft as it was before it."""
 419  
 420      # The proposal this came from, so a repeat of it can be recognised as the
 421      # same edit rather than applied a second time.
 422      edit_id: str = ""
 423      section_id: str
 424      action_id: str
 425      applied_at: str = ""
 426      editor: str = ""
 427      what_changed: str = ""
 428      # The entire previous markdown, not a patch. Undo has to be exact, and a
 429      # patch that no longer applies is an undo that silently does not.
 430      previous_markdown: str = ""
 431      # The one section, before and after, and why the operator wanted it
 432      # (improvement 05). The whole-draft copy above is for undo and is the wrong
 433      # shape for reading a pattern out of: what recurs is a kind of sentence
 434      # being replaced by another kind, and that is only visible at this size.
 435      before: str = ""
 436      after: str = ""
 437      # Typed by the operator, and optional. A reason is the difference between
 438      # "this one was wrong" and "we always want this", and nothing should be
 439      # inferred from its absence.
 440      reason: str = ""
 441      # Which form the article was, so a correction that only ever happens on one
 442      # kind of piece cannot be read as a rule about all of them.
 443      form_id: str = ""
 444      # What the checker said about this text, and -- when it said something an
 445      # editor went ahead anyway -- that they did. Recorded rather than implied:
 446      # "nobody checked", "it checked out" and "it did not and we kept it" are
 447      # three different things to find in a history six weeks later.
 448      review_status: str = "unchecked"
 449      accepted_despite: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
 450  
 451  
 452  class EditHistory(BaseModel):
 453      schema_version: int = SECTION_EDIT_SCHEMA_VERSION
 454      edits: list[AppliedEdit] = Field(default_factory=list)
 455      # The draft as the pipeline produced it, before any hand edit. Kept
 456      # separately from the undo stack: the report asks for the original draft to
 457      # be retained, and an undo stack unwound one step at a time is not that.
 458      original_markdown: str = ""
 459  
 460  
 461  @dataclass
 462  class ApplyResult:
 463      markdown: str
 464      history: EditHistory
 465      rejected: list[dict[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
 466  
 467      @property
 468      def applied(self) -> bool:
 469          return not self.rejected
 470  
 471  
 472  def apply_proposal(
 473      *,
 474      content: str,
 475      proposal: EditProposal,
 476      history: EditHistory,
 477      editor: str,
 478      now: str,
 479      reason: str = "",
 480      form_id: str = "",
 481      review_status: str = "unchecked",
 482      accepted_despite: list[str] | None = None,
 483  ) -> ApplyResult:
 484      """Write one accepted proposal into the draft, keeping what it replaced.
 485  
 486      The hash check is the whole safety property: a proposal read on one screen
 487      while another edit landed on the same section is refused rather than
 488      applied over the top of it. `apply_section_replacements` already enforces
 489      that, along with the rules that an edit may not empty a section and may not
 490      give the opening block a heading.
 491  
 492      The refusal invariant is checked here too, not only where the proposal was
 493      made. `propose_section_edit` normalises a refused answer back to the
 494      original, but a proposal reaches this function as a request body: the
 495      server that decided what a refusal means has to be the server that holds
 496      the meaning, or a client can hand the same object back with the prose put
 497      in again and have it accepted as an ordinary edit.
 498      """
 499      from .content.sections import apply_section_replacements
 500  
 501      if proposal.could_not_do and proposal.changed:
 502          return ApplyResult(
 503              markdown=content,
 504              history=history,
 505              rejected=[
 506                  {
 507                      "section_id": proposal.section_id,
 508                      "reason": (
 509                          "this proposal says it could not make the change and "
 510                          "changes the text as well"
 511                      ),
 512                  }
 513              ],
 514          )
 515      if not proposal.changed:
 516          # Not an error, and not history either. An accepted edit is a record
 517          # of prose a person chose over other prose, and pattern learning reads
 518          # that record: a no-op filed into it is a correction that never
 519          # happened, counting towards the threshold that decides whether the
 520          # voice file should change.
 521          return ApplyResult(
 522              markdown=content,
 523              history=history,
 524              rejected=[
 525                  {
 526                      "section_id": proposal.section_id,
 527                      "reason": "this proposal does not change the section",
 528                  }
 529              ],
 530          )
 531  
 532      result = apply_section_replacements(
 533          content,
 534          [
 535              {
 536                  "section_id": proposal.section_id,
 537                  "text_hash": proposal.text_hash,
 538                  "heading": proposal.heading,
 539                  "content": _body_of(proposal.revised, proposal.heading),
 540              }
 541          ],
 542      )
 543      if not result.changed:
 544          return ApplyResult(markdown=content, history=history, rejected=result.rejected)
 545  
 546      updated = EditHistory(
 547          # Recorded on the first hand edit and never again, so "the draft the
 548          # pipeline produced" survives any number of later edits.
 549          original_markdown=history.original_markdown or content,
 550          edits=[
 551              *history.edits,
 552              AppliedEdit(
 553                  edit_id=proposal.edit_id,
 554                  section_id=proposal.section_id,
 555                  action_id=proposal.action_id,
 556                  applied_at=now,
 557                  editor=editor,
 558                  what_changed=proposal.what_changed,
 559                  previous_markdown=content,
 560                  before=proposal.original,
 561                  after=proposal.revised,
 562                  reason=reason,
 563                  form_id=form_id,
 564                  review_status=review_status,
 565                  accepted_despite=list(accepted_despite or []),
 566              ),
 567          ],
 568      )
 569      return ApplyResult(markdown=result.content, history=updated)
 570  
 571  
 572  def _body_of(rendered: str, heading: str) -> str:
 573      """The prose under a heading, given a section rendered whole.
 574  
 575      The model is shown the section as it appears in the article, heading and
 576      all, because a heading is part of what it is being asked to judge. The
 577      replacement machinery wants them apart.
 578      """
 579      text = rendered.strip()
 580      if not heading:
 581          return text
 582      first, _, rest = text.partition("\n")
 583      if first.strip().lstrip("#").strip() == heading.strip():
 584          return rest.strip()
 585      return text
 586  
 587  
 588  def undo_last(history: EditHistory) -> tuple[str, EditHistory] | None:
 589      """Put the draft back to what it was before the last applied edit.
 590  
 591      Returns None when there is nothing to undo, which the caller reports rather
 592      than treating as a failure: pressing undo on an unedited draft is not an
 593      error, it is a question with a plain answer.
 594      """
 595      if not history.edits:
 596          return None
 597      last = history.edits[-1]
 598      return last.previous_markdown, EditHistory(
 599          original_markdown=history.original_markdown,
 600          edits=history.edits[:-1],
 601      )
apps/backend/app/features/prompt2blog/resume_v3.py
   1  """Resuming a v3 run that failed part-way through.
   2  
   3  A v3 run can spend a couple of hundred thousand tokens before it reaches the
   4  title stage. When the last call of a long run failed -- an exhausted Claude
   5  account, a provider blip -- everything the run had already produced was still
   6  correct and still stored, and the only way forward was to start again from the
   7  outline and buy all of it a second time.
   8  
   9  So each completed node writes the whole graph state to the run's own
  10  `resume_snapshot` stage row, and a resume restores that state and re-enters
  11  the graph at the node the failure interrupted. Nothing is regenerated: the
  12  outline, the draft, the grounding verdict, the audit scores, the repair count
  13  and the best-draft record all come back exactly as they were written.
  14  
  15  Why the stage row and not LangGraph's checkpoints
  16  -------------------------------------------------
  17  The graph already writes checkpoints, and they are already thrown away on the
  18  way out of every run (see `app/ai_graph/runtime.py`). Reusing them would mean
  19  keeping a shared, opaque, run-sized store that nobody can read, and it would
  20  still be empty in the case that matters most -- a process that died hard, which
  21  is when the cleanup never ran either. The stage row is this run's own durable
  22  record, it survives a restart, and an operator can read it.
  23  
  24  Correctness before saving money
  25  -------------------------------
  26  A resume that restored the wrong state would publish an article whose prose,
  27  scores and evidence do not describe each other. Every check here fails closed:
  28  an unreadable snapshot, a snapshot written by a different version of this code,
  29  a snapshot whose brief is not the brief the run started with, or a
  30  run that is not actually in a failed state, all refuse the resume and cost
  31  nothing. Refusing means starting a fresh run, which is exactly what happens
  32  today.
  33  """
  34  
  35  from __future__ import annotations
  36  
  37  import json
  38  import logging
  39  from dataclasses import dataclass
  40  from typing import Any
  41  
  42  from app.core import read_stage_result, read_status
  43  
  44  from .config import FEATURE_NAME, P2B_RESUME_MAX_ATTEMPTS
  45  from .graph.state import Prompt2BlogV3GraphState
  46  from .graph.topology_v3 import (
  47      V3_GENERATION_NODES,
  48      V3_NODE_STAGE_NAMES,
  49      next_v3_node,
  50  )
  51  from .intake_v3 import RUN_INPUT_STAGE
  52  from .models import PipelineV4RuntimeRequest
  53  from .observability import _now_iso
  54  from .run_recorder import USAGE_LEDGER_STAGE
  55  from .support import _safe_dict, _safe_int, _safe_str
  56  
  57  logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  58  
  59  RESUME_SNAPSHOT_STAGE = "resume_snapshot"
  60  
  61  # The append-only record of every resume attempt, written by the orchestrator
  62  # before a resumed leg starts. Named here because the allowance is counted off
  63  # it and the two must not drift.
  64  RESUME_HISTORY_STAGE = "pipeline_resume_v3"
  65  
  66  # Bumped whenever the stored shape stops meaning what this code reads. An
  67  # older snapshot is refused rather than reinterpreted: guessing at a state
  68  # written by different code is how a resume publishes mismatched work.
  69  #
  70  # 4: the headline stage is gone (ADR 0034). A version-3 snapshot can name
  71  # `title` as its next node, and that node no longer exists. Refused by version
  72  # here, so the operator is told the snapshot is from older code rather than
  73  # being handed a vaguer complaint about an unrunnable stage from further in.
  74  #
  75  # 5: the writing packet. A version-4 snapshot carries no `packet`, and the
  76  # stages that read one would either fall over or, worse, resume writing from
  77  # the whole dossier -- the exact silent widening the packet exists to prevent.
  78  # Refused, and a refusal costs nothing: starting again is what happened before
  79  # resume existed at all.
  80  #
  81  # 6: section payoffs (improvement 01). A version-5 snapshot's outline sections
  82  # carry `purpose`, and the formatters that hand the plan to compose and to the
  83  # audit read `reader_payoff`, so a resumed leg would fail on the field name --
  84  # or, if that were papered over, write from a plan whose promises the audit
  85  # would then check against nothing. Refused by version, which says why.
  86  RESUME_SNAPSHOT_VERSION = 6
  87  
  88  # State entries rebuilt on the way back in rather than stored. `request` is a
  89  # pydantic model and is written out under its own key; `completed` belongs to
  90  # the leg that is running, not to the one that stopped.
  91  _UNSNAPSHOTTED_STATE_KEYS = frozenset({"request", "completed"})
  92  
  93  
  94  @dataclass(frozen=True)
  95  class ResumePlan:
  96      """What resuming one run would do, decided without spending anything.
  97  
  98      Answers the operator's question before the money question: what is already
  99      written, what the next call would be, and what the failed leg cost. A plan
 100      that is not resumable says why in `reason`, which is the same string the
 101      resume endpoint refuses with.
 102      """
 103  
 104      run_id: str
 105      resumable: bool
 106      reason: str
 107      resume_from_stage: str | None = None
 108      failed_stage: str | None = None
 109      failure_kind: str | None = None
 110      completed_stages: tuple[str, ...] = ()
 111      tokens_already_spent: int | None = None
 112      resume_count: int = 0
 113      resume_attempts_allowed: int = P2B_RESUME_MAX_ATTEMPTS
 114  
 115      def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
 116          return {
 117              "run_id": self.run_id,
 118              "resumable": self.resumable,
 119              "reason": self.reason,
 120              "resume_from_stage": self.resume_from_stage,
 121              "failed_stage": self.failed_stage,
 122              "failure_kind": self.failure_kind,
 123              "completed_stages": list(self.completed_stages),
 124              "tokens_already_spent": self.tokens_already_spent,
 125              "resume_count": self.resume_count,
 126              "resume_attempts_allowed": self.resume_attempts_allowed,
 127          }
 128  
 129  
 130  def _stage_data(run_id: str, stage: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 131      """The payload half of one stage row, or an empty dict."""
 132      row = read_stage_result(run_id, stage)
 133      return _safe_dict(_safe_dict(row).get("data"))
 134  
 135  
 136  def snapshot_payload(
 137      state: Prompt2BlogV3GraphState,
 138      *,
 139      completed_node: str,
 140  ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 141      """The durable record of one finished node, ready to be stored.
 142  
 143      `next_node` is decided here rather than at resume time, using the same
 144      `route_quality_gate` the compiled graph would have used on this state. The
 145      branch a run would have taken is therefore a fact recorded at the moment it
 146      was true, not a re-derivation from a state that has since been reloaded.
 147      """
 148      request = state["request"]
 149      stored_state = {
 150          key: value
 151          for key, value in state.items()
 152          if key not in _UNSNAPSHOTTED_STATE_KEYS
 153      }
 154      return {
 155          "snapshot_version": RESUME_SNAPSHOT_VERSION,
 156          "run_id": state["run_id"],
 157          "schema_version": request.schema_version,
 158          "brief_fingerprint": _safe_str(
 159              _safe_dict(state.get("brief")).get("brief_fingerprint")
 160          ),
 161          "completed_node": completed_node,
 162          "completed_stage": V3_NODE_STAGE_NAMES[completed_node],
 163          "next_node": next_v3_node(completed_node, dict(state)),
 164          "resume_count": _safe_int(state.get("resume_count"), default=0),
 165          "created_at": _now_iso(),
 166          "request": request.model_dump(mode="json"),
 167          "state": stored_state,
 168      }
 169  
 170  
 171  def write_resume_snapshot(
 172      recorder: Any,
 173      state: Prompt2BlogV3GraphState,
 174      *,
 175      completed_node: str,
 176  ) -> None:
 177      """Store the state after one node, or store nothing.
 178  
 179      Serialization is strict on purpose. `write_stage_result` stringifies
 180      anything it cannot encode, which would leave a snapshot that loads without
 181      complaint and restores a state made of `repr` strings. A snapshot that
 182      cannot be written exactly is not written at all: the run continues, and the
 183      worst case is the behaviour that existed before resume did.
 184      """
 185      try:
 186          payload = snapshot_payload(state, completed_node=completed_node)
 187          json.dumps(payload, allow_nan=False)
 188      except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- never break a healthy run
 189          logger.warning(
 190              "Prompt2Blog v3 resume snapshot skipped after %s: %s: %s",
 191              completed_node,
 192              type(exc).__name__,
 193              exc,
 194          )
 195          return
 196      try:
 197          recorder.record_stage(state["run_id"], RESUME_SNAPSHOT_STAGE, payload)
 198      except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- never break a healthy run
 199          logger.warning("Prompt2Blog v3 resume snapshot write failed: %s", exc)
 200  
 201  
 202  def discard_resume_snapshot(recorder: Any, run_id: str) -> None:
 203      """Drop the snapshot once the run has an article instead.
 204  
 205      A finished run is not resumable, and its state is a whole graph state --
 206      draft, trace and all -- with no reader left. The status guard would refuse
 207      a resume anyway; this keeps the row from outliving its purpose.
 208      """
 209      discard = getattr(recorder, "discard_stage", None)
 210      if callable(discard):
 211          discard(run_id, RESUME_SNAPSHOT_STAGE)
 212  
 213  
 214  def resume_attempts_used(run_id: str) -> int:
 215      """How many times this run has already been resumed.
 216  
 217      Counted from the append-only attempt history rather than from the
 218      snapshot, because a resume that dies before finishing a single node writes
 219      no new snapshot. Counting there would leave the allowance untouched by
 220      exactly the failure it exists to bound, and an operator could re-buy the
 221      same failing tail forever.
 222      """
 223      attempts = _stage_data(run_id, RESUME_HISTORY_STAGE).get("attempts")
 224      return len(attempts) if isinstance(attempts, list) else 0
 225  
 226  
 227  def stored_ledger(run_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 228      """The token ledger the earlier legs of this run wrote."""
 229      return _stage_data(run_id, USAGE_LEDGER_STAGE)
 230  
 231  
 232  def tokens_already_spent(run_id: str) -> int | None:
 233      ledger = stored_ledger(run_id)
 234      totals = ledger.get("totals")
 235      if not isinstance(totals, dict):
 236          return None
 237      return _safe_int(totals.get("total_tokens"), default=0)
 238  
 239  
 240  def completed_stages(run_id: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
 241      """Which v3 stages already have a recorded payload for this run."""
 242      return tuple(
 243          V3_NODE_STAGE_NAMES[node]
 244          for node in V3_GENERATION_NODES
 245          if read_stage_result(run_id, V3_NODE_STAGE_NAMES[node])
 246      )
 247  
 248  
 249  def _brief_agrees(run_id: str, snapshot: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
 250      """Do every record of which brief this run is for say the same thing?
 251  
 252      Three witnesses, of which at least two always exist: the snapshot header,
 253      the request stored inside it, and the state's own brief. A run started
 254      through the API adds a fourth -- the `pipeline_input_v3` row, written
 255      before the first node and never rewritten. They are compared rather than
 256      trusted individually, because the failure this guards against is a state
 257      that belongs to a different article, and one corrupted half is enough to
 258      publish prose whose scores and evidence describe something else.
 259      """
 260      snapshot_state = _safe_dict(snapshot.get("state"))
 261      request_payload = _safe_dict(snapshot.get("request"))
 262      fingerprints = {
 263          _safe_str(snapshot.get("brief_fingerprint")),
 264          _safe_str(
 265              _safe_dict(snapshot_state.get("brief")).get("brief_fingerprint")
 266          ),
 267          _safe_str(
 268              _safe_dict(request_payload.get("brief")).get(
 269                  "brief_fingerprint"
 270              )
 271          ),
 272          _safe_str(_stage_data(run_id, RUN_INPUT_STAGE).get("brief_fingerprint")),
 273      }
 274      # An absent witness is silence, not disagreement; a run recorded without a
 275      # fingerprint anywhere is caught by the empty set left behind.
 276      fingerprints.discard("")
 277      return len(fingerprints) == 1
 278  
 279  
 280  def plan_resume(run_id: str) -> ResumePlan:
 281      """Decide whether one run may be resumed, and from where.
 282  
 283      Reads only. Every refusal is named, because "not resumable" with no reason
 284      leaves an operator guessing whether to wait, reconnect an account, or pay
 285      for a whole new run.
 286      """
 287      status = read_status(run_id)
 288      if not status:
 289          return ResumePlan(run_id=run_id, resumable=False, reason="run_not_found")
 290      if status.get("feature") != FEATURE_NAME:
 291          return ResumePlan(run_id=run_id, resumable=False, reason="not_prompt2blog")
 292  
 293      failed_stage = _safe_str(status.get("stage")) or None
 294      failure_kind = _safe_str(status.get("failure_kind")) or None
 295      done = completed_stages(run_id)
 296      spent = tokens_already_spent(run_id)
 297      snapshot = _stage_data(run_id, RESUME_SNAPSHOT_STAGE)
 298      resume_count = resume_attempts_used(run_id)
 299  
 300      def refuse(reason: str) -> ResumePlan:
 301          return ResumePlan(
 302              run_id=run_id,
 303              resumable=False,
 304              reason=reason,
 305              failed_stage=failed_stage,
 306              failure_kind=failure_kind,
 307              completed_stages=done,
 308              tokens_already_spent=spent,
 309              resume_count=resume_count,
 310          )
 311  
 312      if status.get("state") != "failed":
 313          return refuse("run_not_failed")
 314      if not snapshot:
 315          # Nothing finished before the failure, so there is nothing to protect.
 316          return refuse("no_snapshot")
 317      if snapshot.get("snapshot_version") != RESUME_SNAPSHOT_VERSION:
 318          return refuse("snapshot_version_unsupported")
 319  
 320      request_payload = _safe_dict(snapshot.get("request"))
 321      if _safe_int(request_payload.get("schema_version"), default=0) != 4:
 322          return refuse("schema_version_unsupported")
 323  
 324      if not _brief_agrees(run_id, snapshot):
 325          return refuse("brief_mismatch")
 326  
 327      next_node = snapshot.get("next_node")
 328      if next_node is None:
 329          # The last node the run completed was finalize. Whatever failed after
 330          # that did not owe the operator another writing call.
 331          return refuse("run_already_finished")
 332      if next_node not in V3_GENERATION_NODES:
 333          return refuse("snapshot_unreadable")
 334      if resume_count >= P2B_RESUME_MAX_ATTEMPTS:
 335          return refuse("resume_limit_reached")
 336  
 337      return ResumePlan(
 338          run_id=run_id,
 339          resumable=True,
 340          reason="resumable",
 341          resume_from_stage=V3_NODE_STAGE_NAMES[next_node],
 342          failed_stage=failed_stage,
 343          failure_kind=failure_kind,
 344          completed_stages=done,
 345          tokens_already_spent=spent,
 346          resume_count=resume_count,
 347      )
 348  
 349  
 350  def restore_v3_state(
 351      run_id: str,
 352  ) -> tuple[Prompt2BlogV3GraphState, PipelineV4RuntimeRequest, str, int]:
 353      """Rebuild the state, the request, the entry node and the resume count.
 354  
 355      Call only behind a `plan_resume` that said yes; this raises rather than
 356      guessing, so a caller that skipped the checks fails loudly instead of
 357      running a half-restored article.
 358      """
 359      snapshot = _stage_data(run_id, RESUME_SNAPSHOT_STAGE)
 360      if not snapshot:
 361          raise ValueError(f"Run {run_id} has no resume snapshot")
 362      if snapshot.get("snapshot_version") != RESUME_SNAPSHOT_VERSION:
 363          raise ValueError(f"Run {run_id} snapshot version is not supported")
 364  
 365      entry_node = snapshot.get("next_node")
 366      if entry_node not in V3_GENERATION_NODES:
 367          raise ValueError(f"Run {run_id} snapshot names no runnable next stage")
 368  
 369      request = PipelineV4RuntimeRequest.model_validate(_safe_dict(snapshot["request"]))
 370      resume_count = resume_attempts_used(run_id) + 1
 371  
 372      state: Prompt2BlogV3GraphState = dict(  # type: ignore[assignment]
 373          _safe_dict(snapshot.get("state"))
 374      )
 375      state["run_id"] = run_id
 376      state["request"] = request
 377      state["resume_count"] = resume_count
 378      # The trace is the run's debug record, not its state. It is restored so a
 379      # resumed run's debug payload still shows the stages that ran before the
 380      # failure rather than starting from the middle of the article.
 381      state.setdefault("trace", [])
 382      return state, request, entry_node, resume_count
 383  
 384  
 385  def resume_thread_id(run_id: str, resume_count: int) -> str:
 386      """A LangGraph thread id no earlier leg of this run has used."""
 387      return f"{run_id}#resume{resume_count}"
